sand pit developed on a SE-trending Holocene sand dune. Production from 1950-2013 was estimated at >300,000 tonne for building, concrete, and garden sand products.
coastal dunal sand of the Bridgewater Formation worked for filling sand and top dressing sand. Production from 1979-1982 was estimated at 3,000 tonnes. 1981 resource ~4500 tonne.
freestone slate quarry in host Cambrian Smith Bay Shale. Production from 1985-2008 ~3000t. Potential for large resources to SE side of Smith Creek.

quarry developed on Wisanger Basalt. Close jointing allowed quarrying without explosives or crushing. Production from 1953-1981 was estimated at 23,500 tonnes. resource estimate in 1982 of 152,400 tonne.

basalt flow of the Jurassic Wisanger Basalt, worked for use as road aggregate. Underlying fluvial sandstone ideal for fine quarry aggregate. Production from 1949-2003 was ~206550 tonne. Resource in 1982 of 996,000 tonne.
historic foreshore quarry used in 1840 as a source of material for road aggregate.
quartzite of the Tapanappa Formation as a major source of aggregate for the Middle River Dam project. Production from 1964-68 was estimated at 8,000m3. Resource ~27,000m3.
salt lake evaporite mainly worked for gypsum, with minor salt production from a thin, overlying horizon of halite in the 1900s. Quarrying of lake bed for gypsum from 1975-86 for ~2Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COMMONWEALTH SALT REFINING CO.; KIROKA; ML 1544; ML 47; ML 4902; ML 610; ML 611; ML 625; NEW LAKE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings developed on gypsite/organic mud overlain by 2m of crystalline gypsum, and 1m of gypsarenite. Operations commenced mid 1950s. Production from 1973-1992 ~2.92Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AORANGI GEM; BUICKS CLAIM; COXS CLAIM; HOG BAY; KANGAROO ISLAND AMALG. GEM SYNDICATE; KANGAROO ISLAND CHINASTONE AND CLAY CO.; W.A. KINGSBOROUGH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pegmatite to 80m wide worked for gem tourmaline, feldspar, kaolin and silica. Host was Kanmantoo Group metasandstone and schist. Tourmaline blue and green-coloured, kaolin poor quality. Depth of weathering generally to 126m.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Beryl,  Elbaite,  Kaolinite,  Microcline,  Plagioclase,  Quartz,  Tourmaline

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic shallow pit on weathered, iron oxide stained white clay for supply of material to the Hog Bay Brickworks. The clay may be either transported or deeply weathered Kanmantoo Group metasediment.too Group metasediment.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: C.T. MCGLEW AND J.N. DAVIS; GYPSUM 6; ML 50
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 230 acre lease on salt lake in 1909.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: F.E.R. KASEHAGEN AND W.T. TURNER; ML 329
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lease granted in 1939 on salt crust over a thin gypsum layer, with impervious mud bottom. Recorded production from 1933-36 of 26 tonne.

1m wide manganese oxide gossan on faulted contact Brighton Limestone - Tapley Hill Formation. Lode was associated with band of crystalline marble and calcareous sandstone in mica schist, and micaceous slate. Mn to 23%.
5 diamond holes on IP and soil geochemical anomaly of 3000 ppm Pb over >100m distance. Sub-economic  lead-zinc-copper mineralisation identified in Early Cambrian metasediment.

quartz veins with sulphides and gold in host slatey sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group. There were many small workings and 6 widely spaced shafts developed on minor quartz veins with secondary crystal growths into vugs. No production figure determined.

prospecting pit on a quartz vein associated with an alteration halo. explored by Monax Mining in 2006, with grid soil samples from the alteration halo returning anomalous Pb-Zn-Cu values. Host was sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group.

located in the general area of the Bonaventura and Graingers workings. Area of multiple shafts, and pits north of Bonaventura, and developed on northern extension of the mineralised lode at Bonaventura.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLUE GUM HILL; BONAVENTURA; COPPER MINE CREEK
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pod of bunch copper mineralisation in weathered shale. Production 40 tonnes at 10% Cu. Drilling in 2008 identified Pb-Zn mineralisation associated with NE cross cutting structure. Best value 5m @ 26.9% Zn in broader halo of 30m @ 1.23%Zn.
quartz reef prospected for silver-lead in host mylonite, and in a single shaft, now backfilled.
prospecting shaft and pits on an area of quartz float in host Kanmantoo Group. Location is uncertain, described as between Snaky, and Starvation Creeks, Kangaroo Island.
3 small diamonds were reported to have been recovered from stream sediment sampling in 1897. Report now highly questionable given the level of later sampling.
closely jointed rhyolitic ignimbrite of GRV for road making and rail ballast material. Resource calculated in 1978 ~100,000m3 in situ, with ~25,000 m3 quarried.
veins of celestite sweated out of Bulldog Shale host, and providing samples for the Geological Survey mineral specimen museum.
stream sediment sampling by Stockdale Prospecting Ltd in the late 1980s recovered microdiamonds from 3 separate locations within ~10km distance from each other in an area east of Lake Gilles.
discovery of a single micro-diamond during prospecting via loam sampling.
scrape on weathered Bulldog Shale, and on the east side of a track, with the clay tested for ceramic and refractory use.
group of opal workings on Bulldog Shale, marked as mine symbol on a topographic map.
group of opal workings on Bulldog Shale, marked as mine symbol on a topographic map.
>15 m deep shaft into Cretaceous Bulldog Shale, with no records of opal found.
diggings for opal on Bulldog Shale, not located accurately. No records of opal being recovered.
diggings for opal on host Bulldog Shale, shown on topographic map, but not located when field checked in the late 1980s.
weathered sandstone of the Corraberra Sandstone that was sold as ornamental ""aquarium' rock, due to the honeycombed nature of the weathering.
weathered sandstone of the Corraberra Sandstone that was sold as ornamental ""aquarium' rock, due to the honeycombed nature of the weathering.

trace sulphide near the base of the Andamooka Limestone section in drillcore of PLAYFORD #1. Sulphides as clots to 0.4 cm, being less than 1% by volume of the core. Depth of the sulphides was 151.45 m.
isolated hill of BIF with the appearance of a Palaeoproterozoic BIF (finely laminated), and was interpreted as being stratigraphically equivalent to the Wilgena Hill Jaspilite.

linear magnetic anomaly >1km on outcrop of BIF of Wilgena Hill Jaspilite, dip near vertical. Reconnaissance drilling at E end identified width 175m. Preliminary testwork identified head grade 28%Fe, 33%DTR. No resource estimated.

discordant barite vein, 100 m long, maximum 2 m wide, trending EW. It was located ~1.5 km NNE of Puttapa Zinc Mine, and 0.8 km east of Ajax Copper Mine. Workings consisted of several abandoned opencuts and shafts.
discontinuous vein in Wonoka Formation, maximum 1 m wide, average 0.5 m. Individual pods to 8 m long, and 1 m wide. Incomplete production records suggest ~3800 tonnes recovered.

barite lode 50m long, 3m wide infilling a shear, and crosscutting a shallow dipping shale of the Bunyeroo Formation. Resource estimate in 1980 of 200 tonne, with deposit depleted from 1980-83 with production of 3800 tonne,

NS-trending vein system of siderite-quartz in host red shale of Bunyeroo Formation. Production ~10 tonne @ 17%Cu. Drilling in 1969 identified malachite in fault, average 0.62% Cu for 19.8m. 2 deep diamond holes for values <0.01%Cu.

bulldozer trenches prospected an area of barite float over an area 300 m NS, width 0.5 m, averaging 0.2 m. At the north end was a small stockpile of 10 tonnes of barite. Minor copper mineralisation was also noted.

1 of 4 mines on Black Feather lode, a NS-trending epigenetic vein system composed of siderite and quartz in host red shale of the Bunyeroo Formation. Recorded production 81 tonnes ore, no grade figure.

Cu-Pb-Ba mineralisation in 4 lodes in breccia of host carbonate rock of the Ajax Limestone. A deeper Cu-Ba resource of 909,000t @ 8.25% Cu was delineated by drilling in 1973-75. Production from 1907-18 1473t ore.
fault breccia lode zone with Pb-Ag-(Zn) mineralisation in barite lode. Production not recorded but probably small.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BELTANA BROKEN HILL; BELTANA SILVER; EDIACARA SOUTH; WARRIOOTA; WINNOWIE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: zone of kaolinised, gossanous calcareous silts and shales immediately underlying a limestone bed. Main ore mineral was atacamite, also cerussite, trace copper minerals and gold recorded. Reccoreded production 752t @ 40%Pb, 311g/tAg.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Gypsum,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EDIACARA NORTH; MOUNT JAMES 10; MOUNT JAMES 11; MOUNT JAMES 13; MOUNT JAMES 5; MOUNT JAMES 9
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz veins locally ferruginous or manganiferous. Trend following a splinter fault from the NS Ediacara Fault. Reserves were calculated for the five largest veins, named Lodes A to E.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 4852; MOUNT JAMES 3; MOUNT JAMES HUT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite lode splitting into parallel and anastomosing veins.

barite vein in host Wonoka Formation, and trending N-NE adjacent to the NS-orientated Ediacara Fault. Average width was 1m, maximum to 5m, dip steep, exposed over a distance of 175m. No production, resource ~4200 tonne at 98%Ba.
numerous intersecting/anastomosing fracture-fill, discordant veins over an area of ~15 hectares. 5 main veins, with lode 3 resource estimated at 14,000t.

fracture-fill, siliceous vein, 110m long x maximum 2.5m wide, average 1m, indicated best grade 90.5%Ba. North and south terminations were ferruginous. No production record determined. Estimated resource 1984 at 3600 tonne at 90%Ba.
vein-barite in Wonoka Formation recorded during regional mapping by ACI Resources in 1984.
arcuate vein of barite in Wonoka Formation recorded during regional mapping.
discontinuous, discordant barite vein to 800' long.
2 discordant barite veins near a lithological contact between the Wonoka Formation, and the Pound Quartzite.
small, discordant barite vein near the contact between metasediment of the Wonoka Formation, and the Pound Quartzite.
discordant barite vein.

minor vein of barite of hydrothermal origin, trending WNW. It was the S of 4 sets of minor unnamed barite veins in the Warioota area, and south of Randell Lookout (see amdel rpt MT 149/76). It was prospected via a single shallow shaft.
1 of 4 occurrences in Warioota area. Vein trended NE, and was 30-60 m long, and <1 m wide. The discordant barite vein was possibly located along a splinter fault from the Ediacara Fault.

1 of 4 sets of unnamed barite veins in the Warioota area. At this location three small sets of barite veins trended NE, probably representing infills of small faults being splays off the larger Ediacra fault.

1 of 4 occurrences of minor unnamed barite veins in the Warioota area. This was the northernmost, trending NE. The discordant barite vein was possibly located along a splinter fault from the Ediacara Fault.

barite lode as fault infill. Minor offshoots and bifurcations, and crosscuts. Host was Moorillah Siltstone Member. The lodes radiated SW from the Nuccaleena Diapir. Production from ML 4537 was estimated at 4,500 tonnes from 1979-83.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Goethite,  Hematite,  Limonite,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite veins maximum width 6m, average 1m. Host was Moolooloo and Bayley Range Siltstone Members. The barite occurred as a 200 m wide zone of veins & fractures trending SW from Nuccaleena Diapir. Production from 1980-83 ~5,100 tonnes.
vein of crystalline barite as source of mineral specimens. Dimensions were 200 m long by 18 cm wide, trending NE, dipping 20-30 NW; and concordant with the bedding of the host rocks.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BELTANA RAPID ORE TREATMENT SYNDICATE; ML 4417; ML 4419; ML 4517
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: stratabound Cu mineralisation, with anomalous V in host bleached, brecciated siltstone of the Wilpena Group. Production ~252t ore from 1911-15 @ grades 1-3%Cu.

Cu mineralisation in  shale and sandstone of Wonoka Formation, and near ironstone outcrop in W margin of Beltana Diapir. Active from 1907 and 1911-1913. No production figure or grade recorded. Drill tested in the early 1970s for disappointing results.
soft decomposed slate, with green copper carbonate, with a shaft intersecting a lode ~1.2m wide. Sample collected in 1899 from a northern shaft assayed 7%Cu. No production figure or grade determined.

Cu mineralisation as nodules and malachite staining for >2km in host manganiferous limonitic zone within oolitic dolomite of Hawker Group. No production. Tested in 2 holes for slightly elevated Cu, best Zn 12,000ppm, and anomalous Pb.
concordant copper carbonate show in red shale horizons of the Proterozoic Bunyeroo Formation. The deposit was described as too thin and too low grade to be of any economic significance.
small stratabound copper carbonate shows in host red shale of the Bunyeroo Formation. Hole drilled in 1969 failed to intersect significant mineralisation, values < 100ppmCu.
stratiform Cu mineralisation in shale of the Bunyeroo Formation. Production for 1896 ~3.3t ore @  25% Cu.

discontinuous barite vein in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation,and with segregated quartz pods. Some quartz veining trended 140. Good quality barite was hand picked, estimated resource in 1976 to 2m depth of 340 tonne.
barite vein in host slate of the Wonoka Formation, and sub-parallel to an ENE-trending fault. Production from ML 4598 was estimated at 120 tonne in 1978. Resource estimate 1981 4,650 tonne.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Dolomite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz,  Vernadite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: scattered float of barite outlining a sub-cropping vein.

quartz and barite pods and stringers with copper carbonate staining. 6m shaft excavated. It penetrated barite contaminated with quartz, and iron oxide, with only rare copper sulphide and some carbonate recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.C. FISHER; J.H.M. FUCHS; L.V. ROBERTS AND C. DEMODE; MC 1040; MC 990; MC 993
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings on 4 barite veins, with minor production of 42 tonnes from the largest vein from 1947-49.
small pits on three barite lodes crosscutting host slate of the Wonoka Formation. resource estimated at 5,500 tonne, no grade determined.
area of hematite altered tectonite, with small barite lode in host Wonoka Formation, and located on the Muller Fault, a N-trending thrust fault dipping 45-60E.
small pits on a 200 m long quartz barite vein, with patches becoming dominantly quartz or quartz and iron oxide.

series of pods and lenses of vein-barite over a strike length of 80 m. The pods occurred as two parallel sets, and carried numerous inclusions of country rock. The pods became more siliceous to the NW.
unpublished record during mapping by the Geological Survey in the 1980s, 6m wide, discordant vein paralleling a NE-trending fault set in host Brachina Formation.
vein barite with trace copper mineralisation recorded. Located from mine symbol on Copley 250K map sheet.
unworked occurrence of hydrothermal barite veins, trending SW, and cross-cutting metasediment of the Elatina Formation.

1-4 cm wide vein of galena, with quartz-iron oxide gangue in host metasediment at top of Elatina Formation. 2nd vein, 3-8 cm wide, of quartz, earthy goethite with sparse galena, dip 80, strike 155. Dark cerussite coated a slickensided joint surface.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BULLOCK HEAD GAP; M1; ML 4636; ML 4637; ML 5926
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein with galena, calcite and siderite, width 5-30cm in host Brachina Formation. Production from 1968-85 ~162.1t for 55.1t pb, 13.6kg Ag. Also 1,246 gm gold in 1978.
7.5m shaft on quartz veinlets with rare malachite. Vein quartz, ironstone and siderite were noticed in dumps. Gossan samples assayed Cu to 1.7%, and anomalous Pb.
pits and shafts on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef, with coarsely banded siderite and sulphide mineralization. Host was calcareous siltstone of the Brachina Formation.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: copper carbonate as pods, coatings on slickensided joint and bedding surfaces in host metasediment intruded by diapiric rock, subsequently faulted, and drag folded. Old shaft exposed in a bulldozer cut. Samples gave anomalous Au, Mo.
shallow scrape located in a small gully, with malachite occurring as coatings and veins in ferruginous and calcite veined diapiric breccia.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COULTHARD; MC 6525; MCKENZIE COULTHARD AND MCKENZIE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: group of pits developed on EW-trending quartz-limonite-siderite veins with copper sulphides. The veins were roughly concordant with the bedding of the host metasediment. The sulphides included pyrite, galena, and minor chalcopyrite.

stratabound Pb-Ag-(Cu) mineralisation in quartz, gossans, and siderite veins in host shale of the Bunyeroo Formation.. ~2 tonnes galena ore on site, grab sample 80%Pb, 370 g/tAg. Galena occurred as lumps and blebs in deformed radiating forms.
minor malachite disseminated through a dolomite bed in a stratigraphically controlled trap in the Bunyaroo Formation.
cyclicly banded calcite in fracture zones in host limestone and siltstone of the Wonoka Formation. Worked for ornamental stone, for small production only, resource to 2m estimated at 108 tonnes.

quartz-iron oxide breccia zone showing plentiful copper carbonate. The breccia lode trended 035, dipped 75 SW, following the cleavage plane. The host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale was also partially brecciated.
shear-hosted Cu mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide reef.  Production from 1845-68 @ 650t @ 18-27% Cu. Drilling determined inferred resource of 216,600t @ 0.96%Cu, estimate for Au was ~0.2g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Atacamite,  Azurite,  Chalcopyrite,  Chrysocolla,  Cuprite,  Malachite
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ATICA; DUTTONS; GROVE; HUTTONS; NEW BURRA; PORT PIRIE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings on gossanous, quartz-iron oxide vein with trace copper carbonates, with fresh sulphide penetrated beneath the oxidised zone of host Skillogalee Dolomite. Production records only for 1847-51 of 51 tonne ore recovered.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Barite,  Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: APOINGA COPPER MINING CO.; J. GRANVILLE; J.R. IVEY; MC 553; ML 3; N. GRENFELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: several shafts on small veins trending 350, dipping 40-70 W, and parallel to the strike of the host shale, but discordant to them. The veins consisted of white quartz, calcite, siderite, minor iron oxide, with trace only of malachite and azurite.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-(copper sulphide) lode conformable to host Adelaidean slate. 1930s sampling and assaying of the lode returned only trace gold.

3 shafts to 30m on NS-tending lode of quartz veins to 1m. Limonite and small spots of azurite and malachite were oxidation products of fresh sulphides found in dump material. Vanadium mineral occurred in a yellow-olive mineral as coatings and pods.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Malachite,  Sulvanite
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Limonite,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CARN BREA; ST. ELMO MINING AND PROSPECTING SYNDICATE N.L.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: series of quartz stringers and veinlets in W zone ~8m wide, which could be traced on the surface for >100m in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Reports indicate 20 tonne ore were raised, none treated. 10 tonnes sorted ore at 9.2%Cu in E zone.

several prospecting shafts sunk through alluvium to bedrock onto a horizon of copper carbonate mineralisation (azurite and malachite) in host alluvial clay. Attempts to locate the source of the copper mineralisation were unsuccessful.

ironstone lode following the dip of country rock, trending NS, and dipping W. The lode contained calcite and siderite, with pockets of high-grade copper carbonate ore. Production 1851-61 870 tonne ironstone for flux, 76 tonne copper ore.

quartz-ironstone lode, trace calcite, siderite, pockets copper carbonate. Lode followed dip of country rock. The lode was 3-4 feet wide. The mine had underground development at five levels, mainly for ironstone for flux for use at the Burra smelters.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz lode carrying both copper and lead-silver mineralisation in Tapley Hill Formation.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Bismuthinite,  Chalcopyrite,  Cuprite,  Galena,  Malachite,  Silver

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-veined suphidic phyllite or altered mafic. Drilling identified anomalous Ni, Co, V, Y, Zn and REE in brecciated metasediment. Petrology as metasomatised dolomite-calcite-talc-chlorite breccia, and undeformed diorite intrusive.

scattered shallow workings on milky quartz vein, with some iron oxide boxworks, common large pods of pyrite in host sandstone unit of the Undalya Quartzite. Small prospecting pits located ~1km to SSW on strike of the sandstone unit.
quartz-iron oxide-calcite lode carrying earthy malachite in bleached shales of the Skilogalee Dolomite. Other country rock included granite and gneiss. No production figure determined.

quartz-iron & manganese oxide lode. Host rock was weathered, goethitic, micaceous slate and metasediment. Surface littered with limonite cubes after pyrite, and malachite specks. Production records were incomplete, with 21.8 tonnes exported in 1868.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 5-30cm wide quartz lode, dip 45W, in host sheared slate of the Appila Tillite. 2 grab samples from the lode assayed 33% and 72%Pb. It was reworked in 1935. A 6 tonne sample of Pb-Zn ore sent to Port Pirie contained anomalous Ag-Au.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEECHWORTH; BUTLER; GL 1668; GL 1669; HARRIS AND RAWLINGS; MC 3307; TWIGHAM LEAD; TWIGHAMS EAST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gold-bearing alluvium, and small, brecciated, quartz veins with the gold associated with pyrite. Host was weathered Skillogalee Dolomite. Incomplete production figure of 13.5 tonne for 124.5gm gold at 9.2g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: copper carbonate and manganese oxide mineralisation associated with the margins of serpentinised, mica, peridotite, basic dykes, with kimberlitic affinities in host Saddleworth Formation.

secondary copper mineralisation as pods, and coatings associated with kaolin and limonite in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. No primary sulphides were noted. No production figure determined.

malachite and cuprite, minor chalcopyrite in quartz veins and along schistosity of host schist. No production record. Best value from dumps 2.11%Cu. 5 percussion holes on IP and soil geochemistry anomalies for best value 14m at 0.12%Cu.
low-grade porphyry Cu-Mo-style mineralisation, best assay 0.3% Cu. Drill testing of IP anomaly penetrated intensely altered granite, with pervasive disseminated & vein-hosted Cu-Fe sulphides.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANOMALY F; DIVISION DAM; GL 10556; GL 10557; LILYDALE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 3 lodes of Cu (Au) mineralisation in host shear at contact of black shale of benda Silstone with Willouran Boucaut Volcanics. Production 86.4t Cu ore in 1909. Resource 1997 4.2Mt @ 0.52%Cu. Best gold 10m @ 0.9g/tAu.
COMMODITIES: Copper,  Gold,  Molybdenum,  Silver,  Zinc,  Cobalt
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Gold,  Malachite,  Molybdenite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 1.2 m wide dyke-like structure of vesicular, purple-red to limonitic rock, within diapiric rock in host Cradock Quartzite Member, and carrying some copper mineralisation. Some minor diggings were carried out. The best assay was 1850 ppm Cu.
rock chip sampling by Dominion Metals PL in 1993 identified copper mineralisation in quartz-pyrite veining.

quartz-iron oxide vein to 2m wide, dip 60E, trend 065.  60-70 tonnes of ore was raised, the ore showing trace copper oxide staining, and carrying a little pyrite. Host was slate of the Cradock Quartzite Member. No overall yield or grade determined.

quartz-iron oxide veins trending 200 in host shale, dolomite and tillite of the Benda Siltstone. The veins carry some malachite and galena. Assays of grab samples identified anomalous Ag, As, Pb, and Zn (to 1200 ppm).
copper carbonate stained quartz veins in greisen in host altered biotite granite. Gossanous samples returned values to 1000ppmCu (malachite), also 20ppmMo, 150ppmPb, 500ppmZn, and 50ppmAg.
ferruginous quartz vein, with trace cerussite, average 60 cm wide, trending EW, dipping N in host shale of the Mintaro Shale. Production of 18.3 tonnes of ore for recovery of 264gm gold at 14g/tAu.
ferruginous quartz veins containing lenticular sulphide bodies, closing in 1926. The lode trended NE, dipped 30 SE, and was from 1.2-2.7m wide. Lead values appeared to reduce with depth.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein, striking EW, dipping S, conformable with bedding cleavage of the host slate of the Belair Subgroup, and showing some gold. A surface sample returned 8g/tAu.
2 parallel, 1m wide quartz-iron oxide reefs in host phyllite of the Mintaro Shale. Recorded production was 2022gm gold from 73 tonnes ore at 27.7g/tAu.
Cu-Au mineralisation in host, poddy and discontinuous banded iron formation, and quartz-pyrite-magnetite horizon of the Ethiudna Subgroup with up to 10% pyrite.
fractured, quartz-MnO reef in host metasediment of the Mintaro Shale, & adjacent to felsic intrusive. Later exploration identified pervasive anomalous Au, best value 1m at 4.1g/t Au.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ferruginous quartz vein with boxwork after pyrite, some vuggy intervals and zoned, milky and smoky quartz, trending for ~50m at 065, dip 30-35E in host phyllite of the Mintaro Shale. Recorded production 1939 of 70t for 1132gm bullion gold at 16g/t.
narrow quartz veins in host metasediment of the Pualco Tillite. Recorded production in 1938 of 64.5t for 1516gm gold at 23.5g/tAu.
milky quartz veins, weakly brecciated, pyritic, trend 100, and with minor galena in host slate of the Mintaro Shale. No production figure determined, records of some lead ore production.

45cm wide vein-quartz fill breccia zone, with abundant pyrite in host metasediment of the Mintaro Shale. Incomplete production figures were for 1935 only, with 11 tonnes yielded 117 gm of gold at 11g/t.
gossanous quartz-malachite veins in host Belair Subgroup, values to 2900 ppm copper, veins were controlled by shears.

gossanous quartz veins in host Wilyerpa Formation, with trace galena. Vins trend 060, dip steeply N, and are bordered by sericite. There was a deep shaft on the ridge, with other shafts reported to be west of the road.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz,  Sericite,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic diggings on gossaneous quartz veins in host Belair Subgroup, and that showed traces of galena.

minor diggings for galena on dolomite with quartz veining. Mineralisation extended mainly along the quartz veins, with samples of gossanous rock assaying 500 and 11000 ppm lead, and 6000 and 6400 ppm zinc. Copper values were ~200 ppm.
Cu mineralisation in host meta-dacite and meta-basalt/dolerite of the Boucaut Volcanics. Best intersection 76m @ 0.32%Cu in hole CRD-11.

shallow, low-grade Cu-Mo mineralisation, tested at depth in hole DDH AN7. Penetrated sequence of hydrothermally altered acid to intermediate igneous intrusives, with sparse chalcopyrite & molybdenite veining.

white kaolin and plastic clay were identified during exploration drilling for base metals. Drilling identified a zone ~2km long, up to 500m wide, possibly extending north. Resources estimated at 15Mt, no grade specified.
1.3m wide steeply dipping (60 E) white clay from weathered claystone interbed of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Tested and found to be unsuitable for ceramic uses.

~1.5m white claystone exposed on creek bank. formed from weathered slate of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Test work showed material of low plasticity, discoloured on roasting, and unsuitable for ceramic or refractory use.

numerous fluorite and barite veins over a strike length of ~4km concordant to foliation of host metasediment, and parallel to minor shears. Fluorite distribution was patchy, with minor production recorded from small prospectors.

quartz veins with malachite. The veins trended parallel to the foliation of the host rock of the Burra Group. There was minor malachite extending into the host country rock. The mineralisation was prospected in an old pit/quarry.

shafts and pits were excavated on quartz veins with a trace of malachite in host metasediment, and metavolcanics of the Boucaut Volcanics. Several of the veins paralleled the foliation of the metasediment.
pale pink to white barite vein, 30-190 cm wide, parallel to the foliation of the host rock of the Emeroo Subgroup, and traceable over a strike length of nearly 1.7 km.
workings of pits and shafts on stratabound malachite mineralisation in host Boucaut Volcanics. Later diamond drilled identified only low tenor Cu mineralisation at depth.

workings of pits and shafts over a strike lenght of ~700m on stratabound malachite mineralisation in host Boucaut Volcanics. Later diamond drilled in 2 holes identified low tenor Cu mineralisation only at depth.
quartz vein with malachite, and chrysocolla in host shale of the Saddleworth Formation.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ~450 m long quartz-iron oxide vein striking 226 in host Saddleworth Formation. The largest pit worked a well developed gossan with boxworks. This had a peacock bloom but no malachite was seen in 1992.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Hematite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: recorded during mapping of the Olary 1:250K map sheet by B.G. Forbes. It formed as a replacement deposit in host dolomite of the Nucaleena Dolomite.
recorded during mapping of the Olary 1:250K map sheet, and formed as a replacement deposit in host dolomite of the Nucaleena Formation.

quartz-copper veining in host Belair Subgroup. The underlie shaft followed quarts veins in the weathered zone, which were brecciated and vuggy, with terminations and recemented with calcite. Earthy Mn and Fe oxides were common.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-hematite vein, with minor copper mineralisation with a peacock bloom. Host was weathered slate of the Belair Subgroup. There were secondary calcite fractures, and botryoids.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: extensive copper oxide staining with much malachite, azurite following structural trend in host clay and quartzite of the Pualco Tillite. One quartzite bed with disseminated chalcocite, with sampling returning up to 5%Cu, 560ppmAs, negligible Au, Ag.

shallow prospecting pits developed on minor narrow (<5 cm) cross-cutting quartz veining in host shale of the Benda Siltstone. later inspection by R.A. Callen of the Geological Survey reported observation of flaky gold. No documented production.

1 microdiamond recovered in gravel sample. Drilling identified porphyritic lamprophyre with anomalous Nb, and different to standard Kersantite-type kimberlite. Concluded lamprophyre not source of the microdiamond.
east & west lodes of barite-quartz-iron oxide as fault infill in host Tarcowie Siltstone. Trial pitting in the 1970's failed to confirm sufficient resources.
3 quartz-iron and manganese oxide veins worked for silver-lead. There were open vug textures with quartz terminations, and resilicification. Minor copper mineralisation was noted.

quartz-iron oxide lode carrying sporadic gossan of boxwork after galena, and abundant chlorite, bearing north-south. Host was slate of the Yerelina Subgroup. Recorded production ~2 tonne, no grade determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DRAGONS GUT; DRAGONS HEAD; DRAGONS TAIL; INTERZONE; IRON PEAK; MANUNDA; NORTH BLACK HILLS; ORATON; RAZORBACK RIDGE; RAZORBACK WEST; RED DRAGON; SOUTH BLACK HILLS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: prominent ridge of magnetite-bearing IF of Braemar Iron Formation, being part of a more extensive IF as reflected in aeromagnetics. Resource 1.5Bt @ 21%Fe (Aug 2012). Testwork for product >66%Fe for grind to 45 microns @ 14DTR%.

bat guano on the floor of a cave was sampled and found to contain 83.45% sand, 0.55% phosphoric acid and 1.68% nitrogen. The resources were difficult to assess due to the shape of the cave, that was 15 m long (p 342, H.Y.L. Brown).

ironstone in a shallow, basinal structure 300m x 92m, hosted by coarse-grained magnetite-talc beds of probable Sturtian Braemar Ironstone. Resources were estimated at 1 million tonne low-grade magnetite iron ore.
deposit of hematite-dominant eluvium presumed to be of Tertiary age, underlain by ferruginous shale, and worked for flux prior to 1903. Production ~5-8000t, resource estimated @ >250,000t.
Tertiary ironstone laterite associated with iron-rich Cutana Beds, with minor workings. It was located ~1.4km SSE of Terminus Quarry, one of a group of the Grants Ironstone Quarries
major producer of ironstone for flux in the area, production >8,000t, exposing a bed of concretionary to pisolitic laterite. Bedrock probably Braemar Ironstone. Resources estimated >128,000t @ 45%Fe.
shallow open cut, estimated production >4,000t pre 1903. Eluvial Iron deposit dip 20WNW , no bedrock iron formation evident. Resources ~240,000t @ >40%Fe.

minor pits on a low NE-trending ridge ~450m long x 40m wide being the NE extension of the Terminus Quarry. Residual deposit of limonite prospected in shallow pits overlying ferruginous clay, no production figures apparent.
series of pits on concretionary, goethite/hematit eluvial ironstone deposits developed on host Braemar Ironstone. No production records, estimated resource >80,000t @ 50%Fe.

minor workings on goethitic laterite, & residual goethite-hematite masses developed on shallowly dipping host Braemar Ironstone. No production figures apparent, resource estimate 1922 of 66,000t @ 45%Fe.

boat-shaped basinal structure 2.2dkm x 700m wide Braemar Ironstone. Drilled with inferred resource in December 2012 was 304Mtonne @ 24%Fe at 18%Fe cutoff. Preliminary beneficiation testwork returned concentrate with grade >60%Fe.
shallow historic pits developed on lateritic profile on flat-dipping Braemar Ironstone, presumably for use as flux. No production recorded, no resource estimate.
several historic prospecting pits developed on cemented eluvium on host Braemar Ironstone, presumably for iron ore for use as flux. No recorded production, no resource estimate.

segregations of kyanite in Willyama mica schist near a contact with amphibolite. 1950-63 investigations for refractory grade material concluded grade too low for commercial operation. 1985-86 reappraisal concluded potential for some areas

kyanite-biotite-muscovite schist outcrop, and quartz-kyanite veins. Kyanite as bladed segregations to 3-5 inches long intimately associated with vein-quartz. Resource estimates difficult. Veins persisted >300m in a band ~10m wide.
host Willyama schist with segregations of kyanite, with a sample of ~10 tonne excavated for testing.

elongated segregations of kyanite in mica schist near a contact with amphibolite. 1950-63 investigations for refractory grade material concluded grade too low for commercial operation. 1985-86 reappraisal concluded potential for some this area.

several deposits of intergrowths of kyanite and muscovite-bearing schist interlayered with staurolite schist, with 2 areas evaluated as showing promise. Resources were estimated at 35,000 tonne @ 9.5% kyanite for deposits #1 & #7.
kyanite blades in host schist of the Willyama Supergroup, and semi-continuos over 430m strike. ~50 tonnes was excavated for testwork.

milky quartz vein crosscut Willyama metasediment. The vein had abundant blue blades of radiating kyanite growing from walls into quartz vein.   Metasediments were largely kyanite free. Less than 20 tons was excavated, and no resources remain.

outcrop of enriched, drag folded Braemar Ironstone, with IF continuing to the east for many km with flatter dip. Resource tested by Havilah Resources for inferred resource 147Mt @ 30%Fe. Metallurgical testwork determined ""soft"" classification.

near-vertical ironstone 6-15 m thick, grading 40.6% Fe, being surface residual enrichmented of Braemar ironstone. Similar scattered outcrops 8-14km S & E. 2 holes drilled nearby by Minotaur in 2011 identified 35-75 interval Braemar, 12-15%DTR.

pisolitic goethite in host Braemar Ironstone for flux. Resource ~254,000 tonnes (assuming a strike length of 460m). Recorded production 5-8100 tonne. Possibly same as Alberts (MINDEP #755), but that has not been confirmed in the field (2008).

occurrence of galena and cerussite forming a vein about 30cm wide in host Willyama Supergroup. The galena formed as pure slabs in the vein, with minor cerussite. The associated gossan assayed 570g/tAg.

well defined 1m wide vertical quartz-iron oxide lode carrying chalcocite and malachite and continuous over 150m in host sheared Mesoproterozoic granite. Small parcel of ore removed in 1891, also worked from 1910-1911.
2 shallow pits, one excavated on a weakly malachite-stained dark, medium grained basic dyke rock of the Willyama Complex, trending 075, dipping 70 S.
worked a pegmatite, which showed copper mineralisation, and micaceous hematite over a strike length of about 180 m. Host rock was of the Willyama Complex.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DALKEY 1; MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: discontinuous Cu-Pb-Zn mineralisation in shear zones in host Tapley Hill Formation shale. Recorded production 1890-91 37t @14-20% Cu. Drilling penetrated metasediment with 5-10% sulphide, best value 6m @ 0.17% Cu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DALKEY; MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: northern group of workings on the Dalkey line of lode, and developed on a complex system of quartz veins with lead and silver mineralisation. Location uncertain, se map 1389(IV)-4 in open file envelope 1389.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DALKEY; MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; NILPENA; RADIUM HILL COPPER; SML 207
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: plotted from mine symbol on 250k map sheet, presumably minor prospecting on surface copper show in host Tapley Hill Formation. Possibly Dalkey 2 as plotted on plan 1389(IV)-4 in open file enveloped 1389.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: no details, part of the Miltaldie - Dalkey group of workings for NS distance of ~4km, with Dalkey 3 located near the S end of the line. Workings on vein Cu-?(Pb-Ag-Zn) mineralisation in host metasediment of the Yudnamutana Subgroup.
magnetic anomaly in Willyama Complex associated with copper occurrence was investigated and proved to be of no economic significance.
ironstone reefs with malachite in host tillite of the Wilyerpa Formation. There were 2 exploratory shafts.
no references, gold occurrence in Pualco Tillite.
historic shaft in Pualco Tillite for ?gold. ~800m to SW peak gold value 122ppb soil gechem by Helix Resources in 2008-9. Coherent gold anomaly trends ~295.
""spotted"" lode striking NW following sub-horizontal shears containing several tonnes ilmenite with weak davidite mineralisation.
no details, shaft position recorded during regional mapping by the Geological Survey in th late 1990s. On the 100k digital geology map host is metasediment of the Willyama Supergroup.
area of qz veining with associated Fe- Mn-oxides with anomalous Cu-Co-(Au), when drill tested returned low values.

quartz veining with trace copper carbonate at boundary Nuccaleena Dolomite and Seacliff Sandstone. Mineralisation occurred in host pods of quartz and silicified ironstone, and smaller irregular quartz veining along the fractured boundary.

quartz vein on fracture zone. Pb % trace Cu sulphide in quartz vein in dolomite of the Ketchowla Siltstone, trend ~240 paralleling a vertical axial plane cleavage. A pod of earthy Mn oxide was associated with vein at adit entrance.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Dolomite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: testing of an area of gossanous float in 3 costeans to confirm zones of abundant vein qz-iron oxide to gossan. Geochemistry determined low values only. Petrology identified volcanic porphyry also present in the sequence.

later veins of interlocking quartz crystals, cutting earlier milky quartz veins with pyrite, iron oxide boxworks, and minor galena. Host rock is metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Minor alluvial workings in a creek leading into Chinamans Dam.

series of shallow shafts excavated on a vuggy quartz vein with irregular off shoots in host Benda Siltstone. The vein trended 060, and dipped south. Host rock was an ochreous, limonite-stained dolomite-limestone.
prospecting pit excavated on galena show in host Benda Siltstone, and close to its contact with the Pualco Tillite
one of a series of pits following the strike of bedding in metasediment of host Benda Siltstone, and close to its contact with the Pualco Tillite
galena show in a pit, easternmost of a series of pits following the strike of bedding in metasediment of host Benda Siltstone, and close to its contact with the Pualco Tillite.
galena show in a pit in Ulupa Siltstone.
host slate of the Belair Subgroup appeared flat lying, with vertical vein material of ferruginous gossan and boxworks with very minor malachite staining.
quartz veins with iron oxide lined fractures, and fresh pyrite cubes in host phyllite of the Mintaro Shale. No production figures were determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GS 233; GS 234; GS 235; MC 15287; VON BERG
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz veins with iron oxide-manganese oxide pseudomorphs after pyrite, and muscovite books and tourmaline, in host weathered Anabama Granite. Recorded production of 11 tonnes for 194gm bullion gold at 17.6g/tAu.
abandoned, historic quarry of ~500m2 x 1-8m deep on bluestone of the Cambrian Tapanappa Formation, possibly used as local source of building stone.
group of workings developed on brecciated and un-brecciated quartz veins. Possibly the eastern workings of Marna, mindep #713.
small prospecting pit on milky quartz vein with abundant fresh pyrite visible. Host rock was crenulated mica schist of the Mintaro Shale.
no references, data transfer from earlier version of MINDEP, rinformation source of open file envelope. Presumed quartz lode in host Belair Subgroup worked for lead ore and/or gold.
ferruginous quartz veins, 5-10cm wide. Host rock was hard, massive, blue-grey Benda Siltstone. There were a great many other quartz veins in the region. Sampling of a 10t parcel assayed 46g/tAu.
gossanous float, with samples assaying 8.31%Cu, 1173ppmBi, and 3.5g/tAu. Drill testing failed to encounter any mineralisation. Host rock was siltstone and quartzite of the Benda Siltstone.

copper mineralisation in siliceous IF in contact with granitic dyke of Wiperaminga Subgroup (""Composite Gneiss Suite""). No production figure determined. Drilling identified a magnetite-bearing body, with mineralisation as discontinuous pods.
quartz-malachite vein, trend 067, dip north, in host schist of the Willyama Complex. Recorded production 43.7 tonne raised for 3.5 tonne at ~19.5%Cu treated.

Cu-Ag rich gossan to stratiform pyrite-pyrrhotite (5-15%) at depth, in host retrograde muscovite schist/gneiss of the Willyama Complex. The best intersection was disseminated chalcopyrite, with up to 10m at 1.13%Cu. Production 470tonne @ 20%Cu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Bismuth,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit located ~850m north of the Barrier Highway, and ~4km east of Manna Hill township. Shallow pit of ~8500m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Gumbowie Arkose, presumably for material for use in road maintenance.
show of secondary malachite, and azurite within a goethitic gossan in Willyama Complex. At the base of the pit disseminated copper sulphides were visible.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLEMENT; KINGS BLUFF; STAR PROSPECT; STRINGER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: low-grade copper ore as disseminated sulphide in carbonate veins in host Willyama Group gneiss. Small, non-persistent carbonate veins were “gouged.\xe2\x80? Records indicate 23 tonne of ore raised, no reliable figure on product recovered.

copper soil geochemistry anomaly recorded near some old workings. It was drill tested, with an interval of disseminated copper sulphides in Willyama Complex host. The best assay from the drill samples was 6 m at 1.7% Cu.

4 adjacent roadside council pits developed on deeply weathered metasediment of the Pualco Tillite, presumably for material for use in road maintenance. Pits have combined total area of ~50,000m2 x 1-3m deep.
broad area on surface shows of copper mineralisation of Willyama Complex host adjacent to Quartz Hill. At depth visible disseminated pyrite, chalcopyrite, and pyrrhotite were recorded.
scattered weak copper and zinc geochemistry anomalies from RAB drilling on host metasediment of the Willyama Complex. Best assays were 175 ppm, 830 ppm Zn.

gossan in Willyama Complex with weak Cu mineralisation. Drilling confirmed weak disseminated sulphides in a variety of rock types. Best interval was 14 m at 0.35% Cu, also 0.9 m at 0.9% Cu, with anomalous lead and zinc.

hematite gossan was prospected in several  percussion drillholes to identify a sequence of deep granite intrusive, with a narrow metasomatic halo of magnetite-pyrrhotite/pyrite, with minor anomalous base & precious metal values.
disseminated sulphides in gossan in host graphitic gneiss. Drilling identified best interval 26m at 0.53%Zn. Broad low-grade zinc mineralisation in host graphitic pelite and psammopelite.
magnetic anomaly that was drilled, with minor anomalous lead recorded. Mapping indicated a quartz-gahnite horizon equivalent to the Broken Hill Mine Section. Best intersection was 2m at 795ppm Pb.
drilling identified anomalous base metals in Willyama Supergroup metasediment. Diamond drilling (hole PC1) penetrated 6.1m at 0.54%Pb, and 0.34%Zn. Hole BPPDH 002 assayed 1200ppmCo from 70-74m.
gossanous ironstone in host Willyama Complex that was drilled, with samples returning anomalous values for base metals.

gossanous massive to semi-massive pyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite, chalcopyrite bodies in calc silicate rock of the Bimba Formation. Assays from drill samples returned best results of 8m at 2300ppmCu, 6m at 2400ppmZn and 5m at 2700ppmCo.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GREENS SOUTH EXTENDED; GREENS WORKINGS; HAMLYN; IRON BLOW; ML 5678; MUTOOROO CONSOLS; MUTOOROO COPPER RECOVERY LTD; MUTOOROO EXTENDED; MUTOOROO METALS; MUTOOROO SOUTH; NORTH MUTOOROO; OSBORNE WORKINGS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu-Co-Au mineralisation in shear-hosted lodes in host amphibolite. Production from 1887-1908 ~6,000t @ 7-19%Cu. Estimated resource 12.5Mt @ 1.53%Cu & 0.14%Co, 0.23g/tAu, 2.5Mt @ 20%S.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Bismuthinite,  Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Galena,  Gold,  Sphalerite
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Jasper,  Limonite,  Magnetite,  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 inclined shafts on surface copper mineralisation in Willyama Complex. Shearing appeared to control emplacement of sulphides, with amphibolite in the hanging wall, and schist/gneiss in the foot wall. Shearing was conformable with layering.

EW-trending sheared contact between siltstone and tillite of the Wilyerpa Formation, and with an infill quartz vein with galena veinlets and lenses. 63 tonne ore yielded 33 tonne lead metal product, and 21.4kg silver.

vein quartz in host very weathered Anabama Granite. The vein was weakly ferruginous, trending 127, and had a vuggy appearance. There were also irregular veins of quartz-sericite with cubes to 2cm of goethite replacing pyrite.
shaft in weathered Anabama Granite, assumed developed on a small quartz vein. Host was white biotite granite, with a hint of fabric. Near surface the granite was weathered, kaolinised, sericitised.
small prospecting pit for gold on quartz vein trending 280 in host phyllite of the Mintaro Shale.

2 inclined shafts developed on a quartz vein. The country rock was deformed siltstone of the Mintaro Shale. The vein trended 065, dipped S. The country rock had a vertical dip, and a rodding lineation, strike 100, plunge 10 E.
prospecting pits developed on milky white quartz veins carrying some fresh pyrite on metasediment of the Mintaro Shale.
prospecting pits on creek gravels worked for alluvial gold over a length of several hundred metres.
gossanous quartz vein in host metasediment of the Pualco Tillite. Boxworks and vugs contained relict octahedra after magnetite.
gossanous quartz veins, returning assays of 1000 ppm Zn.

small ferruginous quartz veins carrying Au @ 1.6g/t in host metasediment of the Pepuarta Tillite. There were shallow pits and a vertical shaft to 4.8m on a lode 1.4m wide, trend 080. No production records were determined.
concordant quartz iron oxide veins in host siltstone, slate, schist and sandstone of the Enorama Shale, with a low dip. Recorded production to 1938 of 96 tonne for 1802gm bullion gold at 19g/tAu.
shafts on small galena veins. One was on a gossanous quartz vein with ENE strike and had pyrite and galena, and minor copper carbonate staining. Host was of the Enorama Shale.
ironstone body, 1.5 m wide, prospected via 3 shallow pits and shallow shaft. Strike length was ~200 m. Sampling determined anomalous Cu, Pb, Zn, Ag, later assaying returned 310 ppm Co.
Au mineralisation in brecciated quartz-iron oxide veining in host PepuartaTillite/Grampus Quartzite contact. Production was ~119t ore @ 23g/t Au from 1910-35 for 3.77kg bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Carbonate,  Goethite,  Hematite,  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: persistent quartz vein in host Enorama Shale. 1t parcel yielded 34.2gm bullion gold. Possibly same stratigraphic level as neighbouring Boomerang Mine.
NS-trending quartz-iron oxide vein, with Au-Pb-Cu mineralisation, dip 60E, strike extent 200m. Samples assayed  4.5g/tAu. Minor galena and chalcopyrite recorded. No production figures were found.
Au-Pb-Ag-Cu-As mineralised quartz-iron oxide-pyrite veins trending NE in host metasediment of the Enorama Shale. Production from 190.5t ore treated ~4.5kg bullion gold at 23.5g/tAu from 1903-1938.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Arsenopyrite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GL 1294; GL 1295; GL 1296; GL 1297; GL 1313; GL 1314; KINGS BLUFF GOLD MINING CO.; KINGS BLUFF SYNDICATE; LEARHINAN; MELLORS; MORNING STAR; OUTALPA SYNDICATE; STONES LEASE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au-As-Ag-Pb-Ba-Cu mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide veins in host quartzite of the Wilyerpa Formation. Production from 1887-1933 was ~1000oz bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Chlorite,  Clay mineral,  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Tourmaline

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shaft sunk to ~6m depth, with drive at bottom on a lode with disseminated galena in host limestone of the Wilyerpa Formation. Location uncertain, reported as 1.7km S of Olary Railway Station.

system of en echelon, malachite stained gossanous Cu-Au-(Pb-Zn) quartz veins broadly conformable with layering in host porphyroblastic muscovite of the Willyama Complex. Best drill hole gold assay was 0.23g/t.
COMMODITIES: Copper,  Zinc,  Gold,  Lead,  Silver,  Graphite

MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Goethite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BATCHELOR; LOCALITY 50; MOODYS GREAT IRON BLOW
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu-Ag-Au mineralisation in host discontinuous, siliceous, hematite-magnetite iron formation of the Ethuidna Subgroup, pyrite-rich at depth. The iron formation persisted for over 1.2km along strike.
lens of sillimanite in host Willyama Complex for a few bags in a small surface operation.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup, apparently the continuation of the lode worked at the larger Esmonde Mine. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: JOAN MACDONALD 1 & 2; MCDONALD HILL; RAGGED AND TOUGH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: E-trending gossanous quartz-magnetite body with sulphides and copper carbonates. Host was quartzo-feldspathic gneiss, and biotite rich schist of the Ethiudna Subgroup.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite,  Hornblende,  Jarosite,  Magnetite,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartzite of the Willyama Supergroup, with chrysocolla on the footwall of a massive, banded hematite body.
Cu-Au mineralisation in host EW-trending magnetite-actinolite-biotite-garnet-staurolite post-peak metamorphic shear zone in host Ethiudna Subgroup calc-silicate.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Almandine,  Arsenopyrite,  Magnetite,  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: irregular, flat-dipping 60cm wide vein, with chalcopyrite, chalcocite, bornite, arsenopyrite and azurite in a gangue of white feldspar, quartz, trace pyrite in host gneiss of the Willyama Supergroup. Recorded production 723t @ 7-155Cu.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Atacamite,  Azurite,  Bornite,  Chalcopyrite,  Chrysocolla,  Copper,  Gold,  Malachite,  Molybdenite,  Silver

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: prospecting pits on copper carbonates. Cu and Zn, rare u, was intersected during drilling of a malachite-stained gossan in host Willyama Complex. Drill hole assays included 9 m at 0.25% Zn, and 8 m at 0.4% Cu.

iron gossan with malachite and azurite in host Willyama Complex. Bulletin 34 stated that copper carbonates and pyrite occurred as low-grade disseminations in an epidote quartzite. It was prospected in one pit, with dimensions 5 x 5 x 3 m.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CROZIER AND SHEPHERDS; LEGGE AND WALSHS; SULLIVAN MATHEWS AND LEGGE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu-Au mineralisation in partings in a schistose, biotite, microgranoblastic albite rock in host actinolite quartzite horizon of the Willyama Supergroup. No production figure was determined, grab samples from parcels of ore graded from 1-10g.tAu.

copper mineralisation in Bimba Formation gossan and/or jointed quartzite/calcsilicate worked by early prospectors via a few shallow pits. Later drilling identified best value 13m @ 0.22% Cu, and 17m @ 0.42% Zn.
narrow shear-hosted Au-Cu bearing lode in host slate of the Willyama Supergroup, and marginal to a diorite dyke.

Cu-Au mineralisation in host micaceous quartzite, with mineralisation traced for ~300m along strike. 66 tonnes production. Recorded 24 tonne for 277gm gold at 12g/tAu. Metallurgical testwork indicated gold was very fine.

veins and slugs of galena with calcite on bedding planes of host blue shale. Recorded production 3.71 tonnes sorted ore yielded 2.8 tonne lead at 76%Pb, and 1148gm Ag at 309g/tAg. Grab samples also assayed 2.4% Zn, and 0.043% Bi.
8 separate barite bodies intimately associated with a host quartz-magnetite rock of the Willyama Supergroup. Production from 1946-1950s of 54 tonne, 1949 resource 2,700,000 tonne @ 90% BaSO4.
Au-Cu-mineralised, fractured quartz vein in host granite of the Willyama Supergroup. No production figures were recorded.

large irregular body of pegmatite in host Willyama Complex, and carrying scattered segregations of muscovite. Large quantity was eroded out. Most of the mica was flawed, due to impurities or ""fishbone"" structure, and was sold as scrap mica.
continuation beneath alluvium of the Walter Outapla lode in host amphibolite of the Willyama Complex. No production recorded.

clay & phosphate rock in Angaston Marble and Heatherdale Shalet. Quarry from which 600 tonnes of material, including overburden were removed, roughly half as phosphate rock. Assay gave 78.6% tricalcic phosphate and 5% iron oxide.

clay deposit on early Cambrian Normanville Group metasediment. The pit was worked to supply clay for cement manufacture. In 1959 a production of 1229 tonnes was recorded. Area now used to stockpile agricultural lime.

working developed on a lode of ironstone, and quartz, containing minor malachite, azurite, grey sulphide ore, red oxide ore. Country rock was sandstone & limestone. Best assays for copper were 22.25% and 29.75%.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE BRIGHTON CEMENT; AMATEK; ANGASTON MARBLE; FISCHERS; FISHERS; HABICH; HERRINGS; HOWARD R.G.; MORGANS; PM 100; PM 112; PM 128; SWAIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: opened in 1893 for continuous large production from several quarries on Angaston Marble with production figures recorded for the years 1942-1966 of 1393 tonnes. SWAIN worked one of the quarries in 1961.

fine gold was found in quartz veins in kaolinised dykes in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Recorded production from 1904-11 was 684 tonnes of ore yielding 12348gm of gold at 18g/tAu. The mine was reopened from 1931-36.
copper lodes in host Angaston Marble and Ulupa Siltstone. Ore minerals reported included copper, lead and iron. Prospecting workings not located location is rough centre Section 384.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Agate,  Carbonate,  Chalcedony,  Copper,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Jasper,  Lead,  Manganese Oxide,  Opal,  Phosphate,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: phosphate rock in host marble & schist of the Umberatana and Normanville Group. Worked prior to 1919 for production of 304 tonnes. The deposit was very variable with faces of clay and phosphate rock alternating and low assays of phosphate.
gold-bearing quartz veins within undifferentiated acid intrusive (syn- and post- tectonic), and in Kanmantoo Group metasediment. Good indications obtained. No production figures were recorded.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Kanmantoo Group. Incomplete recorded production of a parcel of 2.8 tonne of ore yielded 14gm gold at 5g/t.

native copper, azurite, malachite, chalcocite, chalcopyrite, red oxide, in gangue of micaceous hematite, magnetite, iron carbonate, chalcedony, opal, jasper in host marble, micaceous schist & sandstone of Normanville & Kanmantoo Groups.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Carbonate,  Chalcedony,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Hematite,  Jasper,  Magnetite,  Malachite,  Opal,  Oxide

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: copper mineralisation in host Early Cambrian Normanville Group. There were two well defined lodes, and samples of ore assayed 30.3% & 33.5% Cu. The copper was discovered in 1844 but little work was done for some time.

quarry of ~4,500m2 x 1-5m deep on a narrow unit of weathered sandstone to quartzite of the Backstairs Passage Formation, and worked for road rubble and concrete aggregate. Production from 1984-2013 was estimated at 70,000 tonne.
marble unit of the Ulupa Siltstone worked for decorative stone, with production from 1991-2013 estimated at >700 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE BRIGHTON CEMENT; HOWARD; LAYCOCK; MORGAN; PM 99; SIBLEY; STANDARD; SWAIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Important historic deposit of limestone and marble of Cambrian Angaston Marble for use as building & monument stone. Operations commenced in 1882. Production from 1924-2013 >250,000t.

waterworn gold recovered from a Tertiary conglomerate overlying the Cambrian Carrickalinga Head Formation, and from underlying, deeply weathered Kanmantoo Group metasediment. No recorded production figures.
red to yellow, slightly gneissic, medium grained granite (closely resembling finer grained Palmer Granite). The quarry was little worked.
quarry developed on marble of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Opened in 1962, the following year the Angaston Marble Co. operated the lease. Production for 1962-64 was >300 tonne.

ironstone outcrop in host limestone initially quarried for road metal, with trace Ag-Cu. 2 shafts identified coal. Inspection in 1890 identified ironstone was a ferruginous cap on limestone. Coal prospected in 1927.
quartz veins in schist of the Petrel Cove Formation, and carrying copper carbonates.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DING DONG; EAST NAIRNE; ESKEAN; HILLMANS; HILLMANS ESKEAN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 main lodes consisting of quartz veins with secondary copper mineralisation. The lodes were 60 m apart, subvertical, trending NW, and to 4.5 m wide. Host rock was mica schist of the Tapanappa Formation.
ochre in a host carbonate rock. Shallow pits mined quartz-siderite-limonite veins over an area 60m x 100m.
anomalous Cu-Pb-Zn-Mn-Ag-Au in a composite chip sample from ironstone body, maximum thickness 15 m, 6-700 m long, adjacent to Milendella Fault. 2 drill holes identified basalt flows.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Copper,  Galena,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: cleaved and jointed shale and siltstone in the Tindelpina Shale Member located on the eastern limb of a syncline, and assassed by the local council as possible source of road making material.
marble of Carackalinga Head Formation. Worked from 1920s-40s. Recorded production from 1931-40 was 2100 tonne. Location uncertain, assumed to be site of large dam on section 509, Hundred Moorooroo.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANGASTON DISTRICT COUNCIL; I.C.I. ALKALI PTY LTD; ML 6233; PM 120; PM 86; RL 109
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cambrian recrystallised carbonate rock of the Angaston Marble. Industrial use for manufacture of soda ash & sodium bicarbonate. Production 1977-2011 ~46Mt, inclusive of 14Mt for construction industry. May 2012 resouce 67Mt.

prospectus appeared in the S.A. register in August 1866. A mining lease for the section was obtained for 21 years. Signs of copper carbonate were found in Angaston Marble, and undifferentiated metasediment of the Normanville Group
brown to yellow phosphate rock, occurring in two bodies. Host was early Cambrian Kapunda Marble (Normanville Group). Recorded production from 1904-22 was estimated at >4000 tonnes.

phosphate rock, and iron mineralisation in early Cambrian white, coarsely crystalline Angaston Marble. The property was first worked for iron for flux in the 1840s. Marble and phosphate rock were later prospected here. No production figures recorded.
lode of ironstone, and quartz-pyrite-limonite in early Cambrian Angaston Marble. A shaft was sunk to 9m at which depth free gold was recovered. No production figure was determined.

minor crocidolite, and widespread white, fibrous tremolite asbestos veinlets to 5 cm wide exposed patchily beneath creek-bank alluvium and associated with zones of tourmalinised and pyritic albite-biotite rock of early Cambrian marble.
gold prospecting on creeks and drainages in the area of Leakes Pass on Sections 189, 193, 346, and 349, Hundred Dutton for poor returns.
irregular quartz-iron oxide veins in host slate and quartzite of the Wilyerpa Formation. Pits were sunk but only traces of gold were found. No production figure was determined.
quartz veins in Delamerian gneissic granite. Reworked in 1934-36. A parcel of 5.75 tonnes ore yielded 37gm gold at 6g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE BRIGHTON CEMENT; BAROSSA WHITE MARBLE; CEMENT WORKS; PM 98; SA PORTLAND CEMENT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: coarsely crystalline Angaston Marble with calc-silicate bands. Adelaide Brighton Cement current tenure as PM 98, only recorded production ~7,000t in 1952.
copper mineralisation in host silty shales and quartzites (Ulupa Siltstone). Further prospecting occurred in 1900 when ore assaying 40% was found.
hydrothermal barite lodes 4-7 feet wide, of good quality within Burra Group metasediment. Recorded production from 1918-47 was 2113 tonne.
historic pit developed on a deposit of limestone and marble of the Angaston Marble, with recorded production of ~1140 tonne from 1987-1989. Area is fully rehabilitated.

quartz reef in host Balquhidder Formation. Workings consisted of two shafts. No production figure determined. Later assays from grab samples of spoil returned anomalous values from a 23m deep shaft on the western section of the property.
seam of brown coal with shale. Drilled in 1917-18, and 1925-27. Holes penetrated calcareous rock and clay, and lignite in seams. No resource figures were attempted.

abandoned quarry of ~3,500m2 x 1-10m deep on slate of the Backstairs Passage Formation for recorded production of ~130 tonne on 1924, and <100 tonne in 1934. The pit was rehabilitated, and is now occupied by a winery processing plant.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: E.C. JOHNSON; HERMITAGE; HOUGHTON; INGLEWOOD; LITTLE HERMITAGE; MC 14689; MC 14690; PM 302
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: recorded total production was 107 tonnes. The barite occurred in a lode, strike NW, dip NE, and discordant to the strike of the Barossa Complex country rock.
hydrothermal vein infill barite lodes for 2nd grade material. Recorded production from 1919-21 was 317 tonnes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CASTAMBUL ESTATE; TORRENS BARITE; TORRENS RIVER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: first worked for copper in the 1890s. Worked for 1st class barite in 1920s, 1950s. Recorded production 287 tonnes from 1940-58. Lodes interfingered with, cut by quartz-calcite-hematite veins. 3 separate lodes, discontinuous, trending NNE for 350m.
vein of barite in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale.
mine located adjacent to Kitchener Fault, which separated Barossa Complex metamorphics from Adelaidean clastic metasediment to the east. Recorded production from 1940-69 was 514 tonnes of ore.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: SOUTHERN BARYTES LTD; SOUTHERN BARYTES LTD.; UDYS ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite vein to 1m wide in host slate and sandstone of the barossa Complex. It was worked for 450 tonnes of second grade barite from 1937-39. In 1954 resources were estimated at 860 tonnes of second and third grade barite.
small lode of siliceous barite to 2m wide, worked in a small open cut sometime before 1950. Host was weathered granite. No production figures were recorded.
barite vein of hydrothermal origins. It was prospected in four pits to maximum 4 m deep. No production figures were recorded.
small lode of barite, and was worked in an adit, and open cut in the 1920's. The lode was 30-60 cm wide. The ore proved to be of no economic value.
barite vein developed in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Tenure was granted as PM 159, but later revoked. Recorded production 245 tonne from 1966-68.
barite vein in host weathered, kaolinised schist of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production from 1909-37 was 135 tonnes.
shallow dipping Tertiary boulder beds with barite. Recorded production was 91.35 tonnes of barite, the bulk of it in 1978.
barite lodes as discontinuous lenses of white medium to coarse-grained barite of high purity in Umberatana Group dolomitic siltstone and shale. Recorded production of 1049 tonnes of ore.
thin seams to 5-50 mm of crocidolite asbestos in andalusite schist, slate and quartzite. Workings were filled in, ploughed over. No production figures were recorded.

shear-hosted Cu-(Ag-Au) mineralisation in quartz-goethite lode in host metasediment of Carrickalinga Head Formation. Incomplete production figures to 1969, 690 tonne @ 20%. Rock chips gave best value 12% Cu, 86 g/t Ag and 0.4 g/t Au.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Chalcocite,  Covellite,  Cuprite,  Kaolinite,  Malachite
