DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed in 1896 on a gossanous quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode within micaceous sandstone and schist of the Kanmantoo Group. Recorded production was 311gm of gold bullion.
kaolinised feldspathic sandstone of the Backstairs passage Formation. The rocks were traversed by pegmatite dykes & quartz veins, some of which carried schorl.

main production came from alluvials with ~2177gm of gold reported recovered. Small mine developed on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host slate and sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group. A parcel of ~10t yielded 206gm of gold at 21g/tAu.
Au mineralisation in alluvium sourced from adjacent gossanous, quartz-pyrite lodes in host sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group. Worked until 1884 for ~121oz bullion gold.
mine developed in 1929 on a deposit of pure white kaolin occurring in a siliceous dyke striking NE. No production figures were recorded.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite-mica lode in host sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group. Production 1885-91 ~100oz. From 1932-36 48.4t ore for 475.8gmAu @ 10g/t. Drilling in 1997 identified veins in brecciated metasandstone, with rare gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Mica,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in quartz vein in host altered granite intruding sandstone of the Kanmantoo Group. Production from 1886-1931 ~4349gm bullion gold.

workings in 1884 on narrow 45 cm quartz-arsenopyrite veins in weathered metasandstone of the Umberatana Group via shallow pits. Several tonnes were mined in 1916-17. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ABC LTD SOUTH; ADELAIDE BRIGHTON CEMENT; EML 3601; EML 4346; EML 4347; EML 4348; EML 4702; EML 4703; HALLETT BRICK INDUSTRIES; JARVIS INDUSTRIES; KAISER REFRACTORIES; LITTLEHAMPTON BRICK CO.; ML 2917; ML 2951; ML 2994; ML 4661; ML 5023; ML 5280; ML 5348; NEWBOLD REFRACTORIES; PM 231
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: residual clay deposit formed on argillaceous slate of the Adelaidean Saddleworth Formation. Production from 1973-2013 >2Mtonne of multiple clay and shale end products.

diggings on deposits of alluvial gold, with reported average width of the gold-bearing layer 30cm resting on a clay base. Total thickness of the alluvium was 1.7m. Reported sample of two buckets of wash dirt yielded 40.6gm gold.
well-defined ferruginous quartz lode in host Kanmantoo Group metasediment. Recorded treated ore was 44.7t for recovery of 1403gm bullion gold. The vein narrowed at depth to ~10-12cm wide.
1890s shallow diggings on a Tertiary gold drift thinly capping a small hill. Underlying country rock was Sturtian phyllite and feldspathic quartzite. No production figures were recorded.
Au mineralised quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host sandstone, quartzite, shale of the Burra Group. Production from 1896 to as late as 1985 was  >200oz bullion gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BIRDWOOD CLAY; EML 3611; EML 4376; PGH CERAMICS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shallow pit of ~1.2Ha x 1-5m deep on white residual over weathered phyllite, schist, and feldspathic quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation of the Burra Group. Production from 1973-2013 was estimated at 44,000 tonne.

silica mined from weathered quartzite within phyllite, schist, feldspathic quartzite of the Belair Subgroup. No production figures for silica for the earlier workings was recorded. See Birdwood clay pit for later recorded production of silica.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: NORTH BLUMBERG; OLD POVERY LINE OF REEF; PROSPERITY LINE OF REEF
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 1 of 3 mines developed in 1931 on the prosperity Line of Reef, being a ferruginous quartz vein in Cambrian Carrickalinga Head formation. Recorded production of parcel of 13.3 tonne of ore yielding 135.4 gm of bullion gold at 10g/t.
Au mineralised quartz-iron oxide-kaolin-pyrite lode in host slate and sandstone of the Tapanappa Formation. Production from 1894-1897 ~500oz bullion gold.
quartz-iron oxide pyrite-kaolin vein carrying rich gold in host soft sandstone of the Burra Group. Production from 1895-1937 ~1000oz (31kg) bullion gold at ~26g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Kaolinite,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in deep Tertiary alluvial/colluvial leads preserved as capping on hills. Recorded production from 1870-85 ~100oz gold bullion.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in micaceous sandstone & schist of the Kanmantoo Group. Shaft was sunk to 12m, but returns proved to be poor, and work ceased. No production figures were recorded. The nearby alluvials were worked for gold.
mine developed on a soft, kaolinised dyke formation some 10-12 feet wide containing rutile crystals. A gravel bed about 12 inches below the surface returned good yields.
diggings developed in 1870 on shallow gold-bearing alluvials located on the banks of a creek. Reworked in the early 1930's. No production figures were determined.

quartz-iron oxide lode within host phyllite, schist, and feldspathic quartzite of the Burra Group. Recorded production from a parcel of ore in 1895 was 7.3 tonnes yielding 54.7 gm of gold at 7.5g/tAu.

diggings developed in 1870 on a deep Tertiary alluvial lead. Gold was also found in the weathered bedrock of phyllite, schist, feldspathic quartzite of the Burra Group. No production figures were recorded. The area was active until the 1960's.

quartz-iron oxide lode in Kanmantoo Group metasediment. Surface mineralisation proved to be the best ore, with gold values at depth being patchy. A parcel of 10.8 tonnes of ore yielding 87gm of gold at 8g/t.
quartz-iron oxide lode within phyllite, schist and feldspathic quartzite of the Burra Group. No production figures were determined.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation, for initial payable gold, with subsequent mining proving unprofitable. No production figures determined.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite vein within kaolin country rock of the Saddleworth Formation. 2 crushings returned grades of ~ 36gm/tonne. No production figures were determined.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode within phyllite, schist and feldspathic quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation.  Assays gave 42.5-85 gm/tonne. The pyritic lode carried fine visible gold.No production figures were determined.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite vein within kaolin country rock of the Saddleworth Formation. It was reported that rich ore was recovered, with visible very fine gold. No production figures were determined.

2 quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. No. 1 reef was 0.6m wide, trend SW, dip 45NW, no. 2 reef trend SE to N. Recorded production was from a parcel of 8.6 tonnes yielded 165gm gold at 19g/tAu.

5-30cm wide quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode, dip 30NW, in decomposed micaceous schist, and clay slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production from 1915-18 was 309.5 tonnes yielding 5670gm gold at 18g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ABC LTD NORTH; FARGO EARTHMOVERS; HALLETT CLAY; ML 5280
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay regolith on Saddleworth Formation, clay mining in 1918 and in the period 1950s to 60s. Now part of the Birdwood Clay operations.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BIRDWOOD CLAY; EML 4702; EML 4703; HALLET BRICK INDUSTRIES; HALLETT SOUTH; ML 6182
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit developed in 1933 on a gold show, then worked leached white regolith developed on host shale of the Saddleworth Formation for kaolin and washed clay products.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host Backstairs Passage Formation. Production ~2582gm gold bullion from 1870, no reliable gold grade available.
alluvial gold recent alluvium formed from reworked Tertiary deep leads. Worked from 1885 to the 1890's for ~2000oz (62.2 kg) of gold bullion.

quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. A parcel of 5 tonnes treated at the battery gave poor results and the mine was abandoned. Weak copper mineralisation recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ALLEN & SCHUTZE; FULTON; GOLDEN FOX; LUCKY HIT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide lode 2.4m wide in host decomposed slate of the Burra Group. Production from 1885-1936 ~650oz (20Kg) bullion gold. Reopened in 1978 for recovery of a small amount of gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode within host clayey slate of the Backstairs Passage Formation. No production figures were recorded, a grade of 15g/tAu was recorded for a parcel of ore.

quartz-iron oxide lode trending EW in host phyllite, schist and feldspathic quartzite of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. No production figures were recorded, with all ore treated in private batteries. Grades of 186g/tAu were reported.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode 90cm wide in host phyllite, schist and feldspathic quartzite of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Fine visible gold was reported, though no production figure was determined.

lode of ochreous ironstone gossan in host claystone & micaceous sandstone of the Burra Group worked for ochre and flux from 1907-48. Grossly incomplete production figures of  91.4t of ochre, 12.2t of flux.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef trending N50E in siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation. It was reopened briefly in 1902. Recorded production figures were 16 tonnes of ore yielding 306 gm gold at 19g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Pyrolusite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-clay lode in host kaolinised white slate, white clay, and sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation. Production of gold from 1945-46 was 8.5 tonnes of ore yielding 94.5 gm gold at 11g/tAu, and 1944-49, 2407 tonnes of clay.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ironstone to quartz-iron oxide lode within decomposed clayey slate of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures were recorded.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host sandstone of the Belair Subgroup. Intensive reworking occurred from 1930-35 for both alluvial and reef gold. Many small nuggets were recovered from the lode by panning. Production figures not recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LUCAS AND PETERS; ML 5045; SOUTH AUSTRALIAN CO
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz reef in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Estimated total gold yield was 7994gm with 6,190gm recorded from section 6624, and 1804gm from section 6625. No ore tonnage or grade determined.

gold-bearing alluvium in a gully running along the south of section 2, proving to be productive, though no production figures were provided. A 12m shaft was excavated to prospect a quartz leader for no returns.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host clayey shale and sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation, with the mine proving unpayable.

quartz-iron oxide lode in weathered, clayey shale of the Saddleworth Formation. Initial parcels of ore sent for treatment assayed 30-150g/tAu, but later parcels gave poor results. Recorded production was 40.25 tonnes, no yield figures determined.

sugary quartz-pyrite reef, in deep weathering metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation . Free gold was reported, with a parcel of 10.4 tonnes of ore yielding 473gm gold at 45g/tAu, with a further parcel of 30 tonnes giving poor yields.

gold-bearing Tertiary alluvium, and underlying kaolinised sandstone/clay of the Saddleworth Formation for 10t @ 33gm gold at 3.3g/tAu. From 1934 to 1940 the area was worked for kaolin, no production figure recorded.
quartz-iron oxide lode, within kaolinised slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production was 9 tonnes of ore yielding 520.5gm gold at 58g/tAu.
lode reported to contain ""rich gold."" Host was metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures determined.

lode of decomposed quartz and ironstone, within host kaolinised metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation.  It was worked for 3 months, and closed due to an influx of water. No production figures were determined.
quartz reef in host phyllite, schist, and feldspathic quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation. It was only active for 3 months, with no production figures determined.

ferruginous quartz within clay slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Pockets of very rich ore, with more than 30oz free picked. Recorded production 78.8t ore yielding 4252.4 gm of gold at 54g/tAu. Total production estimate was 5185gm of gold.
good fine and coarse gold was obtained by the dish from workings of an adit and shaft on a quartz lode in host Saddleworth Formation. No production figure was recorded.
ironstone to gossanous quartz reef, within metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, and from 1894-97. A 1.1 tonne parcel was treated and gave poor returns.
rich pockets of Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide lode in host kaolinised slate of the Burra Group. Production from 78.4t ore treated was 13.4Kg bullion gold from 1914-37.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Shaft to 13.7m depth. No production figures were determined. See plan no. DM 1045/30
quartz-iron oxide hosted by a clayey slate of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures were determined.
small veins of quartz-iron oxide containing rare traces of gold. Country rock was mostly soft alluvial and clay (with quartz). Production of 3 tonne of ochre was recorded.
lode of ironstone, and quartz within decomposed clayey slate of the Burra Group. No production figures reported.
quartz-ironstone lode in decomposed clay slate of Saddleworth Formation, Burra Group. Reported parcel of 3.3 tonne ore for 9.7gmAu at ~3g/t from a 10m deep shaft.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite vein in clayey slate of the Burra Group. Production recorded was 17.7 tonnes of ore yielded 238 gm of gold at 13g/tAu.

mine on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode within claystone and sandstone of the Burra Group. Some good gold was obtained initially, with the leader cutting out at 7m depth. No production figures were available.

quartz-hematite veins in sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Production of gold and copper was from the oxidised surface zone. Total tonnage 32 tonnes, no grade estimated. A parcel of 5 tonnes yielded 134gm at 26.8g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrolusite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: stratabound Cu-Au-(REE) mineralisation in core of Paratoo Anticline in host siltstone of the Burra Group abutting a diapir and dolerite dyke. 1987 drilling identified an inferred resource of 100,000t @ <1% Cu.
calcareous vein stained with malachite. Host rock was quartzite of Tindelpina Shale around nose of anticline. Possibly mis-identified as copper prospect rather than gold. needs sampling to resolve.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BUTLERS; KOONAMORE; ML 4421; ML 4422; ML 4423; ML 4424; ML 4855; NUCLEUS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shear-hosted Au mineralisation, with elevated Cd-Bi-Sb-Pb in quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone of the Wilyerpa Quartzite. Production from 1929-81 ~808.9gm gold bullion.
small irregular veins, shears and leaders of quartz in host altered quartzite of the Ulupa Siltstone. Recorded production was 37.5 tonne for 224gm gold at 6g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 6036; ML 6321; PANNIKIN; PEPEGOONA; RL 18; RL 19; RL 20
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: roll-front type U mineralisation hosted in fluviate sands of the Miocene Namba Formation in the Beverly Corridor Palaeochannel.  Total resource 7.7Mt at 0.27% U3O8 (21 000t contained U3O8).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMONA; GRAINGER; ML 4830; ML 5011; ML 5017; ML 5018
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: stratabound Au mineralisation (anomalous Cu-Zn-Co-As-Ag-Ba) in host fractured basal Appila Tillite, overall double-ended conical pipe form. Production from 1.3km long Grainger line of lode ~46Kg bullion gold, @ estimate ore grade of 10g/t.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu mineralisation in fault-bound block of layered igneous rock, and associated with propylitic minerals in trachyte or epidotised diorite, and in healed fractures in brecciated basalt and andesite. Drilling failed to identify significant mineralisation.

turquoise as secondary cement replacing matrix of sandstone of basal Parachilna Formation. Colour variable from pale green to blue, with occasional brown to yellow. Quality limited due to content of quartz. Refer to sketch plan 76-118 (MRR 145:p71).

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: chalcopyrite and malachite in blebs, small veinlets, joints, along bedding planes in band of dolomite SW of exotic block ~275m long of sediment in Blinman Diapir. Mineralisation also disseminated in dolomitic siltstone adjacent to main dolomite zone.

disseminated malachite blebs and veinlets associated with calcite and green micaceous material within ""mine type"" dolomitic siltstone in the Blinman Diapir. Rock chip sampling across ore zones gave ~16m @ 0.5%Cu.
2 quartz veins with galena, cerussite and copper carbonates in host Etina Formation. Recorded production 17 tonne @ 36%Pb.
2 quartz veins, trend NE, dip ~60SE, and carrying galena, cerussite and some copper carbonates in host siltstone of Etina Formation. Recorded production 17 tonne @ 36%Pb.

quartz-siderite veins in host metasediment of the Nucaleena Formation, and associated with faults located on the western margin of the Bliman Diapir. Grades typically low, early reports of ~6-7g/tAu. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-calcite-siderite-hematite veins with chalcopyrite and malachite around margin of small (~46m diameter) strongly brecciated and altered dolerite plug/raft within diapiric breccia of the Blinman Dome Diapir. There were no records of production.

2 small exploratory pits. Boulders of siderite-calcite with euhedral quartz and trace malachite were found in a stream bed downstream from the workings. No significant mineralisation was found at the site itself.
reference to a calcite vein carrying chalcopyrite in a small fault radial to the Blinman Diapir. The zone, which trended 165, with a width of ~45 cms, was worked for a length of about 20 m.

small silver-lead deposits along a N-trending fault, over a distance of ~1200m. Host was metasediment of the Umberatana Group-Etina Formation. 5 main groups of workings. Yield was low. No records of production.

malachite, specular hematite in quartz reef 45-90cm wide, traced 152m along strike. Lode assaying up to 37%Cu. Host rock was Enorama Shale. Mineralisation associated with ENE-trending fracture system emanating from Blinman Dome Diapir.

copper mineralisation as  chalcopyrite, chalcocite, malachite and minor azurite in remnant (exotic block) of ""mine-type dolomite"" within the Blinman Dome Diapir. Recorded production 287.5 tonne at 1.9%Cu

veins <30cm with siderite, calcite, hematite, chalcopyrite, chalcocite, malachite and azurite. Associated with dolerite plug in Blinman Diapir. Assays from 1899 with significant Co, Ag, Ni. Co as nodules of erythrite (arsenate of cobalt)
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Erythrite,  Malachite,  Unknown

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: massive pyrite, chalcopyrite, lesser bornite in series thin discordant veins in host metasediment of Wilyerpa Formation, and localised in nose of Wyacca fold. No production record determined. Drilling identified low grade primary sulphides in drillholes.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: traces of galena, fluorite and malachite occurred as blebs and stringers up to 10 cm wide in a recrystallised limestone of the Early Cambrian Wilkawillina Limestone.
shear zones in limestone and shale, and with minor hematite, malachite, chalcopyrite and bornite. Located in the Worumba Anticline.

silicified siltstone as exotic block in intrusive carbonate (diapiric) breccia in Worumba Anticline, and cut by quartz-carbonate veins containing chrysocolla as an alteration product of primary copper minerals, also malachite, cuprite and native copper.

prominent ironstone peak in Worumba Diapir comprised of massive magnetite, with minor specular hematite, malachite, azurite, developed as an alteration product of basalt. Possible resource ~30-35,000 tonnes iron ore, no grade determined.

malachite staining in block of siltstone, sandstone, dolomite of Niggly Gap Beds. Mine situated near S margin of exotic block, near its contact with carbonate (diapiric) breccia, and ~2.3 km south of Willow Creek Workings, within the Worumba Anticline.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLD COPPER EXPLORATIONS PTY LTD; MOUNT CRAIG 1; PROSPECT 1; PROSPECT 4
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: malachite and chalcopyrite in calcite veins in shear zones at contacts of dolerite and shale, and in quartz veins in Worumba Anticline-Worumba Diapir area. Main zone 23-60cm wide, discordant to host shale, and sandstone of the Niggly Gap Beds.

dolerite with siderite-calcite-specularite-malachite-chalcopyrite veining. Main vein to 30cm wide, thinning with depth. 2 samples at 0.08%Cu and 3.2%Cu. Dolerite adjacent to veins to 0.2%Cu. Located within the Worumba Anticline.

dolerite with calcite veins with malachite, azurite. Veins numerous, no preferred orientation. Dump material suggested local thickening of veins to ~30cm. Chip and channel samples recorded 0.51% Cu, 0.37% Zn and 0.12% Cu, 40 ppm Zn respectively.

carbonate breccia adjacent to folded block of Wirrawilka Beds in dislocated axis of Worumba Anticline. Malachite probably related to supergene concentration from carbonaceous siltstone and dolomite in porous brecciated zones.
small body of dolerite contained minor malachite concentrated along joint planes near its margin.
massive ironstone (goethite) cap developed on silicified carbonate breccia with weak copper mineralisation. Host was of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
manganese-stained carbonate interbedded with olive-green siltstone, and fine sub greywacke, with weak copper mineralisation.
shallow pit dug in dolomite sedimentary breccia of the Warcowie Dolomite Member for malachite associated with a crosscutting quartz vein.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLD COPPER EXPLORATIONS PTY LTD; MOUNT CRAIG 2; PROSPECT 2; WEBB
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: malachite in brecciated micaceous siltstones and fine sandstones of the Niggly Gap Beds, and in a chloritic breccia. Production records incomplete records indicating recovery of 15.4 tonnes of ore, no grade determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BURRA; NEW BURRA; NEW BURRA BURRA; PROSPECT 8; WARRAWILKA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Shear-hosted Cu mineralisation in quartz-siderite-iron oxide lodes in host metasediment of the Niggly Gap Beds. Production from 1861-88 ~147t ore, grades of hand sorted ore >30%Cu.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: large discordant siliceous ironstone outcrop in host was claystone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Copper mineralisation occurred as small spats of secondary green carbonate. Quartz leader ~80cm wide with 16% Cu, 166oz/ton Ag, and 15.55 g/t Au.

small veins of galena and carbonate located near the junction of kaolinised slate and sandstone, with minor crystalline siliceous limestone (possibly Wilkawillina Limestone and Parachilna Formation sediments of the Palaeozoic Hawker Group).
Au mineralisation at the weathering/fresh rock interface of host Archean gneiss. Second phase identified mineralisation at a contact with mafic gneiss, with best intercept 4m @ 0.51g/t Au.

Au mineralisation at cover/weathered Archean basement interface, with drilling identifying 50-60m wide, steep NW-dipping zone of weak Au-As values. Inferred resource on 24/1/2017 of 360,000 tonne at 0.9g/tAu for 283.5 kg (10,000oz) contained gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLUEBUSH; WOOMERA TANK NORTH; WOOMERA TANK SOUTH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drilling to the Archean bedrock/saprolite interface outlined an area of extensive weak bedrock gold mineralisation within more greenstone-style lithologies than encountered at Challenger.
deposit of dolomite and  limestone of the Cambrian Kulpara Limestone for use as road seal aggregate. Production from 2005-13 was estimated at >2 million tonne.

U mineralisation in Upper Jurassic carbonaceous and pyritic sediments in palaeovalley. Hole 50 intersected ~195eppm U3O8 over 0.76m from ~80m depth. Not confirmed by chemical analysis of poor samples.

white clay similar to that at Imbitcha Bore, and located to the west and south of Charlotte Waters. It consisted of clay seams to 2-3 m thick, and associated with limonite beds. Minor alunite was reported, with no siliceous grit.
claim taken out of copper show on Tertiary silcrete, with a mining return lodged in 1904, no other details, presumably a small operation on a surface show.

discontinuous outcrops to 8m wide of massive micaceous hematite rock over 450m strike. Emplaced on fault separating Late Adelaidean metasediment from Cambrian Wallatina Formation. Production 1995-97 77t, resources ~30,000t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE BRICK CO.; GILBURN BRICK CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay as weathered Saddleworth Formation worked for brick making. Production was 35,040 tonne from 1945-47, and 159,600 tonne from 1956-60. A brick making plant produced up to 5 million red bricks per year.
weathered clay on shale and slate, and quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation. It was worked for cement clay in the late 1930-50s, with production at ~72,980 tonne. It is now an oval and park area.
first clay pit opened west of Adelaide, being opened in 1840. It has been redeveloped as major shopping centre complex.

first worked in 1863. It consisted of a quartz-iron oxide lode in a slate host. The lode was 2-3 m wide, trended EW, dipped steeply, and contained azurite, malachite, chalcocite, chalcopyrite. No production figures were recorded.

quartzite, sandstone, slate of Belair Subgroup worked in 1865, discontinuously till 1951, occasionally to 1962. Production figures combined from Andersons Mid, North, and South quarries. Quarry infilled. Housing within a 10s of metres.
quarry on quartzite, sandstone and slate of Belair Subgroup. Production figures for a combined production from Andersons Mid, South, and North quarries were available.
quarry on quartzite, sandstone and slate of the Belair Subgroup. Production figures for a combined production from Andersons Mid, South, and North quarries were available.
small open cut on Stonyfell Quartzite. No production details. Not infilled, Overgrown, with a residence built on the floor of the quarry (2008).
several pieces of gold were found in a nearby creek. Further prospecting discovered a nearby quartz reef. There were no production details.
Quaternary clay deposit on which brickworks were established in 1912, closing in 1979. Production included 42,045t from 1956-60, and reaching 2 million bricks per year. The site is rehabilitated.
worked for Quaternary sand and gravel. It was rehabilitated, and is now part of Torrens Linear Park.
worked for sand and gravel, and no further details were found. The site as given was on the first hill slope facing the suburban built up area. It possibly worked Tertiary colluvial sand and gravel.
worked for Tertiary sand and gravel, and no further details were found. The site as given was on the first hill slope facing the suburban built up area.
10m deep pit opened in 1927, with the clay used to make coloured, glazed bricks. It was a small operation only, no production figures were recorded. The pit is now an industrial complex (2008).

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay pit to 8 m deep, with associated brickworks. Worked from the 1940s-60s. Production ~40,370 tonnes from 1956-61. The pit was infilled, and the area redeveloped as an industrial site.
deposit of clay for brick making in the 1920's. No production figures were recorded. It was backfilled. The site was redeveloped for housing in 2007/08.

freestone quarry on bed of bluestone about 13m wide of Belair Subgroup. It provided a very strong slate, fit for use as flooring, street flagging, shingles, mantle pieces, fencing, etc. Powdered it made a good cement mixed with limestone.
small diggings on gold show in colluvium developed via trenches and an adit excavated near the summit of Browns Hill in 1932. It was abandoned when a hard white quartz reef was intersected.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate and quartzite of the Burra Group. Returns were poor.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate and quartzite of the Burra Group. Work ceased in a few months due to poor returns. No production figures recorded.

bed of limestone of Beaumont Dolomite Member for use as building stone, and crushed rock for road base material. Worked to 1940s, then change in ownership, reworked to 1956 for 6605t from 1946-55. Minor slate for building stone.
mine developed in the early 1900's, and consisted of prospecting shafts and adits for recovery of 117 tonnes of copper ore, none treated, no grades recorded.

clay suitable for brick making on a dissected area of clay flats marginal to the Little Para River. It was tested in a number of auger holes, which determined that the clay was suitable for brick making.
lode of galena mineralisation in host shale, and was discovered in 1887. It was worked in adits and shafts until 1889. Some rich ore was raised, though no production figures were recorded.
small open cut on deeply weathered, kaolinised phyllite, slate and quartzite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. No production figures were available.
clay and building sand from host flat lying Tertiary sediment. Production 11,384t clay, 67,298t sand. Drilling identified resources of 6Mt in the area. The area is now residential.

area has been infilled and rehabilitated. It lies adjacent to the major open cut in the area, the Christies Sand pit, and separate, and immediately NW of the pit for PGH No. 2. Production figures were aggregated with PGH NO. 2.
white clay deposit of Tertiary age and was worked in an open pit in the 1970s. It is infilled and is an industrial yard used for storage.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Pleistocene sand and limestone to 15 m thick, with production in 1964 of 30,900 tonne of material for use in the construction industry.
pit and brick making plant established in the 1920's on red and yellow Quaternary clay deposits ~7-8 m thick. The pits were infilled, and redeveloped as park and oval reserves.
2 small open cuts into the side of a hill working quartzite and limestone of the Stonyfell Quartzite as early as the 1920's. Production from 1952-66 was 6980 tonne for general purpose aggregate.
pit developed on clay on a property of 7.5 acres. Work started in 1849 and continued for many years with up to 20,000 bricks per day manufactured. The pit was infilled, and is now industrial (2008).
abandoned historic council quarry of ~5,000m2 x 5-10m deep in steep gorge, worked from the early 1900, and developed on Stonyfell Quartzite.
Cu mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide lode in host shale of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Production from 1907-17 was 37t ore.
Tertiary clay worked in pit in 1948 for 4012 tonnes. It is now infilled, and  located within an industrial area (2008).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DUHNE AND SONS; HIGHBURY CLAY; PM 24
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: rehabilitated area on former open cut located west of Halls Road, and on pale brown Tertiary sand to 22 m thick, with minor thin, white clay beds. Production from 1956-61 was 92,900 tonne building sand.

quartzite and slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite, and worked for general purpose aggregate. Worked mainly from 1900-1950's. Production for 1938-39 was recorded at 12,200 tonne. Subsequent rubbish dump, and currently a gun club.
small abandoned quarry on quartzite of the Belair Subgroup, worked early 1900s for building stone. Now part of Carrick Hill recreational area and used for display of sculptures.

large quarry developed on sandstone, quartzite and shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite in the early 1960's, and worked continuously until the 1990's. Now rehabilitated. Production from 1977-1992 ~1.08Mt. Now rehabilitated.
Ag-Pb-Au mineralised gossan in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Production 51t ore, no yields recorded. At depth gold reported within pyrite.
mine developed in 1847 on a gossanous quartz vein with some galena. Returns were poor and the mine soon closed.

Cu-Ag mineralised quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. From 1888-92 production estimated at 46kg silver, & 175kg copper metal.
lode of quartz-iron oxide-galena in host shale. It was worked in an adit in 1844-46. No production figures were recorded.
pit developed on deposit of deeply weathered shale of the Saddleworth Formation for white clay. Seasonal production since 1957 ~1.73Mt.

pit on red clay to 8 m deep, with associated brick works in operation. Opened in the 1920's, closing in the 1960's. Production from 1956-61 was 27,270 tonnes, making up to 1 million bricks per year. It is now Infilled, redeveloped as Basketball stadium.
clay pit developed to 8 m depth on red clay used for brickmaking in the 1920's. It is infilled, now and in a residential area (2008).

location uncertain, described as several quarries on sections 255, 256, 257, Hundred Adelaide in Colonel Light Gardens area, 6,032 tonne of slate presumably of the Belair Subgroup, and quarried in ~1900.

quarry developed on a Lower Cambrian, weathered grits and sandstone used as building stone in the 1850s-80s. It was used in many public buildings. Workings consisted of a main open cut 20 x 10 x 6m, and several smaller surrounding quarries.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gossanous-Pb-Zn mineralised quartz reef in host Burra Group shale and limestone host. Production was estimated at >1118 tonnes of ore, no grades recorded.
slate of the Saddleworth Formation quarried for building stone in the 1850's.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GLEN OSMOND CLAY; HARDYS; PGH INDUSTRIES LTD; PM 58

mine developed on a small quartz lode with copper mineralisation. The lode was discovered in 1905. Workings consisted of costeans and pits.
rehabilitated area on historic quarry opened on quartzite unit of the Saddleworth Formation in 1962. No production figure available. Resource estimate 2.65Mtonne, with potential to the north.
slate of Saddleworth Formation mined for building stone used locally, with limestone at the portal mined, and burnt to produce lime for mortar. Within Adelaide metropolitan built up zone (2008).

sequence of Adelaidean quartzite/sandstone worked from the late 1940s. Reduced production in recent years, with the last major campaign from 1977-1981 for production of ~1Mt. Now a combined operation with Stonyfell Quarry.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY & MINERAL SALES PTY LTD; FRICKER CO.; GOLDEN GROVE; HALLETT BRICK PL; HANCOCK ROAD; PM 56
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Tertiary sand and clay in the Golden Grove area. Production of sand and clay products from 1977-2013 was >1.Mt.
deposit of red, yellow, and grey Tertiary sand, with minor bands of clay. Production from 1977-2009 was estimated at 2.1Mt.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit opened in the 1950s on sands and clays to maximum 35m thick of Tertiary North Maslin Sand Formation. Resources for area north of Greenwith Road, including Christies pit ~58.6Mt. Production from 1977-2013 ~11Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.J. STRACHAN; CHRISTIES SA SAND AND METAL PTY LTD; CHRISTIES SANDS PTY LTD; F.A. CHAPMAN; PM 109; SA SAND AND METAL PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary sands and underlying clay and weathered shale worked in open cut pits from the 1950s until 2002. Production from 1964-2002 was estimated at 120,000 tonnes clay, shale and sand product.
small brickworks operation established in the 1920's. It is infilled and an industrial complex.
clay for brick making worked to ~6 m depth till the 1970's. Now operating brick making factory (2008). Estimated production from 1977-89 was 235,000 tonne of clay and shale products.
clay pit to 8m deep was established for brick making in the 1890's, and worked till 1927. The pits have been infilled, the area redeveloped as residential.
open cut some 70 m long in a gully, and on bluestone slate, worked between 1880-1920 for kerbing and building stone.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; QUARRY C; TORRENS GORGE MAGNESITE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: open cut on a blue dolomite bed, 30-45 m wide, overlain by sandstone, both of the Woolshed Flat Shale. It was used for road base material. The workings appear to have been filled in and rehabilitated (2008).

group of small quarries cut on dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. It was used for road base material by the local council. A thin siliceous bed of magnesite was mined in 1922 by F.A. Nicholls for production of 262 tonne.

gold-bearing alluvials, in particular from a pebble/conglomerate bed, with a blue clay matrix on banks of the Torrens River. No production figures were determined, nuggets were recovered. The area is now part of Torrens Linear Park.
8 m thick red and yellow clay for brick making in the 1920's, closing in the 1960's. Production from 1956-60 was 148,840 tonnes.

small quartz veins in weathered claystone of the Barossa Complex, and located on the Crafers Fault. A shaft to 6m was excavated. The mine was re-opened in 1894. The given location may be inaccurate. No production figure was recorded.
natural salt flats first developed for salt production in 1935. The workings cover ~4000 ha near the coast north of Adelaide. Production for the period 1976-2013 ~16Mt. Operations ceased in 2013.
2 open cut quarries developed on Stonyfell Quartzite, and first worked in the late 1920's.  They closed in 1970, and rehabilitation was completed in 1989.

pit to 7 m depth, and a brickmaking works were established in the early 1920's on a 10 m thick clay bed resting on water-bearing sand and gravel. It is now infilled and redeveloped as part of an oval complex and recreation area.
small pit on loamy clay used for brick making in the 1920's. It is infilled, used as industrial storage yard.

abandoned quarry of ~2500m2 by maximum 10m deep, and first worked in 1878. It was developed on quartzite of the Stonyfell Quartzite for use as building stone, also used by the local council for road fill. The quarry closed in 1927.
pit developed on a red clay deposit for brickmaking, It was worked in a pit to 8 m depth in the 1920's. It was redeveloped for housing in 2006.
clay pit located ~0.8 km north of Salisbury railway station.  Clay pit to 4m deep working in 1926 the alluvial flats adjacent to Little Para River.
initially worked for alluvial gold, then mining of several quartz-iron oxide-pyrite leaders in host slate of the Basket Range Sandstone. Production >60oz bullion gold.

sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale forming N tip of the current Riverview dolomite quarry, PM 35. Old, overgrown benches, not rehabilitated. production in 1955, and in 1962 was 1016t of sandstone, as well as 7840t of clay for brick making.
pit on white clay developed on deeply weathered Montacute Dolomite. Pit ~30 m long by 4 m deep, located on both sides of the main road, worked in the 1890s.
lode of quartz with galena. It was opened in 1844, worked from 1848-50 for some good galena. No production figures were recorded.
3 adits excavated in 1890 on a quartz vein carrying galena in host slate. No production figures were recorded.
worked a lode of copper bearing quartz-iron oxide discovered in 1844, worked to 1846 via an adit.
gold-bearing alluvial sand and gravel located at the foot of Black Hill. A production figure of 22gm (14 dwt) was recorded.
gold-bearing alluvium on 5th Creek. Subsequent small workings on 2 adjacent quartz-iron oxide veins with weak Cu-Au mineralisation. No production figure determined.
open cuts developed on phyllite, schist, quartzite, and sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale, worked for crushed rock in the 1950's.
open cuts developed on phyllite, schist, quartzite, and sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale, worked for crushed rock in the 1950's.

quartzite and slate deposit of the Belair Subgroup worked from 1858-1934 for slate. In later years worked for quartzite for road base material. In 1957 used as a council rubbish dump. Rehabilitation completed in 1987.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit developed to 6 m deep on clay used for brick making. It opened in 1886. It is now filled and rehabilitated, and partly occupied by housing, partly by a park. Only production figures recorded were for 2100 tonnes in 1977.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: weathered phyllite and slate quarried for red bricks. Operated largely during the 1950's. Production was 117,600 tonnes in 1956-60, and ~80,700 tonnes from 1977-86. No workings remain, the area is infilled and residential (2008).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PINKERTON GULLY; PITT LTD; PM 135; PM 136; PM 137; PM 147; READYMIX MONTACUTE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Neoproterozoic dolomite, quartzite, and phyllite of the Burra Group, first operated in the 1920's. Resources (1962) estimated at 12.54Mt to RL 245m. Production from 1977-2013 ~14Mt of limestone, dolomite, and metasediment products.

penetrated in a bore put down at the foot of Montefiore Hill. Seam of lignite 3.5 ft thick. Coal quality was poor, and that the alluvials showed more promise for gold. The location was on North Adelaide golf links, South course.

gold-bearing alluvium on fifth creek and various tributaries to it. Production records indicated recovery of 13 oz (404 gm) gold, but this represented only a small proportion of actual gold recovered.
Tertiary sands to 20 m thick. Production from 1974-87 was estimated at 21,000 tonne building sand. The pit was rehabilitated in 1990.

lode of quartz-iron oxide worked intermittently for silver and copper ore from 1868-1889. Lode with malachite, silver ore, graphite, quartz, iron oxide, pyrite, galena. Workings were extensive. No production figure recorded.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: variable Ag-Pb-Cu-Co mineralisation in several quartz lodes in host metasediment of the Burra Group. Several bags sent to Melbourne assayed 1.6%Co. A parcel of 15.2t gold ore yielded 77.8gm bullion gold.
Pb-Ag-Zn quartz reef in host Wattle Park Member metasediment. Recorded production 50.8t ore, grade of hand sorted ore 20-37% Pb, with payable Ag, and Zn.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host claystone, and sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale, and worked in an adit, with winze for Cu, Pb, Au, and Ag mineralisation. No production figure was determined.

quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate and quartzite, dip 60SE, of the Woolshed Flat Shale. A shaft was excavated to 6m, and extended 6m on the underlie. No production. 2nd claim worked on separate lode as the Morialta Blocks (MSC #172).
fine sand of Holocene age on Torrens Island. From 1967-86 ~212,260 tonnes mined. In 1981 drilling determined resource 1,105,000 tonne. Production ceased in 1986, and it was rehabilitated in 1989.
open cut on quartzite of the Mitcham Quartzite, worked in the 1920's. Now part of Torrens Linear Park (2008).
488 tonne production from slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite was recorded for 1949. Now residential..

8-10 m thick red clay deposit in the 1920's, and operated through to the 1950's in two pits. Production from 1956-61 was reported as 112,200 tonnes. The pit has been infilled and the land redeveloped.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE POTTERIES PL; PGH INDUSTRIES LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small pit working red and yellow Tertiary clays to 8 m depth for brickmaking. Production was 9680 tonnes from 1959-61, with brick making continuing via supply of clay from Tea Tree Gully. It is now infilled with redevelopment of industrial complex.
pit on Tertiary clays in the 1960s. It has been amalgamated into the complex of pits that makes up the Christies sand pit. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ELLIOTT BROS; HALLETT BRICK; LAMBERT AND PARRY; PGH CLAY; PM 68; ST AGNES; TEA TREE GULLY; WHITING ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: worked for pottery clay in numerous shafts to 80 ft deep in the late 1920's to late 1930's. Tertiary clay was in a bed 2-3 m thick, overlain by red-yellow sand. Production ceased in 1996 and the pit has been backfilled.
alluvial sand and gravel excavated from bed of Torrens River in the late 1920's to early 1930's. Dark titaniferous heavy minerals were noted as a residue from the washing, with some free gold noted.
small quarries developed on dolomite and slate for building stone. A small copper ore lode was worked in an adit.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE CEMENT CO; POPES; S.B. POPE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry developed on weathered phyllite worked for clay for cement manufacture, producing 45,280 tonnes from 1957-60, with a small tonnage of clay (7310 tonnes) worked for brick manufacture.
Cu mineralisation in 1m wide quartz-iron oxide lode infilling fault zone in host slate of Tapley Hill Formation. Production ~40,000t @ 5% Cu. Ref: RB95/41

lode to 30cm of quartz vein with Pb-Ag mineralisation, with one sample assaying 627 oz Ag/ton (a world record at the time). Ore minerals were copper (minerals not specified), and argentiferous galena.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: HIGHBURY (RIVERVIEW) QUARRY; PM 35; READYMIX GROUP; RIVERVIEW DOLOMITE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: large open cut developed from the late 1950s on dolomite & host metasediment of the Burra Group. Resources (1958) ~9.2Mm3. Production from 1977-2009 ~12.4Mt.
large open cut working a whitish quartzite and sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite Formation. First worked in the 1890's. Production of construction materials from 1977-2009 ~8Mt.

small quarry of ~0.5Ha x 0-6m deep worked for crushed rock, ie sandstone and quartzite of the Slapes Gully Member of the Stonyfell Quartzite. First opened in the 1890's it was worked occasionally until the 1970's.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CONCRETE INDUSTRIES; GOLDEN GROVE; MONIER SANDS; PM 76; REID CR   PTY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 23 m of Tertiary non-marine sands on Torrensian slate. Current complex of separate pits. Production from PM 76 from 1977-86 was estimated at 80,000 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CONCRETE INDUSTRIES; GOLDEN GROVE; MONIER SANDS; PM 152; REID CR   PTY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary sands and clays to 20+m worked in the 1970s as PM 152. It is now infilled and rehabilitated, currently used as an oval. Production figures from PM 152 aggregated with overall Golden Grove production.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLDEN GROVE; MONIER SANDS; PM 71; ROCLA SAND
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit developed on Tertiary non-marine sand and clay, and worked for brick clay in the 1950s-60s. Resource of ~5.5Mt of sand was estimated. Production from 1993-2009 ~6.4Mtonne.
COMMODITIES: Sand,  Clay,  Silica sand,  Gravel,  Shale

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PGH CERAMICS; RENOWN PARK PUG HOLE; SA COOPERATIVE BRICK CO. LTD.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: red clay of the Pooraka Formation used for brick making. It opened in the 1920's, and closed in the 1970's, with incomplete production figures only for 1960 of 33,500 tonne. The pit was rehabilitated in 1982.
7m wide quartzite bed in host slate, shale, and sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. In 1939 production was estimated at 69,170 cubic yards. Now an abandoned quarry of <7,000m2 x 1-8m deep.
pit on Tertiary gravel, rehabilitated in 1995, and currently in residential area.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; M.J. CARRAILL; PM 54; SA SAND AND METAL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic workings on Tertiary sand and clay to 10 m thickness. Basal weathered Torrensian slate was worked for brick clay. It is infilled, rehabilitated and residential.
pit on Tertiary sand in Golden Grove area, rehabilitated in 1995, no production figure identified.
small quarry on slate and quartzite of the Belair Subgroup, and opened in 1844. It is filled in, and now residential.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale was worked for gold in a series of shallow shafts, and surface workings. No production figure was determined.
low-rank Tertiary brown coal (lignite), with high moisture content, also high volatiles, and high sulphur. Total resources were estimated at 230Mt occurring in 2 seams. Overburden thickness 32-55m.

mine opened in 1888 developing as numerous adits, shafts and costeans on a quartz-iron oxide lode carrying copper carbonate, and galena. Host rock was slate and sandstone. No production figures were recorded.

pit to 8m deep opened for the manufacture of red roofing tiles, but on change of ownership, dedicated to the manufacture of red brick. Production from 1956-61 was 59,000 tons. It is infilled and redeveloped as an industrial area.

mine developed on a small lode of quartz-iron oxide, with galena and cerussite in host sandstone, slate, and limestone. It was worked in shafts and adits for 1 year before closing down. No production figures were recorded.
council quarry developed on quartzite of the Wattle Park Member, and worked for over 60 years for road material, and screenings. It was rehabilitated between 1973 and 1992.
worked from 1844-47 for copper ore in a shaft and adit. Host rock was metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite.
major open cut developed on Stonyfell Quartzite, mining commencing in 1837 for building stone. Production from 1967-2013 ~18Mt. Current production of quartzite/sandstone products.
old clay mine, worked in shallow shafts and pits at various times for white clay.
old clay mine, worked in shallow shafts and pits at various times for white clay for brick making on flat lying Tertiary sediment.
old clay mine, worked in shallow shafts and pits at various times for white clay.

abandoned open cut of >1,000m2 x 1-10m deep opened in 1888, and developed on quartzite and sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. A crushing plant was erected in 1912 by the local council for supply of crushed rock for road making.
alluvial gold prospects along creeks draining the Adelaide Hills in the Tea Tree Gully area. White clay was mined from shafts sunk to 30m. No production figure determined.

large quarry developed on quartzite, and slate of the Adeladean Stonyfell Quartzite. It opened in 1854, with periodic activity to 1982. Production of quartzite and sandstone products from 1974-1982 ~1.46Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: G. HANNAFORDS; QUARRY A; ROADSIDE; ST PETERS; TORODES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: series of quarries commencing operations in 1868 on sandstone and bluestone of the Montacute Dolomite for use as building stone. They were worked in the 1920s for stone for use in construction of Saint Peters Cathedral.

ironstone gossan in Woolshed Flat Shale worked for flux. Host was metasediment, phyllite, dolomite, slate, shale. At depth Cu-(Pb-Ag-Au) mineralisation penetrated. 300 tonnes of iron ore for use as flux was recorded.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Galena,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartzite and sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite, opened in the late 1920s, reopened in 1974 for road base material. It is chemically an unreactive rock used in water supply applications.Production for the period 1977-2011 ~16.5Mt.
small quarry opened in 1957 on a deposit of blue dolomite of the Montacute Dolomite for only minor production. It was located in the Torrens River Gorge, and on the NW corner of section 5539.
weakly cemented sand and gravel worked in open cut on side of hill on banks of Torrens River. Developed in 1920s to form face 7-10 m deep. In 1927 production was ~140 tonnes per day.

7m deep, and brickmaking works were established in the early 1920's on a clay bed from 1.5-6.7 m deep, resting on water-bearing sand and gravel. The pit is now infilled and redeveloped as part of an oval complex and recreation area.
located in upper reaches of Fifth Creek, 466 tons of sandstone of the Wattle Park Member, excavated in 1956-57.

opened in the 1880's for slate of the Belair Subgroup. Reopened by Unley council in 1920's for road metal, and slate for culverts and road base material. Closed in late 1930's, partially reopened in late 1990's for road metal in construction of freeway extensions.

gold discovered in 1914 in alluvium during well sinking. In 1932 an adit was excavated, also returning gold from alluvial. A water inflow of 700 gallons/hour caused mine closure. No production figure determined.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host shale of the Basket Range Sandstone. Incomplete production figures were recorded of 7.1 tonnes of ore yielding 135.3gm gold at 19g/tAu. Some production of alluvial tin.
location uncertain, but located in McDonnell Avenue, Hindmarsh. Now filled and rehabilitated.
quarry worked for crushed stone from quartzite and dolomite of the Stonyfell Quartzite in the 1920s, and closed in the 1970s. No production figure apparent. Minor rehabilitation has been undertaken.
2 workings either side of Dry Creek worked on a quartzite bed to 12-15 m wide, and slate both of the Saddleworth Formation, for road metal. It opened in the 1890s, active in the late 1920s.

manganese and iron oxide gossanous lode in limestone and shale of the Saddleworth Formation, and carrying copper sulphides was discovered, and the mine was developed. Workings consisted of adits worked for a brief period only.

quartz-iron oxide pyrite lode trend 190, dip steep E, in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Geochemical sampling of the spoils returned nil gold, anomalous silver. No production records apparent.
quarry developed on slate of the Belair Subgroup for building stone, and rubble, and opened in 1870.
Cu mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of the Montacute Dolomite. No recorded production figures.

gossanous calcite-barite lode with silver-galena in host Saddleworth Formation. Sections of mine remain open as a tourist attraction, and it is located just east of the old Toll Gate. Recorded production 214 bags, 44.7 tonnes of ore, no grades.
mine consisted of small workings on a quartz vein for copper, in 1846, on Corkscrew Road Montacute.
7 galena-cerussite lodes in gossan, within shale-limestone host of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production 107 slabs of bullion lead.

number of quartz-iron oxide lodes with galena, copper, bismuth and silver mineralisation, and in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production was 71.1 tonnes of ore, no grades specified.
worked a lode of galena in vein-quartz in host slate and sandstone, in 1848. It was later incorporated into the Glen Osmond stone quarries. No production figures were recorded.
lode of iron oxide-rich gossan, with malachite and azurite in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figures were recorded.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Feldspar,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz,  Tourmaline

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein bearing galena and cerussite. Host rock was slate and limestone of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production was ~1524t, no grade specified.

quarry developed on quartzite & sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. First operated in the 1940s. Resource estimate in 1957 2.7 million m3. Production from 1951-56 ~203,000t. Production from 1977-2011 ~13.2Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE POTTERIES LTD; PGH INDUSTRIES LTD; ROSEWALL EARTHMOVERS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary clay bed about 24m deep. Production figures available included 1925-26, 25,450 tonne, 1938-49, 54,680 tonne, and 1956-60, 37,835 tonne. It is infilled, and rehabilitated.

red and yellow clay, with a sand and gravel floor, first worked in the 1920s, closing in the 1970s. Production figures for the combined pits were, 1929, 1941, 1956-61 for 47,300 tonnes. It is infilled and redeveloped as an industrial area.

pit to 11m worked for clay for brick making, and sewer pipes. Opened in late 1800s, initial production to 1908.  Recorded production 19,455 tonnes from 1927-1961 when work ceased. It is infilled and rehabilitated, and used as industrial site.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEDDELLS WOODS; GAWLERS; HAYWARDS; PRINCES; SUGARLOAF HILL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: one of several quarries worked for quartzite products from the Belair Subgroup. The pits first developed in 1861, and passed through various owners from 1861 through to 1931. No total production figures recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEDDELLS WOODS; GAWLERS; HAYWARDS; PRINCES; SUGARLOAF HILL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 1 of several quarries on Belair Subgroup worked for quartzite products. The pits first developed in 1861, and passed through various owners from 1861 through to 1931. No total production figures recorded, 3050 tonnes recorded for 3 month period 1925.

workings on Saddleworth Formation quartzite, slate and sandstone. Opened in 1850 for road metal and building stone, operating until 1927. The old quarries were stabilised and fenced between 1995 and 1999.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MOUNT BONYTHON; MT. BONYTHON; YOULTONS LITTLE MOUNT LOFTY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry on sandstone unit of the Woolshed Flat Shale, and atop of Mt Bonython. 11,000 tons recovered in 1923.
pit developed on a clay deposit in the Pooraka Formation, and is now filled and rehabilitated and used as an industrial site.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: J.F. ATTIAH; W.E. YOUNG; YOUNGS BRICKWORKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: brick making clay pit to 6.7 m deep, developed on a clay deposit of the Pooraka Formation. The pit was infilled, and redeveloped as an industrial area. No production figures were recorded.
mineral claim taken out in 1946 on a mica occurrence in Waturu Gneiss and in the Oodnadatta region.

no details, presumably old workings with grab sample submitted for analysis in 1969 for value 21.5%Cu. Location on 100k geology is Tertiary ironstone developed on metasediment of the Birksgate Complex.

area of fairly intensified pegmatisation 6 miles west of Granite Downs Station. Long crystals of beryl to 3 inches length by 1/2 inch diameter in host pegmatite were found. The colour varied from slightly greenish-yellow to translucent honey-yellow.
small workings on copper shows of malachite in quartz veins occurring from near Mount Chandler, then extending in low-lying areas bordering Indulkana Creek, west towards Mengersons Well.
historic rubble pit developed on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road base material. Recorded production was 2800 tons from 1951-52.
sand deposit in low-lying, swampy drainage marginal to Lake Alexandrina. Production 1973-80 ~4600 tonne. Remaining resources ~10,000 tonne in 1975.
series of 4 adjacent salt lakes surrounded by old, massive sand dunes. The main lake was worked for salt from 1940. Production to 1952 was ~24250t, production from 1976-2013 from PM 38 was ~115,000t.
opal diggings in Bulldog Shale, no production records.

southernmost opal diggings on Andamooka Opal Field. Workings developed at contact of underlying quartzite/sandstone of the Proterozoic Tent Hill Formation, and overlying Cretaceous Bulldog Shale.

original digging discovered in 1930 on the Andamooka Opalfield. opal found encrusting pebbles, infilling fissures in quartzite boulders at a pronounced level of a flat-lying boulder bed that outcropped around the peripheries of the Andamooka Hills.
opal diggings on Bulldog Shale, no production records.
copper show in host diapiric breccia, located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal MEIS 250K map series for mineral occurrences on Andamooka sheet.

carbonate-trace malachite veins terminated against barren quartz reefs. Host rock calcareous siltstone of the Amberoona Formation. Small pis developed on parts of laterally extensive vein sets over a strike of 500m. No production records located.

historic shallow council pit of ~7,000m2 developed on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road base material. Reported production of 8,300 tonne from 1925-33. Rehabilitated and the site of an industrial compound.
gold in Tertiary conglomerate overlying Barossa Complex metamorphic rock. Worked initially in 1869, reworked in 1881, and in the 1930's. No recorded production figures specific to these diggings.
workings on quartz-iron oxide reef trending NE in host slate of the Barossa Complex. No recorded production figures.

alluvial gold discovered in a sandy conglomerate in 1869, with follow up prospecting discovering barren quartz-iron oxide reefs in host metasediment of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. No production details.
quartz-iron oxide vein worked via a shallow pit and shaft in 1930-3 failing to return payable gold. Host rock was metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group.
Reef discovered in 1868.  Work ceased in 1870 after a series of poor crushings.  Over 10 tons of ore crushed, average 4 dwt per ton. Lode consisted of quartz and ironstone.  Country rock is slate.
20-acre claim on section 203 of the Barossa Goldfield, a prospecting venture held by Henry Taylor from 1896 to 1898.
abandoned shallow council scrape of ~3,000m2 x 1-2m deep on section 159, and developed on Tertiary gravels.
section 160, abandoned shallow council scrape of >10,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on 3m deep Tertiary gravels.

location not accurate, recorded as Section 3030 Hundred Barossa, small council quarry developed on thin quartzite interbeds striking SSW, and in sequence of shale, and siltstone of the Castambul Formation.

workings consisting of a series of shafts. Operations were suspended in late 1887, and ceased in 1891 after numerous failed attempts to control the strong inflow of water. No production details given.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No production figures recorded.

shaft developed on quartz leaders that showed high gold assays, and that had been exposed during earlier alluvial mining. Host rock was metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Emeroo Subgroup. No production figures were reported.

6m wide band of hard, blue quartzite of the Stonyfell Quartzite for use in the construction of the South Para dam. No production figures recorded. Resources ~67,500 cubic metres of feldspar-free aggregate, 55,050m3 of lower quality feldspathic quartzite.
outcrop of augen gneiss of the Barossa Complex for use in the construction of a weir wall.
deposit of Quaternary sand, with production from 1982-2002 of ~433,500 tonne of garden sand products. Rehabilitation was completed in 2004.
diggings on alluvials in a small gully carrying gold with workings located east of a granite dyke that crossed the gully.
2 reportedly rich Au-mineralised quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. Lack of finance led to only shallow development. No production figures determined.
quarry on granite gneiss in 1970, with the intention to work back to a dolerite for use as road base material. However the quarry was declared unsafe before the dolerite was reached.

small quartz veins following discovery of alluvial gold in an adjacent creek. Host was sandy shale of the Neoproterozoic Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded production from 688.9 tonnes was 9557.4 gm of gold at 14g/t.
diggings on gold-bearing alluvials, part of the larger Humbug Scrub alluvial field, and located on section 97. No individual production figures determined.
worked for quartzite at around 1900. Location uncertain, possibly excavation in the SW corner of the section, in host Skillogalee Formation or overlying Woolshed Flat Shale.
small gully, part of the larger Gumeracha Diggings, no production details, worked for alluvial and reef gold in the mid 1880's.
quartzite of the Burra Group on a gently N-plunging anticline. Used for the South Para Dam project, production included 25 tonne spalls, 200 tonne as fill. Resource estimated at 8.75Mt in 1989.
mine developed in 1944 on a pegmatite dyke in host schist of the Barossa Complex. There was a small production of poor grade muscovite mica.

mine developed on section 125, Hundred of Barossa on MC 595. Two small open cuts were developed on a pegmatite within schist, for production of 1/2 cwt of beryl, and 1 tonne of mica. It was worked from 1944-46.
location uncertain, described as section 4, Hundred Nuriootpa, iin Martins Gully Gawler east to Gawler South. Produced 5586 tonnes from 1956-1961.

section 237, Hundred Barossa, NW of the Barossa Treasure. Worked in 1896.  Shaft 27.4 m on the underlie. Gold was visible in some of the stone raised. Presumed quartz lode in host Barossa Complex metasediment.
diggings on a narrow modern drainage immediately south of the Afghan Hill Tertiary lead. Only small returns of payable gold recorded.
diggings developed in 1869 on gold-bearing alluvials for return of payable gold. A reef was worked in 1870. No production figures were recorded.

quartz-iron oxide lode trend 150, dip E in slate and sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group. Workings of numerous shafts, with the last reported activity in 1938. A parcel of 52.2 tonnes of ore yielded 1124 gm of gold at 21.5g/tAu.
alluvials prospected in the 1870's and again in the 1930's, for a little payable alluvial gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; COLEMAN BROS; PM 186
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary sand deposit, with production from 1977-86 of ~18,000 tonne for garden sand. The pit was rehabilitated in 1988.
rush in 1869 on alluvials, with payable gold reported, though no production figures were recorded.
mine developed on deeply weathered greywacke of the Cambrian Backstairs Passage Formation. Production figures were recorded with the Cromer ""C"" Clay Mine.
white, kaolinitic clay as weathering of fractured greywacke of Kanmantoo Group. Tenure by various companies until the late 1950's. Extensive workings. Production from 1934-36 was 194 tonne.
sand pit developed from 1973-91 for an estimated production of 56,300 tonnes of sand. Rehabilitation commenced in 1980.
Tertiary sands overlying weathered shale. Production of sand, clay and gravel products from 1960-1975 was estimated at 250,000 tonne of concrete and building sand.
numerous shallow excavations in 1885, and again in 1931-32 on gold-bearing alluvials. No production figures were reported.
small find of alluvial gold, subsequent adit driven on lode of quartz-pyrite in host slate and quartzite of the Burra Group for no payable gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DAY SPRING; ML 4903; ML 4904; ML 5388; ML 5449; NEW DELORAINE; SOUTH DELORAINE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au-Cu-Ag mineralisation in quartz veins infilling fissures and crush zones in host calcareous siltstone, phyllite, and quartzite of the Burra Group. Production from 1909-1940 ~33,270oz Au, 178oz Ag, & 30.5t copper metal from 52,806 ore treated.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DELORAINE BLOCKS; DELORAINE QUEEN DEEPS; GL 1700; ITHACA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au-mineralised lode in host metasediment of the Burra Group. Production of 31t ore for 195gm bullion gold @ 6g/t.

gold-bearing alluvials in a gully, with some payable gold recovered. Further prospecting discovered the Bismarck Deep Lead on the N slopes of the gully, but mining proved to be difficult. No individual production figure determined.
Au mineralisation in gently W-dipping Tertiary gravels. Production from 1935-39 5007gm gold bullion. Resource estimate 64,000t @ 18g/t for 1,152Kg contained gold
deep lead for alluvial gold. Results were poor. In 1870 a rich pocket stimulated further mining, with reports of good payable gold recovered.

quartz-iron oxide reef carrying visible gold discovered at Walkerville Gully. Host was felspathic slates and quartzite of the Neoproterozoic Emeroo Subgroup.  Several shafts were sunk up to 18 m deep. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EMILY SOUTH; LADY EMILY; NEW EMILY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host metasediment of the Burra Group. Production ~3000gm bullion gold at 14g/t.
gold-bearing alluvials worked in 1931. Prospecting shafts in 1933 in an attempt to find a continuation of the adjacent Emily Reef. No production figures recorded.

quartz-iron oxide-copper mineralised lode in host mica schist of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production was from 1849-51 203 tonnes of ore at grades of 28-40% Cu, and 1888-90 51 tonnes at 13-60% Cu.
lode of Cu-Au mineralisation in slate of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. Alluvial gold found in adjacent gully. No production figures recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PM 208; PM 28; READYMIX CONCRETE; RINKER AUSTRALIA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary sand, clay and limestone deposit on PM 28, and 208 and adjoining area, for production from 1960-2009 of ~3.2Mt of multiple end products for use by the construction industry.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CONCRETE INDUSTRIES; PM 80; ROCLA; SCREENINGS PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit developed on Tertiary sand deposit, production of sand, gravel and shale products from 1962-2011 ~6.4Mt inclusive of ~178,000t for industrial enduse.
Quaternary sand and clay deposit, with production from 1973-96 of ~32,000 tonne of mainly foundry sand.

four leaders were struck containing copper ore and gold. The shaft was 70.4 m deep, with a crosscut drive of 46.3 m put in on a lode in host Barossa Complex, and containing indications of copper but no gold. Work ceased in 1877.
alluvial gold recovered from deep Tertiary leads preserved as ferruginous, cemented conglomerates on a hilltop ridge over an area ~300m x 50m to 6m deep. No production figures. Ref: Env 8210
quartz lode in host Stonyfell Quartzite, with trace copper mineralisation. Work ceased as results proved poor. A package of 18.1 tonnes of ore yielded 190.2 gm of gold at 10.5g/tAu.
gold-bearing alluvials, with a rich patch struck where the alluvials emerged onto the flats. It was reworked in 1872. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLDEN GLEN; HIDDEN TREASURE; PM 216; TREASURY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 50oz of washed gold from alluvium, recovered 2,000 tonne at 3.8%Cu, and extracted 12,000 tonne of talcose clay for brick making. A parcel of 30.9 tonne yielded 253gm gold at 8g/tAu. Host was pegmatite dyke in Adelaidean schist.
ferruginised, Tertiary sand and gravel capping a hill carrying gemstones. Later gold mining and production of 50.8 tonnes of ochre. No production figures for gold or gemstones was determined.

location uncertain, described as S of Tieca Mine, and SW of Aladdin Mine. Prospecting venture worked by a small company in 1873.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic mine developed in 1903 for recovery of a rutile concentrate. 6.1 tonnes of concentrate was produced in 1906. The area was the scene of exploration for mica in the late 1980s.
modern and older alluvials for good recovery of payable gold. A parcel of 53.9 tonne yielded 1120gm of gold at 21g/tAu.
small pit 30 x 10 m on Section 1 developed on deeply weathered Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production 9848 tons in 1961.
alluvials worked in 1868-69, with the field abandoned due to lack of water. Many nuggets found, production ~500oz, or 15.6Kg bullion gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No production figure determined.
quarry for road base material on feldspathic quartzite of the Appila Tillite.

abandoned quarry of ~5,000m2 x 3-6m deep that was developed on a steeply dipping sandstone unit ~10m thick, and within the Woolshed Flat Shale. The abandoned quarry is now occupied by an industrial shed.

alluvial gold in conglomerate on the top of Hatches Hill. There was a second rich find in 1870, which prompted a larger rush with better payable gold, grades to 1 oz/tonne being reported. No production figure determined.
gold-bearing alluvials. In 1870 a rich patch was discovered and a rush ensued. There was prospecting for reef gold in 1873. No production figures were determined.

deposit of Tertiary sand and gravel. with production from 1974-75 of 6490 tonne, and 1994-97 of 44,340 tonne, for total 50,830 tonne of multiple products for use in the construction industry. The pit was rehabilitated in 1986-87.

commenced in early 1960s and ceased production in 1992. It consisted of 5 separate pits 3 of which were rehabilitated in 1998-2002. Production was estimated at 162,500t garden sand. Area is now a conservation reserve.

7 quartz reefs in host sandstone and micaceous schist of the Emeroo Subgroup. Grab samples of spoils returned 155g/t gold. Copper ore was subsequently discovered. Work had ceased by early 1899. No production figures were determined.

deposit of Tertiary sand, minor gravel in the early 1950s. Total production from 1950-2001 was estimated at 335,700 tonne for multiple products for use in the construction industry. Rehabilitation completed in 2005.
mine on pegmatitic rock in host metasediment from the Barossa Complex from 1934-36 for ilmenite, tourmaline and rutile. No production figures were recorded.
diggings developed from 1931-34 on an alluvium deposit marginal to a modern creek bed. Fine gold was recovered, no production figures were recorded.
gold-bearing alluvial deposits with reports of grades to 31g/tAu reported. The Lord Vivian reef was subsequently discovered and worked. No production figures were recorded.
gold-bearing alluvial deposits for recovery of some payable gold, no production figures recorded.
recent alluvials with small quantities of alluvial gold recovered, no production figures recorded.
Cu-Au mineralisation in ~120m wide zone for 400m strike in host gneiss of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. Incomplete production records to 1904 of 200t copper metal & 18.4kg bullion Au.
sericite-altered quartz-iron oxide reef in host granitoid of the Barossa Complex. The company wound up in 1876, and the mine closed in 1879. No production figures were determined.

Quartz-iron oxide-pyrite, with black copper ore worked in 1873. A fine gold leader was struck in a number of costeans 5 shafts sunk.  Cu ore struck in the northern claims, no payable gold was found. Work ceased in 1874.
quartz reef in host quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup, with no payable gold recovered. The workings included of 2 adits to ~30.5m, and 21.3m.

Au mineralisation in conglomerate bed, and underlying quartz reef leaders in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No production figures recorded.

deposit of feldspathic quartzite of the Adelaidean Wilyerpa Formation, for road metal and concrete aggregate product for use by the Tanunda DC. Recent operators are Adelaide Brighton Cement. Production from 1977-2013 ~430,000 tonne.

copper mineralisation on host Woolshed Flat Shale on sections 1024, 1504. Worked in 1947-48. Precise location unknown. Section plan see MER plans database, plan no. FO0477, mine tenement plan for Hundred Para Wirra 1926-1950.

located between Hamlin and Try Again mines, and worked in the latter part of 1873. A lode 90 cm wide in host Barossa Complex was struck at 14.6m containing quartz, pyrite, and copper sulphide, but was barren of gold and work ceased.
historic diggings developed in 1889 on conglomerate of a remnant Tertiary palaeo-channel for reported recovery of 9.3gm gold from 12 buckets of wash.

location uncertain, section 510, part 512, Hundred Barossa. Cu-(Au) mineralisation on quartz lode in host Skillogalee Dolomite discovered in 1846. Operations were limited (12.2m shaft and shallow holes), and was short lived.

talc-albite lode in host mica schist of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production in 1945 was 50.8 tonnes of talc ore. It was reworked in the 1960s, and again from 1976. Recorded production from 1976-81 was estimated at 2450 tonnes.

quartz-iron oxide lode carrying Cu-Au mineralisation in host quartzite and sandstone of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production was ~60 tonnes ore for 9.1 tonnes copper metal, and 40 oz (1244 gm) gold.
auriferous quartz vein in host dark, pyritic to veined phyllite of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figures were determined.
gold-bearing, Recent alluvium for recorded production ~459gm gold. It was re-worked intermittently to 1936 with no payable gold reported.
Au-Cu mineralisation in vertical sandstone reef in host slate and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. Production to 1906 was ~18.3t Cu metal, 941.6gm Au at 2g/tAu.
gold-bearing Recent alluvium, as part of the rush at the Humbug Scrub Diggings. Numerous shafts were excavated, with the pay zone found at 7-10m depth. No production figures were determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 4584; EML 5513; MCKECHNIE; SLOAN SANDS P/L
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sand and foundry sand pit production from 1977-2013 was estimated at 335,000 tonne, inclusive of ~30,000 tonne for foundry sand.

15 m shaft was sunk and some rich ore was raised from a lode 2.4 m wide. A parcel of ore was treated at Wallaroo. Assays gave 34% copper and a trace of gold. Possibly same as Lady Pearce or Royal Phoenix.

gold-bearing alluvials on Barossa Goldfield. Considerable alluvial gold was recovered though no production figures were recorded. Many small nuggets to 11/2 oz (46gm) were recovered. It was reworked in the 1930's.
float of quartz in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No evidence of a quartz reef in 3 shafts. Assays from iron-stained quartz gave 1.5g/tAu.
gold rush in 1870 and lasting 1 year, with gold recovered from a hard Tertiary conglomerate. Production was estimated at 61 tonnes yielding 1378 gm of gold at 22.6g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate and quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup. Production ~3250gm bullion gold at 1.8g/tAu.

diggings developed in 1870 on reportedly rich gold-bearing alluvium along the creek immediately south of the Moonta Hill lead. No production figure was determined.

workings developed on Tertiary alluvium in 1870. The rush lasted ~3 months with good finds reported. A source reef was found and worked briefly for no payable results. Later the Tertiary gravels were worked for road rubble.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Adjoining Lady Alice to the N.  A close-bearing leader was cut at 10.7 m from the surface. 2 machines full washed at Goddard's puddler yielded 2 oz. 5 dwt gold.

yield of >103,230 tonne mainly for iron flux, and as a filler in paint. Occurred in basal member of Aldgate Sandstone at unconformity with underlying Archean rock. Average grade for 9 samples was 53.8% Fe, 18.3% SiO2, and 0.65% TiO2.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: claims worked for common opal in 1845, and again in 1903. Host was weathered Woolshed Flat Shale.
abandoned council pits, location not accurate, described as several pits on Sections 131, 5615 Hundred Munno Para, presumably working gravels and clay marginal to Goulds Creek for road rubble.
2 claims were taken up in 1889 on a deep lead. Seven men were employed. Work was carried on for about a year. The deepest shaft was 24.4 m. A parcel of ore treated by battery gave 1 oz. 1 dwt 1 gr.

4 copper lodes were reported to have been found, with trace only of gold reported. Lack of finance led to the closure of the mine in March 1874. The lode mineralogy was quartz, malachite, iron oxide, and chalcopyrite.

quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of Barossa Complex. Very good specimen gold obtained, in places vein material with abundant fine gold. Trial crushing reported to grade 18-25g/tAu. Recorded production was ~4oz (124gm) gold.

high level Tertiary palaeo-alluvium at the top of a gorge. The deposits were reworked in 1898, 1919, and 1936. No production figure determined. In 1919 an 8.1 tonne parcel of conglomerate ore yielded 70.3gm gold at 8.7g/tAu.
gold-bearing alluvium. Nuggets to 1oz were recovered. No total production figure was identified.

quartz lode in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite, and between Clarks Deloraine and Deloraine King. 2 shafts excavated for a recorded production of 20.6 tonnes ore for 191gm gold at 9g/tAu. The mine closed when returns fell away.

2 main lodes of quartz-iron oxide reefs carrying copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. No production was recorded, the venture failing due to lack of financial backing.

possibly same deposit as Murray Mica, worked from 1910-18, low grade mica product produced from mica-bearing pegmatite trending NW in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production 38 tonne from 1910-16.
approximate location only, considerable prospecting was carried out over a wide area on quartz-iron oxide lodes in an area between hamlin Gully and Lady Alice mine area in 1896.

quartz, clay, iron pyrite and copper sulphide. In line with the Lady Alice Mine at S end. A shaft was sunk to 15.2 m, and a drive was put in from its bottom. Although copper sulphide was found through the lode, there was no gold.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: resource of Tertiary sand and gravel estimated at 573,000m3 or 916,800 tonne. Though no production has been recorded there is a shallow scrape ~20m long by 30m wide.
scene of a rush for alluvial gold in 1870. Payable gold was found, no production figures were reported.
