small mine developed by BHP in the early 1900s on a deeply weathered pegmatite dyke  for use at their Port Pirie lead smelters. No production figure has been determined.
only production from Tertiary sand deposit was 10 tonne for concrete sand in 1989 and rehabilitation was completed in 1990.
not located accurately, described as 3.4km NE of Lyndoch, and on section 583. Show of copper carbonates prospected in the 1840s.
shallow prospecting pits in 1899 for gold in host Tertiary sediment on sections 2706, 2707, Hundred Barossa, 1.7km NE of Rowland Flat. No production figure recorded.

shallow prospecting pits and shafts developed in 1870 on gold-bearing alluvium on section 102, Hundred of Barossa, with good finds reported. It was prospected again in 1886, with a 2oz nugget recovered. No production figure determined.

diggings for alluvial gold developed along the entire length of a gully. At the northern end and with the same trend was an opaline vein with serpentine. Some granite dykes in the gully were prospected for beryl. No production figure was determined.

deposit of Tertiary sand , with production from 1977-2013 estimated at 530,000 tonne of garden and packing sand inclusive of ~40,000 tonne of foundrysand. Worked out areas are being progressively rehabilitated.
position uncertain, recorded as sections 1710-11, Hundred Barossa, minor prospecting of Tertiary alluvial for gold in 1870, with reported quartz reef nearby.

quarry on thin quartzite in shale and siltone sequence of the Castambul Formation. It was worked also for material for the South Para Dam project, but the material was rejected because it was considered too soft.

council quarry on lenticular bed of weathered sandstone, trend SSE, dip 70ENE, and of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Used by the council for road fill, and minor for building stone. Site in mindep is that of a large dam.
historic clay pit for brick making, and developed on alluvial silty clays, with lenses of silty sandstone over river gravels and Tertiary clays. Area now rehabilitated, and close to residential area.
section 14, several small quarries developed on Stonyfell Quartzite.
not located, described as located on section 1524, Hundred Barossa, covered by waters of the South Para Reservoir
located on section 174, Hundred Barossa, quarry opened in 1869 for road making material on quartzite of the Barossa Complex.
small, abandoned council quarry of ~1,000m2 x 1-6m deep, and developed on micaceous feldspar schist of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Worked for road fill.
mine developed in 1933 on a quartz-mica schist of the Barossa Complex from which a concentrate of 96% rutile was separated by jigging.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production ~600gm bullion gold at 30g/tAu.
60cm quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Work ceased in 1897, with only recorded production being a parcel of 5 tonnes, no grade mentioned.
alluvial gold recovered from a Tertiary conglomerate bed at the head of Spike Gully, and Two Speck Gully. No production figures recorded.
shallow and deep leads worked from 1867-68. Minor development on quartz reef in host kaolinised shale and sandstone of Neoproterozoic Emeroo Subgroup. Production ~600oz, 18.7kg bullion gold.

a party from Smithfield took up a claim, formed the Smithfield Mining Co, and in 1873 a prospecting shaft to 15.2 m was sunk. No payable gold was found and the company went into liquidation in 1874.
gold-bearing alluvium for reported good returns. No production figure was determined.
diggings on a show of alluvial gold for small recovery, no production figure was determined.

scene of a large rush in 1868 work continuing until 1872 on gold-bearing alluvium. The field proved to be very rich with nuggety and ragged gold recovered. It was reworked in 1898, and again in 1930-32. No production figure was determined.
worked a pegmatite dyke host for low grade mica in 1933. Located on section 335, Hundred Para Wirra. Pegmatite was 2-4m wide, trending NW. Worked in shafts and open cut to 60m long.

gold-bearing alluvium for recovery of considerable gold. No production figure determined. A quartz-iron oxide reef in host Delamerian granite worked in 1934 for a parcel of 5.1 tonnes of ore yielding 17.3gm gold at 3.4g/tAu.

quarry on sandstone of the Castambul Formation for building stone in the early 1900s. Stone from this quarry was used in the early construction of the Gawler Hospital.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gold-bearing Tertiary drifts and conglomerate for a small amount of gold recovered, no production figure recorded.
Tertiary sand deposit, with production from 1952-60 of ~172,000 tonne of mainly concrete sand. The pit was rehabilitated in 1999.

3 claims in Barossa Complex. Thomsons, Schramms in the gully where a 21.3 m shaft was sunk in the slate rock, and the third claim on which a long adit 79.2 m was driven toward the copper lode. No reef was cut.
Au-Cu mineralisation in host Barossa Complex gneiss. Production records were incomplete with the yield estimated at 628 gm of gold, no copper returns available.
total production from Tertiary sand for 1977, and in 1991 estimated at 2550 tonne for both packing sand, and foundry sand. Rehabilitation was undertaken in 1977-1978.
rush for alluvial gold in 1869. The diggings were reported as rich, though no production figures were recorded.

worked for dolomite in a quarry, 20 x 15 x 4 m deep in a sequence of metasediment of the Burra Group consisting of dolomite, marble, and quartz-mica schist.
alluvial gold worked in 1869, proving to be rich and worked  continually for 2 years. Incomplete production figures 170.4 tonnes ore yielded 40.2Kg bullion gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone and micaceous schist of the Barossa Complex. Reported production of 100oz gold bullion. The mine was later incorporated into the Menzies Barossa.
quartz-iron oxide vein in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. It was reworked in 1933. A parcel of 2.3 tonnes of ore yielded 129gm gold at 56g/tAu.

rush on alluvial gold in 1868. Good returns were reported over a wide area, with the field active for over a year. it was reworked in the mid 1890's, and again in the early 1930's. No production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: residual Cu-Fe oxide mineralisation in host altered, talcose marble of the Woolshed Flat Shale, local fault control. Recorded production 65.5t Cu metal from 400t ore from 1846-1919.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: hydrothermal clay deposit in deeply weathered sheared metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: scene of an alluvial gold rush in 1869. No production figures were recorded.
2 quartz-iron oxide-micaceous hematite veins in feldspathic slate and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, and at the foot of Walkerville Gully. No production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sandstone quarry on Woolshed Flat shale, recorded production from 1950-55 of 787t.
quartz-iron oxide lode within schist of the Emeroo Subgroup. Good gold was discovered in the top drive, visible freely in the stone that was crushed and panned. No production figure was determined.
quartz-iron oxide lode in slate and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. No production figure was determined.
alluvial gold within the Ulooloo Goldfield. No production records.

steatite (talc) of pharmecutical grade mined from host mica schist, marble, and quartzite beds of the Emeroo Subgroup from a 15 m deep adit for recovery of 57 tonne. Leases were taken out in 19th July 1944, worked until 1945.

Tertiary sand deposit, with production from 1977-1993 of ~156,400 tonne foundry sand. It has been rehabilitated using EARF - see file MB00594.
alluvials on creek bank worked for gold in 1846, and intermittently in the following years. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lenticular band of graphitic rock in host feldspathic quartzite of the Burra group. Worked in a series of shallow cuts from 1914-15, and again in 1917-25.

current-bedded arkosic sandstone, with heavy mineral laminations. Resource ~45Mt sandstone at 7.7%Fe and 1.24%TiO2. Magnetic separation test work gave recovery  75% iron oxide minerals, and 55% of ilmenite in concentrate at 60%Fe, 7%TiO2.

deposit of residual clay on deeply weathered claystone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Production was ~361,000 tonnes of clay from 1985-87, and rehabilitation was completed in 2003.
old shallow workings adjacent to Docs sand pit. No production figures were recovered.
prospecting in 1889 on section 573 Hundred Williamstown for the continuation of the gold-bearing alluvium from the adjacent Enterprise Deep Lead workings. Location uncertain.
buried, gold-bearing alluvium. A rush ensued, with numerous shallow shafts and pits excavated. Recovery of gold was reported to be good. No production figures were recorded.
small rush for alluvial gold in 1869. No production figures were recorded, with reports identifying both fine and nuggety gold recovered. It was reworked from 1930-32 for no returns.

quartz-iron oxide reef with Cu-Pb-Au mineralisation. Country rock was altered sandy claystone of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. 40.6 tonnes were crushed (yields not recorded). The lode was reported as very rich on the hanging wall.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide leaders that were very rich in gold in host shale of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. No production figures were recorded, with over 10oz of nugget gold reported as hand picked from the ore.
large 5m wide reef in Barossa Complex. 5 tonne parcel for 93gm at 18g/tAu. Silver reported in a second reef.

alunite recognised in lake bed in 1948. Drilling identified a resource was estimated at 233,000 tonnes at 7.33% potash. Later drilling indicated neither the alunitic lake sediments encountered, nor the lake brines were of commercial interest.
8 holes totalling 284 feet were drilled. Neither the alunitic lake sediments encountered, nor the lake brines, were deemed to be of commercial interest.

alunite recognised in lake bed in 1948. Drilling identified a resource was estimated at 233,000 tonne at 7.33% potash. Later drilling indicated neither the alunitic lake sediments encountered, nor the lake brines were of commercial interest.
lignite of Middle Eocene age in host Pidinga Formation in palaeodrainage channels. From limited drill hole information a global resource estimate was 800Mt.
shallow pit of >20,000m2 by 1-3m deep located adjacent to Eyre Highway, and developed on Pleistocene Ripon Calcrete. Worked mainly for road fill.

small hill of ironstone, with dimensions 90 m long, with an estimated historical resource of 150,000 tonnes per 30 m depth. Drill tested in 2010 to confirm source as magnetite gneiss with head grades >20%Fe.

10m seam of lignite. Outcrop in the lake bed. Deposited in Tertiary to Pleistocene in a topographic low. Drill hole penetrated 2 seams of lignite, 6 and 7 ft thick, but not considered to be of sufficient quality to be of use as a fossil fuel.

Tertiary (Eocene) lignite seams flat lying, ranging in thickness from 0.5-5m at depths of 20-50m. No resource or grade estimate. Lignite has been penetrated over a SW trend for ~30km, open ended to the SW.
curvilinear magnetic anomaly, length 7-10km. Hole DD86EN32 penetrated interval of BIF beneath 66m cover. 151-191m at 25%Fe. Estimated true width of 38 m.

magnetite skarn, with weak Cu mineralisation associated with series of circular gabbro intrusions, with reversely polarised magnetic signature. Located in strongly deformed Karari Fault.Tested in holes DD88LR 19-23.

linear aeromagnetic anomaly source as metasomatic magnetite-qz-feld-garnet gneiss beneath 40m of cover. Resource estimate (May 2012), 569Mt @ head grade 27%Fe, good results for recovery of magnetite concentrate from DTR testwork.
leases held on a small salt lake ~6km east of Lochiel from 1932-40 for recorded production of 193t.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Gold in series of parallel, gently dipping quartz veins in host quartzite of the Gumbowie Arkose. Production from 1931-63 13.67kg from 351t ore & from 1987-90, 19gm bullion gold.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone and at the southern end of the Mongolata Goldfield. Recorded production for 1 year of 6.45t for 70.2gm of gold @ 10.9g/t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANDREWS METAL SUPPLIES; N.E. SPARN; PM 214; YOUNGS WARNERTOWN 8
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of quartzite of the Adelaidean Bungaree Quartzite worked for production of road base material. Recent workings in sandstone units of the Skillogalee Formation. Production from 1973-2011 ~2.1Mt.
yellow-brown dolomite amd marble deposit, heavily fractured and jointed, laminated, trending NNW with a westerly dip, and near a fault zone. The carbonate is a member of the Skillogalee Dolomite.

fissure quartz veins cross-cutting Burra Group sandstone, with trace of copper carbonate. Base shaft malachite to chalcocite transition noted. Also anomalous silver to 106 g/tAg. No production figure recorded.
quarry developed in 1923 on a deposit of feldspathic quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation. There were no production details.
erratic Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide lode in host weathered slate, sandstone, and quartzite of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Production from 1932-45 42.6kg or 1370oz bullion gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BARTSCH A.J. PTY LTD; BRINKWORTH FREESTONE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry for sandstone for use as dimension stone developed in River wakefield Formation. Recorded production of 1992t from 1962-66.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COX; MC 1961; MC 1968; PETER; STEWART; WALTER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deeply weathered metasediment of the Skillogalee Dolomite, recorded production in 1958 was 35 tonnes.
reported minor prospecting of narrow beds of magnesite on MC 658, no recorded production.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BHP MAGNESITE; MC 12215; MC 12216; MC 12246; MC 664; MC 665
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: produced 1722 tonne for trial refractory from shallow open cuts in 1947-50.  High-grade magnesite (MgCO3, 80-90%, CaCO3, 0.1-4%, SiO2, 1-6%) confined to 1m bed in host impure magnesite and chert.
auriferous quartz lode in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone. 51 tonnes raised for 34.5 tonne treated for 571gm gold at 16.6g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: APOINGA ASBESTOS; BLUE SUCCESS; FARLEYS BLUE HOLE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed in 1941 on crocidolite veins in host magnesian marble and dolomite beds of the Skillogalee Dolomite.  Recorded production from 1941-51 was 82.3 tonnes.
N extension of Burra Mine lode. Poor recovery of economic mineralisation. From 1883 water in the main shaft was used as the water supply for Burra township.
lode carrying copper mineralisation. Only a small quantity of ore was recovered from workings consisting of several shallow shafts.

ironstone mined to supply flux to the Port Pirie smelters. Silver was reported in part of the quarry, and a prospecting shaft was sunk to 36 ft depth. Host rock was sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GREENS; MARSHS KAPUNDA; MELLORS; NIEMANS; WILLIAMS AND OLEARY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide reefs in slate and shale host of the Skillogalee Dolomite. It was worked for silver in the late 1880's. No production figures were recorded.
mine developed in 1939-40 on section 52 on a quartz reef in host metasediment of the Ketchowla Siltstone. Recorded production was 10.5 tonnes yielded 36.3 gm gold at 3.5g/t.

copper mineralisation in a quartz-micaceous hematite lode in dolomite and quartzite host rocks of the River Broughton Beds. Mining ceased in 1860. The mine reopened from 1872-74, then was worked sporadically until 1899.
shallow prospecting pits excavated in 1873 on a surface show of copper mineralisation withing the Rhynie Sandstone.
council quarry developed on dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production from 1926-47 was 18,695 tonne including 17,422 tonne of limestone, and 1,273 tonne of shale.

well defined lode of copper ore (with reported silver), over a strike length of 275 m, and ~3 m wide, in host weathered slate of the Appila Tillite. It was prospected in 1865, with no production recorded.

various pits worked by the local council for roadworks, no locations specified. Production was recorded from 1925-52 of 115,474 tonnes including 94,903 tonnes of limestone, and 20,571 tonnes of shale.

council quarry of >20,000m2 x 1-10m deep developed on blue-grey, thin bedded dolomite with shale bands, and of the Saddleworth Formation. Beds trend NNW, dip 70SW. Historic quarry re-worked in the early 2010s for road making material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; LOCATION 12; NORTH BOOBOROWIE LIMESTONE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council quarry developed on a 10m wide horizon of well jointed, thin bedded limestone within the Saddleworth Formation.

located on section 1, Hundred Kooringa and on the western slopes of a range of hills immediately east of Burra. 1-3 foot stratiform thickness of phosphate rock for ~60m along strike. 2 analyses variable 13-53% eCa3P2O8.

shear & breccia-hosted Cu mineralisation in host siltstone of the Kooringa Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Mineralisation associated with feldspar porphyry volcanics dated at ~790 Ma. Production from 1845-1981 ~2.7Mt ore @ ~3.3%Cu.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Chrysocolla,  Copper,  Covellite,  Cubanite,  Cuprite,  Gold,  Libethenite,  Malachite,  Pseudomalachite,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed on a quartz-iron oxide lode in host Tarcowie Siltstone. Incomplete recorded production was a parcel of 6.1 tonnes for return of 54.4 gm gold at 9g/t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUCUCO LTD; BYLES MONGOLATA; ML 5742; MONGOLATA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide-micaceous hematite-manganese oxide lode in host quartzite of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1930-52 122.5Kg bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite  Micaceous,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. A small pocket of specimen gold was recovered. Incomplete production records were 1.52 tonnes of ore yielded 10.1gm gold at 6.6g/t.

abandoned council road rubble pit originally >40,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed in 1933 on slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production of 180 tonne. Rehabilitated and now the site of the Jamestown rubbish dump.

2 adjacent salt lakes, the first developed in the 1920s on a lease of ~40 acres, salt layer 3-7 inches thick. ~10200 tonne harvested in 1921. 2nd on a 120 acre lease in 1934. Leases renewed with the last recorded tenure surrendered in 1948.

80cm wide quartz-hematite lode containing malachite, azurite, and gold in host micaceous schist of the Wilyerpa Formation. Samples from a small open cut returned assays of 8%Cu, and 7.8g/tAu. No production figure determined.

old diggings on Chalk Cliffs were visited in 1934 consisting of numerous shallow workings on quartz-iron oxide veins in host slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. One 25 cm vein was prospected to 15m depth, with no gold returns determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUSTRALIAN MINING CO.; ROCKY CREEK; ROCKY RIVER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: old workings on weak Cu mineralisation in narrow lodes in host fractured limestone of the Appila Tillite. Drilling on IP anomalies identified scant sulphides, with peak values 640 ppmCu, weakly anomalous Pb-Zn-(Ni-Au-W).
limestone of the Woolshed Flat Shale worked by Clare DC for road base material, production 1950-52 of 1803 tonne, now rehabilitated and within Clare township business centre as car park.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; FARRELL FLAT; SALT CREEK ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council rubble pit developed on weathered, laminated shale of the Bungarider Subgroup.
council rubble pit in weathered sandstone and shale of the Watervale Formation.
shallow council borrow pit of ~12,000m2 x 1-3m deep developed on weathered, white to pale green, clayey siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation for road fill material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; MANOORA SLATE; WATER RESERVE ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council scrape of >1,500m2 x 1-3m deep developed on deeply weathered, white, kaolinitic, laminated siltstone to slate of the Saddleworth Formation, dip 80E. Inspected by the Geological Survey in the 1960s. Now re-used as site of a small dam.

council pit of <10,000m2, with dimensions ~180m long NE x 70m wide x 1-4m deep, and developed on thin bedded shale and coarse sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone. Inspected by the Geological Survey in the early 1960s.
deposit of limestone and sandstone of the Adelaidean Gilbert Range Quartzite. Production from 1977-2013 ~ >1Mt. It is being progressively rehabilitated.
council pit of <5,000m2, with dimensions ~120m long NS by 40m wide, and developed in the 1950s and 60s on deeply weathered, white, to pale red-brown fine sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BURRS LODE; CLARE MAGNESITE; GRAY; MEAD; TODDS LODE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 claims west of Clare on magnesite in host Blyth Dolomite, section 1976, and section 1995, ~2.5km to NNW. Recorded production was 96 tonne in 1929. Point location is for the deposit on section 1995.
gold-bearing alluvials in Coglins Creek, also quartz reef gold in host Woolshed Flat Shale. A parcel of 31.2t reef ore yielded 449gm gold at 14g/tAu.

2 pits developed on Quaternary clay deposits either side of the Clare to Blyth road. Active from the 1870s to 1964, producing from 2500-3000 bricks per week. Recorded production from 1956-61 was 7,021 tonne.
silty sand for railway embankment fill. Drill tested in 1985 for recommened use as fill only.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CRYSTAL BROOK; DISTRICT COUNCIL; TRANSPORT SA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: white to pale pink, cross-bedded quartzite and sandstone of the Barunga Sandstone unit of the ABC Range Quartzite used by Transport SA for road fill.
prospecting of old gold claim for gold via a shaft on metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone, with poor results.

quartz reef in Tarcowie Siltstone, no details, see plan 89-0078 for detailed map of workings that consisted of several adits into side of low hill. Recorded production 1930-1950 ~750 tonne ore treated for 56,527gm gold at ~75g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode carrying copper mineralisation in host limestone of the River Broughton Beds.
adit developed on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode carrying silver mineralisation, and in host clayey slate of the Appila Tillite.
northern of 2 salt lakes harvested by Dolling family since 1919. Total production from 1919-94 was estimated at >2500 tonne.
lease taken out by Dolling on southern of 2 small salt lakes, section 296, Hundred Baringa, and 6.5km NNE of Snowtown. Recorded production of 1695 tons salt from 1921-48.

shallow prospecting pits on gold and copper mineralised quartz veins in host slate of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Three claims were taken out in 1931-32 south of the Orinda Block. No production figures were recorded.
mine working a quartz lode in 1936 and 1937 (G. Evans), with recorded production of 58t for 132gm gold at 2.3g/tAu.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. It proved unpayable, with recorded production 26.2t for 17.8gm gold at 0.7g/t.
small but rich quartz veins in host Saddleworth Formation, and prospected for silver and lead minerals in the 1860's and again in the 1890's.

location uncertain, recorded as section 376, Hundred Andrews, possibly from road reserve marked on Hundred map for Andrews. Production from 1939-40 of 31,150 tonne from limestone unit of the Tarcowie Siltstone.
large gossans in host Skillogalee Dolomite found to contain anomalous silver.  In 1885 they were prospected in 2 shafts to a depth of 15m. No lodes were discovered and work ceased within the year.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EAST VIEW; LUCKY CHANCE; MONGOLATA GOLDFIELD 2; RAMPTONS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: group of gold workings extending for ~300 m along strike. Recorded production from 1930-1955 was 561 tonne for 17841gm bullion gold at 32g/t. See plans S14812-S14815.
quarry developed on sandstone of the Leasingham Quartzite member in the 1920s for use as building stone.

2 main lodes of quartz-barite-iron oxide-calcite carrying abundant malachite, azurite, chalcopyrite, chalcocite, cuprite in host micaceous slate, limestone, and dolomite of the Blyth Dolomite Beds, with ore smelted at nearby Kooringa township.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Barite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: phosphate rock in host Skillogalee Dolomite, with chip sampling of phosphate rock returning 2540ppm U. Recorded production ~116 tonne at 60% Ca3P2O5.
shallow workings on a small quartz vein in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone, no production figures determined.An assay of the lode was taken giving a grade of 9.3 gm/t Au.
alluvial clay deposit, with recorded production of 3235 tonnes from 1925-37.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CASTLE SALT COOP; CHEETHAM SALT; G.S. AND M.A. FREEBAIRN; ML 56; OCSALT; SNOWTOWN SALT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: tenure first granted in 1912 on a salt lake 1.5km SE of Snowtown. Production for 1977 was ~30,000 tonne.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite. Series of open cuts and pits on a gold claim granted in the 1930's, with poor returns recorded.
recorded as on section 18S on the Mongolata Goldfield. Quartz-iron oxide reef worked for gold for poor returns. No production recorded.
diggings on mining claim MC 13733, on section 25, Hundred Mongolata, that worked alluvials near a dam for gold in 1932 in a series of trenches, for poor results.

series of council quarries operated from 1925-50. Recorded production of limestone of the Marola Sandstone member from several quarries of 98,658 tonnes material for building stone, and 140,515 tonnes for road works.

council quarry of ~12,000m2 x 1-4m deep, and developed in 1972 on weathered, white, kaolinitic limestone of the Marola Sandstone Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production of 14,378 tonne in 1972.
alluvial clay deposit worked for red brick manufacture only. From 1950-54 production increased from 400,00 to 700,000 bricks per year. Recorded production from 1956-61 was 12,125 tonne clay.
shallow pit developed on deposit of Holocene clay for supply of material to Gilbert brickworks in Clare. Production from 1973-82 estimated at 1100 tonne.

ferruginous quartz lode in host metasedement of the Tarcowie Siltstone. small 2 inch wide vein was followed down at the underlie, but it proved unpayable. Recorded production was 15.2 tonne ore for 107gm gold at 6.8g/tAu
ferruginous quartz lode in host metasediment of the Wildildie Sandstone Member. No production figures were determined. 50.8 tonnes ore yielded 402gm bullion gold at 8g/tAu.

quartz-iron oxide lode in sandstone of the Cox Sandstone Member. The mine was active for a number of years with some very rich patches were encountered. Most production was incorporated with Byles, with 235gm reported as a separate claim.

2 quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone. A number of shafts, and 2 lines of shallow pits along separate stratabound quartz lodes were sunk. 3.8 tonnes ore yielded 104.2gm gold at 27.7g/tAu.

quartz reef in host Waukaringa Siltstone, mine not located accurately, quoted as on sections 59 & 60 Mongolata Goldfield. The claim was worked in 1934. 28.45 tonnes of ore treated by battery gave 95gm gold at 3g/tAu.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite, and on the Mongolata Goldfield, no production figure determined, no reference found, located from plan no. 78-900.

fine grained albite-biotite tourmaline rock, with minor crocidolite recorded. Large boulders of tough, crocidolite-bearing marble occurred at the surface, and spread over a few hectares on a low NS saddle following the strike of host Skillogalee Dolomite.

flux quarries located on section 1904 (now 194-196), Hundred Reynolds, 2 miles from copper mine on the same section. Brown, goethitic hematite was mined for iron flux for the Port Pirie smelter from an open cut.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CALLER BRAE; MONGALATA 4; MONGOLATA; TERRYS CLAIM; W. TERRY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ferruginous quartz lodes in host sandstone and slate of Tarcowie Siltstone. Returns were generally poor, with some small rich patches struck, but many veins were barren. Recorded production 63 tonnes for 1598.4gm gold at 25g/tAu.

originally worked for slate of the Tindelpina Shale member, later worked extensively by local council for road fill. Deeply weathered, white to yellow, to pale red-brown, kaolinitic, laminated, pyritic slate and limestone. Pit of ~25,000m2 x 1-5m deep.

shallow council scrape adjacent to Farrell Flat golf course, and of ~5,000m2, with dimensions 140m long EW by 40m wide x 1-3m deep developed on deeply weathered, grey and brown slate of the Saddleworth Formation for road fill.
mine developed in 1886 and was an ironstone lode in metasediment that carried anomalous silver. Best assay 250g/t Ag. No production figures were recorded.

ironstone, primarily formed as replacement of diapiric breccia, mined for flux for +70,000tt, remaining resources ~30-100,000t @ 60.2%Fe. Analysis of a surface sample of phosphatic ironstone returned values of 2400Ce, 1300La, 33%P.
COMMODITIES: Iron Ore,  Iron,  Phosphate,  Rare Earths

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: position uncertain, originally located on section 41, hundred of Clare, and described as 800m N of Clare centre. It was worked in ~1900 for building stone from sandstone of the undalya Quartzite, no production figure apparent.
old pit developed on sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone, material used to supply building stone at Clare.
beds of phosphate rock in weathered shale and sandstone in a general limestone sequence of the Tapley Hill Formation. Samples assayed to 57.7% Ca3P2O5.
diggings developed in 1876 on gold-bearing alluvium, with prospecting recovering some small nuggets. It was reworked briefly in 1881-82. No production figure.

location uncertain, probably rehabilitated and on cropping land. Recorded as on section 79, Hundred Blyth. Pit developed on Quaternary limestone for road ballast with production of 60,230 tonne in 1947.
quartz-ironstone occurrence in host decomposed slate of the Appila Tillite. No lode was intersected, no production was recorded. Samples were said to assay up to 850 gm/tonne silver.

stratabound MnO seam >7.5km distance in host shale of Ulupa Siltstone, production ~520t. Rock chip sampling & drilling identified anomalous Mn, BM and REE, including Li, Ni, Zn, Cu, Mo, Sr, Ce, Nd, and Y, ie presence of lithophorite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLACK POINT; MC 5459; MC 5460; MC 5461; MC 5462; MC 9101
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lode of quartz-iron oxide in host Saddleworth Formation, and carrying visible copper carbonates, and galena. Sorted ore assayed 21%Cu and 16oz silver.
quarry developed on sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone in the early 1900s for road making material.
quartz vein in host Tarcowie Siltstone. It was located at the foot of the hill near Windmill Creek. A parcel of 7.1 tonne yielded 70gm gold at 9.9g/tAu.
quarry developed on decomposed feldspathic quartzite of the Rhynie Sandstone for use as building stone.
lease taken out on gypsiferous dunes E of salt lake for recovery of gypsum for production of 28 tons in 1927.
2 quarries developed by the local council on quartzite, sandy tillite, sandstone and shale of the Appila Tillite for use as road base material.

seed gypsum of the Yamba Formation, production from 1921-2015 estimated at 170,000 t for an end use of plasterboard manufacture. Resources estimated in 1950 at 406,000t of impure seed gypsum, and 610,000t of flour gypsum.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUSTRALIA SALT CO.; CASTLE SALT; LAKE BUMBUNGA; ML 18; ML 224; ML 54; ML 55; ML 7
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: salt production from saline lake recorded since 1912. Production from 1940-50 ~28,250t per year. Production from 1940-2007 ~745,000t.
quarry developed on sandstone of the Mintaro Shale from 1912-14 for use as building stone, closing down due to the poor quality of the stone.
quarry developed in quartzite of the Watervale Sandstone Member.
prospecting shaft excavated on alluvium to 14.5m with drives to the east and west. No gold was reported.
phosphate rock developed on limestone of the Upper Member of the Skillogolee Dolomite. Production of 10.15 tonne in 1903.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate of the Anama Siltstone Member. Initial assays that returned good values were subsequently thought to have been contaminated. No production figure determined.

Tertiary lignite in Northern St Vincent Basin Coalfield. Low-rank brown coal (lignite), with high moisture content, also high in sulphur, sodium and chlorine. Resource estimated at 625 Mt in 3 seams, cumulative thickness 14m, depth to the top 20-70m.

ground magnetic surveys, rock chip, local soil and gravel sampling, re-sampling of old drill holes, and reverse circulation drilling of potential kimberlite. 1 microdiamond recovered. Further work failed to recover any microdiamonds.
area of abandoned, local council excavations <5,000m2 x 1-3m deep for road rubble, and developed on limestone of the Appila Tillite, with recorded production in 1945 of 4183 tonne.
small brickworks on the west side of Laura township set up adjacent to a 2m thick deposit of alluvial clay in the bed of Rocky River.

quarries opened in 1856 on slate beds in host Mintaro Shale. Flagstone used for paving, panelling, floor tiles and for architectural work, full size billiard tabletops a specialty. Production from 1924-2013 >65,000t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MITTOPITTA GOLDFIELD; ML 4835; ML 5375; ML 5493; ML 5494; ML 5495; ML 5496
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings on a deep alluvial bed, with gold proving to have an erratic distribution. Worked occasionally from 1904-1930s for production estimated at 86t ore for 750gm of gold at 8.7g/tAu.
gold-bearing alluvium on the plains below Curlew and Central mines. Recorded production was 16.2 tonnes for 21.3gm gold at 1.3g.tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode with copper carbonates in host quartzite and slate of the Cox Sandstone Member. Production figure was 73.8 tonne for 4520gm gold at 61g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host Cox Sandstone Member on the main Mongolata line of lode. Recorded production for 1937 of 41.45 tonnes ore for 226gm gold at 5.5g/tAu. See Plan 89-0113.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host calcareous sandstone of the Cox Sandstone Member. Recorded production was 29.72 tonnes for 1770gm gold at 59.6g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. An adit was driven into the hill, with for initial poor reults. Recorded production was 63 tonnes ore for 495gm gold at 8g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode in sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. 3.05 tonne ore yielded 39.7gm gold at 13g/tAu.
veinlets of quartz and calcite carrying trace galena in host limestone of the Yudnamutana Subgroup.No production was recorded.
quartz-iron oxide lode in sandstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone. Specks of gold were seen in the stone from the southern vein, but overall the gold values were low and erratic.

workings from 1932-34 on quartz blow in slate for 11.43 tonne for 36.5gm gold at 3g/tAu. Several small prospecting pits are scattered irregularly along the line of lode on quartz blows to the south of Morrisons and north to Oates Mine.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Carbonate,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Tertiary clay, recorded production of 81 tonnes in 1950.

2 parallel formations with pyrolusite and psilomelane. Drilling identified anomalous REE and Sr in thin, clay intervals. Best values 2m @ 0.3%REE in K9RC009. Also anomalous Mo to 1850ppm for 1m in hole K9RC009

abandoned pit of >25,000m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road fill. Profile is that of a hard, flaggy layer to 30cm thick overlying friable, nodular to rubby calcrete. Maximum thickness to 1.5m. Resources likely to N & S.
abandoned pit worked by Len Mosey in the 1960s for supply of material for road fill.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone. Reported production was 28.35 tonnes ore for 396gm gold at 14g/tAu.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone, and reworked in 1932 by J.H Hindle. The Mt Edith G.M Syndicate carried out work in this period but results proved poor.

copper lode discovered in 1864, with location uncertain, described as in the vicinity of Stony Gap, Hundred Apoinga. Some ore was reported as being carted from the mine in 1866. Possible host of the Appila Tillite.
extensive workings on a quartz-iron oxide-calcite lode in host slate and dolomite in the Tarcowie Siltstone. Discovered in 1874, recorded production from 1901-07 was 52 tonne at 13-30%Cu.
workings were constructed in 1934-35 on a quartz-micaceous hematite lode in host metasediment of the Rhynie Sandstone. No production.

copper carbonates and iron oxide lode in host mica and chlorite schist of the Umberatana Group. Workings of 2 shafts, several pits and openings. No production records, surface samples assayed up to 18%Cu.
adit driven onto a quartz lode in host Grampus Quartzite, and east of the main ridge at Mongolata. The venture proved uneconomic.
many claims taken out along the drainage for alluvial gold. The most successful were tenures over Duffer and Phar Lap. No production figure determined.
clay deposit formed by deep weathering of Tapley Hill Formation. Worked for refractory clay for use in the Port Pirie Smelters. Production from 1926-37 of 3150 tons, and again in 1952-57 of 60 tons.
deposits of alluvium in Noltenius Creek, part of the Ulooloo Goldfield. No production records determined.
gold-bearing quartz lode in host metasediment of the Grampus Quartzite. Recorded production of 68.4 tonne for recovery of 327gm gold at 4.8g/tAu.

quartz reef on a low, mallee-covered hill of brown slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production was 11.4 tonne ore for 33.7gm gold at 3g/tAu. Drilled by Phoenix Copper in 2009 for best value 6m @ 23g/t.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host Waukaringa Siltstone. Recorded production of 11.4 tonne ore for 105gm gold at 9g/tAu.

adit to 4.8m, and costeans and pits developed on a quartz lode in host metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone. An assay from the quartz reef gave 1.4% Cu, 4.5 g/t Au. No production figure determined.

location uncertain, described as near Port Germein. Series of large pits and scrapes on limestone of the Semaphore Sand Member, and developed by the local council for road ballast. Quarry returns for 1947 of 10,160 tonne.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Ketchowla Siltstone for 5.1 tonnes ore yielding 16gm gold at 3g/tAu.

4 parallel lodes of surface copper shows in quartz veins in host Adelaidean metasediment. The claims were located on Mildren's property, located 3.4km from Hoyelton. A shaft was excavated, but the enterprise quickly folded.

bed of thick-bedded siliceous slate trend NNW, dip 35 ENE possibly of the Watervale Sandstone Member. The slate is well jointed enabling the slate to be broken into blocks, and was an important source of building stone.
claims worked for gold in 1933-34 in two adits, two shafts and an open cut to recover a trace of gold from thin quartz veins. Host rock was sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; PORT PIRIE COOP; ZIVER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: several council pits developed on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road base material, and minor agricultural use. Production from 1937-49 was estimated at 18,860 tonne.
few tons of rounded pebbles were excavated from the southern end of the lake of a deposit of pebbles around the margin of the lake.
leases taken out over Porter Lake in 1931 for salt production, with recorded production from 1931-37 of 874 tons.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone for little return.

2 pits developed on deposits of Tertiary, fine to coarse sand for heavy minerals. Recorded production of 100 tonne in 1972. Lease expired, and partly rehabilitated in 1973. Drill tested for sand for construction materials in 1985.
council pits on Pleistocene calcrete excavated for road rubble, with records for 2000 tonne removed in 1972.

quartzite of Barunga Sandstone for road seal aggregate. Investigated by SADME for suitability as railway ballast. Resource identified of 342,000m3 of good quality ballast from lower unit. Additional 193,000m3 of upper.
shallow prospecting pits on sections 41 and 42 on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone for no gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host shale of the Waukaringa Siltstone. 45.7 tonnes was treated for 193gm gold at 4g/tAu.
quartz reef in host sandstone of the Tapley Hill Formation for a small amount of gold recovered.
quarry developed on sandstone of the Leasingham Quartzite Member, originally for use as building stone in Clare, later for road base material.
crocidolite veinlets in dolomitic marbles prospected by shallow pits and trenches, no mining.
council rubble pit developed on jointed and cleaved, green siltstone and tillite of the Wilyerpa Formation.
council rubble pit developed on hard green shale and fine sandstone to siltstone of the Appila Tillite.
council rubble tst pit opened in the 1960s on a deposit of weathered tillite and silty shale of the Appila Tillite.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: numerous shallow pits developed on pockets and lenses of magnesite in host dolomite and slate of the Lower Member of the Skillogolee Dolomite.

quartz lode with galena-cerrusite in host dolomite and weathered slate of the Upper Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production 1912-13 28t Ag-Pb-Zn ore, minor copper, visible gold. 10 tonne parcel assayed 62g/tAg, 29%Zn, 36%Pb.
small brickmaking works developed adjacent to a deposit of alluvial clay in the early 1920s, with production recorded of 2,500-3,000 bricks per week in 1927.
quartz reef near the Golden Guinea mine. Gold values were very low. Host rock was metasediment of the Fortress Hill Formation.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: veins and bunches of blue crocidolite in host magnesian limestone of the Lower Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Worked from 1894-99 for recovery of 12 tons, and again from 1912-42 for recovery of 586 tonne of fibrous blue crocidolite. .

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ABERDEEN BALLAST; SA RAILWAYS; V.P. KEANE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deep open cut developed on dolomite of the Lower Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite by SA Railways for use as ballast material. Production in 1929 of 66,650 tonne.

small occurrence of poor quality kaolinitic clay examined in the mid 1950's. Petrology identified considerable quartz. Host deeply weathered Adelaidean metasediment. A small exploratory pit was found on site (2008).
white clay deposit reportedly resulting from the hydrothermal alteration of metasediment of the Appila Tillite. It was worked in 1956 for clay shale, and also for road base material.
pits developed on Pleistocene calcrete deposit for supply to lime kilns for use in the manufacture of lime. Production 1950-52 1330 tonne.

near Orinda Mine. Workings on quartz-iron oxide viens in host Tarcowie Siltstone. Workings both north and south of the creek. Trenches and pits on auriferous veins from which good gold was recovered initially to 3.1 g/tAu.
small open cut excavated into the hill above Windmill Creek on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone for no gold.
57m deep shaft excavated from 1934-35 on gold-bearing alluvium on slate bedrock of the Tapley Hill Formation. A 25.4 tonne parcel of ore sent for treatment yielded 11gm at 0.4g/tAu.

area of diggings for alluvial gold at the confluence of 2 large creeks. Historical shaft excavated in 1866 on copper lode in host metasediment of the Undalya Quartzite. Recorded production of 6 tonne at 20%Cu.
shaft to 39m on gold-bearing alluvium, with 76.2 tonnes sent to the battery yielding 212gm gold at 2.8g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GK PIT; OLOUGHLIN PIT; RURAL BRICKWORKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shale of the Saddleworth Formation, for brickmaking over area ~300m long, total thickness ~20m. Trenches and pits were excavated in the late 1930s. There were minor interbeds of sandstone suggesting selective mining would be necessary.
historic pits developed on quartzite of the Aldgate Sandstone, and investigated by the Geological Survey in 1959. Resource estimate ~4Mt.
quartz-iron oxide lode carrying copper and gold mineralisation in metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation. No production figure determined.
abandoned council pit of ~2,500m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed in the late 1990s on weathered, orange-yellow shale/slate of the Wilyerpa Formation for road fill.
location uncertain, decribed as on section 26, Hundred Bright. Patch ~30m long of brecciated marble, with fibrous crocidolite, talc, albite in host Skillogalee Dolomite(?).
historic diggings developed in 1934 on gold-bearing alluvium. Records for 3.1 tonne parcel for 73.4gm gold at 23.7g/t Au. Location uncertain, reported as Section 30 Hundred Mongolata.

2 adjacent, and abandoned small council quarries of total <1,000m2 x 1-4m deep, located adjacent to an abandoned railway line, and developed on a weathered, brown slate with interbeds of cross-bedded siltstone, and of the Saddleworth Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; EMU FLAT; SCOBIE ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: weathered dolomite of the River Wakefield Group developed by local council for road base material.
abandoned council quarry of ~8,000m2 x 1-5m deep, and developed on laminated, dark grey, pyritic slate of the Tapley Hill Formation for use as road fill.
quarry developed on grey laminated dolomitic slate overlying dense, blue dolomite of the Saddleworth Formation, and used for road base material. The pit was ~250m west of a residence.
quartz reef in host slate of the Pepuarta Tillite for little return. The workings consisted of a small open cut with a drive. No production figure was determined.

not located accurately, possibly a small pit on eastern boundary of section 146. Recorded as on section 146, Hundred Yackmourundie, and 4km W of Yacka. Iron-stained sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone, and excavated for road ballast.

2 Tertiary coal seams, maximum cumulative thickness 7m. Rank is low, with high moisture, sodium and sulphur. Average overburden 85m. Drilling from 1975-1986, with 43 holes completed. Reported in-situ resource were >270Mt inferred.

council quarry developed on limestone of the River Wakefield Formation for use as road base material. Production from 1933-52 from 3 sections on Hundreds Hall, and Blyth was estimated at 36,620 tonne.
prospecting of a copper bearing iron oxide lode.

abandoned quarry of >2,000m2 x 1-5m deep, and developed on hard, grey, banded slate to siltstone of the River Broughton Beds. Recorded production from 1938-49 of 14,914 tonne produced by the owner on demand from the local council for road fill.

section 116, Hundred Tarcowie on a patch 30m x 6m of limonitic shale/slate adjacent to a ferruginous quartzite of the Tapley Hill Formation. 3 prospecting costeans were excavated across the rock. One sample for 31% Ca3P2O5.

extensive workings on a quartz lode carrying malachite, azurite and chalcopyrite in host dolomite of the Blyth Dolomite. Discovered in 1846, production from 1873-75 recorded at 144.8 tonne @ 17%Cu for recovery of 21.9 tonne of copper metal.
2-3m thick deposit of red clay with irregularly distributed gravel beds worked in the 1920s for local brick manufacture. Cover of 2m of soil and loam.
quartz lode in Tapley Hill Formation for gold an silver. No production records.
Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide-siderite-pyrite reef in host sediment of the Cox sandstone to Tarcowie Siltstone. Production 84.4kg bullion gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOTTALOCK COPPER MINING CO; MUNJIBBIE SOUTH; TEROWIE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lode of copper ore worked in shallow pits but found to be uneconomic and soon abandoned. Taken up in 1906 for production of 10 tonnes @ 35%Cu.
quartz reef in host calcareous sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Recorded production was 25.4 tonnes for 44gm gold at 1.7g/tAu.
diggings on the Ulooloo Goldfield developed in 1869 on gold-bearing alluvium, no production figure identified.
1m wide alunite vein worked in 1914-17 for recorded production of 50 tonne. Host was metasediment of the Marola Sandstone Member.
shallow costean and shaft ~500m ESE of Wheal Sarah, surface copper mineralisation in quartz-carbonate vein in host siltstone of the River Broughton Beds.
surface show of mineralisation in host River Broughton Beds, and exposed in Spalding Quarry (MINDEP # 7667).
quartz-barite-iron oxide lode carrying malachite and azurite, and in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Prospected in 1845, and soon abandoned.
quartz-iron oxide reef in clay, sandy slate, limestone, sandstone of the Skillogalee Dolomite. The alluvial gold occurred in Tertiary gravels. No production figure determined.

series of lodes, with main lode ~45cm wide quartz-iron oxide-carbonate-feldspar with copper oxide and carbonate, trace sulphide in host dolomite and slate of Wilyerpa Formation. Production from 1913-16 27.1 tonne @ 29%Cu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Dolomite,  Feldspar,  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 3 lodes of quartz-carbonate veins in host Adelaidean siltstone. Recorded production 25 tonne for 7.6 tonne treated @ 26%Cu from 1910-11. In 1968, 7.1t raised @ 22.8%Cu. 2011 soil sampling identified anomalies associated with mafic intrusives.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Hematite  Micaceous,  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: alluvial gold deposit, with adjacent quartz lode in host clay, calcareous slate, limestone, quartzite and sandstone of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Recorded production from qz lode was 34.96 tonne for 240 gm gold at 7g/tAu.

copper mineralisation in host calcareous shale of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Rich surface ore quickly gave way to a narrowing of the lode and poor grades. recorded production was 40.6 tonnes no grades supplied.
quartz-iron oxide reef, in sandstone of the Cox Sandstone Member crossing a creek. Recorded production was 296.43 tonne for 4597gm gold at 15.5g/tAu.
shaft on a quartz vein in decomposed white shale of the Ketchowla Siltstone. There was no reported production.
nodules boulders and masses of phosphate rock in soft clay in host limestone and slate units of the Callanna Beds worked in a series of several trenches and pits over an area of several acres.
quartz vein in Tarcowie Siltstone, and on the Mongolata Goldfield just north of the Mongolata North claims and on section 36 in 1936 for poor returns. Not located accurately, see plan no 78-900.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: NAPOLEONS HAT; WAUPUNYAH CREEK; WONNA DIGGINGS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in sandstone and slate of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Some rich specimens were initially found, though with time the reefs yielded very little gold. Recorded production from Holders Claim for ~4 tonne for 31gm gold at 7.7g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DEPOSIT 26; FITTON TALC 26; ML 4580; MOUNT FITTON; MOUNT FITTON 26W
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: scrape for recovery of high grade white talc. The talc occurred in narrow seams with chert and grey dolomite interbands. Tested in 2 holes confirmed the persistence at depth of the interbanded nature and narrowness of the seams.
previously referred to as #8 North Deposit. A small open cut 15m long x 4m wide x 4m deep. Drilling prior to 1980 identified the deposit was small.  .
2 pits for >10Ha x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene sheet calcrete located north of the Old Wentworth Road, and worked for road making material.
similar to and adjacent to NO. 20, drilling identified 5 of 33 holes intercepting talc, with maximum 5m talc intercept.
major producer of high quality talc over many years. Though large volumes were extracted, the ore was characterised by high acid solubles due to carbonate inclusions.

talc lode in EW shear zone where strike-slip faults can be traced from the country rock into the lode. Lode with dimensions 140ft long by 12-24ft wide. Drilling in 1986/87 identified a continuation of the lode west, and behind the pit face to the NE and E.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: FEDERAL MINING CORPORATION; LINDSCHAU AND WARNER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: reported as 1.7km N of Hamilton Mine open cut and tunnel on 4m wide quartz lode trend ENE with weak copper carbonate staining.

Approximate lovcation recorded as 1.7km W of Paralana (Brindana?) Gold Mine. Tunnel driven into creek bank on a show of copper carbonate. Large 4m wide qz vein trend ENE on hill top with green copper staining.
specimen of scheelite taken from pegmatite host in a shaft on a copper show. Location uncertain, described as 1.7km W of Hamilton Mine and on slope of hill S of Hamilton Creek.

talc exposed in an open cut developed prior to 1976. The talc is very white, and free from staining, with minor zones of carbonate reported. Tested in 18 air core holes in 1987 identified only minor talc intercepts.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUSTRAL BLACK; BLACK HILL GRANITE; EML 3072; EML 3073; EML 3075; EML 3085; EML 3086; EML 3087; IMPERIAL BLACK; MARTINS; MARTINS GRANITE; MC 1091; MONIER TILLETT; RL 130
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry developed on a gabbro/norite marketed as Austral Black or Imperial Black Granite for use as a dimension stone. Production from 1974-2008 ~115,000t.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Biotite,  K-feldspar,  Opaque mineral,  Plagioclase,  Pyroxene

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council pit developed on a deposit of weathered norite for use as a road base material. The shallow pit had dimensions 180 x 70 m, and was located east of, and adjacent to Black Hill Rock road.

small Pb-Ag lode of bunches and veins galena in gangue barite, calcite. All the workings showed ore bearing material. Although ore was found over a large area no payable lode was discovered and the mine was only operated during 1908.
Au-Bi mineralised quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production >100oz bullion gold & 450kg Bi.
marble quarry on the Sellick Hill Formation worked in the 1860s, with many buildings in second valley built from stone quarried from there.

argentiferous galena in ferruginous gossan in host Fort Tree Limestone. Production records incomplete, with ~508 tonnes ore raised for 112 tonnes lead, 6322oz (196.6kg) silver, stockpiled 42%Zn, no yield recorded.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Bismuthinite,  Cerussite,  Galena,  Gold,  Smithsonite,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: nodular masses of alunite to 30cm diameter in darl clay immediately above a siliceous limestone of the Sellick Hill Formation. Discovered in 1918, with no significant production.

deposit of greyish, banded marble of the Normanville Group to 200-300m thick in NE-trending overturned syncline. Production from 1942-2013 ~17Mt, dominantly for industrial use, but inclusive of 740,000t for the construction industry.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: POOLES; SECTION 1504; SECTION 1508; SECTION 1509; SECTION 1510; SECTION 1511; SOUTH AUSTRALIA CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: tenure granted in 1844 on copper shows on limestone of the Sellick Hill Formation, and SE of the current Rapid Bay open cut. Workings of a prospecting nature, no production.
minor prospecting on an insignificant copper show.

galena rich lodes in host Fork Tree Limestone. Lodes with barite, calcite, gossan, galena, cerussite, smithsonite and copper ores. 500 tonnes of ore raised for 113 kg Ag, 122 tonne Pb, no Cu or Zn recovery reported.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Cerussite,  Galena,  Malachite,  Smithsonite,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz vein with Cu-Pb-Ag mineralisation. Worked from 1845-1909. Host rock was limestone and marble of the Fork Tree Limestone. Production figures probably in the order of >200 tonne, for recovery of copper and lead ore, no grade identified.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Cerussite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Galena,  Malachite,  Silver,  Smithsonite,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: low hill of goethitic rubble representing surface weathering of an Archean iron formation, dimensions 600 m long x 90 m wide. The aggregate thickness of BIF was estimated at 20-30 m in several bands.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GYPSUM WORX; ML 5218; ML 5270; ML 5704; ML 5812; ML 5813; PFEIFFERS; ROTTEN LAKE CALPERUM; ROTTEN LAKE MCKEE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gypsum of Yamba Formation in lake bed. Drilling identified resource of  >80% gypsum of ~450,000 tonnes, and 60-80% gypsum of 350,000 tonnes. Production from 1991-2015 was estimated at 125,500 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: JAEGER; MARSCHALL; ML 5122; ML 665; ML 730; ML 731; ML 732; ML 733; ML 734; NELDER; PROLETA; WARATAH GYPSUM
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Holocene gypsum, with production for use in agriculture, and of plasterboard rade, also minor in the manufacture of cement. Tonnage mined from 1973-2015 was estimated at 595,000 tonne.
gypsiferous dunes and playa lakes. 5 shallow auger holes helped determine resource seed gypsum of ~10Mt @ 70% CaSO4.2H2O, and not more than 5Mt of crystalline gypsum at 60% CaSO4.2H2O.
small, isolated hill of Archean iron formation with dimensions of 305 m long x 122 m wide.

large magnetic anomaly of strike length ~6 km. Field checking revealed the anomaly was coincident with a low rise of rubbly goethite, possibly overlying Archean iron formation, though this was not confirmed by drilling.

deposit of 6 main Permian coal seams, cumulative thickness 25m, occurring in the Phillipson Trough as 2 long, shallow NW-trending sub-basins in the S margin of the Arckaringa Basin. Cover depth 50-143m. Resource ~5000Mt.

shear zone with lens malachite, chalcocite mineralisation in host Archaeocyathic limestone of the Ajax Limestone. Later surface sampling of limonite-stained limestone identified willemite. Total production was estimated at 178 tonne copper ore.

A zone of intense surface hematitic alteration within outcropping Cambrian Ajax Limestone. Drilling identified an interval of willemite mineralisation of 6m @ 2.2%Zn, within a broader envelope of 30m @ 1.24%Zn in drillhole P139.

weak Cu-Pb mineralization in 120-150m zone in shale and dolomite at base Wonoka Formation, for a distance of ~700m. Best result 8m at 3675ppmCu, and 7190ppmPb. Disseminated malachite, chalcopyrite, minor galena was observed.
gossanous lode trend 060, dip 20SE, 4.6m wide, and traceable for a short distance. No production figure determined.
historic prospecting of cross-cutting quartz-siderite-calcite veins carrying thin rods to pods of galena on the northern part of expired mineral claim 5276.
reconnaissance drilling by Perilya Limited outlined a small resource of zinc mineralisation in host Pound Subgroup, no further details released (2008).

carbonate-quartz-sulphide veins in host diapiric breccia splay of Mount Stuart Fault. Sampling for best values 3ppmAu. Host with strong chlorite/phlogopite alteration. No production figures, though MR 10 reported fair amount ore at 15-25%Cu recovered.

rare torbernite occurs in a haematitic breccia body associated with pyrite and molybdenum in a granite breccia host. Indicated resource 795 000 ton at 1.9 lb U3O8/ton and 495 000 ton at 2.3 lb U3O8/ton.
COMMODITIES: Uranium,  Copper,  Rare Earths,  Uranium Oxide
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Chalcopyrite,  Malachite,  Molybdenite,  Rare Earths,  Uranium Minerals (Non Specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of poddy willemite Zn-(Pb-Ba) mineralisation in hematite-altered host Wilkawillina Limestone, and located on the Aroona Thrust. Indicated resource 26,000 tonne at 27.5%Zn, 0.6%Pb. Mineralisation traced >1.4km along strike..
location uncertain, located from mine symbol on 250K map, copper show in magnesite lode in host Wonoka Formation.
zone of widely spaced NS-orientated, narrow quartz veins occupying joints in host siltstones that trended EW. Ore minerals were galena and malachite.
several well defined, cross cutting, parallel lodes of galena in host slate and thin dolomite beds of the Myrtle Springs Formation. Lodes vary from a few cm to >60cm wide, and trend NS.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: geochemical sampling of a surface outcrop retuned a value of 6000 ppm Zn. It was tested in drillhole PDH AVD P1, which penetrated dolomitic siltstone, then blue and grey dolomite.  Best assay was 1000 ppm Zn from 30-35 feet.

rock chip Cu geochemical anomaly from banded calcite marble over 1200m distance. Subsequent drilling identified best assay of 6m @ 1.1% Cu from near surface primary sulphide zone in a shear, beneath a thin oxidized layer enriched to 5.5%Cu.

show of copper carbonate in vein quartz in 1873 in a shallow pit for no returns. Host rock was fractured diapiric dolomite in contact with dolerite intrusion, and adjacent to diapiir - Tapley Hii of metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation contact.

quartz vein to 3m over 150m. Host shale impregnated with malachite, and small mineralised veins. Tested in 3 holes for no mineralisation. Production figure incomplete. Samples from dumps best values 7.65%Cu, 0.72g/tAu, 6g/tAg, and 0.56%As.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Cuprite,  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small prospecting pit on a copper show. The 1 m wide lode was hosted by quartzite trending 169, dipping east. A sample assayed a trace of gold, silver, and 20% Cu. Location uncertai, lode reported as across Wallace Gully.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 7218; ML 7219; ML 7224; ML 7225; ML 7226; ML 7227; ML 7228; MOUNT PELE; MOUNT PELEE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: located 2.5 miles east of the Nichols Nob group of mines, and worked from 1905-1919. The workings consisted of two open cuts, a prospecting shaft 12 feet deep, and several shallow pits. The main open cut was 40 feet long by 20 feet wide.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: palaeozoic breccia and hydrothermal deposits within Proterozoic basement.

sampling identified 3 values >1%P in host limonitic siltstone and sandstone of the Bunkers Sandstone. Individual phosphatic bands to 5-10cm in width. Beds traced for~4.5 km east.Values probably represented secondary enrichment.
adjacent to Lubra (Peer Mahomets) Mine, and 1.7km S of Mochatoona Springs. Recorded production of 50 tons in 1905-6. Presumed copper lode in host metasediment of the Bunyeroo Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMALGAMATED CLAIMS; BLACKFELLOW CREEK; W.W. TERRELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: show of copper mineralisation in metasediment of the Bunyerro Formation. Incomplete production details were 19 tonne of ore raised, 6 tonne treated, with no yield figures provided.
mine symbol on 100K topographic map, copper show in host Balcanoona Formation.
show of copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Balcoona Formation. Production was recorded of 2.5 tonnes of ore yielding 200kg of copper smelt.
veins and nodules of copper carbonate in an EW-trending 10-12m wide belt of host decomposed sandstone and slate of the Curdimurka Subgroup. There were no production details.

location not certain, recorded as west of Nevada Mine, developed on a copper mineralised lode in 1905. Production figures were incomplete being ~60 tonne of ore, grades variable from 19-30% of hand picked ore in Wonoka Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOOLOOROO EAST; BOOLOOROO EXTENDED; BOOLOOROO SPRINGS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings ~800m east of and on eastern extension of shows of copper mineralisation on the Boolooroo Copper Mines, and in host diapiric metasediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup..
palaeozoic breccia and hydrothermal deposits in host Radium Creek Metamorphics.
area of surface manganese oxide nodules 3.3km NNW x 700m wide drill tested in 2 holes by Western Mining in 1980 to identify no significant depth extent of the manganese.
2 small excavations developed on copper mineralisation in a quartz lode within host metasediment of the Rawnsley Quartzite. Recorded production was small, in the order of a few tonnes only.

malachite in quartz vein/breccia over distance ~900m at contact of siltstone and dolomite. Massive, specular hematite and manganese coatings were commonly associated with the mineralisation. Minor disseminated chalcopyrite noted.

thin caps of manganese oxide on dolomite hills. Numerous excavations on sides and on top of the main hill from whence manganese oxide was gouged. Several hills nearby had a similar capping. It was doubtful if any payable ore was extracted.
barite lode in host metasediment of the Wilkawillina Limestone. Recorded production was 72 tonne in 1947.
mine developed pre 1899 on a lode in ABC Range Quartzite and worked on a show of lead and silver mineralisation. No further details established.
mineralisation in upper Blue Mine Conglomerate, structurally controlled, and confined to a narrow and discontinuous siltstone, and of limited extent.
copper show in host Curdimurka Subgroup, located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map, with 2nd mine 200m to N.

malachite and azurite as smears along joint and cleavage planes in tillite, at contact with overlying Tapley Hill Shale. Tested by auger and percussion drilling in the 1970s by Bridge Exploration to confirm widespread Cu grades 0.2 - 0.5%.
thick lode trending EW of several seams of copper ore in a quartzite, sandstone bed, with abundant vein quartz, and quartz-iron oxide veins.Host is of the Tapley Hill Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLACK HORSE; DOLOMITE; MOUNT SERLE COPPER; WHITE VIRGIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: extensive workings on qz-calcite veins in host Bunyerro Formation, and carrying argentiferous galena.
no details, located from mine symbol in unpublished State mineral occurrences 250K map series. Host mapped as metasediment of the Rawnsley Quartzite.
not located, recorded as 2.5km W of Constitution Hill, and 8.5km ESE of Mount Serle Homestead. Copper show in siliceous limestone in host slate. lode 1-1.3m wide trend W20N, steep dip N.
shallow pit on low rise of Pleistocene sheet, and rubbly calcrete, presumably developed by the local council for road base material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: FLINDERS RANGES DEVELOPMENT SYNDICATE; HALLS OPEN CUT; KYNOCH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mass of secondary goethitic ironstone carrying Cu mineralisation in host Cambrian Ajax Limestone worked for copper ore from 1899-1908, subsequently for ochre. Production ~28t Cu ore, 1,964t ochre from 1906-1952. Resource to 30m ~700,000t iron ore.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CUTAWAY; LEIGH CREEK COPPER; ML 5467; MOUNTAIN OF LIGHT; ROSSMANN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: well defined 4-5m wide lode of low Cu mineralisation in host Tapley Hill Formation. Production 543t for 17.32t copper metal @ 3%Cu. Resource estimate 2010 Phoenix Copper annual report of 110,000t @ 1% for 1100t contained copper.
no details, located from mine symbol on unpublished State mineral occurrences 250K map sheet for Copley. Located in host metasediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup on the 100K digital geology dataset.
no details, workings developed on copper-bearing lode in host metasediment of the Bunyeroo Formation. Located from mine symbol on plan nos FO0362, and 0376.
copper show on host Skillogalee Dolomite. Location uncertain, current site is surface scape for road material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DEPOT CREEK; DEPOT SPRING; STONES CLAIM

recovery of ~114 tonnes of ore. The workings were prospected in 1967 with copper mineralisation traced for a strike length of ~3.4 km. A parcel of 14 tonnes of ore was excavated. Host rock was metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation.
mine developed in 1889 on copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Rawnsley Quartzite. 4 tonnes were raised, no grades supplied.
veins related to Palaeozoic breccia and hydrothermal deposits within Proterozoic basement.

location uncertain. 20cm wide iron oxide vein carrying splashes of copper glance in host dolomitic limestone of the Rawnsley Quartzite. 2 small prospecting pits excavated prior to 1902, no recorded production.

quartz veins over 100 x 200m with siderite, hematite, goethite,trace bornite, chalcopyrite, chalcocite. Host shale of the Angepena Formation, with thin interbeds of dolomite and greywacke, dip 70 N. Diapiric structures occurred nearby to the east.
mine developed on a copper show in 1917. Host was metasediment of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Only production figure recorded was 1917, 20 tonne raised for 5 tonne treated, no grade information.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CORONATION WELL; ML 3375; ML 3376; ML 3377; ML 3378; RL 96
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 4 main magnesite beds along fold axis of a syncline, with bed 4 ave 8m thick. Drilling identified 25 beds averaging 2.2m thick, dip 15-45. Total resource ~215Mt @ ~40%MgO.
strong lode running down the face of the hill for ~275m, with 2 parallel subordinate lodes. Location from archival Mineral Resources plans database is SW of Wheal Austin.

percussion and diamond drilling identified discordant, lenticular weak copper mineralisation in host argillite of Boorloo Siltstone. Chalcocite and chalcopyrite were associated with disseminated pyrite, and metamorphic chlorite, biotite, and sericite.
show of copper mineralisation in metasediment of the Dome Sandstone. Incomplete production records were for 1907 19 tonnes mined, 13 tonnes treated of 8% copper ore, no yield indicated.
Cu mineralisation over an area of several km2, mainly associated with quartz-carbonate veins in sandy units of basal Tapley Hill Formation. No recorded production figures.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANOMALY B; FARINA PROJECT; OLD CALLANA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: iron oxide-quartz-calcite-siderite lode carrying copper mineralisation in tectonised metasediment of the Dome Sandstone. No production figures were recorded.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: discovered in 1904. Worked intermittently since. Host siliceous shale exposed in eroded tablelands. Occurred in veins and fissures, with opal shot through with gypsum, often cracking badly when exposed to the atmosphere.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CORONATION; DAY DREAM; TWO FRANKS; WHEAL VIRGIN; WHITE SWAN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu-Co-Ni, lesser As-W-Ba-Fe-Au mineralisation in siltstone of Callanna Group, & on margins of a diapir. Drilling in 2004 identified weak sediment-hosted sulphide mineralisation.

Tertiary siliceous, indurate clay to 10 m thick on 3 mesas, with estimated resources of 1,000,000 tonnes. Limited sampling suggested that the grade was variable, probable only isolated pockets of kaolin grade.

malachite or cuprite, with rare residual copper sulphide in quartz-siderite veins in dolomite. Discontinuous mineralisation over 460m. Drilling identified mineralisation associated with black pyritic shale and dolomitic arenite, best value 8m at 0.6%Cu.

several 80 acre claims for copper granted in 1890. Described as located 19km WSW of Marree, ie in the vicinity of The Dome, and adjacent to Callana Mine. Point location chosen is that of Utah drill hole WP 104 1km SE of The Dome.
3 diamond holes tested the Euraminna Igneous Complex for unconformity-related copper mineralisation. No mineralisation was encountered, with only hole WD033 reaching the target zone.
copper show in Myrtle Springs Formation, located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal mineral occurrences 250K map.

attenuated and contorted veins, with malachite, cuprite, chalcopyrite as disseminations in gritty bands in large blocks of dolomitic sediment in diapiric breccia  intruding Tapley Hill Formation. Best chip sampling assay 0.8% Cu.
copper show in Amberoona Formation, located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal mineral occurrences 250K map. Recorded production in 1901 of 114 tonne for 31.5 tonne treated at 18-24%Cu.
single diamond returned from gravel sample. Repeat samples for no confirmation. Location from mineral symbol #19 Curdimurka internal database 250K mineral occurrences map.

1of several adjacent copper shows in host Skillogalee Dolomite. Mining returns from 1901 of 19.3 tonne raised, and treated, grade 15%Cu.  Modern prospecting in late 1960s including some ground geophysics and geochemistry.
one of several adjacent copper shows in host Boorloo Siltstone prospected in 1917.
group of 3 workings along a NE-rending line of lode, and over a distance of ~150m. Host is Boorloo Siltstone with prospecting activity dating from 1917.
cross-cutting quartz-iron oxide veins in host deformed limestone, sandstone, and slate of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Alluvial gold was also reported. No production figure was determined.

quartz-siderite veins on drag folds in host slateof Callana Beds. Width of lode to 8m. Drilling down dip identified 80m at 0.2%Cu from 0-80m, the last 25m in sulphide zone. The system extended for at least 1.5 km along strike.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: J. BURNS; MC 10506; MC 6250; ROSES; ROSIE; S. VICARY; TOP MOUNT DIGGINGS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: one of several adjacent surface copper shows in host Dome Sandstone with production from 1906-07 of 182 tonne raised, for 41 tonne treated at 11%Cu for 4.1 tonne copper metal product.
copper show on Skillogalee Dolomite, with mineralisation worked in shaft in 1900-01 for 5 tonne treated @ 17%Cu. Location uncertain, recorded as 1.7km N of Warra Warra mine.
minor workings north of the West Willouran group of workings, and developed on a show of copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Top Mount Sandstone Beds.
surface copper show in Tapley Hill Formation, located from symbol Cu18 SE of 3 mile bore on Geological Survey internal mineral occurrences 250K map.
celestite as veins or coatings in host Oodnadatta Formation. Mineral Symbol 25 on Curdimurka MEIS 250K mineral occurrences map.
celestite as veins or coatings in host Oodnadatta Formation. Mineral Symbol 25 on Curdimurka MEIS 250K mineral occurrences map.
poddy vein celestite in host Mackunda Formation, known only from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal database 250K mineral occurrences map.
flat lying lacustrine dolomite deposit at S end of Lake Eyre North. See MINDEP record for Babbage Peninsula 1 for estimated resource.
region of flat lying Pliocene-Pleistocene lacustrine dolomite deposit S of Lake Eyre South. Resource estimated at 500Mt at 19%MgCO3.
poddy vein celestite in host Mackunda Formation, known only from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal database 250K mineral occurrences map.

Cu mineralisation in ferruginous quartz veins in host kaolinised sediment of the basal Burra Group. Production ~1250t ore @ >20%Cu.

geochem anomaly drilled to identify weak Cu mineralisation recorded in host silty to arenaceous argillites of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Mineralisation from WD 3 was 114-119m, 5m @ 0.22%Cu, 113-123m, 10m @ 0.16%Cu, 126-127m, 1m @ 0.4%Cu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DOUGLAS; DOUGLAS EAST; DOUGLAS GULLY; ML 4886
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu mineralisation in discordant quartz-carbonate veins in host sediment of the basal Burra Group. Drilling identified best value from hole WD17, 10m @ 0.5%Cu. Production 31.5t ore from 1894-1921.
anomalous Cu-(Mo-Zn-Au-Ag) values associated with NS-trending fault in host metasomatised, altered quartz-albite metasediment of the Willyama Supergroup.
copper stained slate of the Willyama Complex at 2-4%Cu worked in the early 1920s. In 1922 1 tonne of hand picked ore was recovered with grade of 12-14%.
brannerite associated with Mesporoterozoic biotite-feldspar migmatite and alaskite intruded by biotite adamellite.
brannerite occurs in association with black rutile on fractures in trondhjemite and occasionally in soda alaskite.
torbernite and gummite occur in phlogopite veins and on fractures in trondhjemitic-alaskitic rock.
presumed U mineralisation in veins in host Mesoproterozoic granitoid.
minor vein style Uranium mineralisation associated with IOCG deposit. Best assay result of 145ppm U between 113-116m in drillhole MPRC029.

Au mineralisation in horizontal gold-rich layer ~70m below surface at basal Tertiary-weathered Willyama Supergroup bedrock. Resource 1866kg or 60,000oz @ ~4g/t. Significant mineralisation in basement, best value 26m @ 15.4g/t Au.
gem variety of andalusite formed during regional metamorphism of host Willyama Complex host schist. Located from Curnamona 1:250,000 MEIS (Mineral Exploration Information Series) map only.
