near Lake Frome. Palygorskite clay is associated with dolomite beds of the Namba Formation. The palygorskite is associated with high levels of sand and silt. Elsewhere beds up to ~1 m thick occur with a purity of up to ~80%.

near Lake Frome. Palygorskite clay is associated with dolomite beds of the Namba Formation. The palygorskite is up to ~1 m thick with a purity of up to ~80%. Acceptable suspension and water absorbancy values.
veins with weak U mineralisation related to formation of Palaeozoic breccia and hydrothermal deposits within host Mesoproterozoic granitoids.
veins with weak U mineralisation related to formation of Palaeozoic breccia and hydrothermal deposits within host Mesoproterozoic granitoids.
davidite, minor torbernite and uranophane mineralisation in lodes within foliated mignatitic gneiss of the Willyama Complex. Grade 0.26-0.58% U3O8.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.J. WEBB; AUSTRALIAN SALT CO.; CROUCH A.E.; ML 124; ML 273; ML 279; ML 284; ML 682; PORT PARHAM SALT; WHITE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: several leases granted to the Australian Salt Company over coastal salt pans in the 1930s. Incomplete production record of 488t from 1931-40.
shell grit on a beach over a distance of ~5km, up to 550m wide, estimated resource of 1,248,000 tonnes (1953).
several roadside council pits on limestone (calcrete?) on section 229, Hundreds Grace, Dublin, and Port Gawler. Production from 1929-52 of 53,000 tons of road ballast and 2,500 ton building stone.
leases taken up prior to 1958 on coastal salt pan. Recorded production from 1931-35 of 70t. Leases granted to new aplicant in 1962.

pit on 3m thick beach deposit of unconsolidated shellgrit of the Holocene St Kilda Formation mined for use in glass manufacture. Production from 1909-1986 >900,000 tonne, plus ~8,000 tonne for filling from 2007-13.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; INKERMAN CC#1; PORT WAKEFIELD CC#1
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: reported as calcrete worked for road base material and road seal aggregate. The location is within an area mapped as Quaternary calcrete.
mine developed in 1884 on a quartz reef for gold. Host rock was metagranite of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. The mine was worked intermittently to 1938 for ~400oz (12.4kg) of bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite  Micaceous,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gold diggings on beds of Tertiary conglomerate of basin shape formed in hollows in the topography. Initial returns were good, petered out within a few months due to the patchy nature of gold distribution. No production details were determined.
large vein quartz blow in host Barossa Complex, with production from 1977-2013 of >360,000 tonne of road base material.
quarry developed on a quartzite deposit of the Belair Subgroup. Estimated production from 1977-90 was 54,000 tonne for road base material.

mine developed in 1858 on a quartz blow. It was reported that the reef was very rich, with free gold visible. No production details were recorded. One parcel of 10t yielded 272gm bullion gold at 27g/t.
diggings developed on gold-bearing alluvial flats bordering a creek. Hundreds of shallow shafts developed over 12 sections. Recorded production to 1888 of 20,000oz (622kg) gold.
alluvials on the Onkaparinga River worked in the 1870s for gold. Nuggets to 1/2oz were recovered.

mine developed in 1872-84 on a quartz reef carrying visible gold, host being metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Colluvial gold was found on the surrounding hill slopes. No production figures were determined.
mine developed in 1890 on a quartz vein in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Returns were poor and the show proved to be uneconomic.
mine inspected by H.Y.L. Brown in 1887, location doubtful, recorded as section 2882, Hundred Macclesfield. Reported shaft sunk on a silver lode, with alluvial gold workings in the vicinity.
recorded by Sir Douglas Mawson in 1926, being a small lode of barite on the side of a hill. Described as located east of the main Bull Creek road, and directly opposite the Bull Creek Church.
located on section 4268 on Verdun Goldfield, location uncertain. Worked a quartz lode in 1931 for 5.5 tonne for recovery of 1oz 14pennyweight 2 grains.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DODDS RUN; HALL; HOSKINS LEAD; SANDYS LEAD; YORKEYS LEAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: initial rich alluvial leaders running in all directions from the top of Chapel Hill. No production records apparent. Returns petered out, later worked in 1930s and 1950s for no payable gold.
Alluvial gold, within 3 months ~5000oz (155.5Kg) gold recovered including nuggets to 5oz (156gm).
quartz reef in the Chapmans Gully alluvial field. Host rock was metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figures determined.
diggings developed in 1854 on Tertiary gold-bearing conglomerate. No individual production figure recorded. Part of the regional Chapel Hill Diggings.
quarry worked from 1950-53 in quartzite of the Tarcowie Siltstone for estimated production of 90,000 tonne for road base material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; ECHUNGA CLAY; EML 4426
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary clay on weathered shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite, estimated production from 1978-79 was 14,600 tonne red plastic clay product. The quarry was rehabilitated in 1982.

eastern of 2 quarries of the same operator, this one a small quarry operating on section 926, Hundred Noarlunga for 508 tonne from 1952-54 on sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. Quarry not visible, location is on NW corner of the section.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host weathered slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Good, shotty gold was identified. A parcel of 10 tonne yielded 124.44gm at 12g/t.

silty alluvial clay on weathered clay of Belair Subgroup. Open cut to 6m developed in 1875, with some blasting required in 1927 on weathered bedrock. The kiln had a capacity of 40,000 bricks, product was a good, solid, dark red brick.
quarries on quartzite and clay deposits of host Emeroo Subgroup worked for many years for road making material.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figures were recorded.
abandoned council quarry of ~300m2 x 1-4m deep, and developed on limestone of the Tapanappa Formation for recorded production in 1927 of 508 tonne for road fill.
alluvial gold show worked in shallow shafts in 1873, and located 3.4km N of Echunga. Very poor returns documented.

alluvials worked periodically from 1852 to the 1930s, with good returns reported. There was some development on reef gold shows. Production figures were bulked into those for the larger Echunga Goldfield.
State government sponsored exploration in 1886 of Tertiary deep leads via shafts and drives. 5 shafts on sections 158, 159, and 5 on sections 337, 339, Hundred Kuitpo. No encouraging results.

quartz-iron oxide lodes in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. Worked periodically to 1898, with a minor revisiting for poor returns in 1930. Total production was >600oz (18.66kg), with a recorded 599t yielding 6221gm @ 10g/t.
small quarry developed in Woolshed Flat Shale in 1961 for recorded production of ~210 tonne.
quarry developed in 1927 on quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup for road making material.
quartz-pyrite-clay lode in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. No payable gold was recorded. 6oz gold recovered from the adjacent alluvials.
quarry developed on purple, weathered, fine grained sandstone of the Tapley Hill Formation for use in building industry in Mount Barker.

long abandoned quarry of ~1,000m2 x 1-5m deep developed on weathered, purple fine grained sandstone of the Tapley Hill Formation for local use in Mount Barker for building. Location uncertain, recorded as section 2909 Hundred Macclesfield.

location Hundred Macclesfield, section 2670. Small quarry on limestone of the Backstairs Passage Formation for road ballast and building stone, production 8433 tonne road ballast, 498 tonne building stone from 1937-49.

workings developed in 1852 for several km along a gully on Recent and Tertiary conglomerate beds. Some nuggets were recovered. Reworked periodically in the 1890s and 1930s for poor returns. No production figures were determined.

workings in 1872 on alluvials. Reports of 4-8oz production per week were recorded. It was reworked in 1882 for recovery of 3g/tAu. Many nuggets were found. Last major activity was in the 1890s. Total recorded production was >100oz (3.1kg).

3m wide, white quartz blow, with cavities, and abundant pyrite in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Poor returns and a large influx of water led to mine closure in the same year. It was reopened and deepened in 1895 for no payable returns.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host sandstone and shale of the Emeroo Subgroup. No payable gold was returned, and the venture closed the same year.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Worked again in 1895 for no payable gold.
shallow workings of a prospecting nature developed in 1895 on scattered quartz on crest of a hill of Woolshed Flat Shale for no payable gold.
clay vein carrying gold, and in host weathered slate of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Reworked in 1895 with a second shaft on a quartz-iron oxide lode. Near surface gold values petered out at depth.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small quartz-iron oxide leaders in metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. No production figure determined.

quartz-iron oxide-calcite carrying copper mineralisation in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded product from 1875-76 of 416.5 tonnes of copper matte. Samples of lode material taken by mines inspectors in 1913 were assayed at 8.5%Cu, 4g/tAu.
gold-bearing alluvials in a river bed. Reworked in 1862, and again in 1870, and 1894, when returns of a few gm/day were reported. Last reported activity was in 1931 for poor returns.
abandoned council quarries located on Sections 695, 693, and part Section 4234 on Hundred Kuitpo, and developed on quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup.
gold-bearing Tertiary conglomerate. Workings on 27 acres of section 393, located below National Dam. Recorded 746gm recovered in 2 weeks.

gold discovered in alluvials in 1858, with an immediate rush ensuing of >100 men. Good recovery reported of rough and rugged gold. Further periods of activity in 1896, and the 1930s. Reported recovery of several hundred ounces.
quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup worked for production from 1977-79 of ~1800 tonne for road base material. The quarry was rehabilitated in 1987.
quartz-iron oxide reef with argentiferous galena and cerrusite in host kaolinised slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production of >50t of ore @ 71%Pb, and 650g/tAg.
placer tin discovered in 1861. Follow-up mining on a lode in host Woolshed Flat Shale returned an assay of 17.5% Sn. Anomalous Pb and silver was also reported.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host weathered Emeroo Subgroup. The gold proved to be patchy, with production of 5oz (155.5gm) recorded at ~4.7g/tAu.

Recent to Tertiary conglomerate and gravel beds carrying patchy gold values. Reworked periodically to 1931 for recorded recovery of gold, garnet, tourmaline, amethyst and rutile from the gravels. No production figure was determined.
deposit of limestone of the Tapanappa Formation worked in 1950 for ballast and road base material for production of 2642 tonne.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figure was determined, a small grab sample assayed 168g/tAu.

deposit of quartzite of the Emeroo Subgroup, with quarry opened in 1960s to supply road metal for the construction of the South East freeway. Production from 1986-89 was ~6,000 tonne. Rehabilitation was completed in 2005.
shallow pit on sandstone of the Belair Subgroup, no recorded production.

quartz leaders in host kaolinised slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale first worked in the 1850s on the west side of Chapel Hill. No recorded production. It was reworked in 1953, and 1958, with a lengthening of the adit, with no payable gold recovered.

gold-bearing alluvial field declared over an area of 19 acres. 70 licences issued, with subsequent returns poor, best recovery of 1oz/ton, best nugget to 8dwt (12.4gm). By 1894 the field had been abandoned. No production figure determined.

lode of quartz-iron oxide pyrite in host quartzite and argillaceous sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. The ill-defined lode consisted of bunched veinlets. No recorded production figure, grades reported at from 5-15g/t.
quartz-iron oxide leaders in host kaolinised slate and sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production was >60oz (1866gm).

initial claims were for alluvial gold, with most claims returning payable quantities. A venture took out tenure over a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex in 1872, with a parcel of 4.42t yielding 147.7gm @ 33g/t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ALBERN SLATE; EML 4712; EML 5713; FAULKNER; KALLANA GRAZIERS; KANMANTOO FLAGSTONE; MC 4405; RL 132
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of metasiltstone of the Tapanappa Formation, with production from 1979-2011 of ~179,000 tonne of multiple products for the construction industry including dimension stone.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host weathered slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Good returns were recorded. Tailings reported to assay 19g/tAu. From the early phase recorded production was 59.4t for 1171gm bullion gold at 19.7g/tAu.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host weathered shale and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, worked in 1872 for good returns. The gold was very fine and proved difficult to recover. No production figure determined.
shallow workings near Sailors Gully on quartz reef in host Woolshed Flat Shale developed in 1904-05, no recorded production.

1m wide lodes of quartz-iron oxide-pyrite in host sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Several parcels raised, one of 20.3t yielded 77.8gm @ 3.8g/t. The workings were abandoned in the same year due to poor ground conditions.

quartz-iron oxide reef in weathered micaceous shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. A parcel of clayey lode material was dollied and panned for recovery of 41oz gold. Further work recovered gold for a total estimated production of >50oz.

alluvial workings first worked in 1870, with nuggets from 1-3oz recovered. Good early recoveries, later workings for poor recoveries, with last activity in 1897. Estimated total production was >150oz ( 4.67kg).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CHILDS AND SON BRICKWORKS; LITTLEHAMPTON BRICKWORKS; PM 82
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pits opened in 1885 on deeply weathered Precambrian bedrock. Incomplete production figures. Peak activity in early 1950s ~70,000 bricks requiring 200-300 tonnes clay/week. Recorded production 1956-2005 ~230,000t. Pit closed in 2005.
small quarry developed by local council in the 1920s and 30s for road making material on a sandstone of the Belair Subgroup.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale worked in 1870 and reworked in 1905, no recorded production.
soft pink sandstone worked in small open cuts in 1880 providing stone for the Macclesfield Institute. Reworked in the 1950s. No production figure determined.

3 quarries developed on marble of the Normanville Group. Fist worked in the 1850s, material was used to face Clarendon Dam, and as facing in the Strathalbyn Roman Catholic Church. Production 1650 tonne from 1952-59.
quarry developed in the late 1920s on quartzite of the ABC Range Quartzite. Estimated production from 1927-81 of >90,000 tonne of road base material, and general purpose aggregate.
deposit of weathered, fine grained, clayey sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone, worked for dimension stone from 1996-99 for production of 224t.
1.2m wide quartz lode in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup located in German Gully. A parcel of 6.1t yielded 93.3gm gold bullion at 15.3g/tAu.
2 short prospecting adits driven on lodes in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup for no returns.
several small quartz-iron oxide reefs in host weathered slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Some bismuth ore recovered. Total production ~200oz (6.22kg) gold.
prospecting workings developed in 1931 on a quartz reef in host Woolshed Flat Shale for no payable gold.
large, abandoned quarry of ~7,000m2 x 1-10m deep, and developed by the local council for road fill on weathered quartzite of the ABC Range Quartzite.
small, abandoned council quarry of ~800m2 x 1-4m deep, and developed for source of road fill from quartzite, shale, sandstone sequence of the Belair Subgroup.

quartz-iron oxide lode in host clayey, deeply weathered Woolshed Flat Shale. Good values were reported, and a parcel of 10 tonne was raised, but not processed. The nearby alluvials were worked, with reported good gold recovered.

gossanous quartz lodes carrying visible copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. In 1874 a second gossanous lode was worked for gold, with a small mine in operation in 1882. No production figure was determined.
quarry developed on marble bed of the Tapley Hill Formation, with a considerable amount of stone removed.
council quarries on sections 3912, 4101 Hundred Kuitpo, developed on limestone of the Burra Group from 1947-52 for production of 5921 tonne.
not located, recorded as on Section 4452 Hundred Macclesfield, historic council quarry developed on sandstone unit of the Belair Subgroup for road fill in the early 1900s.
small amount of quartzite of the Belair Subgroup removed for road making.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EMERALD; MOUNT BARKER SUMMIT; PM 193; RAYNER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry developed on 30m wide quartzite bed of the ABC Range Quartzite. By 1972 excavated to 35m. Recorded production from 1957-72 was 255,694t of crushed and screen quartzite product, and 24,732t of quarry sand.

weathered, white, fine grained sandstone, including a 2m thick sandstone of purple colour, and of the Tarcowie Siltstone. The material was used for building stone in Mount barker and also in Adelaide.

quartz reef in host sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. The mine was reopened in 1936. An open cut was developed on a quartz lode showing visible gold, and 3oz gold were recovered. No total production figure was determined.

not located accurately. Recorded as on slope of Mount Venture and ~2.5km E of Verdun on section 4107. Discontinuous NS-trending quartz-iron oxide vein in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. A sample of ore assayed 77g/tAu.

gold-bearing alluvium worked from 1870, again in 1877. Reworked again in the early 1880s, late 1890s, and sluiced from 1906-11. Estimated production to 1908 was 4,000oz (124.4kg). In 1908 sluicing over an area of 22,575m2 yielded 2,494.5gm gold.
quartz lode in Belair Subgroup. No recorded production. The shaft was deepened in 1935, and a small parcel of a few tonnes of ore sent to the battery for processing, no results have been found.
quartzite bed of the Backstairs Passage Formation in 1960 for use by the local council in road making. Resources in 1960 estimated at 38,230m3. It is rehabilitated and the area now a housing estate.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BALHANNAH SURPRISE; LE HUNTE; LITTLE SWALLOW
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: well defined quartz reef in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production from 1897-1906 of 192.3t for yield of 4407.3gm gold bullion @ 23g/t.

Tertiary conglomerate bed worked for reported grades 12-14oz/tonne. In 1859 the first discoveries of diamonds were recorded. Work resumed in the 1930s and 40s at a small scale for poor returns. No production figure was determined.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lodes in host blue slate and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, and located adjacent to the Non Pareil and Echunga Mines. Worked in 1882 for poor results, with work ceasing when funds ran out.

well defined lode in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup at the head of Long Gully. Leaders of up to 30cm width carried good visible gold. Further development however gave poor returns and the venture wound up in the same year.
quartz-iron oxide leaders in host Woolshed Flat Shale, and on the northern extension of the King Mine lode. No gold values returned and the venture wound up the same year.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host mica schist & quartzite of Belair Subgroup. Production to 1899 ~11,177t @ 18.7g/t for ~210Kg gold. Reworked until 1935, with production from 1930-35 of 41.3t for yield of 100.3gm bullion gold at 2.4g/t.

gold-bearing alluvium north of Diamond Gully workings. Reports of a good showing of gold, however workings were soon abandoned after an influx of water, and a shortage of labour. No production figure determined.

pale coloured marble of the Normanville Group in 1906. Building stone won from this quarry was used in many major buildings in the Adelaide city district. Incomplete production records only of 1194t mined from 1955-66.
workings developed in early 1900s on blue, foliated marble of the Fork Tree Limestone.
workings on cream-grey, pyritic, ""seawave"" marble of the Fork Tree Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CHAPEL HILL; NATIONAL GOLD; OLD ECHUNGA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: rush on alluvial gold in 1854. Nuggets to 1/4-1/2 oz were recovered. A second rush occurred in 1857 with further shaft sinking, with some diamonds recovered. From 1866-69 an extensive operation was established. No production figure was determined.
quartzite of the Belair Subgroup worked in the early 1900s for road base material. Production records incomplete for 380m3 in 1926. Resource estimated at 23,000m3 in 1963 above the 380m level.
gold-bearing alluvium, with a small rush ensuing, with many shafts excavated for poor returns. Reworked briefly in 1870, and 1892 also for poor returns.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host weathered slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded production of 81.75oz or 2543gm of bullion gold from 1868-69, no tonnage determined.

gold-bearing alluvium, with mine extending onto quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host mica schist and sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Total production 2146gm gold, with 3 parcels of reef ore for 41 tonne yielding 355gm at 8.5g/tAu.
Bertrams Reef in host sandstone, quartzite and weathered slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded production of 32.5 tonne for an estimated 256gm gold at 8g/tAu.

abandoned quarry of ~12,000m2 x 1-8m deep on narrow stratigraphic unit of weathered, white, kaolinitic quartzite of the Belair Subgroup, no production details known. Central of 3 quarries developed on the same strike ridge over a distance of 1.7km.

abandoned quarry of ~15,000m2 x 1-3m deep on narrow stratigraphic unit of weathered, white, kaolinitic quartzite of the Belair Subgroup, no production details known. Northern of 3 quarries developed on the same strike ridge over a distance of 1.7km.
sandstone and quartzite of the Belair Subgroup, with production from 1988-2013 of ~47,000 tonne of road base material.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. A single shaft with crosscut was excavated to 18m depth, no recorded production figure.
quartz-pyrite leaders in host Woolshed Flat Shale. Minor prospecting also of alluvials. Results were poor.
quartz leaders in host Emeroo Subgroup. Several shafts excavated on material recovering gold from each leader, but high influx of water brought work to an end. No production figure determined.
2.1m wide quartz reef carrying a little gold. Host rock was metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figure was determined.
alluvial gold show, with initial rush in the 1870s reporting rich finds including nuggets. Activity continued intermittently to the late 1930s. No production figure determined.
many shallow adits developed on alluvial gold show in 1872. No production figure determined.
slate quarry 4km SW of Kanmantoo, now an industrial site.
small production from shallow pits developed on sandstone of the Tapanappa Formation for use as building stone.
quartz-iron oxide leaders in host micaceous schist of the Burra Group. Worked in shallow shafts from 1932-35 for recovery of 30-40oz (933-1244gm) gold.

locations uncertain, historic small quarries located on Section 4479, Hundred Macclesfield, and developed in the early 1900s on quartzite unit within the Belair Subgroup for road fill. Now the site of a residence.

opened in the 1860s, on deeply weathered, kaolinitic, shale of the Emeroo Subgroup, and used for brick making.  Incomplete production records were for ~27,000 tonne from 1961-2012. The pit has been progressively rehabilitated.
quartz leader in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. Poor gold returns and high influx of water brought activity to an end in 1883.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GS 602; GS 605; SOUTH QUEEN; SOUTH QUEEN GOLD MINING CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite worked in 1882 for poor returns. Activity ceased due to a high influx of water.
1m wide quartz lode in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup prospected in 1873 for poor returns.
2 lines of lode of quartz-iron oxide-pyrite in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup were worked for recovery of minor gold, but the mine was abandoned within the year.
gold-bearing alluvium, with initial  recovery of a quantity of nuggets. A rush ensued, but results proved to be poor. Minor prospecting of quartz reefs proved unsuccessful.
Tertiary limestone deposits worked by the local council for recorded production from 1925-52 of 35,546t (cumulative total from several pits), and 2032t of limestone for use as building stone.
quartz leaders prospected for gold for poor returns, host rock being of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figure determined.
sandstone of the Belair Subgroup, with production from 1977-2013 of >60,000 tonne for road base material, and concrete aggregate.

central of 3 quarries developed on a narrow unit of quartzite to 18m wide, and of the Belair Subgroup. The quarries were worked in the 1920s and again in 1972. Combined production from 2 quarries was 3800m3, and in 1972 1353 tonne.
gold-bearing alluvium on section 372, Hundred of Kuitpo, reworked in 1926, no production figure determined.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Mitcham Quartzite, and reported to carry gold with anomalous Ni-As, no production figure determined.
lode of quartz-iron oxide in host mica scist of the Barossa Complex. Discovered in 1893, with bursts of activity up to 1936. No production figure determined.
quartz reef in host sandstone and slate of the Emeroo Subgroup first worked in 1872, and again in several separate ventures until 1898. No production figure determined.
quartz reef in host sandstone and slate of the Emeroo Subgroup first worked in 1872, and again in several separate ventures until 1898. No production figure determined.
quartz veins in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Only weak gold returned. No production records apparent.

workings of 4 shafts and an adit developed on series of quartz lodes returning good gold values. Some silver and bismuth mineralisation encountered. Host was slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production records.
quartz blow returning excellent gold values initially. Host was metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale, no production records apparent.

quartz reef in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. The adit did not penetrate the lode, eventually being terminated in hard granite. The shaft returned good values for gold. A parcel of 5 tonnes yielded 62gm bullion gold at 12.4g/tAu.
exceptionally rich Au-Bi mineralised quartz reef in host metasediment of the Burra Group. Production from 1893-1905 ~2500oz or 77.8Kg bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Bismuthinite,  Carbonate,  Feldspar,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Kaolinite,  Magnetite,  Manganese Oxide,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-bismuth-iron oxide reefs in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Whilst initially some good patches of gold-bearing lode were found, the mine soon closed when returns were barren of gold.

well developed quartz reef carrying a good showing of auriferous pyrite, worked from 1888-89. Hanging wall of sandstone, footwall slate, both of the Stonyfell Quartzite. No production records apparent.
alluvial deposits first worked in 1852, again in the 1880s and 1930s, no production figures apparent.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: J.S. WATTS AND SONS; PM 37; WATTS BRICKWORKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: one of the first clay-for-brickmaking pits developed, opening in 1863. Incomplete production records of 21,750 tonne, the bulk from 1925-49, 1043 tonne in 1972. Production 1973-83, ~4050 tonne, with rehabilitation completed in 1988.
reef gold in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. It was worked from 1893-1906, and again in the 1930s. Recorded production was 13.5 tonnes for 148.3gm gold at 11g/tAu
diggings developed on alluvials in 1872. Grades of 1/2 - 1 oz/ton were reported, though no production figure was determined.

gold-bearing alluvium formed in a basin-shaped hollow. Excellent recoveries of gold were reported, with several tonnes of gold reported to have been recovered by 1853, after which time the field was largely abandoned.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PM 194; WISTOW 1; WISTOW 3; WISTOW BLUESTONE; WISTOW STONE AND SLATE; WISTOW STONEWORKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: schist/metasiltstone quarried for paving and walling stone. The quarry developed in host metasiltstone of the Tapanappa Formation of the Kanmantoo Group. Used for walling/paving stone, production from 1977-2009 ~62,000 tonne.

quarry on marble of the Tarcowie Siltstone worked from early 1900s. Beds included a 6m wide bed of white-cream marble, and soft pink marble, limestone and marl. Only recored production is for 1927 of 3556t.
historic pit of ~3,000m2 x 3-4m deep, and developed on Holocene sand. Quarry is located within 100m of a residence.
historic shallow council pit of >50,000m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on surface Pleistocene calcrete for road fill..
abandoned council pit of ~1,500m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on calcreted limestone of the Murray Group overlying metasediment of the Cambrian Balquhidder Formation.
2 adjacent, and abandoned shallow quarries of total <20,000m2 x 1-3m deep, on weathered, white limestone of the Murray Group, and worked for road fill by the local council over many years.

small, abandoned council pits for total area ~1,500m2 x 1-3m deep on a low rise of Tertiary Blanchetown Clay, and worked for road fill. The area borders the outlet of the Murray River into Lake Alexandrina on its eastern side.
clay deposit formed by deep weathering of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Production from 1956-59 was recorded at 319 tonne, and from 1973-76 ~25,320 tonne. The pit was rehabilitated in 1981.
part of the Hack's Bridge Diggings with considerable prospecting carried out on a hillside for alluvial gold in 1918 for poor returns.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 457; ML 462; W.R. WILLIAMS; WATKINS SALT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mining leases on a salt lake taken out in the 1940s. Recorded production from 1940-48 of 518 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ARCADIAN BRICKWORKS; PM 183; PORT ELLIOT BRICKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: developed on deposit of Quaternary sedimentary clay in 1921. Last recorded production in 1980 for incomplete figures indicating >9,000 tonne recovered.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ARCADIAN BRICKWORKS; D.J. SAMELS; MARTINS BRICKWORKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of alluvial clay with a long history of sporadic production from 1921 to the 1970s. No complete production figures available. Reportedly the clay was excellent for brick making. Now rehabilitated, and adjacent to a residence.

quarry developed in the 1920s on limestone of the Balquidder Formation. Recorded production of 1428 tonne from 1925-26. It is now a large holding dam for water supply to the McCracken Country Golf Club, Victor Harbour.
quarry developed in 1878, and 1882 on N side of the island for granite material for use in the nearby breakwater.
pink quartzite of the Middleton Sandstone quarried in the 1920s to 1930s.
sand of the Cape Jervis Formation, with production from 1981-2002 of ~25,300 tonne of garden sand. The pit is being progressively rehabilitated.
sand of the Cape Jervis Formation, with production from 1998-2013 of ~30,000 tonne of packing sand. The pit is being progressively rehabilitated.
Quaternary aeolian sand, with production from 1979-2013 of ~130,000 tonne building and garden sand.

Quaternary sand and calcrete, with production from 1978-2013 of ~210,000 tonne of multiple sand, calcrete, limestone end products for use in the construction industry. The operation is being progressively rehabilitated.
deposit of Cambrian metasiltstone of the Balquhidder Formation, and for production of material for multiple end uses in the construction industry. Production from 1967-2011 was >3.7 million tonne.

alternating beds of mica schist and quartz-mica schist of the Balquidder Formation. Material considered for use as ballast in barrage construction. Current area of light industry. Recorded production in 1939 of 3048t.
small quarry on porphyritic granite of the Encounter Bay Granite. It provided building stone for use in the base course of Parliament House, Adelaide.

mine located in Hundred Neales 2km SE of Eudunda was mined for copper in 1874. An assay on the ore gave 14.5% copper. A 15 metre shaft was sunk with a lode of copper 0.6 metre wide cut carrying rich ore.

road side quarry ~3,500m2 x 1-4m deep developed by the local council for road ballast material. Production from quarries on 7 sections on Hundred Julia Creek from 1926-31 of 11,180 tons limestone, 9404 tons slate, Hundred Eudunda 9404 ton.
large swamp area with underlying gypsum layer of the Holocene Le Hunte Member. Mining Leases granted in the late 1930s, with recorded production from 1938-42 of 2,040 tonne.

located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal mineral occurrences 250K map. Copper show in host Terrapinna granite. Workings adjacent to the Pinnacles group of workings and developed on a copper show.
no details, known only from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal database 250K mineral occurrences map.
location not well established, recorded as 800m S of Darleys. Shallow pit developed on a quartz lode trending EW and carrying fine gold. Host was Glenloth Granite. No production records apparent.
ML 196 of 640 acres just S of the railway granted in 1918, no production records.

location uncertain, possibly mine N of Royal Tiger. 30cm wide quartz vein as shear infill, trend NW, dip NE in host sericite-altered Glenloth Granite. Reported as worked in open cut to ~4m depth for little returns.
no details determined, presumably a claim on a quartz lode in host Glenloth Granite. Location uncertain, appears on satellite imagery as an area of vein quartz float.
historic clay pit now a car parking area.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BENNETTS; EML 4684; TUREAN EXCAVATORS PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: short WNW-trending Quaternary sand dune, with production from 1979-88 of ~59,700 tonne garden sand. It was rehabilitated in 1989.
historic clay pit now residential.
historic clay pit now residential. It was developed in 1856, and by 1908 was a pit to 3.7m deep from which an estimated 350,000 bricks had been manufactured.
shallow pits on ~2m thick alluvial sand deposit worked on sections 5026-29 from 1958-64. recorded production was ~6,000t.
shell grit of the Saint Kilda Formation developed on an alluvial plain. Worked from open pits from 1929 for production of 122t, and also in the 1930s.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; EML 5264; REEVES PLAINS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Quaternary WNW-trending dunal sand and adjacent sand spread worked over a distance of ~600m for production from 1986-87 ~66,000 tonne of loam and garden sand. The pit was rehabilitated in 1987.
4m deep pit excavated on sand and loam of the Pooraka Formation in 1964. Reworked, and rehabilitated for construction of Northern Expressway.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A. WEAVER; HALLETT BRICK IND; W. GOODGER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: section 1, Hundred Mudla Wirra, and near Willaston. Locally significant clay pit active for over 100 years from 1866. No complete production records. Production from 1947-60 of 45,080 tonne.
Quaternary aeolian sand deposit, with production from 1997-99 of ~475 tonne garden sand. Rehabilitation was completed in 2006.

2 shallow pits developed on separate, and adjacent NW-trending longitudinal dunes of Quaternary aeolian sand. Estimated production of sand products from 1977-2009 was 344,000 tonne mainly garden sand.

workings on the western half of a prominent 1.7km long WNW-trending longitudinal dune of Quaternary sand. Production from 1978-83 from PM 51 was ~36,400 tonne mainly foundry sand. It was rehabilitated in 1984.
WNW-trending longitudinal Quaternary aeolian sand deposit worked from 1987-89 for ~138,500 tonne filling sand, with rehabilitation completed in 1995.
quarry on arkosic quartzite bed prior to 1958, and of the Stonyfell Quartzite for use as road base material. Estimated resource of quartzite >sandstone of 200,000 tonne.

very small abandoned council quarry of <100m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered quartzite bed of the Stonyfell Quartzite, ~33m wide, trending NS, dip ~30 E. Resource estmate 220,000m3 (290,000 cubic yards), or >500,000 tonne.
shell grit of the Saint Kilda Formation developed on an alluvial plain. Worked from open pits from 1926-28 for production of 193t.
shell grit of the Saint Kilda Formation developed on an alluvial plain. Worked from open pits from 1930-32 for production of 622t.
location uncertain, described as sections 56, 57, Hundred Mudla Wirra, excavation of 197 ton in 1948 of Tertiary limestone.
48 acre lease on salt pan granted in 1937.

Pleistocene and Tertiary shale, calcrete and sand mainly for road base material from 1932-72. Recorded production was 25.4t of shale in 1932, 87,272t of calcrete from 1927-52, and in 1972 406t of limestone and 2817t of sand.
small, abandoned roadside council pit located on a declared road reserve on Section 791, Hundred Mudla Wirra.  Located on the Tertiary Hindmarsh Clay, and Pleistocene calcrete.
longitudinal dune of Quaternary aeolian sand worked from 1981-2013 for production of ~74,000 tonne of garden sand.
shell grit of the Saint Kilda Formation developed on an alluvial plain. Worked from 1930-52 for production of 18,606 tonne for use in agriculture.
show of malachite discovered in 1863, no payable ore recovered.

deposit of quartzite/sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite worked for multiple products for use in the construction industry. Production from 1977-2013 ~8.4 million tonne, with recent production rate at <100,000 tpa.
WNW-trending Quaternary longitudinal sand dune, with production for 1987-1989 of ~25,000 tonne garden sand, then rehabilitated in 1990.
operations ceased in 1992 and it is being filled with rubbish by Northern Adelaide Waste Management Authority. Production from 1977-92 was estimated at 910,000 tonnes from the Stonyfell Quartzite.
Stonyfell Quartzite, production 1955-63 531,000 tonne for road base material, ceased operation in 1963, reopened briefly in mid 1970's by Quarry Industries. .
location uncertain, reported as near Mundoo Barrage. Quarry returns for 21,134 tonne from 1938-39.
shallow pit on calcrete worked in the 1920s. Recorded production in 1924 of 325t for road making, and 284t for building industry. Now park area.
scattered shallow pits on 1.2m thick calcrete for use in road making.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUBURN BLUESTONE; B.I. MELLOR; EML 5168; EML 5778; ZWIERSON-SCOTT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: worked for most of last century mainly for building stone. Details of production recorded were 272 tonnes from 1926-49, ~330 tonnes from 1992-99. Also ~400 tonne for ballast from 1926-49. Operations ceased in 1999.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Emeroo Subgroup worked initially for Ag-Pb, then Au. No production figures were determined.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Kaolinite,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry developed on Bungaree Quartzite by the local council, reopened in 1960 for road base material.
prospecting shaft sunk on copper mineralisation detected during sinking of a well near the Rhynie Garage in 1866.

cream to white freestone (sandstone) of the Bungaree Quartzite, and said to have been weakly weathered, hardening on exposure. Several thousand cubic yards were excavated though exact production figures were not recorded.
clay deposit on the banks of Light River, on section 332, Hundred Alma in the 1920s. Riverbank clay resource ~500m to S of 92,000 tonne.

abandoned, and rehabilitated small council pit on Tertiary conglomerate and calcrete on sections 485, Hundred Light. Reported as 0.5 to 1m of kunkar overlying partially cemented, coarse Tertiary conglomerate.

located on weathered marble of the Skilogalee Dolomite. Recorded production from individual pits in 7 sections not recorded, estimated 25,000 cubic metres from all pits in the Hundred of Alma is recorded against this MINDEP record only.

abandoned council quarry of ~20,000m2 x 1-5m deep, and developed on weathered, white to pale grey marble of the Skilogalee Dolomite. The pit has been partly rehabilitated. Geology described as thin mantle of calcrete  over marble.

abandoned council quarry of >5,000m2 x 1-4m deep, and developed on weathered marble of the Skilogalee Dolomite. Strike is north, dip variable east. Rippable marble appears to be confined to the top 30cm.
located on weathered marble of the Skilogalee Dolomite. Recorded production from individual pits in 7 sections not recorded, estimated 25,000m3 from all pits in the Hundred of Alma.

abandoned quarry of >5,000m2 x 1-6m deep on 45m wide unit of grey to white, friable talcose marble of the Lower Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite.Marble appears to be unsatisfactory for use as road fill.

abandoned council pits on Section 40, Hundred Light, and developed on interbedded shale and sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation. The material is rippable to 1.2m. has moderate strength, with a considerable proportion of oversize recovered.
dunal shell grit of the Saint Kilda Formation. Recorded production from open pits from 1946-52 of 190t.
lease on salt pan, with recorded production of 311t from 1934-48.
prospecting pits on dunal shall grit deposits prospected in 1955, with subsequent granting of 2 tenements, no recorded production.

slate deposit of Saddleworh Formation. Initial product road base material for main north road. Also use for building stone. The slate dipped 30E, and there was prominent vertical jointing. Production in 1927 was 7645 m3.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BELVIDERE CC#1; BELVIDERE CC#2; PM 111; TRANSPORT SA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of marble of the Cambrian Angaston Marble Formation for dimension stone. Vertical bed of marble to 85m wide, medium to coarse grained, colour white, grey, and streaky pink. Production from 1978-2013 ~80,000t.
phosphate rock in host slates. Average grade 10%P2O5. Production commenced in 1908. It was reworked between 1919 and 1925 with production figures recorded for the years 1920-1922 of 2264 tonnes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EAST KAPUNDA; SIR JENKIN COLES PROPERTY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: fault-controlled quartz lodes with azurite, malachite, red copper oxide, black copper ore and ironstone in host bleached slate of Tapley Hill Formation. 70-80 tonnes ore raised per month. Rich lodes cut. In 1876 a great influx of water forced mine closure.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.J. BARTSCH PTY LTD; ERINGA PARK SANDSTONE; KAPUNDA SANDSTONE; PM 139
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: freestone quarry on sandstone of the Appila Tillite. Production of 201 tonne of sandstone was recorded.
quartz reef in host slate of the Neoproterozoic Yudnamutana Subgroup. Recorded production of 52 gm gold from 10 tonnes ore at 5.2g/tAu. Later crushings gave poor returns.

gossanous quartz blow in host slate of the Wilpena Group. It was reworked in 1904-05 for returns of rich ore, then again in 1931-32 for unpayable returns. Production 7.6 tonne for 668 gm in 2 parcels, combined grade of 88g/tAu.

1 of several pits developed on grey clayey slate of the Saddleworth Formation, each one developed on a small anticline. This pit located on section 294, Hundred Gilbert. They were worked in the 1920s.
lode of black and grey copper ores, malachite, azurite, quartz in host kaolinised clay slate. Production is estimated at over 1000 tonnes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOJEN NOMINEES; MATTHEWS; PM 180; TARLEE; V.P. KEANE LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: major production ceased 1990. Quartzite of the Mintaro Shale. Production records from 1977-1998 ~69,000 tonnes, prior >30,000 tonnes, for total production >100,000 tonnes. Old dumps were rehabilitated.
quartzite bed 1.8m thick worked to supply local building stone. Deemed unsatisfactory for use in Adelaide buildings, useful supply of road metal.
council quarry developed on shale of the Tapley Hill Formation for road ballast for road works. Seasonal production 1929--49 totalling 4698 tonne. There is a residence within 100m of the quarry.
lode of quartz, chalcocite, black oxide, malachite in host kaolinised clay slate. 698 tonnes of ore were removed from the mine from the period 1849 to 1900.
deposit of limonite associated with phosphate rock in host micaceous slate. Production of order 100s tonnes. In the centre of the deposit very large and extensive caves were discovered.

series of 29+ en-echelon, sub-parallel lodes on W-flank of domal fold in host kaolinised siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1844-1877 69,000t ore yielded 13,700t copper metal product. Resource (1993) ~3.7Mt @ 1.2%Cu.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Bornite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Covellite,  Cuprite,  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay pit developed for supply of material to Krieg Brickworks. Mining commenced in the 1950s. Recorded production from EML 2968 from deposit of Tertiary clay from 1956-61 was estimated at 8700 tonne.
section 119, Hundred Nuriootpa, large open cut excavated for clay for brickmaking, also resource of silica sand identified, estimate in 1951 of 30,500 tonne.
small clay pit developed on Tertiary white clay formed on deeply weathered Wilyerpa Formation for supply of brick making material to Krieg Brickworks. Recorded production of 665 tonne in 1972.

brick making plant active from the 1870s, with supplies opened on new sections in the 1950s. By 1956 production had peaked at 2.5 million bricks per annum. Recorded production from 1956-60 was ~52,000 tonne clay. Total production not determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DAVEYSTON CRUSHING SITE; DISTRICT COUNCIL; LEAKES; MC 2952
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarries on quartzite of the Undalya Quartzite, worked in 1934 for recorded production of 45t building stone, then from 1942-55 of 6945t road base material & RSA. Worked to 1972 for road base material,

kaolinised siltstone and mudstones. Open cuts on shale originally part of Kapunda Mine, later worked by council for road material.  Production for the quarry for the period 1938-1949 was recorded as 643 tonnes.
marble, limestone, slate with phosphate-limonite within and as capping. Average grade 30-35% CaP2O5. Production ~300 tonnes phosphate rock. Discovered in 1904, only worked for a short time.

quarry developed from 1933-39 on a weathered shale of the Saddleworth Formation in a series of small quarries and one main quarry on sections 215/216, Hundred Gilbert. Overall production from all quarries was 1213 tonne of shale.

quarry developed on shale and slate of the Saddleworth Formation in the 1920s, reworked from 1933-41 for recorded production of 478 tonne building stone and 8857 tonne of kunkar for road base material.

host slate, schist and steeply dipping quartzite of ABC Range Quartzite. Average grade of 19.63% CaP2O5. Worked for a short time with a small tonnage produced. Prospects for further deposits not promising.
rubble quarry developed on quartzite of the Mintaro Shale in the 1930s.

worked for road metal in the 1860s, stone for monuments and building work in 1970s. In 1888 for a 3 year period marble supplied to B.H.P. and Dry Creek for flux. Total production was not recorded but many thousands of tonnes.
Recorded as on sections 1400, 1429 adjoining Kapunda Mine to the NE. 2 prospecting shafts excavated in 1846 for no returns.
council quarry developed on shale of the Saddleworth Formation for use as road base material.
abandoned council pit of >5,000m2 x 1-4m deep, located on Section 361, Hundred Gilbert, and developed on weathered, green-brown shale and claystone of the Bethel Shale Member for use as road fill.
council quarry developed on shale of the Saddleworth Formation for use as road base material.
shallow council rubble pit developed on a sequence of grey shale, partly calcareous to dolomitic overlying pale grey phyllite of the Saddleworth Formation, and for use as road base material.

small quarry on basal grits of a sandstone unit of the Tarcowie Siltstone. First worked in the 1890s for building freestone, and active in 1948, with 2 circular saws in operation. resource estimate 143,000t.
phosphate rock in host marble and slate. Average grade 57.23% Ca3P2O5. Production to end 1905 <300 tonnes, operated periodically to 1979.

quarry developed on consolidated aeolinite, with resource estimate in 1954 of >450,000 tonne.
limestone deposit within the Parilla Sand for production of 1007 tonne from 1929-40.
leases granted in 1933 for 90 acre area on a slat pan. Recorded production from 1933-44 of 123t.
quarry developed on limestone of the Tertiary Gambier Limestone. Production from 1924-48 of ~40,000t for use in road making, as building stone, and 955t in the manufacture of lime.
quarry on Bridgewater Formation limestone, was used as a motor cycle track and now rehabilitated.

low-rank lignite, 1 seam in 2 lobes, maximum thickness 12m, ~5km wide by 27km long, 30-80m overburden.depth to  top lignite 40-75m. Recent recalculated JORC compliant resource by Hybrid Energy Australia based on 1980s drilling of 578Mt.
council pit on limestone of the Semaphore Sand Member, and on section 508 Hundred Lacepede, just SW of Kingston. Quarry returns for 1925-52 of 38,686 tonne.

deposit of rhyolite of the Ordovician Mount Monster Porphyry for road seal aggregate and ballast. Production from 1955-76 of 548,000t. Estimated potential for large resources. Engineering testing identified high quality as road aggregate.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: D.G. AND V.A. PITT; EML 3394; EML 3395
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sand of the Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation, with production of ~103,600 tonne concrete and garden sand product from 1973-2008. Likely enormous resources available.
produced road aggregate from rhyolite, no production records were apparent.
section 509, Hundred Lacepede, location now rehabilitated. Limestone quarried, no production figure determined.
abandoned pit of <15,000m2 x 1-3m deep opened by SA railways on limestone of the Padthaway Formation for rail ballast.
quarry on sandstone of the Bridgewater Formation for use as building stone. Recorded production of 409t in 1956. Large resources are available.

pit opened in 1955 on clay to 3-4m thick of Molineaux Sand. Mottled, sandy clay in the manufacture of a poor quality brick. The clay extends over a wide area. Testwork confirmed their unsuitability for brickmaking.
quarry developed in Ordovician Taratap Granite mainly for road aggregate.
quarry developed in Ordovician Taratap Granite mainly for road aggregate.
quarry developed in Ordovician Taratap Granite mainly for road aggregate.

barite lode to 3.6m wide, ~190m long worked to a depth of 85m. Host slate of Umberatana Group. Production 1st grade barite ~32,500 tonnes from 1918-1947, and 270 tonnes from 1948-52. Diamond drilled in 1941-42. Closed 1952.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CONCRETE INDUSTRIES; DYSON SAND; EML 5767; EML 5964; MASLIN BEACH EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRY ZONE; MONIER BESSER SAND; PM 20; PM 232; PM 43; ROCLA QUARRY PRODUCTS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit on Tertiary North Maslin Sand to 24m depth & overlying Permian sandy clays. Mining commenced in 1960 after completion of resource drilling programme. Resource 1973 ~24.6Mt washed sand. Production from 1977-2013 ~10.3Mt.
mine operated from 1913-21 on a barite lode 1.2m wide, trending NW by W, with a near vertical dip. Host was metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded production of 5050 tonne.
quartz lode carrying lead and silver mineralisation in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Workings consisted of two shafts and a short adit. No production figures were recorded.

Cu-Ag-Co-Bi-As-Au mineralisation in gossan in Adelaidean phyllite. Production from ~1850-1902 10,000oz Ag, no Cu production figures. A surface sample collected in 1980 returned anomalous Cu, Co, Bi, Ag & As.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Acanthite,  Chalcopyrite,  Gold,  Iodargyrite,  Malachite,  Tetrahedrite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sandstone of the Belair Subgroup worked for building stone in the 19th century. Former council dump. Now filled and rehabilitated.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BAKER GULLY; CLAY & MINERAL SALES; PM 220
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: red & cream clay from a Tertiary regolith profile on shale of the Adelaidean Belair Subgroup was mined from a shallow pit. ean Belair Subgroup. Production from 1977-2013 is ~620,000t. In 1980 indicated resources were 700,000t.

4 lodes of ironstone in host shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Worked for silver from several shafts and adits in 1868. Shut down when no payable ore recovered. Reopened in 1955 as Mitchells Clay Pit. No production figures were recorded.
sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation quarried from 1956-57, with production of 385 tonnes. The area in now semi-rural, and a hobby farm, being filled by the landowner in 2008.
small quarry operated in the 1950s in soft sandstone, quartzite, and slate of the Saddleworth Formation for building stone. The site is now rural, with the quarry now rehabilitated.
clay pit developed in 1914 on a clay deposit, and was worked to 10 m depth. It is now the site of an oval (2008).
small, compact barite lode worked in 1918. Production of 920 tonnes from 1922-27. The lode was ~1.3 m wide, and the host rock was slate of the Wilmington Formation.
workings developed on a white clay deposit, about 10 m thick, and worked in the 1940's from a shaft and adit with cross drives. The area is now residential. No production details were available.
initial rush on alluvial gold deposits in basal tertiary conglomerate, then working of reef gold in host slate, sandstone and quartzite. Production ~150oz bullion gold.

extensive quarrying on weathered tillite. Produced up to 7 million bricks per year. Area in-filled and rehabilitated, now an open paddock in a semi-rural area, with residential nearby (2008). No figures for total tonnes clay removed were apparent.

small open cut in Brighton Limestone worked for cement manufacture in 1920s. Recorded production from 1924-29 was 41,088 tonnes. Now an office and general industrial area related to the activities of the adjacent Linwood Quarry (2008).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BRIGHTON GARDEN SUPPLIES; CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; EML 4425; SETTLEMENT ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Quaternary to North Maslin Sand deposit worked in a shallow open cut for multiple sand products. Production from 1975-2013 was estimated at 100,000 tonne. 2002 resource 300-400,000 tonne.

18m thick bed of quartzite in siltstone and shale host of the Saddleworth Formation. Production from 1970-77 was 873,730t. Iferred resources (1976) were 1Mt of quartzite, beneath ~720,000t of shale and siltstone. Quarry filled in and rehabilitated.

small open cut in Brighton Limestone worked for cement manufacture in the 1920's. Recorded production from 1924-29 was 41,088 tonnes. It is now an office and general industrial area related to the activities of the adjacent Linwood Quarry (2008).
discontinuous lode of barite of good quality in host Tapley Hill Formation. Production 1918-21, ~1450 tonne, 1922, 265 tonne, and 1944-47, 362 tonne.
series of shafts and pits excavated in 1887 on deposits of Tertiary alluvial gold atop a hill. No production records were determined.

gossanous quartz vein with argentiferous copper ore of malachite, azurite, minor galena, cerussite in shale, slate, sandstone host. Recorded production 152 tonnes ore. In 1858 a magnificent block of malachite, weighing 1 tonne raised.
open cuts developed on quartzite of the Belair Subgroup , being a re-opening of older quarries in the 1960's, and worked through the 1970's. No details on production were available.

quartz-iron oxide lodes with lead-silver mineralisation in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures were recorded. A site visit in 1977 confirmed scattered workings and quartz lodes carrying rich surface indications of mineralisation.

quartz-iron oxide lodes carrying rich lead-silver mineralisation in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures. A site visit in 1977 confirmed scattered workings and quartz lodes carrying rich surface indications of mineralisation.
deposit of sand of the Tertiary Maslin Beach Sand. Operations from 1947-57 for production of ~1Mt, closing when the resources were exhausted.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CHRISTIES SANDS; EML 5217; HALLETT BRICK IND.; NOARLUNGA SAND; PM 65; ROSEWALLS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Tertiary North Maslin Sands overlying weathered Adelaidean Marinoan slate and siltstone worked predominantly for sand products, also clay and shale products from the underlying shale. Production from 1964-2007 2.5Mt.
mine developed on 2 small lodes of poor quality barite in host Seacliff Sandstone, and worked in 2 shafts to 6 m depth in 1940, and for a few months only.
small quantity of sandstone mined in the 1920's. Production was 830 tonne reported for 1966. The workings are no longer visible, with the area now a hobby farm (2008).
quartz-hematite breccia lode in shale of the Skillogalee Dolomite, worked for silver, lead ore, with some zinc ore, some arsenic reported.

western of 2 quarries, this one a small quarry operating on section 924, Hundred Noarlunga for 366 tonne from 1952-54 on a sandstone deposit of the Emeroo Subgroup. Quarry not visible, point location is that of a dam.
open cuts on Stonyfell Quartzite, relatively important in early 1960s. It is now abandoned, not filled in. Located in heavily treed terrain, semi-rural, with nearest residence ~200 m distant (2008).
small clay vein with nodules of galena. Host was slate of the Saddleworth Formation. It was worked in a 11m deep shaft in 1890. Now rural, open paddocks, no visible sign of workings (2008).

barite lode 8m wide in host slate of the Emeroo Subgroup. Discovered in 1928, worked in 1933-1941. Production ~580 tonnes of mostly second grade, some first grade. The area lay within a heavily treed area of the Mount Bold Water Reserve.
small open cut on Tapley Hill Formation. It is now abandoned and appears to be occupied by a house off Cameron Ave.
several tons of silver-lead ore recovered from a quartz lode in Saddleworth Formation. Assays of 30-70% Pb were reported with 25-40 oz/ton silver.

small quarry on limestone, and slate. Worked intermittently for stone supplied to the local district council. Production was 15,277 tonnes of limestone from 1925-52, and 5640 tonnes of slate. Location not precise.

1 of 2 small open cuts on slaty Tapley Hill Formation, with rock used locally as building stone. It was worked briefly in 1955 for production of 72 tonnes of rock. It is now infilled, rehabilitated, and in a residential area (2008).

1 of 2 small open cuts on slaty Tapley Hill Formation, with rock used locally as building stone. It was worked briefly in 1955 for production of 72 tonnes of rock. It is now infilled, rehabilitated, and in a residential area (2008).
2 pits mined for sand production of 1,500 tonne in 1979. Now rehabilitated as small dams.
Tertiary sand and clay worked for building material. It was discovered in 1868, and mined sporadically up to the 1960's. Also prospected for gold. Now the site of a large dam (2008).
worked alluvials for gold near the Jupiter Creek goldfield, reportedly for returns of 7kg gold.

ironstone in gully on sea front. Host Marinoan shale. The deposit was of whitish clay with a good deal of goethite in bands. Production to 1910 was 34 tons of ochre, and 1000 tons clay to 1916. Also from 1908-1940, 2199 tons clay.
pit developed in the 1930s on a slate deposit in the Tapley Hill Formation. recorded production in 1938 of 173t.

irregular, lensoid barite lode in host Marinoan shale and sandstone. Production from 1935-1947 ~2900 tonnes. Generally of low grade. The workings have been filled in, the land resumed to farming (2008).
2 small quarries on blue slate of Tapley Hill Formation worked in the 1920's.

small quartz-iron oxide lode within shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. It was worked in 2 adits, 2 shafts from 1868-71. The lode was 30-50 cm wide, average grade was 33.7 oz/ton Ag before petering out.
sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup in a deep cutting on the side of a hill marginal to a main road. It was worked for building stone in the late 1920's. Area is residential (2008).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADAMS; DISTRICT COUNCIL; FRANKLINS; J. EMMETT & SONS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small open cut on slate of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked in the early 1900s for building stone, and road making material by the local councils.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: FRICKER SAND AND CLAY; OLIVERS; PM 279
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of clay, minor sand of the Tertiary North Maslin Sand, producing clay and sand products for the construction industry. Production from 1977-2013 ~535,000t.
weathered slate of the Umberatana Group for clay in a series of shallow open cuts in 1925-26, for production of ~100 tonnes. In 1967 samples were taken for testwork for use in brickmaking.

gold-bearing alluvium, with best returns from the Great Boulder claim yielding well from both alluvials and leaders. Later work identified deeper alluvial for good yields. Production details poor, with recorded production in 1893 of 326.6gm gold

several small quarries developed on Saddleworth Formation weathered quartzite, within jointed, siliceous slate worked for building stone in the last century. It is located within the Belair National Park.
worked a deposit of limestone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and is now a vacant lot in an industrial site.
deposit of Quaternary clay worked by Hallett Brick Industries from 1963-1976.  Rehabilitated in 1977.
3 pits excavated in 1962 on ferruginous sandy clay of Tertiary age on soft, argillaceous sandstone host. The area is now residential.
Tertiary, deeply weathered metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded seasonal production 146,700 tonne from 1958-1992. Ceased production in 1993.
quarry on clay deposit developed from weathered shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production from 1956-59 of 3759t.
prospecting of an ironstone lode in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation returned poor results. A water bore nearby penetrated a lode carrying galena.
Pliocene fresh water sand and clay in the 1960s-70s, no production figure determined. Drilling in 1964 identified resource of 1.53Mm3 or 2.3Mt. The area is now residential.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. The old workings consisting of a small, shallow pit ~3m2. No production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EVANS RUBBISH DUMP; F.S. EVANS; LOFTY BRICK CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: coarse white sandstone of Emeroo Subgroup, originally for brick making, but in the late 1920's quarried for cut building stone. It was worked to late 1950's for 32,520 tonnes. Currently the quarry is the site of the Heathfield Municipal Rubbish Dump.

quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation, and was opened by the local council for road base material. Production of 500 cubic yards was in 1926-27. Located on W side Ackland Hill Road, and close to a residence.
small open cut opened on Brighton Limestone in 1924 for recovery of ~10,000 tonne (5,500 cubic yards) of rock.
worked for clays for brick manufacture in the 1920's and 30's, and is now residential.
located ~800m west of Ironbank, near Woodcutters road. The ironstone was mined for flux. It was also worked as a silver claim from 1868-1869.
COMMODITIES: Iron Ore,  Ironstone - construction materials,  Silver

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: located north of the Colorado mine. It was a ferruginous, lateritic cap on Woolshed Flat Shale mined for iron flux in 1891-92. 350 tonne produced from pits and trenches. It was also used as a source of road metal in later times.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: nuggety gold recovered from Tertiary alluvial sands and gravels. Minor activity on reef gold shows. Production >25,000oz.

quartz-clay-goethite-pyrite in a quartzite-siltone host of the Saddleworth Formation. Surface samples 56%Pb, 60ozAg/ton. Worked sporadically from 1884-87. Rexamined in 1969 with for no favourable results.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed in 1941 on a vein of quartz-feldspar in host Emeroo Subgroup. Workings consisted of shallow pits for clay and feldspar.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5730; EML 5731; EML 5732; PM 22; PM 3; PM 4
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: major metropolitan quarry developed in 1862 on a deposit of Adelaidean metasediment of Marinoan and Sturtian age. Production stepped up in the 1930s, with production for the period 1977-2013 ~30Mt.
small quarry south of th major Linwood Quarry, and one of several quarries in close proximity working limestone deposits on the Brighton Limestone in the 1920's.
council quarry developed on slaty limestone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and opened in the 1950s. No production figures were located. rehabilitated, and forms embankment to Southern Freeway.

abandoned council quarry of ~2500m2 x 1-10m deep, and developed on quartzite unit within slate host of the Belair Subgroup. A small crushing and screening plant was erected. No production figures were located.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BRADBURY INDUSTRIES; KAOLIN LTD; ML 2754; NICHOLLS CLAY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sediments worked for kaolin including Skillogalee Dolomite worked for clay, flint, Woolshed Flat shale for pottery shale. Production figures 60,115 tonnes.
quartzite and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup worked by the local council for >50 years. Records exists for production from 1984-2013 of >115,000 tonne for road base material.
pit developed on weathered Woolshed Flat Shale. Pale yellow to white clays with abundant mica, low grit, was first worked in 1895. Production figures for 1912-42 were 1,130 tonne.
copper and silver mineralisation in ironstones in host pale cream shale of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Ore recovered at 21.5 oz/tonAg and 26%Cu. In 1970 there was some more prospecting.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ABERFOYLE PARK; CLAY AND MINERAL SALES; MATTHEWS; PM 21; PM 74; PM 75
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Pliocene sands overlying weathered Sturtian shale, slate and quartzite. It was mined in the 1960's and 70's for garden sand. Production records are incomplete, with only record for 1977 production of 190 tonne packing sand.
small quarry 6.5km N of Mclaren Vale, 5m wide by 2m deep on metasediment of the tapley Hill Formation for use as building stone in the early 1900s.
northern of 2 areas mined for clay. Hydrothermally altered slate/schist to quartz-kaolin rock. Production from 1956-1963 was 15,730 tonne.

southern of 2 areas mined for kaolin clay as hydrothermal altered slate/schist of Woolshed Flat Shale, and with abundant hydromica. Worked from 1946-63 for pottery, fire, brick making clay. Production from 1956-1963 15,730 tonne.
Tertiary sand deposit, worked for 3317 tonne garden sand in 1979.

old workings inspected in 1978, with several shallow shafts and a small open cut nearby. Also ruins of a kiln and buildings. No records of mining at this locality were found. The lode was a quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate of the Belair Subgroup.
gold-bearing alluvium as bars across the Onkaparinga River. Worked occasionally for several years, with no production records determined. Now located beneath the waters of Mount Bold Reservoir.

Cu-Pb-Ag mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide in a slate host. Ore minerals included galena, malachite, azurite, chalcopyrite. Production of ~400 tonne recorded. Grades reported include 15-22 oz/ton Ag, 20-30% Cu.

lode of qz-Fe oxide-Cu-Pb-Ag in slate host. Ore minerals included galena, malachite, azurite, and chalcopyrite. Production of ~400 tonne. Grades at 15-22 oz/ton Ag, 20-30% Cu. Grades reported include 15-22 oz/ton Ag, 20-30% Cu.
quarry closed in 1937 after having worked a quartzite of the Stonyfell Quartzite for road works material. It is now a part rehabilitated and treed area, No production records located.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ACKLANDS; HALLIDAYS; HOCKINGS; MOUNT LOFTY FREESTONE; PEPPERS; PINKS; PM 304; PM 83; W. TORODE; WAKEFIELDS; WRIGHTS; ZADOWS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: weathered feldspathic sandstone, worked for building stone over a long period. Production from 1976-2013 ~25,000 tonnes. A disused quarry is used by a shooting club and was rehabilitated.
Pb-Ag-Cu mineralised vein-barite in host Saddleworth Formation claystone and sandstone. Production was ~1882 tonnes of ore yielding 32,991oz (1026kg) Ag, and 965 tonnes lead.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Cerussite,  Chalcopyrite,  Galena,  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ochre, silver, and lead recovered from reef quartz. Assays gave up to 28 oz Ag/ton, but re-assaying did not confirm these values. The exact location is unknown. The area is farming land (2008).

shallow workings opened in 1868. Workings consisted of adits, trenches, and pits on a small lode, with abundant, disseminated pyrite in host slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Surface samples assayed 25 oz/ton Ag.
sand pit operated for a short period in the 1960's. No production records were apparent. The site is now residential.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: B MINE; BUDGENS; C MINE; D MINE; F MINE; SHEPHERD & MURPHYS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Host rock Reynella Siltstone Member, shale and slate, with 2 lodes worked by an adit and many shafts, and open cuts. Production from 1918-1961 ~18,500 tonnes. The area is now under cultivation, there is no visible sign of the mines (2008).
14 ft thick seam of Tertiary lignite, with interbedded carbonaceous shale. Recorded production was 40 tons in 1927.

copper lode at 4%Cu at the surface. The lode was 20-60 cm wide in host Belair Subgroup, and was tested in a series of shallow workings. The lode material consisted of copper carbonate, copper oxide, copper sulphide in vein-quartz.
historic District Council quarry ~ 60 m square developed in arkose of the Marina Arkose, and worked from 1904-65 for production of ~120,000 tonne.

council quarry 46 x 12 x 10 m deep on near flat dipping Tertiary Limestone ~12m thick. It was worked in the 1930's and 1940's intermittently for road base material. It is rehabilitated. No production records located.
6 lodes of copper and lead ore in host Angepena Formation. In 1841 a mine was opened on section 61. No further reference appeared until 1846 and 1847, when it was reported that work was underway.

quarry operated from 1964-73 for production of 600,000 tonnes of limestone for road aggregate. Host slate of the Umberatana Group, underlain by Brighton Limestone, underlain in turn by calc-silicate rock. It is now an industrial site (2008).
extensive prospecting on 4 lodes of argentiferous gossan in host shale of the Saddleworth Formation.
1.2m wide bed of phosphorite in host calcareous siltstone and limestone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Recorded production from 1919-23 of 1071t. resource ~4000 tonne at 50-60% Ca3P2O5.

alluvial gold diggings in the bed of Onkaparinga River and a tributary just south of the Onkaparinga Copper Mine were found to be auriferous, with one prospector reported to have recovered a full pickle bottle of gold.

quartz-clay-pyrite lodes in host micaceous shale and sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. Ore minerals included gold, chalcopyrite, native copper, chalcocite, malachite, azurite. No production figure determined.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Gold,  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small open cut worked for quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation for use as road metal in the 1920's. It lay adjacent to the Mount Malvern historic mine.

clay production of 567 tonne from 1957-58 from small quarries 1.7km SW Mylor. Quarries no longer visible, point location is SE corner of section 1393. Deposit of clay formed by deep weathering of metasediment of host Emeroo Subgroup.
gold-bearing alluvium, worked again in the mid 1890, with many small nuggets were reported. No production figure determined.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. It was reworked in 1928. Incomplete production record was 3.8 tonne treated for 54.2gm gold at 14g/tAu.

gold-bearing alluvium. Reworked In the early 1930's. Further prospecting identified mineralised lodes in bedrock from which visible gold was seen. No production figure was determined, yield was reported as a few ounces.
3 small open cuts on Brighton Limestone. Production recorded as ~49,500 tonnes.

quartz-hematite breccia in host Woolshed Flat Shale. Ore minerals malachite, azurite, proustite, native copper, chalcopyrite, with anomalous zinc arsenic. Production was 13.5 oz Ag from 1.52 tonne in 1867, 120oz Ag from 20.3 tonne in 1869.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Malachite,  Proustite,  Sphalerite
