DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Tertiary North Maslin sands, first worked in 1961. Production from 1977-2013 >2.8Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.B.M. NOARLUNGA SAND CO.; EML 2569; PM 40; READYMIX CONCRETE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pit developed on Tertiary North Maslin Sand to 28m thick, overlying Permian sand and clay. It opened in 1927, closing in the late 1970s when it was used as a local council dump. Production from 1964-91 >715,400t of multiple end products.
clay worked for red brick material in the 1950's and 60's. Host was weathered soft to hard shale. It is fully rehabilitated, and within semi-rural residential area (2008).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BORAL REYNELLA; PM 107; PM 222; PM 23; PM 48; QUARRY INDUSTRIES; SA PORTLAND CEMENT CO LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: initially on Brighton Limestone for limestone products for local cement works. Later production from associated metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1923-2011 ~6Mt. Seasonal activity on campaign basis.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: OLD REYNELLA; PM 23; PM 48; SA PORTLAND CEMENT CO LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: open cut on Brighton Limestone. Part of operations centred on main Reynella open cut ~1km SE. Some residential development on the land atop the scarp, and close to the quarry (2008).

veins of barite in host Saddleworth Formation. Production from small pits and open cuts was 13 tons in 1928. The grade was thought to be marginal, due to the level of iron oxide staining, and the pyrite content. No visible sign of the workings (2008).
quartzite of the Wilmington Formation quarried in the 1950's and 60's, now rehabilitated.

3 quarries on thin bed of quartzite within a slate host of Belair Subgroup excavated into the side of a hill below Windy Point, Belair. The area is open bushland with the nearest residential area ~350 m away (2008).

small quarry on Belair Subgroup used by the Mitcham Council in the 1920's. 3m sandstone overlying 3m white clay used locally for brick making, and basal quartzite. No production records located. The area is residential (2008).
2 elongate, deep (to 20 m) quarries opened in 1904 on a quartzite bed within slate host of the Belair Subgroup. It was worked throughout the 1930s.
clay on weathered Woolshed Flat Shale in 1961, and operated for 10 years. Now rehabilitated, and the site of a small dam (2008).
gold-bearingTertiary conglomerate above, and adjacent to modern gold-bearing alluvium. Production was estimated at 100oz (3.1kg), with nugget gold reported as well.

quarries 1 & 2 developed on slate of Tapley Hill Formation for building stone. Workings up to 40m long, with large blocks were excavated. No production figures were located. The location of the site is not known accurately.

location uncertain, section 135, Hundred Noarlunga is open paddock on the fringe of built up area, no visible sign of workings remains. Quarry worked in the 1960s for freestone. Recorded production 4947 tonnes from 1961-66.

weatherd feldspathic sandstone for building stone in the 1920's, and closed in 1927. There was 3-5 m of overburden of weathered sandstone, and host rock was slate. It is located along the crest of a ridge.

series of 12 quarries developed on Adelaidean quartzite of the Burra Group. Opened in 1916, providing construction material for the metropolitan area for many decades. A public walking trail has been established in the area.

historic small open cut for limestone of the Angepena Formation opened in 1927 for production of ~7650 cubic metres, with total production incorporated into figures for section 559. Now rehabilitated.
small quartz lode in host Saddleworth Formation. The lode contained galena and argentiferous copper ore. The mine was worked in several shallow adits and a shaft for only a short time in 1859.

several open cut quarries developed in blue quartzite of the Belair Subgroup. Now overgrown, not backfilled. The area is in a heavily treed semi-rural zone, with built-up area within 250 m (2008). No production figure located.
historic council pit located on a stone reserve declared in 1885 in Hundred Noarlunga, section 428. Quarry worked sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup for road fill material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: STIRLING; STIRLING QUARRY RESERVE 3; TORODE FREESTONE QUARRY; W. TORODES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: beds of pale grey sandstone to 1-2 m wide of the Emeroo Subgroup, and worked for freestone mostly in the 1920's.
small quartz-infilled shear zone in micaceous sandstone, shale and grit of the Emeroo Subgroup. Total production was estimated at 1,493gm (48oz), no ore tonnage or grade determined.

Pb-Cu mineralisation in host slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. The lode was sideritic quartz veins carrying galena, with a separate vein set carrying covellite in quartz-goethite-orthoclase-apatite gangue. Location not clearly established.
barite lode in Marinoan shale of the Reynella Siltstone Member. Production was ~223 tonne of low-grade barite. It was located ~50 m north of Elliotts Barite.
quarry developed on Tapley Hill Formation slate worked for building stone in the 1920's, and was one of three neighbouring quarries.

clay pit opened in the 1870s, and was worked in the 1920s. The pit developed to 8 m deep on clay used to make bricks. There were irregular lenses of gravel throughout. No visible signs remain of the pit, the area is now residential.
Tertiary sand deposit, with pit developed from 1976-88 for production of ~9700 tonne garden sand. It was rehabilitated in 1988.

no details, apparent large amount of prospecting for gold in late 19th century in a deep adit and numerous open cuts, presumably on quartz reef in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. No recorded production.
series of discontinuous barite lodes worked from 1920-1940 for production of ~2240 tonnes. Host was purple and grey Marinoan slate of the Wilmington Formation.

2 historic quarries on limonitic sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, located NE of Mount Barker road, and opposite the Aldgate railway Station. Worked in the 1920's, presumably been infilled. The area is now residential.
adit driven on a 1-1.7m wide quartz-iron oxide reef trending NS in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. Returns were poor and the venture soon collapsed.
clay pit developed to 9 m depth, and was worked in the 1920's for clay used in the manufacture of bricks. The site is now residential.
workings developed from 1907 and through the 1920s on a phosphorite of the Brighton Limestone, with manganese and iron oxides present.
2 small open cuts over an area ~150 x 120 m on a small hill of Brighton Limestone. The excavated material was used for road seal aggregate by Nourlunga Council in 1926.
reported in HYL Brown, 1908, occurrence of galena in vein in host Woolshed Flat Shale that was worked in an adit and a shaft.

3 shafts excavated in 1875, through alluvium to prospect for gold-bearing basal gravels. There was prospecting for gold on quartz lodes in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation on the surrounding hills. No production figure was recorded.

small barite lode in host metasediment of the Umberatana Group worked from 1922-23 for a few tonne. The lode was 60-90 cm wide, and iron oxide stained, with vugs of goethite. No complete production figure determined.

historic council quarry developed on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked from the 1930s to 1952 for production of ~34,000 tonne for road base material. Filled in and within residential area in McLaren Vale.

minor prospecting for gold took place via several shallow shafts. The lode at the surface consisted of copper oxide, and copper carbonate in a gossan within host limestone and slate of the tapley Hill Formation. No production figures were provided.
initial mining of deep bed of alluvial clay in a valley floor. Subsequent production from within deeply weathered shale of the Saddleworth Formation. Incomplete total production records >532,000t.

gypsum lake deposit of the Yamba Formation, with production of 2600 tonne plasterboard-grade (94% CaSO4.2H2O) product to Sydney in 1994, 450,000 tonne mined in 1990 and winrowed on MPL 43 to leach salt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LAKE MACDONNELL; ML 500; ML 706; ML 707; ML 708; ML 709; ML 710; ML 711; ML 712; ML 713; ML 714; ML 756; ML 757; ML 758; ML 759; ML 760; ML 761; ML 762; ML 763; RED LAKE; SEESALT LTD; WARATAH GYPSUM PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: salt produced by solar evaporation of brine, which seeps into a shallow lake through porous coastal dunes, or is pumped from nearby gypsum operations. Production from 71ha of crystallising pans from 1973-2013 ~2.4Mt.

2 crosscutting quartz-iron oxide reefs trending 338, crosscutting siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. No recorded production. Minor barite recorded. Sampling returned anomalous values for Ag, As, Bi, Cu, Co, Pb, and Ni.
mine developed on quartz veins in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. The workings consisted of five underlay shafts .
occurrence of anomalous Pb-Zn recorded in layered calc-silicate and baritic BIF of the Willyama Supergroup. Close by sample of gossan by BHP Minerals returned a maximum value 400ppbAu.

mine developed in the early 1930s on a quartz-iron oxide vein carrying lead and silver mineralisation. Workings consisted of a main shaft and pits scattered over a wide area. No production figures were recorded.
hematite-enriched horizon of Braemar Ironstone to a maximum width of 2.5 m. 2010-15 geological assessment of Braemar Iron Formation in MacDonald Corridor as low grade iron ore.
workings on several, narrow quartz-iron oxide reefs trend NW in host siltstone of Tapley Hill Formation. No individual production figures determined.

small mine working a quartz reef on the Teetulpa Goldfield. Later inspection identified 6 shafts developed on quartz and ironstone reefs in host siltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. No production figures were determined.
mine developed on quartz reef in metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. 40 cm wide quartz-filled shear, dip 75 E, strike 355. No individual production figures were determined.
Au-(Cu) mineralised quartz-iron oxide reefs trend 325-345, dip steep E, in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. No individual production figures determined.

mine developed on quartz reefs in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Workings consisted of four shafts and pits. Shaft A worked 2 veins dip steep east, with the western vein more ferruginous. Shaft E worked a 20 cm wide ferruginous quartz vein.
mine location not certain. Stated as located on quartz reef immediately N of New Milo. Production records indicated 19.8 tonnes treated yielded 223.2 gm gold at 11g/t.
alluvial diggings in creek bed at the junction of Goslins Gully, and Bradys Gully, minor production in 2006 of 1.6 oz.
workings developed from 1889-91 on alluvials. Recorded production was 5 oz (155.5 gm) gold.
workings on a NNW-trending narrow quartz vein, which persists for a distance of ~50m. No production figure determined.
several workings on a near NS-trending narrow quartz reef that can be traced for ~400m. No production figure determined. Host was siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation.
Recorded as NW of Walparuta Springs, and ~20km NW of Outalpa township. Production was 12 tonnes at 18% Cu.
presumed developed on quartz reef in host metasediment of the Burra Group, recorded 1 tonne yields 8gm gold.

series of excavations for ~70m distance along a 350m long, NNW-trending quartz reef. No reliable historical production figures established. Minor copper carbonates observed. Cut by an EW trending later barren quartz vein.

Au-(Pb-Cu) mineralised banded, quartz reef 15-45cm wide, trending EW, dip 44S. Gold visible in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Parcel of ore of 4.9 tonne ore yielded 306gm bullion gold at 62g/t.
2 shafts to 30m sunk on micaceous and hornblendic schist carrying quartz veins showing a little visible gold. Located near the Queen Bee mining area and 7 miles SSE from Cutana railway station.
claims taken out over quartz vein carrying veinlets of galena. Analysis returned anomalous silver. recorded as 3.4 km west of Taltabooka Well, and near Lion Hill.

several quartz reefs from 2.5 to 3m wide, trend variable from 333-342, dip steep E, in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. There were 6 shafts, 2 on the underlay and an open cut. No individual production figure recorded.

location uncertain, recorded as gold claim GL 379, near Taltabooka on the Wadnaminga Goldfield, and adjacent to the Triumph Mine. Shaft developed on quartz-iron oxide lode. Samples of ore showed elevated Au-Ag.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. 3 shafts worked 10 cm wide quartz reefs, strike 342. No production figures determined.
quartz reef in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation, located on same lode as the Golden Record, and to the SW. No production records apparent.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: series of linear aeromagnetic anomalies west of & abutting the W margin of Ordovician Anabama Granite. Drilling identified source as IF of Braemar Iron Formation. Preliminary DTR testwork was encouraging. No resource estimate.
workings of two shallow shafts and a pit, and worked a quartz reef located in flat-lying siltstone of Tapley Hill Formation. The lode trended 348, dipped steep east. No production figure recorded.
mine developed on quartz reefs in host dolomitic siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Quartz-ironstone veins to 10cm wide, strike 345-360, dip steep east. No production figure recorded.

quartz reefs in host siltstone of Tapley Hill Formation dip 20S. 2 shafts, costeans on 2 reefs 5cm & 15cm wide. Veins ferruginous, dipped vertically, with several small stringers adjacent, and quartz veins along the bedding, strike 333.
workings developed on quartz-iron oxide reef, with trace malachite and talc, trending E30N, dip 60N, ~30cm wide in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. No production records apparent.
presumably developed on a quartz reef in metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. In 1938 a parcel of 6.96t ore yielded 503gm gold at 72g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EIFFEL TOWER SHAFT; GL 1628; ML 13814; NEW GOLDEN RECORD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: narrow 10-45cm wide quartz-iron oxide reef carrying pyrite and galena, in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Trend NE dip 15-25SE. Production to 1936 ~25 tonnes for 1052gm bullion gold at 42g/tAu.
ferruginous quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. The vein was 10 cm wide, dipped steep east, strike 335. No production figure determined.
presumed mine developed on quartz reef in host Tapley Hill Formation, no production figure determined.
EW-trending quartz-iron oxide carrying trace copper and lead mineralisation in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. No production figures were determined.

Surface copper mineralisation. Described as on Hundred L7, 6.8km east of Mingary. Inspected in 1885, pits on a quartz-iron oxide lode trending NNE for ~800m. Grab surface sample returned ~370g/t silver.

30 cm wide quartz-iron oxide reef carrying visible coarse gold and trace argentiferous galena in host slate of the Belair Subgroup. The lode trended EW, dip 27S. Recorded production to 1936 was ~22t for 981gm bullion gold @ 45g/tAu.
narrow 5-10cm wide white quartz to quartz-iron oxide veins, dip steep E, trend 335-345, also 073-075. Host was siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation dipping 0-30S. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ALBION; IRONCLAD; LYKKE VIKING; ML 5886; SCOTCHMAN; TAVEN CORE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: several quartz reefs from 5-40cm wide, dip steep E, trend 332-345, and in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, dip 10-30S. Many shafts, costeans, and open cuts were excavated. Production 1994-2006 ~22 oz.
Recorded as 3 km NE of Trenordans Mine (Kings Bluff Mine), and south of Olary.
presumably mine developed on quartz reef in host Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure determined.

deeper workings on a narrow NNW-trening quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation, no production figure determined. It is located ~100m south and on the line-of-lode of 4 shallow workings on a NNW-trending quartz vein.
quartz reefs in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Shallow shafts and pits on 10-30 cm wide quartz reefs, dip steep east, strike 340. No production details determined.
quartz lode in host albitic schist of the Willyama Supergroup. A parcel of 250Kg yielded 35.4gm gold at 140g/tAu.
narrow, steep E-dipping, 345 trending, 2-40cm wide quartz veins in host dolomitic siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation on the Teetulpa Goldfield. No production details determined.

structural setting of anticlinal arch broached by high angle fault in host Enorama Shale. Best surface sampleof quartz lode at 2.4g/t Au. Drill hole M22 assayed 0.45g/t Au over 3.5m from 20.5-24m. No production figure was determined.
quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. The reefs were 15-40 cm wide, dipped steeply east, and had a strike of 333 to 336. No production figure determined.
narrow, quartz-filled shears, trend 335, dip steep east in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Two shallow shafts were excavated. No production figure was determined.
narrow, Au-(Pb-Ag) mineralised quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lodes in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. production from tailings from 2003-09 estimated at >500 oz.
quartz-iron oxide reefs in host dolomitic siltstone, micaceous siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production records.
location uncertain, point location is for claim MC 15238 adjoining and west of the Thunder Queen. Returns of 372 gm gold from 16.3 tonne at 23g/tAu in 1935-36.
located from historic internal mineral occurrences database, presumably prospecting of a copper mineralised quartz vein in host Mesoproterozoic granite in the Willyama Inliers region.
workings on quartz reefs in host grey siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation.
Approximate location only. Reported as 1.7km S of Walparuta Mine. Reported production from 1911-14 of 1500 ton of copper ore at 5-12%Cu.
located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal mineral occurrences 250K map. Site of shallow workings on copper shows in barite in host schist of the Willyama Complex.
shaft on southern extension of the massive sulphide lodes worked at West Mutooroo (see mindep # 843).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BIRTHDAY; FILSELL; GAWLER CRATON RESOURCES; ML 4967; ML 6037; ML 6038
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in siltstone in host Belair Subgroup. Production from 1888-1940 ~11,000oz bullion gold, & from tailings from New Milo & other mines in the vicinity from 2003-09 18Kg bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Arsenopyrite,  Carbonate,  Galena,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Scorodite

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MC 6853; MC 6854; MC 6855; NEW WEST MUTOOROO COPPER MINING CO. N.L.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 miles west of Mutooroo mine, claims on copper show in host gneiss of the Willyama Complex, and worked in 1907.
located from plan no 1986-0541, and on the Teetulpa Goldfield, presumably on quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. Records indicate >200 tonnes ore raised, but no yield figures apparent. A parcel of 20 tonne ran at 31g/tAu.
old workings on quartz lodes in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Marked on map number S15582 on the State Geological Survey unpublished plans database.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. No production record determined.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Dolomite,  Goethite,  Hematite,  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. The veins were 40-50 cm wide, dip steep E, trend 330-338.
quartz reefs in host micaceous siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. The lode was a 30cm wide ferruginous quartz vein, with a steep easterly dip, trend 343. No production figure determined.
workings on narrow NNW-trending quartz reef in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure determined.
reported as ~360m from Taylors Shaft at the Radium Hill Mine. shallow prospecting pits on a lode rich in octahedral magnetite with trace copper carbonates within host Adelaidean metasediment.
quartz reefs dip steep E, trend 332, in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure determined.

shallow workings on white quartz-iron oxide-pyrite-As reefs in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. Two shafts on 20-50cm wide quartz reefs, with minor siderite, Mn & Fe oxide, dip steep east, trend 340-345.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Arsenopyrite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz lode 10-30cm wide, trend EW, dip 45 in host calcareous slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production in 1936 of 4.7 tonne ore for 148.5gm gold at 31.6g/tAu.
workings on narrow NNW-trending quartz-iron oxide lode in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure determined.

weakly ferruginous 50cm wide quartz reefs, trend 330-338, dip steep E, in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. Some copper carbonate reported in the dump material, alluvial production 1988-2006 ~3 oz.
narrow quartz vein trending NS in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Tenure current as ML 5486, no records for production known.

Au mineralisation in quartz reef in host sediment of the Belair Subgroup. Production from 1914-1939 ~2,000oz or 62.2kg bullion gold. 1975 resource estimate 19,000gm between Nos 3 & 5 shafts above water table (3800 tonne @ 5g/t).
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup, some alluvial gold recovered. Recorded production 1899-1936 of 35924gm bullion gold. Seasonal production from 1984-92 ~122gm.

quartz reefs in host sitstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. 2 shallow shafts, and pits developed on 5-10cm wide quartz-iron oxide lodes, with steep dips to the east, strike 334-341. No production figure determined.

Au-Pb-(Ag-Zn-Cu-As) mineralisation quartz-iron oxide-pyrite veins in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. Production from 1890-1934 ~8430oz (262kg) gold bullion. Reserves of 9.5kg contained gold in tailings (1985).
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Cerussite,  Galena,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shallow workings on ferruginous quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. Quartz reefs 10-20 cm wide, with two bedding plane veins were exposed in one of the shafts. Vein dipped vertically, strike 347.

quartz reefs in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. 2 shallow shafts and pits on 6cm wide reef, dip 25E, trend 336-342. Folded siltstone host seen on the wall of a shaft. No production figure determined.

location inaccurate. 2 claims worked from 1907-09 for recorded 560 tonne ore, no grade information. Described as 8.5km due east along the fenceline from Duffield Dam, and just east of the NS fenceline.

quartz veining carrying copper staining in host quartz-feldspar schist. Malachite, azurite, rare chalcopyrite at depth in a lode from 2m to few cm wide. Production records 6 tonnes mined for recovery of 3 tonnes of 22.25% copper ore.
several Cu-Au-(Co-Ni) mineralised quartz-iron oxide lodes in host metasediment of the Montacute Dolomite. Production ~281 tonnes of ore (figures incomplete, estimated 76 t contained copper metal).
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Gold,  Malachite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: large quartz lode to 50 feet wide in host Woolshed Flat Shale, prospected in small pits for best sample 1%Sn.
Au mineralisation in 2 quartz reefs in host mica schist of the Emeroo Subgroup. No recorded production figures.
claims taken out for alluvial gold, and worked in 1886, and 1935. No production figures were recorded.
Cu-Au-Bi mineralisation with anomalous Ag, Pb, Zn, As in quartz reef in host slate/phyllite of the Emeroo Subgroup. Recorded recovery 185t copper metal, 5.5t bismuth. Also 64t ore yielding 142gm Au.

MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Sericite,  Siderite,  Talc

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sandstone of the Basket Range Sandstone, with operations commenced in 1952, producing 20,000 tonne sandstone products from 1952-66, and from 1986-2013an estimated 39,000 tonne, mainly for building stone and filling.
mine developed in 1888 on a quartz-iron oxide reef in host schist of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group. No production figures were recorded.
worked a deposit of sandstone of the Basket Range Sandstone after 1918, and was closed before 1938.
sandstone deposit of the Belair Subgroup. Worked in the early 1970s for recovery of 10,277 tonne of aggregate. Production from 1977-2006 was estimated at 231,000 tonne mainly for road base material.

located ~170m south of the Bird in Hand mine developed in 1882 on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Umberatana group. No individual production figures determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MAIN REEF; MC 4113; MC 4421; ML 5169; WHITE REEF; YELLOW REEF
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in quartz-sulphide reefs in metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Production  9215oz bullion gold. Later drilling identified resource of  421,000t @ 12g/t for 162,000oz contained gold (2007).
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Galena,  Gold,  Silver,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: talc-albite bodies in host mica schist and quartzite of Burra Group. Production from 1945-75 ~6,270t.
Au mineralised quartz-iron oxide vein in host slate of the Umberatana Group. Production 22.9kg bullion gold.

northern bank of Torrens River at Birdwood. It was an important surficial deposit of ironstone in host Mitcham Quartzite, and was worked for use as a flux last century, from which a large quantity of ore was produced from open cuts.
worked alluvium for gold in 1932 for recovery of 97gm of gold.
mine developed in 1933-34 on three quartz reefs in host metasediment in Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. No production figures were determined.
diggings in 1872 on Tertiary, gold-bearing alluvials worked for poor returns. Reworked in 1886. No production figures were determined.
historic clay workings on weathered feldspathic gneiss of the Barossa Complex reopened in the 1930's for road making material. Production of crushed rock from 1931-32 was ~20,000 tonne.
small quarry developed on weathered shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite on PM 288. No production figures were recorded.
mine developed in 1897 on a 1m wide quartz-iron oxide-pyrite vein in host Cambrian Kanmantoo Group metasediment. No production figures were recorded.

mine adjacent to the Bird in Hand working the alluvials, and a similarly mineralised reef. Overlying surface material produced nugget gold. Production from the reef ~436t for 4234gmAu at 9.7g/t. Combined production ~5914gm (136oz).

mine developed from 1931-32 on a quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group. Production records incomplete, with one parcel of 2.3 tonnes yielding 36 gm of gold at 15.7g/t.

discordant talc lode associated with albite in host micaceous schists and quartzite of Undulya Quartzite and Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figure recorded. In 1976 limited auger drilling determined there was no economic resource.
6 km NE of Birdwood, on Hundred Talunga, section 8, claim MC 14732 taken out for gold in 1934.

mine developed from 1931-32 on a quartz reef in host metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Umberatana Group. Incomplete recorded production records , with a parcel of 4.7 tonne yielding 16.1gm at 3.4g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CAREY GULLY FREESTONE; CAREY GULLY SANDSTONE; N.L. HILL & CO.; PM 110
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sandstone of the Carey Gully Sandstone Member for building stone, minor road base material. Production from 1973-2013 was estimated at 90,000 tonne.
worked from the 1960's for building stone from the Carey Gully Sandstone Member. Production from 1977-2003 was estimated at 77,800 tonnes. Worked out areas were  rehabilitated.

mine location uncertain. Several lodes in host Barossa Complex metasediment were worked from 1845 to the 1890's with reported production of good copper ore, though no production figures were recorded.
talc-albite lode in host mica schist of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production from 3 workings from 1939-2004 ~64,750 tonne of talc ore.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef worked in 1870. Host rock was sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group. In 1894 a parcel of 51 tonnes yielded 1322 gm gold at 26g/t.
presumed gold claim worked in the 1933-34. Host rock was undifferentiated Tertiary sediment.
small quarries in Stonyfell Quartzite worked for freestone in the 1900s, later assessment in 1960.
quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Burra Group. Periodic activity in 1870, 1887, and 1931. No production figures were determined.
quartz-iron oxide lodes in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Recorded production of 65.7t for 591gm gold at 9g/t.
abandoned roadside quarry of <4,000m2 x 1-8m deep on weathered sandstone of the Basket Range Sandstone, possibly worked for both building stone, and road fill.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Burra group. Production was recorded at 8.8 tonnes yielding 92gm gold at 10g/tAu.
Au mineralisation in lode of pyritic quartzite in host slate of the Burra Group. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 4540; GUMERACHA TALC; MINERALS (SA) P/L; ML 2514; PM 73
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: oldest talc mine in SA. Metasomatic talc deposit in host Stonyfell Quartzite worked from 1901-79 for production of 57,528 tonne of pharmecutical-grade talc.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: series of prospecting pits and shafts from 1914-15 on a 15-100cm wide quartz vein in host metasediment of the Burra Group. The claim was adjacent to the Federal Mine. No production figures were recorded.

quartz reef in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. It proved to be rich in copper and bismuth minerals. The area was reworked in the 1920-30s for alluvial gold. No production figures were recorded.
quartz-iron oxide reef in vicinity of the Eclipse Mine hoping to penetrate the same reef at depth. No production figures were recorded.
quartz reef containing gold and bismuth, and in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Worked for 1 year, then sporadically until 1932. No production figures were recorded.
location inexact, recorded as section 5607, Hundred Yatala, quartz lode worked in 1847-48, no production figure recorded.
copper lode from 1847-48 in host metasediment of the Montacute Dolomite, no production figures recorded.
Au-Pb-Zn-Cu mineralised quartz-iron oxide reef in host schist of the Neoproterozoic Umberatana Group. Production was ~8352t ore for 140.2kg bullion gold from 1884-1941.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: abandoned quarry of ~1,600m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered sandstone unit of the Basket Range Sandstone, and worked from 1956-67.

developed in the 1890's on rich alluvials. A quartz-iron oxide reef was worked from 1904-17, and again in 1935-36. Host was metasediment of Stonyfell Quartzite. Production 60oz from alluvials. parcel of 41.7t ore for 648gm gold @ 15.5g/tau

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: 5 ACRES; BLUMBERG BLOCKS; LLOYDS REEF; MCCORMACKS REEF
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz reef in host Cambrian Backstairs Passage Formation. No production figures were determined.
gold-bearing alluvium. Small pockets of rich ore were recovered, but the field proved to be poor and it was abandoned within 4 months. Estimated production was from 60-100 oz (1860-3100 gm).

quartz-iron oxide vein in host kaolinitic sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Saddleworth Formation. No reliable production figures were determined, with estimates put at 25 tonnes of ore recovered at 3-5 gm/tonne.

quarry on sandstone with 30% kaolinised feldspar, and of the Basket Range Sandstone. Recorded production 338t in 1956. Resource estimated in 1955 for an area adjacent to the old quarry of 76,500 tonne.
2 small quarries for total area <1,000m2 x 1-6m deep, located either side of Deviation road, and developed on weathered micaceous sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite.
metasomatic talc deposit in host Stonyfell Quartzite prospected in a series of trenches and pits. Production from 1980-85 was estimated at 250 tonne pharmecutical-grade talc.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5860; GUMERACHA TALC; ML 4398; ML 4447; ML 5055
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: metasomatic talc lode in host Woolshed Flat Shale. Production 1937-75 of 2809t, and from 1982-89 ~5200 tonne pharmecutical -grade product. Minor production of barite, also sandstone for use in the construction industry.
quartz-pyrite vein in host sandstone and pipeclay of the Neoproterozoic Tarcowie Siltstone. It was worked again briefly in 1934. No production figures were determined.

clay pit on deeply weathered barossa Complex metasediment. Incomplete records for production. From 1957-61 927 tonne, with last production in 1995 and rehabilitation using EARF completed in 1997 - see file MB 729.
clay as weathering product on metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Production from 1978-80 was estimated at 1840 tonne coloured clay for brickmaking. Rehabilitated in 2000-2002.
Tertiary clay deposit worked from the 1950's to 1960's for production of 28,345 tonne. Recorded production from 1977-80 was ~3600 tonne red clay for brickmaking.
clay pit developed on deeply weathered, kaolinitic sandstone and shale of the Montacute Dolomite, and was worked for fire clay (kaolin). No production figures were recorded.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. Production from 4.8 tonne of ore was 80 gm of gold at 16g/tAu.
quartz reef mined from 1931-38 for ~ 575oz (17.9Kg) of bullion gold from 767t ore. Host was metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Mitcham Quartzite.
horizon of thin quartz veins in host slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. No production figures were determined.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host schist of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. Small quantities of gold were recovered but nothing payable. The mine was abandoned in 1926.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite  Micaceous,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz iron oxide reef adjacent in host slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production from 1931-34 ~9.2 tonnes for 495gm of gold at 54g/tAu. The mine was abandoned due to poor returns. ~435gm (14oz) gold was recovered from the adjacent alluvials.

quartz-iron oxide vein in host slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Reworking of the area in the 1890's & 1930's recorded recovery of rich pockets of ore. Parcels of ore totalling 53 tonnes yielding 1688gm gold at 32g/tAu.

10-50cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein in host weathered schist of the Barossa Complex. The vein trended NW dipped 60NE. Worked periodically to 1936, production from this later period 54.7t ore yielding 621gm gold at 11g/tAu.

~15cm wide fissure-fill quartz-iron oxide-clay vein in host blue claystone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. A parcel of 11 tonnes of ore yielded 368gm gold at 33g/tAu. There was some further prospecting in 1931, and again from 1983-85 for recovery of 30gm.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host mica schist of the Cambrian Backstairs Passage Formation. It was worked from 1931-34 in a series of shafts. Production was recorded of 99 tonnes for 1792.6gm gold at 18g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CARN BRAE; CARNBROY; G.J. SAMPSON; SAMPSONS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein in host weathered, kaolinitic sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. It was reworked from 1903-10, and again in 1931-32. Production was estimated at 223.9 tonnes for 2863 gm gold at 13g/tAu.
quartz vein in host micaceous schist of the Palaeoproterozoic Barossa Complex. Production was 75.2 tonne for 521 gm gold at 7g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GORDON AND BROWN; GUMERACHA TALC; MC 779
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 small lodes of talc-albite rock for recorded production of 5 tonne of pharmecutical-grade ore. Exploratory drilling in 1976 failed to penetrate any talc-albite intervals.

gold-bearing alluvium, with recorded production 800oz (24.9kg). The alluvials were worked out within 3 months. Mine developed on quartz reef in host Saddleworth Formation. Recorded production was 103 tonnes ore for 919gm bullion gold at 9g/tAu.
slate of the Saddleworth Formation, quarry worked in 1871 for small production, resource assessment in 1950s estimated 153,000m3.
historic council quarry on sections 6594-95, Hundred Talunga developed on Mitcham Quartzite, initially for building stone, later for road base material. Location not accurate.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MC 430; MC 431; MC 432; ML 3023; ML 3024; ML 3025; SA SILICATES PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed in 1933 on a 120m wide pegmatite dyke in host Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production from 1933-66 was 39,878 tonne.
near vertical, 6m wide quartz-iron oxide reef, trend 340, in host mica schist of the Emeroo Subgroup. It was worked in 2 shafts. No production figures were determined.
1m wide quartz-iron oxide vein in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. Best grade of 93g/tAu was recorded, though no production figures were reported.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLDEN GROVE; HALLETT BRICK CLAY; PM 79
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of  Tertiary sequence of sand and clay, and deeply weathered Adelaidean shale worked from 1977-2011 for 2.2Mt of sand, clay and shale products.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Good returns were reported from a rich lode, which was reworked in 1930-31 for production of 51.3 tonnes of ore yielding 2131gm gold at 41.5g/tAu.
structurally controlled supergene/residual pitchblende in deeply weathered Palaeoproterozoic paragneiss of the Houghten Inlier. U4/7 drillhole assay returned ~360ppm U from surface to 14m.
gold-bearing alluvials on Barossa Complex basement. There was a small rush of ~60 men with poor returns of very fine to dust gold. No production figures were determined.
gossanous quartz lode in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Returns were poor and the mine was soon abandoned. It was prospected again in 1934-35. No production figures were determined.
building stone quarry in medium to coarse grained felspathic sandstone of the Aldgate Sandstone worked from 1950-60 at production rate 80 tonne per week. 1956 resource >50,000 tonne.  .
quartz-iron oxide lodes in host schist of the Tapley Hill Formation. There were several shafts, the deepest to 11m, with some good show of gold reported, though no production figures were determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: HOUGHTON CLAY; MITCHELLS HOUGHTON; MITCHELLS PIT PGH; PM 57
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of pale grey to white clay being deeply weathered profile over shale of the Emeroo Subgroup. Production from 1952-98 ~385,200t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5553; EML 5968; INGLEWOOD BRICK CO LTD; INGLEWOOD BRICKWORKS; PM 141
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay as product of deep weathering of Barossa Complex metasediment, with recorded production of coloured shale products from 1989-98 of ~94,420 tonne. Rehabilitation was completed in 2005.

quartz reef in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Returns were poor and the mine closed in 1871. Production of 437gm was recorded. Diggings had developed earlier in 1870 on neighbouring gold-bearing alluvium.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Ilmenite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: structurally controlled pitchblende in Palaeoproterozoic paragneiss of the Houghten Inlier.
talc-albite lode in host mica schist of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Recorded production from 1939-71 was 3420 tonne of pharmecutical-grade talc.

worked initially in 1851. Later in 1931 a party prospecting alluvials on Kangaroo Creek on Section 336, Hundred Onkaparinga extracted ~2oz (62gm) gold, but the general run along the alluvials was discouraging.
historic quarry on quartzite unit of the Skillogalee Dolomite, now occupied by a residence.

7 auger holes identified potential for a resource of refractory clay. Host was Quaternary sand, clay and gravel overlying mica schist, and schistose quartzite, and located on the western limb of a NW-trending syncline.
quartz vein in host  Glen Osmond Slate Member. Production was recorded at 282.4gm gold, no tonnage figure determined.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Glen Osmond Slate Member. A parcel of 3.6 tonnes of ore yielded 20.4 gm of gold at 5.6g/tAu.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Reopened briefly in 1931. A parcel of 11.7 tonnes yielded 66.7 gm of gold at 6g/tAu. Alluvial gold had been discovered earlier in 1870.

quartz-iron oxide vein in host weathered slate of the Mitcham Quartzite. It was closed in 1934 when the veins pinched out. Gold values were poor and gold distribution erratic. Production from 20 tonnes of ore was 117.3gm at 6g/tAu.

narrow quartz-iron oxide lode in metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale, and inspected in 1929 by Mines Department geologist. It was worked in a short adit, shallow pits, costeans and trenches. The ore showed streaks of galena.
shallow shafts on quartz-iron oxide lode in host sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked in 1881-82. No production figure recorded, early sampling reported at 93g/tAu.
Pb-Ag-Au-(Cu-Co) mineralisation in 3 quartz lodes in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production figures incomplete.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BORAL LOBETHAL; EML 4603; EML 5589; EML 5770; EML 6319; PM 87; ROCKFELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: major quarry developed on a deposit of metasiltstone of the Burra Group. Production from 1976-2011 was estimated at 9.2 million tonne of multiple end products for use in the construction industry.

quartz lode in host slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. Initial prospecting returned rich specimens, with returns quickly decreasing, the mine closing in late 1885 when there was a large influx of water. No production figures were determined.

quartz vein in host sandstone of the Barossa Complex. Only poor returns were recorded, no production figure was determined. The sandstone was decomposed containing bunches of kaolinitic material and some copper mineralisation.
quartz vein in host schist of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Returns were poor and the mine soon closed. It was prospected again in 1934. A parcel of 11 tonnes yielded 48gm gold at 4.4g/tAu.
clay pit developed in 1959-60 on deeply weathered metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production was 8975 tonnes.

prospecting of the creek identified alluvial gold. Quartz reefs were discovered on the adjacent hills, with samples returning 6-15g/tAu. Worked in several shafts and pits, no recorded production figure. Host was Saddleworth Formation.
quartz vein in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite for a trace of gold found within a small offshoot quartz leader. No production figures were determined.
quartz reef carrying rich specimens of gold. Host rock was mica schist of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 4314; ML 4316; ML 4317; ML 5889; MONTACUTE GOLD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu-Au-Ni-Co-Ag mineralisation in quartz reef in host dolomite of the Montacute Dolomite. Production records of 42kg (1,353oz) Au, 4.1t Co-Ni ore, 300t copper ore, 14t copper ore from 1974-79.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Galena,  Gold,  Malachite,  Smaltite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate of the  Woolshed Flat Shale. Production unknown, with grades reported at 7-50oz/tonAu (217-1,555g/tAu), and 40-50% bismuth. Operations ceased in 1873, resuming briefly in 1881.
quartz-iron oxide-kaolin vein carrying silver, lead and antimony mineralisation in host slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Recorded production was 15.6 kg (500 oz) of silver, no tonnage recorded.
quartz reef in host sandstone of the Mitcham Quartzite. The area was reworked from 1931-38. Total production figures unknown, with a package of 33 tonne yielded 626 gm at 19g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CRAWFORD; DOCHERTY; HANCOCKS; KOLLOSCHE AND BARRON; MOLYNEUX; MYSTERY; RICHARDSON; WICKHAMS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide lodes in micaceous schist of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Incomplete production record of 373gm (12oz) from Wickham's shaft.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein in host schist of the Barossa Complex. Recovery generally was poor, with 10 tonnes of ore yielding poor returns. A parcel of 0.9 tonnes yielded 4.1gm gold at 4.6g/tAu. The vein was prospected again in 1935-37.
bed of marble quarried in the early 1900s, and was reworked in 1956. No production figures were recorded.
10-head Government Stamp Battery and Cyanide Works. About 26,000tonnes of tailings remained on site.
mine developed from 1844-46 on a quartz-iron oxide-copper carbonate mineralised vein in host clayey slate of the Woolshed Flat Shale. No production figures were recorded.

1.2m wide quartz-iron oxide vein in host sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. No production figures were determined. The mine was abandoned in 1884 due to a large inlux of groundwater. The reef was prospected again in 1934-36.

siliceous, gossanous rock in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. It was located on the slopes above the Torrens River. Only poor returns were obtained with 6.2 tonnes yielding 29.9gm gold at 4.8g/tAu.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host clayey schist of the Tapley Hill Formation. The mine was located close to and NE of the productive New Era mine. Ore raised showed free gold. No production figures were determined. It was reworked in 1934.
,Au mineralised quartz-iron oxide reef in host sandstone and mica schist of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production ~8,262oz bullion gold.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide vein in host metasediment of the Brighton Limestone. It was reworked in 1895 and again in 1934. Production figures for the mine were incorporated into the production for the New Era Mine.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COLINE D'OR; G.O.M. HUTCHENS; JOHN WESLEY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide, rare galena, zinc blende, pyrite vein in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. Prospecting failed to return any payable gold. The vein was reworked briefly in 1934-36.

quartz reef in host slate of the Saddleworth Formation. Workings consisted of a main shaft and several smaller shafts/pits, some developed on alluvials. Only traces of gold were recovered and the company wound up in 1882.

15-45 cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein, trend EW, dip 55N, and in host Backstairs Passage Formation. The mine was reworked in 1945. Total recorded production was 14.3 tonnes yielding 950.5gm gold at 66g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: FALZON BRICKWORKS; LOBETHAL SHALE; ONKAPARINGA BRICK CO.; PM 305
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of weathered shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Worked for coloured shale products for brickmaking from 1958-88 for ~101,500 tonne. Resource estimate in 1983 of 180,000 tonne. Rehabilitation completed in 1992.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LOBETHAL; ONKAPARINGA BRICK % SAND; ONKAPARINGA BRICKWORKS; PM 288
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: opened in 1935, recorded production of coloured shale products is incomplete. Available figures of 64,360 tonne from 1956-61, and 100 tonnes in 1979. Rehabilitation completed in 1989.
gold-bearing alluvium. No total production figure determined, reported 467gm recovered in 1869.
Au-(Cu-Bi-Pb-Zn) mineralised quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in Barossa Complex metasediment. Production 105oz bullion gold at 9g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Bismuth,  Bismuthinite,  Covellite,  Galena,  Gold,  Malachite,  Sphalerite

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: HOUGHTON SAND AND GRAVEL SUPPLY CO. LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: soft, white, plastic clay developed on deeply weathered, Archean feldspathic gneiss. A minor prospecting shaft removed ~20 tonne in 1940. Further drill tested in 1950's determined an estimated resource of 150,000 tonnes to ~8 m depth.
quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation for only poor returns of gold, no production figures recorded. The best gold was in a gravel patch near the reef.

deeply weathered sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, and worked for building sand in the 1960's. Production for 1964 was reported at 14,733 tonne. The pit ceased production 1999 and has been rehabilitated.
historic building stone quarry on the basket Range Sandstone reworked in 1965-66 for production of 1393 tonne.
small open cut developed on limestone of the Carey Gully Sandstone Member in the 1930s on section 114, Hundred Onkaparinga. Recorded production of 45 tonne in 1933.
quartz-iron oxide lode, trend 070, dip N, in host weathered slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. It was reworked in 1931 via an adit and two shafts. No production figure was determined.
quartz reef in host micaceous sandstone of the Backstairs Passage Formation. A parcel of 42.5kg ore yielded 46.5gm gold at 23.5g/tAu.

operated from 1929-33, and in the late 1970's. The earlier phase of mining produced 4788 tonnes of ore from No.1 and 3 deposits. Production from all 3 mines as recorded against PM 42 in the late 1970s was estimated at 270 tonnes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: J. PORTER; KENTON VALLEY ASBESTOS SYNDICATE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: talc mine operated from 1937-78. Recorded production was 4384 tonnes of ore.
talc mine operated from 1929-33, and in the late 1970's. Most production from earlier mining from No.1 deposit. Production from Porter 3 estimated at 250 tonne.
Au mineralised quartz-iron oxide veins in host schist of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production 285oz bullion gold at 41g/tAu from 1911-1939.
quartz reef in host schist/micaceous hematite rock of the Barossa Complex. A parcel of 4.8 tonnes of ore yielded 115gm gold at 24g/tAu.
clay as weathering product of host slate of the Glen Osmond Slate Member. Recorded production from 1958-61 was 2525 tonnes of fire clay (kaolin).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LOBETHAL SOAPSTONE & FELDSPAR CO.; PYRO-MEG AND FELDSPAR CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: albite dyke in host Saddleworth Formation for recovery of feldspar and talc products. Recorded production for 1930-32 was 5467 tonnes.
sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, and opened in the 1870's for local supply of building stone, reopened in the 1890's for supply of material for use as road base. Production was 13,773 m3 in 1972.
quartz reef in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation. It was reworked in 1924. A parcel of 18.8 tonnes of ore yielded 389.5gm gold at 20.7g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: C. CLARK; ELDRIDGE AND TRINDERS; ENDEAVOUR REEF
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Mitcham Quartzite. Production was mainly from 1870-1895, with later working in 1924 and again in 1930. Total production was estimated at 277.4 tonnes yielding 2527gm gold at 9g/tAu

initially developed in 1895 on gold-bearing alluvium, subsequently development of workings on a quartz reef in host metasediment of the Carrickalinga Head Formation. A parcel of 3 tonnes of ore yielded 22gm gold at 7g/tAu.
Au-Pb mineralised quartz reef in host schist/sandstone of the Neoproterozoic Tarcowie Siltstone. Production from 2766t ore was 16Kg bullion gold, also 6266t tailings treated for 30.4Kg gold.
pit developed on sand recovered from deeply weathered sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup. Last production was in the 1960s. Rehabilitated in 1984. Crushing plant also rehabilitated.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BORAL RESOURCES; MOUNT CHARLES; PM 50; WOODSIDE QUARTZITE; WOODSIDE RUBBISH DUMP
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: operations on deposit in Mitcham Quartzite commenced in the 1940s, ceased by 1970. No complete production figure, reported production >100 tonne per day in 1960. Rehabilitated in 1970s, used as a rubbish dump by the local council.

Tertiary gold-bearing sand, loam and gravel for the entire length of Rocky Gully, along with minor working on quartz reefs in surrounding host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup. No production figure determined.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. It was this find that sparked the first Lobethal gold rush. No production figure was determined.
quartz iron oxide reef in host weathered metasediment of the Mitcham Quartzite. No production figure was determined. It was worked periodically until 1939.
quarry on a quartzite of the Mitcham Quartzite, with 20cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein with rare gold. Rehabilitated in 1991.
deposit of sandstone of the Basket Range Formation for use as dimension stone, with production from 1977- 2013 estimated at >16,000 tonne.
diggings developed as shallow workings on alluvium in 1931. No production figures were recorded.

prospecting in 1933-34 on section 96, presumably on quartz lodes in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Activity ceased post 1934 when the area became a forest reserve. No production figures were recorded.

gold-bearing soil profile on mica schist of Glen Osmond Slate member, with considerable gold recovered initially. Reworked in 1918 with parcels of the weathered rock sent for treatment. Recorded production 75.1t ore for 404gm gold at 5.4g/tAu
gold recovered from the creek bed from 1846. Sporadic activity continuing up to the late 1970s, including minor activity on adjacent quartz reef. No production figure was determined.
quartz reef in host ferruginous sandstone and clayey slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production from 4.8 tonnes of ore was 64.6gm gold at 13g/tAu.
gold-bearing alluvium, and reworked from 1930-31. Production from 4.7 tonnes was 68.4gm gold at 279g/tAu at 14.6g/tAu.
gold-bearing loam and alluvium on section 5171, Hundred Onkaparinga. Traces of gold were recovered from shallow pits and trenches over a wide area, no production figure was determined.

Recent drift sand, loam and gravel to Tertiary drifts of ferruginous conglomerate, and gravels. There was minor working of quartz reefs on the surrounding hillsides, in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. No production figure was determined.
quartz reef in host Stonyfell Quartzite for a parcel of 5.1 tonnes of ore yielding 6.5 gm gold at 1.3g/tAu.

talc-albite lode in host schist of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production from 1941-2013 was >35,000 tonne of pharmecutical, lesser filling grade talc ore. 1978 resource cestimate to 15m, >250,000 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: IRM TALC; ML 3080; TORRENS  MINING CO.
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: talc lode in host Stonyfell Quartzite. No production records for the period 1929-38, from 1939-74 estimated 14,540 tonne pharmecutical-grade talc produced.

quartz-iron oxide infilled shear in host schist of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production was 429 tonnes ore for 5535gm gold at 13g/tAu. There was some production of copper and bismuth, but no production figures were determined.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Bismuthinite,  Bornite,  Chalcopyrite,  Copper,  Cuprite,  Gold,  Malachite,  Wittichite
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Apatite,  Calcite,  Chlorite,  Garnet,  Hematite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Magnetite,  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Sericite,  Sillimanite,  Tourmaline

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry in Tarcowie Siltstone Formation. Unknown if this was a commercial operating quarry or a Departmental Crushing operation circa 1948. Limited correspondence suggests marginal quality both of the rock and the PSD of the products.
developed from 1939-41 on a talc-albite lode in host mica schist of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Recorded production was 152 tonnes.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host sandstone of the Cary Gully Sandstone Member. Recorded production of 3.25 tonnes of ore for 3.3gm gold at 1g/tAu.
quarry on sandstone of the Barossa Complex, dimensions in 1927 of 25m x 30m x 15m, for recovery of >200,000 m3 or 500,000 tonne for SG 2.5.
3 well defined Au-Sn-bearing parallel lodes for recovery of ~500oz (15.6Kg) of fine gold, also rubies and garnets, and minor cassiterite recovered.

talc deposit in host mica schist and quartzite of the Stonyfell Quartzite. The lode of talc-albite rock was subparallel to the host rock. Recorded production from No.1 and no.2 mines from 1939-74 was estimated at 15,000 tonnes.
location uncertain, claim taken out in 1849 on copper show in Woolshed Flat Shale, recorded as on section 5669, Hundred Yatala. No production recorded.
quartz reef carrying Au-As-Pb-Zn mineralisation in host schist/sandstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1882-1936 ~14.5Kg from 2265.8t of ore.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Arsenopyrite,  Galena,  Gold,  Zincian mineral, undifferentiated

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: first operational gold mine in Australia. It was a reef gold-copper occurrence in host metasediment of the Montacute Dolomite, discovered in 1846 and operational to 1851. Production was estimated at 746gm gold, no tonnage determined.

quartz leader in host sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite, and along strike from the McGuires Seam, and on section 5171, Hundred of Onkaparinga. A few grains of gold were recovered by panning, no production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ADELAIDE SYNDICATE; CAMBRIAN; EASTER; GUMERACHA SYNDICATE; HUTCHINSON CLAIM; KAPUNDA SYNDICATE; PHILLIPS UNITED; ROYAL BLACKBIRD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gold at shallow depths in modern alluvium, and in cemented Tertiary sediment on adjacent hillsides. Production ~1000oz (31Kg).
small open cut developed on a lens of alluvial sediment in 1918. Lack of water led to early closure. No production figures were reported.

quarry developed on quartzite of the Belair Subgroup by Quarry Industries until early 1970s. Reopened by Gumeracha DC from 1986 to about 1990. It was rehabilitated in 1994, with further rehabilitation in 2006 by Adelaide Hills Council.
alluvials in the gullies returned payable gold, with some nice specimens of nuggety gold reported. Location used was bed of the most prominent creek within the old Woodhouse Estate area.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation. Production from 1879-92 was estimated at 200oz (6221 gm). Rich pockets of gold ore were reported.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LANGBEIN; ML 3003; MORONYS; PM 78; WOODSIDE FIRECLAY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine developed in 1956 on a clay deposit in host weathered shale of the Glen Osmond Slate Member. Recorded production from 1956-61 was 2445.6 tonne of fire clay (kaolin).

deposit of dolomite in host metasediment of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Production from 1978-86 was estimated at 28,340 tonnes of dolomite products, minor sand products. Rehabilitation was completed in 1988.

ferruginous quartz veins in host metasediment of the Carey Gully Sandstone Member via several costeans and shallow shafts on sections 1154 and 3929, Hundred Onkaparinga. Samples from 2 lodes assayed  5g/tAu, and 40g/tAu.

deeply weathered sandstone of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production of sandstone products from 1977-2008 was estimated at 10,000 tonne of multiple products for the construction industry. Quarry is being progressively rehabilitated.
gold mineralisation in sheet conglomerate overlying basement of Palaeoproterozoic rock. No production figures.
5 claims taken out in 1928 on a graphite lode in host Peake Metamorphics. Trenching recovered 18.3 tonne material at 20-25%C, but the graphite proved to be too fine for economic sale.

copper mineralised outcrop traced 450m along strike. Small workings on lode with improved grades at depth. Exploration by Australasian Mining Corp Ltd in 4 diamond holes in 1970 for U identified best value 290 ppm U3O8 from 24-26.21m in hole DDH 1.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Hematite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Magnetite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gold show in Curdimurka Subgroup, located from mine symbol on Oodnadatta 250K MEIS sheet. Described as 20-25 km NW of Algebuckina homestead, and further up the Neales River.
copper show in Curdimurka Subgroup, located from mine symbol on Geological Survey internal 250k mineral occurrences map.
lease granted in 1946 on Tertiary clay deposit, no production.
4 claims, 9 miles and 4 miles north-west from Oodnadatta, granted in 1923 for ochre. Host rock was a ferruginous shale/clay, red and mauve in colour. Production from 1924-25 of 103.6 tonne.

Permian coal deposit in the Arckaringa Coalfield consisting of 6-7 persistent seams, with a cumulative thickness of up to 20m. Ttop of mineable coal at a depth of 220-300m. Resource ~690Mt of sub-bituminous coal.
workings for alluvial gold developed by J.L. Able on Tertiary colluvium to alluvial conglomerate. Workings located on claim nos. 959, and 1071, and on township blocks 383, 384, 385, Hundred Coglin.

quartz-specular hematite in host Belair Subgroup, and worked intermittently in shallow pits from 1886-96 for Au & Ag, without success. A sample from a large quartz lode on section 82 returned ~1.6g/tAu.

calcrete developed by local council for road ballast. Point location is that for Hundred Morgan, section 53. Quarry returns of 51,400 ton from 1938-51 are for this scrape, plus pits on Hundred Yongala, sections 16, and 52.
location uncertain. Recorded as section 218, Hundred Yongala on north Peterborough. 20m deep shaft on a narrow 30-40cm quartz vein in host Appila Tillite. Recorded 10 tonne for 40gm gold at 4g/tAu.
shaft adjacent to Triumph Mine, and on the Waukaringa line of lode. No details determined, presumed workings on quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation.
pits on dolomitic slate of the Skillogalee Dolomite developed by the local council for road ballast on the Port Germein to Murray Town road near Bangor. Quarry returns for 1925-48 were 59,284 tonne.
magnesite deposit in host Lower Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. BHP worked the deposit from 1914-19, with incomplete records of 37 tons produced in 1916.
stratabound Cu mineralisation in host shale of the Tapley Hill Formation. Estimated production was 40,000 tonne @ 5%Cu.

underlie shaft developed at the turn of the 19th century on a quartz-iron oxide vein in host schist of the Appila Tillite. Recorded production of >4oz (124gm) gold from 17 tonnes ore. ~1km S of Hennigs and on same line of lode.
located 27.4 km northeast from Quorn. A sample taken by the Inspector of Mines assayed 32% Mn, and he reported good ore in sight (1891).
stratabound Pb-Zn mineralisation in host Parachilna Formation, with minor historic workings developed on surface enriched, manganese rich unit.

quartz-iron oxide vein 30cm to 2m wide with copper carbonates as nodules, splashes, disseminated in host rock adjacent to vein. Workings extend NE for >600m. Ore minerals dominantly malachite and azurite.

copper mineralised vein in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production of several hundred tonnes reported of ore raised in the 1870s for unknown tonnage of hand picked ore product at ~15%Cu, some cobalt ore reported as well.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings in 1945 on Township Blocks 388, 391, and 26, Hundred Coglin. Located N of the railway station, presumably on deposits of gold-bearing Tertiary colluvium to conglomerate. records for production of 46.5 tonne ore for 47gm gold at 1g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: RADFORD CREEK; SA LAND MORTGAGE & AGENCY CO.

MINEROLOGY_ORE: Malachite,  Rare Earths,  Uranium Minerals (Non Specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small pit of ~1,800m2 x 1-5m deep developed by SA railways in 1964 on dolerite for use as railway ballast. Located on declared Railway Reserve 312.
quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation worked by the SA Railways in the early 1900s. Re-opened in 1965 for production of 5,000m3. Estimated remaining resource 40,000m3.

quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and equivalent to Main Reef. The mine operated from 1881-89, no production figure was determined. A grab sample from the lode assayed 14g/tAu.

hematite-goethite lode in slate and limestone host of the Tapley Hill Formation, and on section 108, Hundred Morgan. Prospected for gold in 1898 via open cuts and shallow shafts. Sampling failed to return anomalous assays.
location innacurate, reported as section 112 Hundred Pekina, and close to the boundary with Hundred Tarcowie. No large deposit recognised. Asample returned a value of 63% Ca3P2O5.

phosphate rock occurring in irregular pockets and vein like structures where secondary faulting has occurred in host Koonunga Phosphorite. Production from 2006-13 >10,000 tonne. Resources ~60,000 tonnes to 10m depth at 4%P cutoff.
location uncertain, recorded as on Section 20, Hundred Uroonda, and south of Chalcome. Prospecting pits on copper shows in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite.
shallow prospecting pits excavated in 1907 on a quartz-iron oxide lode, with malachite in host limestone of the Saddleworth Formation.
small workings ~1400m E of the main Alma Shaft, and on the Waukaringa line-of-lode on a low EW-trending ridge of Tapley Hill Formation. No details determined, located from plan no. 1981-0412.
claim taken out over a series of manganese-oxide bearing quartz veins worked for silver in 1886 for about 3 months. Host was sandstone and claystone, possibly Saddleworth Formation.
deposit of grey-white, plastic clay developed on weathered shale of the Cambrian Mernmerna Formation. Worked in 1933-34 for recovery of ~10t of clay product.

lode few cm to 2m wide. Production 1897 195 kg copper ore from 5.1 tonnes of ore, and in 1898, 483.4 kg of copper ore from 2 tonnes ore. Mineralogy calcite, chalcocite, malachite, and red copper oxide.
quartz-iron oxide vein in host Skillogalee Formation, and carrying copper and silver mineralisation. Location uncertain, given as Hundred Eurelia, section 84.

persistent quartz-iron oxide reef carrying copper mineralisation for recovery of ~175 tonne of hand picked ore. Host was tillite of the Emeroo Subgroup. Diamond drill hole identified oxidised lode at depth.

location uncertain, recorded as Hundred Walloway, allotment 320. 50 ton limestone excavated in 1939 for the manufacture of lime.

part of the Aureous line-of-lode, workings developed on quartz-iron oxide lode in host slate of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Recorded production from 1900-01 of 30.58 tonnes for 90.21gm bullion gold at 3g/tAu.
well defined 30-60cm wide quartz-iron oxide lode trend NE, dip 45NW in host metasediment of the Umberatana Group.

occurrence in host Uroonda Siltstone Member, located from Orroroo 1:250K MEIS mineral occurrences map sheet only, no further information.

workings on magnesite beds in host Skillogalee Dolomite by Franke and Hooper in 1924. Production 189 tonne.
sedimentary magnesite beds to 1.6m thick in host Skillogalee Dolomite. BHP extracted bulk sample by underground mining in 1944.

host is metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, no further details, located from mine symbol on the State Government unpublished 250K mineral occurrences map dataset.

copper and gold mineralisation in an iron oxide-quartz lode in host talc schist of the Appila Tillite. Ore minerals included chalcocite and malachite. A 6 tonne sample of hand sorted ore assayed 37%Cu.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lode of quartz-iron oxide carrying malachite in host slate of the Appila Tillite. Worked in several shallow workings from 1890 to the mid 1910s.
pit developed in 1936 in alluvial clay deposit for recorded production of 14t.
or Broken Hill Syndicate, historic workings developed on quartz blow in host Saddleworth Formation, and on the Lovely Gully Goldfields. No production figure determined.

location uncertain, recorded as about half mile NE of Oodlawirra, and on section 17, Hundred Coglin. Shaft developed by T. Ward in 1908 on Tertiary ironstone. 1 sample with estimated grade 80% ochre per ton, but no production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 3432; EML 3433; EML 3434; EML 3435; EML 3436; NORTON MARBLE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: marble resource worked in main pit on ~10m wide marble unit, dip 60E for building aggregate. The marble was reddish to red-grey, with pale purple-brown streaking. It was of the Nuccaleena Formation. Production 1963-74 of 1,411 tonne.
on Waukaringa line-of-lode, no details known, presumably developed on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, located from plan no. 1981-0412.
discovered in 1885, and four claims were pegged. A shaft was sunk, and the ore, assaying 72% MnO, was raised and shipped to England. Blocks of 10-12 tonnes were found on the surface.

quartz lode carrying minor argentiferous galena in host Tapley Hill Formation. Spot geochemical sampling of dumps returned anomalous silver values. Incomplete production record of 2 tonnes for 334gm gold bullion at 165g/tAu

quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Lode trended EW, width variable from 38-137 cm, average 60cm. Sample from lode in 1907 above water table assayed 5g/t. No production figures apparent.

located at SW end of the Ajax group of mines. No individual historical details, presumed working on quartz lode in host Tarcowie Siltstone. Reported production to end 1947 of 102 tonnes for 1309gm gold at 12.8g/tAu.
2 quartz-iron oxide lodes in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and on the Waukaringa line of lode. Recorded production to 1941 was 1163 tonnes for 23,441.5 gm gold at 20.2g/tAu.
2 seam of manganese oxide adjacent to dolomite beds in the Tarcowie Siltstone. 3 small shafts have been excavated.
no details, located at the western extremity of the line of lode for the Waukaringa Goldfield, presumably on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation.

small, circular, deep depocentre, with multiple thin coal seams of Triassic age in 5 drill holes from ~40m depth. Samples of doubtful quality gave analyses of 49.44% fixed carbon, and 8.94% ash. Seams considered to be non-economic.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: WILLOWIE FOREST RESERVE; WILLOWIE MANGANESE WADS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: analysis in 1886 returned values in manganese oxide with cobalt 1.7-2.31%. Inex Pty Ltd confirmed Co-Cu-Zn anomalism in manganese wad in 1991. No further testing was carried out. Host rock was metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation.
prospecting of ~180m strike length of copper shows in 1908 in host 2-3m wide grey shale bed in purple shale of the Wilmington Formation.
exploration of a manganese blow in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. An analysis returned 155 gm/tonne silver.

one of several ventures near the Penn Mine. It has not been accurately located. It developed in 1903 on a quartz-iron oxide vein carrying copper carbonate mineralisation in host slate of the Appila Tillite.

located on Hundred Yanyarrie, section 168, and 7 miles NNW of Carrieton, was worked for manganese ore in 1933 from a shaft and shallow open cut. Production in 1933 was 12 tonne, then 145 tonne from 1940-42 (total 157 tonne).
small brickyard developed in the 1920s on clays in an alluvial fan of the Pekina Creek. No production figure determined.
small prospecting pit that revealed short fibre crocidolite in host soft dolomitic limestone. Small occurrence of talc nearby.
Approx location only, described as 1.7km west of Blinman on the Parachilna Road. Open cut excavated in 1907 for 48 ton of ore treated at Blinman for recovery of 2.5 ton of copper at 5%Cu.
shaft with drive on a lode ~1m (3 feet) wide, dip low to the SE. It was composed of feldspar with small veins of chalcopyrite and chalcocite.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite lode in host sandstone and slate of the ABC Range Quartzite, and exposed on the steep slope of a hill. The lode varies from 0-2.5m wide, trends NS for !45m.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite lode in host sandstone and slate of the ABC Range Quartzite, and exposed on the steep slope of a hill. The lode varies from 0-2.5m wide, trends NS for !45m.

lode 2m wide with few small veins and pockets of copper carbonate ore, and large quantity of specular hematite. At 13.7m rock less weathered, fresh sulphides encountered of pyrite, but little primary copper sulphides.

strong calcite lode, ~2 m wide, on which a shaft was excavated to 6m depth. The lode contained green copper carbonate ore, chalcocite, and iron oxides, with the mineralisation of low grade only, no production figures were recorded.
guano deposits in an extensive belt of caves developed on a vertically dipping unit of dolomite of considerable strike length. It was worked for less than 1 year, no production figures were recorded.

extensive area of decomposed dolomitic siltstone with small pockets of crocidolite. Discovered 1886, worked for <1 year, prospected by different ventures until 1957. No production figure recorded. Host metasediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
copper show opened up in the early 1860's, and worked again in the 1890's. No production records were preserved.
small workings on a copper mineralised iron-oxide gossan, 1-2 m wide. First opened in 1873, then again in 1899. In 1914, ~10 tonnes of 55% copper ore was produced.

location uncertain, recorded as 1.7km S of Irvines Lookout (see plan 6981-1 in envelope 6981). Silver-lead occurrence in Woodendinna Dolomite, reported in Record of Mines of South Australia, 1899 edition.
steep barite lodes in fracture zone cross cutting host shale of the Tapley Hill Formation. Recorded production of 2000t from 1973-78. Resource ~13,000t.

stratabound Cu mineralisation persisting along strike for 7.2km, within narrow quartz-siderite layer in Sturtian Wilyerpa Formation. Production from 1901-52 293t raised, 34.5t treated, yield 5.1t copper metal product.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BARATTA; EUKABY; ML 2017; ML 2032; ML 2033; ML 5362; ML 5758; NEW DISCOVERY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: structurally controlled Ag-Pb vein mineralisation in host, folded Tapley Hill Formation metasediment. From 1925-27 35.6t hand sorted ore yielded 24.4t lead, 35.8kg silver.
prospecting on an ironstone blow in limestone of the Curdimurka Subgroup. Though samples returning good silver values were reported subsequent prospecting returned no assay values of interest.
workings developed in 1967 on a barite lode in host metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation. Recorded production was 25.4 tonne.

ferruginous pseudogossan with weakly anomalous base metals and arsenic geochemistry. The occurrence sits astride a major ENE-trending fault. Probable origin development over sideritic veins in host siltstone of the Sunderland Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLINMAN IRONSTONE; BROWN AND FARGNERS; MC 3335
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: pear-shaped outcropping mass of hematite, with a NS-orientated long axis, hosted by diapiric breccia. It was originally mined for iron flux for use in the Blinman Mine copper smelters. Remaining resources were estimated at 35,560 tonne.

Aboriginal Ochre Reserve, red ochre, developed in narrow seams in Wilkawillina Limestone. Small beads of mercury detected, confirmed by testwork which returned 0.5%Hg from one sample. Some willemite is associated with the ochre.
copper mineralisation in host metasediment of the Curdimurks Subgroup. Recorded production was ~137 tonnes at ~4.5% Cu.

several lines of steeply dipping, manganiferous crush zones striking parallel to the bedding of the host Woodendinna Dolomite. No production figures were recorded. A resource estimate to a depth of 1.2m was 508 tonnes.
barite lode in Brachina Formation. Lode trends 080 dips 70N. Average width is 60cm for a distance of 60m. Bulk sample gave BaSO4 92.6%, SrSO4 3.1%, and SiO2 3.75%o. Possible resource of 2,000 tonne.
no details, located from mine symbol on unpublished State mineral occurrence 250K map series. Presume vein-barite in host ABC Range Quartzite Member.
located from mine symbol on unpublished State mineral occurrences 250K map series. Host sequence from 100K digital geology dataset is of the Bayley Range Siltstone Member.

ferruginous pseudogossan after siderite, with only weak malachite development. Host was siltstone of the Sunderland Formation. Located on a major NE-trending fault, tracable for >20km. No potential for an economic copper deposit.
workings on copper lode in host River Wakefield Formation.
workings developed in 1947 on lead-silver lode in host Enorama Shale. Production from 1947-50 was reported to be 2 tonne of lead metal and 400gm of silver. Ore raised not specified.

deposit of very pure, fine grained kaolinite stretching for 100m along a 3m high cliff face on the northern bank of Gum Creek. It was used as a refractory clay in the zinc smelters at Broken Hill, being considered a quality source of refractory clay.
location highly uncertain, recorded as Hundred Moralana, Block 16, and near Arkaba Homestead. Copper show worked in 1897. Possibly same as the Mora occurrence (mindep # 6399).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MC 10898; MC 10899; MC 10900; OLD EDEOWIE; SOUTHERN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: anomalous values of Pb & Zn in the lower dolomitic member of the Wilkawillina Limestone near major faulting, and in calc-dolomite unit near mapped smithsonite gossans. Manganese deposit on palaeo-surface.
silver-lead lode in host dolomite of the Woodendinna Dolomite, with minor production of 2.54 tonne lead, 1.1kg silver in 2 periods, 1949, and 1956.
old workings on copper lode in host metasediment of the Moolooloo Siltstone Member.
MnO mineralisation in crush zones in host basal Cambrian Woodendinna Dolomite. Production from 1940-47 ~5175t @ 45%MnO.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Clay mineral,  Dolomite,  Iron oxide (non specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: traverse of 3 holes identified outcropping phosphate rock as gently undulating capping on erosion surface on cherty limestone. Further drilling recommended at contact of the Parara - Wilkawillina Limestone.
numerous surface workings and shafts developed on eleven identified quartz veins striking NE, with widths from 60 cm upwards in host Enorama Shale. Assays carried anomalous Pb, and Ag.
area of shallow pits and shafts to 30 m depth, in particular focused on one quartz lode to 1 m wide, and of ~180 m strike extent in host Tapley Hill Formation.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au-Pb-Zn bearing quartz-iron oxide lode in host contorted, laminated siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1973-96 16.9kg bullion gold, 5600kg Ag, 170t Pb. Drilling confirmed pipe-like shoot of low-grade Pb-Ag-Au mineralisation.
