DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: zone of several Pb-Ag mineralised quartz-carbonate veins in host metasediment of the Enorama Shale on S limb of a regional syncline, with beds dipping 45NW. Workings consisted of shafts, pits and costeans. No production figure.

series of enechelon lodes each approximately 10m long, with maximum thickness 60cm in host Enorama Shale. The barite quality is good, but costeaning showed no increase in continuity or thickness with depth to 6m.
manganese oxide located in shear zones in the Woodendinna Dolomite. Workings in several small open cuts exposed faces of soft manganese ore. Recorded production in 1960 was 11 tonne of manganese ore.
surface float containing copper and galena were reported to have yielded good silver and lead assays, though later sampling did not confirm this.
extensive cave system in blue and grey limestone, with interbeds of slate, and of the Tapley Hill Formation. A pit and shaft were excavated on bat guano deposits in the early 1930's (MR058, p32).

several diggings on 2 parallel lodes of copper mineralisation in host siltstone of the Curdimurka Subgroup inspected in 1899. Disseminated malachite, azurite, and chalcocite. A surface sample assayed 32% Cu. No recorded production.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host shale and sandstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Position uncertain, located on section 16, Hundred Arkaba. No production figure determined.
small show of manganese oxide on a water works reserve with special permission given to peg mineral claims. These were taken up in 1918 and some production ensued.
discovered in 1942 by L.C. Dulfen, phosphate as nodules in clay, with MnO staining, in host limestone of the Mernmerna Formation. Samples assayed 6-48% Ca3P2O5.

small, sparse outcrop primarily a ferruginous diamictite. The potential as a low-grade beneficiable iron ore resource appeared limited by its small size and beneficiation difficulties. It had no magnetic expression.
claim staked in the 1960s over a barite lode in host metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation.
copper lode trending EW, 80cm wide in host soft, argillaceous limestone of the Curdimurka Subgroup.

no definite lode, copper stained metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation worked in shallow pits pre 1899. Tested in 3 diamond holes  in 2015 for return of no significant geochemical values for Au, Ag, Cu, Zn.

lode of quartz-iron and manganese oxide, with chalcopyrite, malachite, azurite, red copper oxides, and pyrite in host clay, sandstone and shale of the Kirwan Siltstone. Only a small tonnege of ore was raised.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Pyrite,  Quartz

surface show of copper mineralisation in vein siderite in host metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation, and located along the fold axis of the Bibliando Dome, and on its western flank.
copper lode in host Curdimurka Subgroup. recorded production of 275.3 tonnes, with 199 tonnes treated, grade estimated at 2%Cu.
location uncertain, small occurrence of asbestos and feldspar in host Brachina Formation, tenure granted in 1941.
barite lode to 0.4m wide developed in a breccia fault zone at the boundary of quartzite and calcareous siltstone of the Trezona Formation.
small manganese show in Etina Limestone host. Numerous small pods, scattered lensoid masses. Resource ~100 tons at 24% Mn. Grab samples showed anomalous Cu, Zn, Co, Ba, Li, Ti, Sr.

manganese oxide as scattered, loose blocks of black rock, with a brecciated appearance. Also tabular lens of pyrolusite and manganite emplaced along fracture planes. The resource was estimated at ~150 tons at 36% Mn.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COADS HILL; E.M. COAD; FOUR CORNERS; MARTINS WELL; ML 4519
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite in host metasediment of the Trezona Formation. Production from 1976-93 of an estimated 1,700 tonnes from lode ~300m in length, trend ENE along a major ENE fault tracabe for ~18km.
mineralisation of red copper oxide in host Tapley Hill Formation as a southern extension of the Prince Alfred lode, discovered in the 1870s, no recorded production from shallow workings.

prospect for iron ore located in the Middleback Range and ~14.5 km NNE of the Iron Prince mine. It was an occurrence of lateritised goethite, to goethitic BIF drill tested by the Mines Department in the mid 1940s, no resource figure published.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML; ML 115; ML 116; ML 68; ML 83; OCEAN SALT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mining leases held from the 1920s to the 1940s over 1,445 acres of area of a salt lake. Production from 1921-47 estimated at 98,500t.

sparse copper sulphides in narrow band of chlorite schist interbedded with quartzite of the Skillogalee Dolomite, and over ~360m. Results disappointing (Cu to 235 ppm, Zn to 145 ppm, Pb to 56 ppm), with no encouragement for follow-up exploration.
prominent linear magnetic anomaly trend over 12km, source magnetite-bearing BIF of the Lower Middleback Jaspilite. Inferred resource 194Mt @ 27.1%Fe.
old pits developed on deposit of recent gravel for use as road base material.
location uncertain, mine summary card location given as 6km NE of Port Augusta West on sections 237, 205.
minor workings on Cu-mineralised, ferruginous quartz vein in host diorite of the Beda Volcanics. Several parcels of payable ore raised, no recorded production figures.
several leases taken out on a small resource of gypsum.

Australia's first major producer of iron ore for steelmaking. Initial tonnage mined for flux for Port Pirie smelters. Total production 731,500t from 1899-1915. 2 tabular zones of massive hematite dipping steeply E in host Proterozoic ferruginous mica schist.
Reported as on water reserve #47. Production of 26 tonne in 1941.
copper mineralised lode in host Skillogalee Dolomite worked in a single shaft prior to 1899. Production of 1.2 tonne @ 13%Cu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MINERALS PTY LTD; TURNERS; WHITE FRIEND; WHYALLA BARYTES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: barite as a series of near vertical lenses traced discontinuously for 570m along fault offshoot in host Pandurra Formation. Production 2188 tonne from 1938-67.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CARDASSIS; CROZIER; ML 2833; ML 2834; MUNDALLIO BHP; MUNDALLIO STATION
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: magnesite occurred as beds up to 1 m thick interbedded with dolomite, chert and siltstone of the Skillogalee Dolomite. A total of 2,554 tonnes was produced continuously from 1940-53.

on surface as loose stones, also as fragments, geoids to maximum 2cm in host sandstone of the Pandurra Formation. Finely banded alternating red-white is common variety, some shades of grey. Some carnelian and amethyst crystals occur.
shear-hosted Cu mineralisation in lode at contact of Whyalla Sandstone and Tregolana Shale. Resource estimate @ 122,000t @ 0.3-0.4%Cu. Mapping indicated possible strike extensions.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: J.C. PAUL AND J.R. GORDON; MC 1822; ML 3051; MRS L.W. KOSTER; NORTHERN PLASTIC POTTERY CLAYS; W.G. KOSTER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: kaolinised Tregolana Shale. The off-white clay was used for pottery manufacture, minor brick making. Recorded production from 1956-61 of 244 tonne.
quarry developed on a deposit of quartzite, possibly Simmons Quartzite Member, for use as road base material.
Quatrnary alluvials in active creek, with the operation mining the current bedload. Previous tenure on Hundred Copley, sections 215, 219. 1972 production of ~8,000 tonne.
location uncertain, recorded as 9 km NW of Hesso railway siding and adjacent to the railway line. Produced 49 tonne of building stone, presumably of the Whyalla sandstone from 1954-1963.

area of ~8Ha of council pits, and developed on Quaternary dunal red-brown sand, with minor pedogenic calcrete. Located on sections 217, 219, Hundred Copley for recorded production of ~17,000 tonne from 1923-52.

stratabound copper mineralisation in arkosic siltstone of the Bungaree Quartzite. Tested in 4 diamond holes for disappointing geochemical values. Mineralisation occured in 2 horizons, extending over 800m in the upper horizon, and 300m in the lower.

2 barite lodes from 0.5-2m wide in host metasediment of the Umberatana Group worked in shallow excavations from 1913-17, and again from 1940-59 for recorded production of 822 tonne of mostly 2nd grade product.

copper, malachite in quartz-iron oxide-carbonate vein in host metasediment of Umberatana Group, mined in 1874-75, and again in 1891-92 in shallow pits and a shaft to 25.6m. Location uncertain, reported as 1.7km NW of Saltia railway station.

red copper oxide, copper carbonates, and sulphides worked in shallow shafts prior to 1899. It was located adjacent to the boundary of the Appila Tillite and Tapley Hill Formation. Grab sample of ore assayed 37.5%Cu.
low hill of Palaeoproterozoic BIF west of Middleback Range. Reconnaissance drilling identified magnetite-bearing BIF, grade ~30%Fe, 1 sample for DTR testwork gave favourable results.

mining lease granted in 1946 on a clay deposit exposed in a 10m high cliff face on the west bank of a creek. The off-white, gypsiferous clay was formed from deep weathering of the Tregolana Shale. Suitable for pottery manufacture.
copper show in Skillogalee Dolomite, with prospecting claim granted in 1914.
white kaolinised shale and siltstone quarried for furnace lining clays. Kaolinised shale and siltstone and sandy interbeds, consisting of weathered Tapley Hill Formation.

mining lease worked in the 1960s for red clay and kaolin, which were blended for use in brickmaking. The kaolin developed as the product of deep weathering of Adelaidean metasediment in an area of faulting. No recorded production figure apparent.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LEASE 3420; PORT AUGUSTA BRICKYARD; ZANKER BRICKCLAY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: old pit developed on clay floodplain deposit to supply material for brickmaking for local use in Port Augusta.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PM 144; PORT AUGUSTA BRICKYARDS; ZANKERS PORT AUGUSTA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: clay pit possibly partially filled. Only production figure located was 356 tonne in July-Dec 1972. .

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; MC 1244; MC 1245; MC 16095; MC 16150; MC 1777; MC 344; MC 754; STOECKEL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council rubble pits on Pleistocene calcrete, production from several MCs estimated at 118,000 tonne for road base material from 1937-1952.
deposit of Tertiary limestone. Recorded production from 1940-82 was estimated at 7385 tonnes. The quarry was rehabilitated in 1987.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLANCHETOWN PLAIN; EML 6169; EML 6170; EML 6171; LINKE GYPSUM; ML 4921; ML 4922; ML 4984; ML 4985; ML 4986; ML 535; ML 5961; ML 6357; ML 650; ML 651; ML 652; ML 653; ML 657
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposits of gypsum around margins of topographic lows and ~2m from top of host Blanchetown Clay. Resource ~30Mt in 1980 @ 81-85% gypsum, with good potential for additional resources. Production from 1989-2015 ~3.2Mt.
prospect taken up for clay in 1959 in mineral claims 2542-45. The clay was tested but found to be of poor quality, with the claims abandoned by 1961.

white limestone of Morgan Limestone. Initial high demand locally for building stone. First production 1858 for Overland Corner Hotel, main production 1945-58 for ~11,000 tonne for 6,000 tonne ashlars, ie 55% recovery for tonnes mined.
deposit of tripoli as remnants of fresh water lake of Coonambidgal Formation of Pleistocene age, maximum thickness ~3m. Resource estimate 2740 tonne, a sample assayed 88.82% SiO2, 7.755 Al2O3.
production of 12 tonne dimension stone limestone of the Tertiary Murray Group in 1941.
recorded as near Cobdogla, west of Sugarloaf, and on old section 10. Production from 1947-61 estimated at 11,900 tonne calcrete for road making and building stone.
Bungunnia limestone 1-2m thick, with underlying Loxton Sand to 6m deep. Quarry commenced operations in 1989. Production to 2000 estimated at 12,800 tonne for road base material.

Tertiary limestone for road making, minor for lime manufacture. Production figures are cumulative for many sections, and are not specific to this point location. Recorded production of Keane operations from 1938-52 of 786,812t.
located on Section 14, Hundred Markaranka, pit developed on Pleistocene Ripon Calcrete for road ballast for recorded production of  3471 tonne from 1930-41.
Holocene sand, seasonal production from 1972-83 of 2880 tonne of garden sand product.
not located accurately, recorded as Hundred Holder, section 71, and some 15km NE of Maggea in the Riverland mallee country. 10 ton production in 1952.
pit opened in 1958 on a clay deposit for local use in the manufacture of cement.
mine worked by Aborigines for chert for tools, and for ochre.

area of abandoned roadside council pits of ~500m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on calcrete on Hundred Paringa, declared road reserve on section 68, and western part section 118, and for use as road fill.
leases taken out for gypsum mining of gypsiferous dune and lake beds adjacent to a railway line in 1916-25. No production figures recorded.

abandoned roadside council pit of ~2,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed in the 1920s by the local council for road fill on a thin 0.6m thick mantle of Pleistocene calcrete over Pliocene sand, gravel, and marl.

deposits of yellow, hard siliceous limestone marginal to the lake were assessed for use in construction of the proposed Chowilla Dam. Also a miscellaneous licence for salt adjacent to the railway siding granted in 1938.
Pleistocene calcrete worked for road base material. The pit closed in 1983 and rehabilitation was completed. Production from 1973-1983 was ~188,000 tonne.
sand of the Holocene Coonambidgel Formation, worked for over 50 years, though only recorded production against EMLs 4005-06 was 2134 tonne in July-Dec 1972.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 4125; EML 4841; EML 5566; EML 5831; LOXTON CRUSHING SITE; LOXTON/GORDON CC#1; LOXTON/GORDON CC#2; LOXTON/GORDON CC#3
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarries on a deposit of surface Quaternary calcrete. Two adjacent shallow open cuts for production for the period 2000-2013 of >760,000t.
shallow quarry of ~1Ha x 1-2m deep worked a bed of oyster shells for shell grit for lime manufacture. Now a recreational, area, and environmental reserve.
abandoned, elongate council pit of >40,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on low ridge of white, pedogenic Pleistocene calcrete for road fill material.
Holocene gypsum deposit of the Woorinen Formation worked periodically from 1917-53 for production of >1120 tonne for use in agriculture.
tenure granted in 1956 on limestone of the Murray Group for buiding stone. No production recorded, resource estimated at 10-15,000 tonne mineable.
worked a limestone deposit for building stone from 1940 to the 1960s, recovering 1121 tonnes.

gypsiferous dunes of Yamba Formation. Source of agricultural gypsum for Riverland from early 1900s. Drilling located further large resources. Recorded production from 1916 17,790t, but considerable mining without mineral tenure.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANLABY; DUCK PONDS; LINKES; SITE E
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: weathered, friable, iron oxide stained siltstone of the Appila Tillite worked for road base material.
abandoned council quarry of ~8,000m2 x 10m deep, and developed on weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation for recorded production from 1950-52 of ~650 tonne for road fill material.
silver-lead mineralised quartz vein in host phyllite of the Mintaro Shale. From 1848-51 more than 152 tonnes of galena ore was produced, as well as a few tonnes of copper ore, no grades determined.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Argentite,  Azurite,  Bornite,  Cerussite,  Chalcocite,  Covellite,  Digenite,  Galena,  Malachite,  Smithsonite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: soft grey and brown siltstone of the Auburn Dolomite quarried for road building purposes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MANOORA CC; SADDLEWORTH CC; TRANSPORT SA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry on Gilbert Range Quartzite, no total production figures, production in 1956 was reported as 200-250 tonnes per day.

weatherd quartzite of the Stonyfell Quartzite in early 1900s for building stone. 3 quarries opened in the 1960s-80s for road rubble and building stone. Current lease as PM 122. 2 quarries rehabilitated, one operating, 224 tonne in 1972.
quarry developed on a siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation for use as road base material.
prospecting venture developed in 1919-20 on a quartz-iron oxide vein carrying visible galena in host clayey slate of the Gilbert Range Quartzite. No payable ore was recovered.
in 1956 production was reported as 610 tonnes per day from quartzite of the Appila Tillite. No total production figures apparent.
shale for use as road base material. It was the largest quarry in the Saddleworth district.

abandoned council quarry of <2,000m2 x 1-8m deep, and developed on grey shale of the Saddleworth Formation, overlain by thin mantle of Pleistocene calcrete. Historically it was an important source of material for use in road making.
quarry developed on blue-grey siltstone to fine, sandy shale of the Mintaro Shale for road base material.
council quarry on Section 136. Production from 1950-52 was estimated at 11,800 tonne dolomite of the Skillogalee Formation, and for use as road base material.

shallow, abandoned council pit of >5,000m2 x 1-5m deep located immediately west of the Barrier Highway, and developed on varicoloured, weathered shale to sandy shale of the Saddleworth Formation, and for use as road fill.
road side scrape for road metal on steeply dipping, pale grey phyllite of the Saddleworth Formation.

quartz-gossan veins on host weathered Bonney Sandstone drill tested in 4 holes, Returned best interval 1m at 0.66%Pb from 143m in MRRC002. Hole 6 was located adjacent to an historic prospecting shaft, possibly excavated on quartz veins for gold.
several pits in Tertiary quartz conglomerate.

surface deposit of kunkar and lateritic nodular ironstone, with minor vein quartz overlying basement rock of white quartzite and siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation. Material described as providing good rubble.

abandoned council  pit of <5,000m2 x 1-4m deep on deeply weathered shale, and quartzite of the Skillogalee Dolomite of the Mundallio Subgroup of the Burra Group, and overlain by a thin mantle of Pleistocene calcrete.
abandoned council pit developed on grey to fawn shales, strike north, dip steep east, and overlain by thin 30-60cm mantle of Pleistocene calcrete.
abandoned council pit on weathered siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill material.

abandoned council pit of ~1,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on weathered green, massive, soft claystone and shale of the Saddleworth Formation. It was too soft to provide good rubble, but satisfactory foor use on secondary roads.
pit on shale for road ballast. Located on road reserve between sections 902 and 904, Hundred Gilbert. No production figure recorded, no trace of pit remaining.

scattered deposits of flour seed gypsum in a lunette dune system. Production on campaign basis from 1919-61 of ~52,000 tonne for use in plasterboard manufacture. Resource 1984 of ~243,000 tonne at 43% gypsum.
broad area of low grade U mineralisation in paleo river sediments.
broad area of low grade U mineralisation in palaeo river sediments.
broad area of low grade U mineralisation in palaeo river sediments.
no references, known only from map no 1999-0596 in unpublished Geol Surv plans database. Small group of workings immediately SW of the Welcome Home & Golden Hope group of workings.
reported as on GS 807, located in granite and west of the historic hospital reserve. Recorded production 1903-41 of  1048 tonne ore for 12567gm gold at 12g/tAu.
no details, possibly eastern shaft of Tarcoola Consols on gold lease 1040. Reported quartz-iron oxide-galena lode in host kaolinised slate of the Tarcoola Formation.
no details known, located from plan 1999-0596 in Geol Survey internal plans database. Field check in 2002 failed to locate any trace of workings.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COMPANY WELL; LAKE LABYRINTH; THESEUS PROJECT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mine on the Lake Labyrinth Goldfield. Workings developed on a quartz reef in host Kenella Gneiss. Recorded production to 1936 was 27.6 tonnes ore treated for 1866gm bullion gold @ 68g/t.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Recorded production of 106.7 tonnes ore treated for 3368.5gm gold bullion at >31g/tAu from 1922-49.
quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation developed in 1904-06. Recorded production 95 tonnes yielding 866 gm of gold at 9g/tAu.
no details available, scattered workings of shallow pits and trenches on Brown Hill over an area ~200m EW x 150m wide, presumably on small quartz lodes on host Tarcoola Formation.

residual lateritic Ni-Co-Fe deposits developed on host mafic and ultramafic rock of the Giles Complex. Drilling identified enrichment over strike of ~1.6km x 200m wide x 30-40m depth. No resources figures released.
small, isolated hill of Archean  iron formation.

prominent 1.7km x 400m aeromagnetic anomaly source magnetite-bearing BIF of Wilgena Hill Jaspilite. ~80m cover of Tarcoola Formation. Head grade 35%Fe, DTR% 39% at 25 micron grind for concentrate to 67%Fe. Exploration target 700Mt.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GL 1978; GS 790; TARCOOLA UNITED; WARRIGAL EAST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz vein on the Tarcoola Goldfield from 1917-40 for production of 48.9Kg gold bullion from 1043t ore.
no details known, possibly western shaft of Tarcoola Consols, Single shaft in host slate of the Tarcoola Formation, with some galena reported. Used by Tarcoola Blocks for water supply.
60cm wide quartz vein in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation, reportedly returning good values of gold. Recorded production from 1912-34 of 1.63Kg gold bullion from 85t ore treated at 19g/t.
quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Recorded production in 1915 of 11.3 tonnes yielding 445gm bullion gold at 39g/tAu.

quartz-iron oxide lode trending NS in host Paxton Granite, and located a short distance N of Mauser Rock. Good colours of gold reported. Incomplete production records of 10 tonnes treated for 24gm bullion gold at 2.4g/tAu.

EW-trending quartz vein carrying visible gold at the surface, and in host quartzite of the Tarcoola Formation. Production from 1900-1939 estimated at 69 tonnes ore treated for 766gm bullion gold at 11g/tAu.
45cm wide quartz-iron oxide-pyrite vein trend NNE, dip steep W in host Paxton Granite. Recorded production from 1915-40 was 468 tonnes for 9190gm bullion gold at 19.6g/tAu.

35cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein trending NS, dip steep E in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation for good returns initially, values decreasing at depth. Recorded production from 1922-33 of 3.5Kg bullion gold from 74t treated at 47g/tAu.

immediately east of Tarcoola Blocks eastern lease boundary. Presumably developed on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation. Recorded production from 1913-36 of 89.2 tonnes for 1826gm bullion gold at 20.5g/tAu.
Occurs on GC 15712 on the Lake Labyrinth Goldfield. Recorded production to 1936 15 tonnes for 493gm bullion gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PERSEVERANCE; PERSEVERANCE-LAST RESOURCE; TARCOOLA GOLD PROJECT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shear-hosted Au mineralisation, along strike from Perseverance mine & hosted by Paxton Granite. Production from 1904-38 ~6000gm gold bullion. Later drilling identified resource of 11,000oz Au.
workings on gold lease 1060 on quartz vein in host fractured Paxton Granite for recovery of some rich specimens. The lode was lost at depth. Located NE of Mauser Rock.
gold lease 938, shaft developed on quartz lode in Tarcoola Formation immediately east of Government Battery. Recorded production 9.7 tonne for 114.7gm gold at 12g/tAu.
group of 4 ironstone outcrops, each 60-90 m long, developed on Archean iron formation. An historic ore resource was for 0.5-1 million tonnes per 30 m depth.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Recorded production to 1940 of 189 tonnes for 2198gm bullion gold at 11.6g/tAu.

quartz vein in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Exact location unknown, recorded lease was GL's 796 & 852 on western extremity of Tarcoola Ridge. Recorded production from 1931-36 of 62.44 tonne for 1234.7gm gold at 19.8g/tAu.
quartz reef in host slate of the Tarcoola Formation worked from 1915-49 for recovery of 26Kg gold bullion from 817t ore.
gold-bearing quartz lodes. Host was Tarcoola Formation slate, with thin streaks of pyrite indicating a favourable character. No production figure was determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GL 1000; GL 1001; GL 239; NW PROSPECTING ASSOCIATION
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings developed on the southern slopes of Tarcoola Ridge seeking southern extension of the Warrigal line of lode. Rock encountered was deeply kaolonised slate, minor salt water only. No reports of lode identified, nor gold returns.

quartz-iron oxide vein <1m wide, dip 60S, trend EW in host kaolinised slate of the Tarcoola Formation. Development was not extensive, dollying of the lode formation consistently recovered minor gold, no production figure determined.
location uncertain, recorded as on leases immediately east of the Royal George. Mine on a large quartz blow in host Paxton Granite, no production records identified.
quartz-iron oxide vein in host Tarcoola Formation metasediment. Recorded production from 1916-38 of 145 tonnes ore treated for 3.96Kg gold bullion at 27g/tAu.
no details known, located from plan 1999-0596 in Geol Survey internal plans database. Mine presumably developed on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation.

Brown coal reported in several water bores near Malbooma siding. Drilling identified coaly sediment from 71-113 ft, with high ash content, and included a 5 ft interval between 83-88 ft with a relatively low ash content.
no production figure determined, presumably developed on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ENTERPRISE; GL 1020; GL 1192; GL 1680; GL1021; HISGROVES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz lodes in host Paxton Granite. Production from 1903-1953 ~1250t treated for 24Kg gold bullion. Sims shaft on GL 1020 located near amygdaloidal basalt and diorite, with good showings of free gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Recorded production from 1906-74 tonnes ore treated for 3.69kg bullion gold at 50g/tAu.
3 separate quartz-iron oxide lodes trending NS to NE in host Tarcoola Formation, and traced for some distance on surface worked for small returns, with no production figure determined.
no details known, located from plan 1999-0596 in Geol Survey internal plans database, presumably developed on quartz lode in host Paxton Granite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COORABIN; GL 1045; GL 1047; GL 1865; GL1046; HARRY JOHN; TARCOOLA 2
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide-(Pb-Ag) lodes in host quartzite and slate of the Tarcoola Formation, also in host Paxton Granite. Some mine development along colluvium-granite contact. Incomplete production figure of 104.7 tonnes ore for 1083gm gold at 10g/tAu.
No details known, located on eastern end of the main Tarcoola ridge, presumably on a quartz leader in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation.
No details known, located on eastern end of the main Tarcoola ridge, presumably on a quartz leader in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation.
mine possibly that on GL 935, with workings developed on quartz lodes in host Tarcoola Formation prospected the extension of the mineralised lodes at Warrigal. No significant gold returns recorded.
quartz-iron oxide reef in host quartzite of the Tarcoola Formation. Reported good gold was recovered from dollying the lode. Parcel of 5 tonnes of ore in 1915 yielded 56gm gold at 11g/tAu.

one of several mines of the same name worked by a consortium that held 14 x 20 acre blocks. This mine on GL 1072 on western end of Tarcoola ridge developed on a quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation. No production figure determined.
location is unreliable, and refers to a prospecting shaft on GL 1073, section 786, SE from Napperby Mine. No significant lode was encountered.

shallow pits were developed for weak gold returns on GL 1084. More extensive workings on GL 1082, developed on an irregular quartz lode carrying good gold at the surface. Production figures unique to this lode were not determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GL 1086; GL 1087; GL 1090; GL 1091; GL 1093; VICTORY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz-iron oxide veins in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Some good returns reported. No production records apparent. Shafts encountered stock and potable water at ~27m depth, flow ~950 litres per day.
reef in host Fabian Quartzite, and parallel to the lode mined at the Royal George, with the shaft ~40mS of the Royal George main shaft. Production ~2500gm gold.

mine site located from map no. 1999-0596, but no other details known, nor references found. Presumably developed on quartz lode in Tarcoola Formation. Workings of a trench and shaft over a 20m length of NNW-trending quartz lode.

located only from the 1:250K MEIS series of hard copy maps, presumably prospecting of quartz lode in host Muckanippie Suite igneous rock. Of interest was high Al2O3 analysis of 25-30%Al2O3 from host anorthosite.
location uncertain, recorded as on gold lease GL 997, one of several shafts NE of Hidden Treasure developed on quartz lodes in host Tarcoola Formation. No production figure determined.
reported as located on gold lease GL 752, no details known, no references found, exact location uncertain, workings on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation.
located from plan 1999-0596 on Geol Survey internal plans database. presumed mine on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation. No production figure determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ATMIL SYNDICATE; GL 1656; TARCOOLA BLOCKS; TARCOOLA WELCOME HOME; WESTERN REEF
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Au mineralisation in quartz reef in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation. Production to 1952 ~2914t for 64.6kg bullion gold. Later drilling defined resource in the oxidised zone of ~4000t @ 10g/t. The primary zone was not penetrated.
1-1.3m wide quartz-iron oxide vein in host decomposed granite. Production from 1932-42 888t ore yielding 31.7kg bullion gold.

location uncertain, This mine relates to gold lease GL 951, section 748 located immediately east of Evening Star. No references found, no details known, presumably developed on quartz lode in host Tarcoola Formation.

prospecting south of Glory Quayle Rock. Work commenced on a shaft on a quartz reef in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation in 1900 but ceased soon after due to lack of funds. Drilling ~130m to NW as the Schools Prospect, mindep #3115.
one of several mines of the same name on the goldfield. Workings on GL 958 on 45cm quartz vein in host Tarcoola Formation, reportedly returning good values for gold, no production records known.

45cm wide quartz vein trending EW, carrying rare coarse gold at contact of slate to west and quartzite to east of Tarcoola Formation . Recorded production from 1904, and 1915 12.4 tonnes for 270gm bullion gold at 21.8g/tAu.
quartz vein in host Paxton granite. Recorded production from 1916-39 was 5727gm from 169.6t ore. Resources contained gold ~3,000oz (93Kg).
mine developed on quartz-iron oxide lode, trend ~NE in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Reported production of 40.4 tonnes ore yielding 348gm bullion gold at 8.6g/tAu.

alluvial gold discovery on River Torrens, nuggets to 9gm. Subsequent 2m wide quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation worked, no production figures. Later sampling returned a value of ~40g/t.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in several shafts, with limited underground development. Drew (RB 92/00053) reported production of ~400 oz (12441 gm) from 1895-1903.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. No production figures were determined, with sampling of dumps returning values of assays reported at 2-3 oz/tonne.

location uncertain, reported as 6.8km east of Birdwood, Hundred Talunga, sections 6280, 6344. Recorded production 25.7 tonne for 121.5gm gold from 1948-49 from quartz lode in host Backstairs Passage Formation.
auriferous quartz-iron oxide veins worked in shallow pits and trenches. A package of 6.1 tonne yielded 36.5gm @ 6g/tAu.

auriferous quartz-iron oxide veins in metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Reported production 268.3t yielding 4056.5gm gold at 15g/t, though the figure probably incorporated production from other mines.
auriferous quartz-iron oxide lodes in host mica schist and sandstone of the Backstairs Passage Formation. No individual production figures reported.
quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Production from a parcel of ore presumably from 1896-97 was 10.2 tonnes yielding 119 gm of gold at 11.7g/tAu.
Au mineralisation in quartz-iron oxide-pyrite reef in host micaceous schist of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Production from 1870-1936 ~12.7Kg bullion gold.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host schist of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Production from 84.7 tonne ore of 719gm bullion gold at 8.5g/tAu.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Records of production of 13.7 tonne ore for 288gm gold at 21g/tAu.

very approximate location, located south of Woocalla. The commodities mentioned were copper and manganese oxide. It was held as a series of mineral claims from 1914-1923, and some manganese ore was produced.
claim granted in 1918 near the Sweet Nell mine. No recorded production.

claims taken out in 1922 over shows of mananese oxide. They were located 3 miles northeast of Mount Gunson copper mine. There were no records of production.
percussion (17 holes totalling 2619m) and diamond drilling (6 holes totalling 627.65m) identified significant stratabound zinc-lead-(copper-silver) mineralization in the basal Tapley Hill Formation.
small abandoned clay pit adjacent to the Stuart Highway. testwork indicated suitable for production of stoneware, but not for whiteware. Potential large resources. Adjacent to railway siding.
occurrence of manganese oxide developed in Woocalla Dolomite host. There was minor production only.

workings developed in 1862 on on a quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lode carrying copper mineralisation in unknown host, possibly Kulpara Formation or Proterozoic basement.

kaolin deposits, high grade, uneconomic due to isolation and difficult extraction. Host was bed in Coorikiana Sandstone Member.

malachite, and blue, fibrous crocidolite associated with quartz, biotite and goethite in hydrothermal aggregates in host metasediment of Duff Creek Beds. Mineralisation as late-stage hydrothermal products from intrusion of Bungadillina Monzonite.

series of open cuts, 2 shafts to 9.75 and 3 m, and an adit. The copper mineralisation occurred within a small gossanous zone, and adjacent to pegmatite in host Peake Metamorphics.

deposit of 6 major and several lesser seams, cumulative thickness 35m, of Permian coal in Boorthana Trough on E side of Arckaringa Basin. Top of mineable coal @ 130-150m. Resource ~1,000Mt, with potential for additional significant resources outside drilled areas.
small copper show, with later exploration by ground scintillometer returning readings of up to 1000cps from small dolomite outcrops. 550ppm U obtained from dolomite surface sample.

weak U anomaly in sheared gneiss and silicified brecciated Katunga Dolomite along NW-trending fault.

quartz vein in silicified, limonitc country rock mapped as of the Lower Middleback jaspilite, and carrying malachite and azurite, with dump material carrying minor graphite, and recording anomalous radioactivity.

located in the South Middleback Range, and south of the Iron Chieftain prospect. It was a surface exposure of goethite. Drilling confirmed supergene enriched interval of goethite/limonite ore with grades 50-55%Fe.

exact location unknown, but on section 242 3.5 km east of Kadina. Appears to one of several shallow excavations of a prospecting nature on the New Cornwall-Kadina Line of Lode, with exact location uncertain. No recorded production.

minor U in Carnotite-bearing Mangalo Schist and Katunga Dolomite of the Hutchison Group metasediments.  742-1 intersected anomalous zone 11-18m which assayed at 110ppmU.

exposure of goethitic outcrop in the South Middleback Range in host Lower Middleback Jaspilite. Tested in 10 holes as a drill traverse across a gravity only anomaly, with holes penetrating oxidised BIF, magnetite-bearing BIF, and dolerite.

seams of irregular, discontinuous  chrysotile asbestos seams to 12cm wide in a host serpentinised, magnesian, crystalline marble band to 36m wide, trend 075, dip 70N. The fibre length was to 2.5cm long.

outcrop 20 x 1 m of dolomitic marble and epidotite associated with 6 lenses of jade.
lens of dark green, jade in host dolomitic marble, tremolite, and calc silicate rocks. Its dimensions were 14 m x 3 m.

prominent, large jadeite outcrop measuring 40m x 4m. Estimated total production attributed to ML 4634 to 2009 was 5370t.
outcrop of jade, dark green, low translucency. From 1978-89 production 72 tonne. Host basal Warrow Quartzite unit of banded calcsilicate gneiss.

worked on part-time basis since 1965 for small quantities of gem-quality jade, carving-grade talc, and ornamental marble. Production details incomplete for ~2600t nephrite from a lode 5m x 2m, 8t talc, 30t ornamental marble.

N of Wallaroo Mine, and seeking the extension of the Wallaroo-Devon Consols Line of Lode in 1872. a lode of Cu mineralised quartz-calcite-Iron oxide was encountered, but mining was abandoned by 1874. No production records apparent.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 regular mineralised, quartz lodes trending EW in host Palaeoproterozoic dark mica schist. Incomplete production records of 30 tonnes @ 25%Cu dressed ore in 1863.
shear zone in host schist of the Warrow Quartzite. Numerous cross cutting quartz-iron oxide veins from 10-100cm wide carrying Pb-Ag mineralisation.
minor U associated with Cu mineralisation in Warrow Quartzite metasediment. Best assay 4.1lbs U3O8/long ton. Petrology of gossan identified iron oxide after chalcopyrite.
amethyst occurrence known from records only. Located from the old hard-copy Whyalla 1:250K MEIS (Mineral Exploration Information Series) map sheet.
short, silky fibres of chrysotile asbestos in 1m wide serpentinite zone in host recrystallised limestone of the Warrow Quartzite. Worked in 1929 for recovery of 0.6t of asbestos fibre.

quarry in predominantly marble, quartzitic gneiss of Hutchison Group. Production of 24,800 m3 chippings in 1967-68 to seal Cowell-Cleve road. 1983 resource estimate of total yield of 105 000m3 chippings.

lease taken out over shoreline dunal shell grit deposit of the Saint Kilda Formation, and by Pasminco Port Pirie, but no production recorded. Dunes extend for ~3km NS immediately inland of the hgh tide water line. No resource estimate.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: POINT HUGHES; WALLAROO BEACH; WHEAL MIXTER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 talc-iron oxide-copper rich lodes exposed close to the tidal line near Point Hughes for ~150m strike. Worked very early on, no production figures apparent. Grab samples of ore assayed 7-17%Cu.

quartz vein in host Charleston Granite. Trace chalcopyrite, argentiferous galena, sphalerite was recorded. No production figure was determined. Later exploration included IP over the main workings, with no anomaly detected.
shaft developed on a 1.3m wide quartz-iron oxide lode carrying green and blue copper carbonates.

complex of pods of massive hematite in host Lower Middleback Jaspilite, significant mafic intrusives. Production from 1933-1990 estimated at >30Mt. Small resource of >55%Fe at base of open cut & in low-grade stockpiles.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: IRON CAVALIER NORTH; ML 2386; ML 2678; ML 2694; ML 2695; ML 2696; ML 2699; ML 4753; ML 4754; ML 4757; ML 4758
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: goethite-hematite body as lateritised scree/weathered bedrock. Grade predominantly 55-60% Fe. Some mining had taken place. production figure not published, in order of <1Mt, resource remaining unknown, probably only minor.

E-dipping body of hematite in host BIF of Lower Middleback Jaspilite. At depth ore grades to magnetite-talc-carbonate rock. Mined in the late 1980s, no production record. probably <5Mt. No resource estimate for low-grade magnetite-bearing BIF.

poddy deposit of massive goethite, goethitic hematite, dip 30W, overlain by quartz-hematite to quartz-magnetite BIF, and clay of the Lower Middleback Jaspilite. Active mine, production commenced 2011. Resource 32.36Mt @ 53.5%Fe June 2014.

minor occurrence of enriched banded iron formation (BIF) in Ash Range, a small hill of iron formation immediately east of Kimba Gap. Hematised breccia zones with quartz in a BIF host. Drill hole suggested the enrichment was surficial only.

steep to moderate E-dipping, poddy deposit of massive hematite in host BIF of the Lower Middleback Jaspilite. Active mine, N extension of Iron Duke, with production figure incorporated with those from that mine. Production in order of >10Mt of >60%Fe.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: discontinuous pods of massive, goethitic hematite in host BIF of Lower Middleback Jaspilite. Active mine, with production figures incorporated into those for Iron Duke. Estimated resource 2014 6.2Mtonne at >59%Fe.
2 hematite pods mined out. Workings extended for ~300 m NNW by maximum 90 m wide. Resources remaining in the north pod were not published, but were likely to be relatively small.
small hematite occurrence identified by BHP Steel in the 1970's, of no economic significance.
located at the southern tip of the North Middleback Range, and was a pod of massive hematite with drilling confiming a depth extent of 15 m. No resource calculated, probably only minor.
Described as on section 24, Hundred James. Small pit of pegmatite? Host was granite and sandstone, possibly of the Warrow Quartzite.
magnetite-bearing metasomatic gneiss with anomalous Fe-Cu-Mo-U values. Possible autunite in DDH 160, average 235ppm U over 42.7m core length (max 920ppm U)
or Kadina Mine, worked N extension of NW-trending lode of the Wandilta Mine for production of ~50 tonne ore 10-20%Cu from 1870-74.
brown to almost black smoky quartz in shear zone in host Warrow Quartzite. Better quality occurs between 0.3-0.6m. Production from 1977-2007 was ~20 tonne.
shallow prospecting on malachite show identified a mineralised quartz lode, but grade proved to be low, no production ensued.

series of EW-trending quartz-iron oxide veins with shallow secondary Cu mineralisation, chalcopyrite at depth in host altered quartz-biotite schist. Production ~20,500t dressed ore ~25%Cu from 1863-1905.
weak copper mineralisation in quartz vein in host ferruginous Warrow Quartzite. Workings of inclined drive into hill side, with cross cut.
minor deposit of magnesite in host Katunga Dolomite of the Palaeoproterozoic Hutchison Group. BHP held leases over the area in 1927, and production was 4 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MATTA LODE; MATTA MATTA; STIRLINGS LODE; WALLAROO
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Cu mineralisation associated with local shears in host Proterozoic quartzite & mica schist. Recorded production 1863-66 of ~2,450t @ 23%Cu.
tenure as RL 116 taken out over outcropping Middlecamp Granite for potential use as dimension stone.

1m wide crush zone in partly serpentinised magnesian marble. Within the shear seams of chrysotile asbestos, with maximum length 5cm. Recorded production in 1931 of 70 tons of material for recovery of 8 tons of commercial ore.

nephrite jade associated with dolomitic marble and calc-silicate of Hutchinson Group. Mining exposed 3 jade zones associated with ~50% tremolite rock, and ""near-jade"" material. Hand selected jade was comparable to varieties from Cowell.

no production records. Diamond drilling identified stratabound pyrite-pyrrhotite-sphalerite-galena-chalcopyrite-marcasite-argentite in host marble-calc-silicate of Warrow Quartzite. IP surveys identified sequence with strike extent of several km.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shear zones with talc and asbestos in host serpentinised magnesian marble of the Katunga Dolomite. Also minor ochreous carnotite, and common opal reported. Production of talc in 1921 of 109.7 tonne. Being investigated for U by Lincoln Minerals Ltd 2024.

6km linear aeromagnetic anomaly, N extension of Bungalowt. Source magnetite-bearing BIF of Hutchison Group. Inferred resource 99Mt at head grade 27%Fe, 32.2%DTR for magnetite concentrate 69.2%Fe (May 2012). Cover 100-120m.
prospecting venture in 1872 involving 12 miners working via shallow pits a copper show on mineral section 4124, Section 1302, Hundred Wallaroo.

quarry on metasediment of the Moonabie Formation, being metasiltstone, meta-arkose, and meta-sandstone used for road base material. The historic quarry has not been rehabilitated, lying close to, and south of the Lincoln Highway
council quarry on section 965 on calcrete for road base material. Quarry records identify 10,700 tonne excavated from 1925-52.

Cu-Ag-(Pb-Zn-Th) mineralisation in an area of several lodes associated with pegmatite and aplite dykes in host mica schist of the Warrow Quartzite. Production record from 1898-1912 of 189t ore, no metal yield recorded.

lenses of high quality barite as infill of fracture zones in quartzite of the Moonabie Formation. The vein system was traced for 125 m, average width 0.55 m. 45 tonnes of industrial grade barite were extracted. Only a small tonnage remained.
deposit of siliceous metasandstone and metasiltstone of the Palaeoproterozoic Moonabie Formation worked for sandstone products. Production from 1979-2011 >2.8Mt.

mineralised crush zone to 2.5m wide carrying patches and veins of argentiferous galena. Host rock mica schist of the Warrow Quartzite. Workings developed on 30m hill above gully and consisted of several shallow pits and a single shaft.

drilling identified carbonaceous material and lignite in host Kanaka Beds. Coal analyses and oil shale determinations were carried out on the lignitic intervals. Global resource estimate 100Mt lignite/oil shale.

apparent highly weathered slate, possibly of the Rhynie Sandstone, with clay suitable for blending, though not suitable on its own for refractory use. Recorded production from 1926-37 of 4064 tonnes.

no details, located from mine symbol on 250K map Whyalla, low grade copper mineralisation probably related to feldspar-iron oxide-calcsilicate skarn.

deposit of Holocene clay, with production from 1973-78 of ~3,000 tonne red plastic clay for brickmaking. Rehabilitation was completed in 1988.

located south of the Morowie mine on section 3339. It developed on a 3m wide lode in host metasediment of the Warrow Quartzite. No production records apparent. A 3 tonne parcel assayed 30%Cu.

worked slate of Tapley Hill Formation from mid 1840s along with Martins Quarry to the north. Last worked in 1970's. Recorded production figures were combined with those from Martins, see MINDEP # 7339.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLACKFELLOWS CREEK SLUICING WORKS; MCCARTHYS; SCRYMGOURS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: diggings developed on gold-bearing alluvial flats in 1887. A small rush ensued with up to 60 men on site. The diggings were abandoned by 1906. No details of production were determined, there were reports of finds of small nuggets.
Quaternary sand, with production from 1977-81 of ~1300 tonne garden sand. It was rehabilitated in 1983.

quarry opened in 1956 on quartzite of the Belair Subgroup for road making material. Suitable for use as concrete aggregate, though individual quartzite units are too small to be mined on a large scale.

blue-grey slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. Opened in 1840, worked intermittently until 1903. Reopened in late 1950s for production of ~1,000 tonne. Production of slate from 1976-2002 estimated at 800 tonnes.
clay pit developed on deeply weathered Balquidder Formation, production from 1977-78 was ~1500 tonne of coloured clay for brick making. It was rehabilitated in 1986.
worked sandstone of the Saddleworth Formation until 1999 and rehabilitated from 2001-2006.

1.4m wide quartz-iron oxide lode in host Barossa Complex. Workings included an underlie shaft to 13m length, and several surface pits. 8.1 tonnes of ore was treated for recovery of 29.6gm gold at 3.6g/tAu.

alluvials & quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Mainly of a prospecting nature, active sporadically from 1896-1913 for incomplete results from 3 parcels of ore for 42 tonne at 9.7g/tAu.
quartz vein in host slate of the Barossa Complex. It was prospected periodically from 1897-1912 via a series of shallow shafts for only a trace of gold.

quartz-iron oxide-pyrite veins in host schist of the Barossa Complex. Parcel of 1 tonne ore for 9.3gm gold. Worked on a small scale in 1930s. Some colour was reported from alluvium in the surrounding creeks.
quartz lode in host Tapanappa Formation was reported to carry silver mineralisation. A prospecting shaft failed to return sample with anomalous values.
small abandoned council pit of ~2,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white sand of the Pleistocene Molineaux Sand, and worked for road fill material.
2 marble beds, upper 4m thick, lower 3m thick separated by slate bed to 2.5m thick, all of the Macklesfield Marble. Resource estimate ~1100m3, only minor production in 1919.

massive ironstone outcrop trending E for ~130m, in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, and near the base of a hill. Initial sampling returned 62g/tAu, and 124g/t Ag. A 16.26 tonne package from a shaft yielded 369.5gm gold at 22.7g/tAu.
15-20cm thick, horizontal bed of Tertiary porcellanite discovered in 1940. it was worked in 1951 for 70t raised, and 44t sold.

narrow 10-20cm quartz-iron oxide veins in host slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite. They were mined in a series of shallow pits to 2m depth. No production figure determined. The area was first prospected for alluvial gold, with fair results reported.

quartz-iron oxide lodes in host calc-silicate rock of the Houghton Granulite. The lode was of irregular strike, being ~60cm wide at the mouth of an adit, decreasing to 15cm. Best assay was 4.7g/t Au. No production figure determined.
quartz vein in host calc-silicate of the Barossa Complex,  prospected via a number of shallow pits, with no gold reported.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A.V. JENNINGS; BASTIANS; PM 117; WILLUNGA SLATE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: slate of the Tapley Hill Formation worked from the early 1840s, with recorded production combined with Bastians Quarry. Production >55,000t dimension and decorative stone from 1925-2013.
quarry developed on a cream to grey-brown dolomite-cemented sandstone of the Permian Cape Jervis Formation, producing sandstone in the last century, no production figures recorded.
1m wide quartz-iron oxide lode in host schist of the Barossa Complex. Total production 1.5-3kg (50-100oz) of gold. Grades to 7g/tAu were recovered.

lode of titaniferous hematite-limonite prospected for gold in 1887. Host Houghton Diorite. MC 11121 was taken out for iron in 1919-21, with nothing eventuating. Tested for use as road base material in 1956-57.
workings sometime prior to 1911 on a lode of titaniferous ilmenite in host Barossa Complex.
workings of a prospecting nature developed from 1931-32 on quartz-hematite vein in host clay slate of the Stonyfell Quartzite via two shafts, one with a drive, and for poor returns.
quarry developed in gneiss of the Barossa Complex on the west side of Mount Effie for use in road making, now site of a dam.

claims were taken out for rutile. 20 ton ore raised, with ~7 ton bagged and sold. Reopened in 1955-56. Anomalous radioactivity (as Thorium) was noticed in the vicinity. Lodes were quartz-rutile-hematite-ilmenite in host gneiss and schist.

irregular-shaped secondary hematiteilmenite body in host felspathic schist of Barossa Complex. Estimated resource 5,080 tonne. Surface samples assayed 65.2%Fe, and 4.9%Ti. Production estimated at 1-2000 tonne.
historic quarry in Belair Subgroup reworked in 1956 for recovery of 38,200m3 for road base material. Rehabilitated in 1991.

wide quartz-iron oxide reef in host slate of the Barossa Complex. A package of ore ran a grade of 378g/tAg. A small 15 cm leader on the opposite side of the creek graded 35g/tAu. No production figure was determined.

1 of several claims on a 1 m thick bed of phosphate rock assaying 45-53% tricalcic phosphate. It was discovered in 1903. Claims were abandoned by 1910. Excavations were limited to shallow pits and shafts.

1 of several claims on a 1 m thick bed of phosphate rock assaying 45-53% tricalcic phosphate. It was discovered in 1903. Claims were abandoned by 1910. Excavations were limited to shallow pits and shafts.
quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Worked occasionally to 1940 for recorded production of ~1403gm gold from 562.4 tonnes at 2.5g/tAu.
in 1932 rutile recovered from pegmatite in host micaceous schist of the Barossa Complex.
1 of 2 small quarries on Quaternary gravel developed early 1900s for road making material.
1 of 2 small quarries developed on Quaternary gravel in early 1900s for road making material.
gold-bearing alluvium. Workings consisted of a number of shallow shafts. Production figures were not determined.

quartz-iron oxide reef in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex. The lode trended NE, dipped 45SE, worked from an adit, shafts, shallow pits and a costean. In all some 61 tonnes of ore was raised, no grade or yield determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MYPONGA GOVERNMENT PROSPECTING PARTY; OLD BURMAH ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: extensive diggings on lower end of Meadows Creek, for recovery of average grades 3-5g/tAu, no production figure determined.

historic council roadside cut on a quartzite bed of the Belair Subgroup, dip 80W. Inspected by Geological Survey in mid 1950s to identify sequence of phyllitic slate, sandstone and quartzite. Quartzite of good quality, though in relatively thin beds.
workings were described as developed on host Tapley Hill Formation, with recorded production of 4,100 tonne of slate for road ballast and building stone from 1933-1947.
quarried from 1940-41 for recorded 252 tonne for cement manufacture. Host rock was metasediment of the Angepena Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BULLION; COTSEDA CINNABAR; DOROTHY TIN; MYPONGA MERCURY; SA MERCURY PROSPECTING SYNDICATE; WILLUNGA MERCURY; WILLUNGA QUICKSILVER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: discovered in 1885 when prospecting for gold. Native mercury was reported to be freely visible in host decomposed granite and quartzite of the Barossa Complex. Extensive prospecting occurred in the early 1910s.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ARCKARINGA; PURE KALE PRODUCTS PTY LTD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: kaolin deposit in high cliffs bordering Arckaringa Creek in host Coorikiana Sandstone Member.

minor allanite (cerium-bearing epidote) collected from pegmatite. The allanite was estimated not to be an economic source of rare earth elements (REE). Crystalline specimens of allanite might have some value as mineral specimens.

small amounts of allanite (cerium-bearing epidote) collected from pegmatite. The allanite was estimated not to be an economic source of rare earth elements (REE). Crystalline specimens of allanite might have some value as mineral specimens.
Quaternary dunal sand, with production from 1972-87 of ~663,750 tonne of mainly foundry sand, inclusive of ~1300 tonne of garden sand.
abandoned quarry established in 1932 on quartzite of the Belair Subgroup for road construction. Residence within 100m.
small, abandoned council quarry of >100m2 x 1-8m deep, and developed on limestone of the Heatherdale Shale. Worked intermittently from 1929-31 for production of 152 tonne for road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CARRICKALINGA SILVER; QUEEN MARY; WHEAL MARY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gossan carrying silver-lead mineralisation. 132 tonne of ore were raised by 1869, no grade recorded. Host was claystone and limestone of the Fork Tree Limestone.
quarry on limestone of the Fork Tree Limestone initially worked by Brown, taken up in the 1950s by the local DC. 2 diamond holes completed in 1958 confirmed a 6m wide weathered zone.

location uncertain, recorded as mineral claim 15373 for mica filed in 1936 by Tom Burgess who worked similar material  1.7km west of Myponga Hill in aplitic pegmatite in host Barossa Complex metasediment.
pods of alunite to 1.3m across in host slate and limestone. Mining from 1913-19 for recorded production of 356 tonne.
shallow pits on a manganite-limonite-galena lode in Archaeocyathic limestone host of the Sellick Hill Formation. It was tested 1n 1967 in 8 drill holes for no encouraging results.
limestone quarry in Barossa Complex worked in 1940 for production of 305t.
discovered in 1860 on the side of a hill. Quartzose rock carrying copper staining in veins. Worked from 1865-67, briefly again in 1898 and 1921. No production figures were recorded.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BURGESS; MC 10824; MC 12308; MC 13094; MC 15355; MYPONGA FELDSPAR; MYPONGA PEGMATITE; MYPONGA TITANIUM
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 open cuts developed from 1926 on pegmatite and aplite dykes in host Barossa Complex gneiss. Recorded production of 2t mica product from 1926-29.
historic quarry developed on a deposit of limestone of the Sellick Hill Formation. Production recorded from 1925-26 of 3860 tonne for cement manufacture. Resource estimate in 1926 of 1.28Mt.
pegmatite in host micaceous schist of the Barossa Complex. Recorded production from 1918 of 70t for recovery of 2t of rutile product.
workings on silver-lead mineralised lode in limestone of the Umberatana Group, recorded production ~30t at 2177g/tAg.
occurrence of minor magnetite-martite lodes in host proterozoic metasediment. It was referred to as Outcrop 2, and was located ~300 m NE from outcrop 1.
phosphate deposit in host Mount Terrible Formation. Recorded production from 1941-42 of >900t. Resource estimate in 1975 was 12,000 tonne at 22.5% P2O5.
lode of calcite carrying silver lead mineralisation in host metasediment of the Fork Tree Limestone, with ~20t raised in 1886.

marble of the Fork Tree Limestone, with production from 1977-1983 of ~200 tonne marble for decorative stone. It has since been incorporated into the south-western extension of the main open cut of the Sellicks Hill Quarry.
historic workings from 1863 on a small silver-lead show. No recorded production. Small seams of galena with up to 62g/tAg reported.
worked a creek bed in 1970 for pebbles for use in a grinding mill.
prospecting pits for thorium-uranium developed in 1954-55 on quartz veins in sericite schist host of the Barossa Complex.
lode material was iron ore and quartzite with trace galena. Host rock was crystalline, blue limestone of the Fork Tree Limestone. An inspection by the State Geologist deemed the prospect worthless.

quartz lode with Pb-Ag mineralisation. Best value 7 oz Ag/ton. Inspection by the State Geologist deemed the prospect worthless. Host was limestone of the Mount Terrible Formation, lode being iron ore and quartzite with a trace of galena.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5054; EML 5440; HEATHERDALE LIMESTONE; HILLSLEY; MYPONGA LIMESTONE; PM 163; PM 19; PM 234; PM 237; PM 308; SOUTHERN QUARRIES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Cambrian limestone, dolomite and metasiltstone. Production for the period 1977-2013 was ~20 million tonne, the bulk being multiple products for use in the construction industry, and ~186,000 tonne for an industrial enduse.  .
limestone of the Belair Subgroup worked from 1924-28 for 1220 tonne road base material.
small prospecting pit on a monazite show. ore zone was hydrothermal monazite-hematite-ilmenite rock in host schist of the Barossa Complex.
pits developed on monazite occurrence in aplitic dyke in host metasediment of the Barossa Complex.
structurally controlled pitchblende mineralisation in Palaeoproterozoic paragneiss of the Myponga Inlier.

abandoned council quarry of <5,000m2 x 1-6m deep, and developed on limestone of the Sellick Hill Formation, with campaign mining from the early 1940s to 1970s for ~35,300 tonne for road fill material, also minor sand and gravel products.
area of abandoned council pits on declared Road Reserve No.25. Pits developed on weathered shale of the Barossa Complex for building stone in the early 1940s.
2 x adjacent, abandoned council sand pits of combined area >10,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on Pleistocene Molineaux Sand for road fill material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 4701; EML 6071; EML 6231; EML 6359; EML 6360; YANKALILLA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: central pit of 3 separate operations developed on a ridge of sandstone and shale of the Saddleworth Formation ~3km NE of Yankalilla. Production from central pit from 1979-2011 was ~666,000 tonne for road base material.

originally a council scrape developed on weathered sandstone, slate and shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Later tenure granted as EML 6193, with estimated production from 2005-2013 of ~100,000 tonne of road fill material.

quartzite of the ABC Range Quartzite, worked for concrete aggregate in the late 1950s for construction of Myponga Dam. Historic production of 5 tonne slate, minor shale for dimension stone in 1942. Analysis indicated SiO2 to >97%.
abandoned council rubble pit in colluvial rubble of schist and gneiss of the Barossa Complex, and shed from a prominent seaside strike ridge, no production figures apparent.
6 km x 200 m aeromagnetic anomaly tested in drill holes CRBC 11 and 12, which penetrated quartz-magnetite gneiss with very high magnetic susceptibility readings, but with no assaying for iron.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5728; MIN 36; MINNIPA GRANITE; MINNIPA HILL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: granite outcrop, being coarse grained, reddish quartz, pale feldspar, trace biotite, marketed as Desert Ruby. Quarry produced 1397t of dimension stone from 1993-1998 and was rehabilitated in 2007.
2 shallow pits on deeply weathered Warrow Quartzite, northern, abandoned pit on heavily iron-oxide staned material, and more recent pit on white, kaolinitic quartzite.
roadside sand spread of the Holocene Moornaba Sand in 1970s for production of ~1150 tonne concrete sand.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DIRTY BACK ROAD; MOUNT CHRISTIE SIDING
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drilling identified 3 zones of chromite in host weathered layered ultramafic intrusive. Best assays 11m at 1.8%Cr, 15m at 2%Cr and 8m at 5.34%Cr.

anomalous Ni-Cu in komatiite. Sulphides and opaques of chromite, ilmenite, pentlandite, violarite, mackinawite, millerite, bornite, chalcopyrite. Best assay 6400ppmCr, 4200pmNi, 188 ppb Au. Potential confirmed by further drilling in 2014.

surface geochemical sampling of magnetic lag identified  4000 ppm surface nickel anomaly. Drilling identified Ni halo >900mEW x 150m wide. Downhole Ni values average >1500ppm over 30-35m interval, maximum 7000ppm.

lead-zinc mineralisation associated with small pods and veins on granite-rhyolite contact, and Cu-Ni mineralisation associated with gabbro-hornfels contact intruded by granite. Drilling identified occurrence was not of any economic significance.
deposit of albite in host Palaeoproterozoic amphibolite of the Morialpa Inlier. Production from 1998-2001 was ~2,250 tonne.
sandstone and quartzite of the Backstairs Passage Formation, with total production from 1991-2013 of ~200,000 tonne mainly for quartzite for road base material, minor sandstone for spalls.
deeply weathered quartzite and limestone of the Barossa Complex. Total production from 1984-2013 of ~336,000 tonne of mainly sandstone products, minor quartzite, limestone, clay and gravel.
clay deposit formed from deep weathering of metasediment of the Barossa Complex. Production from 1977-80 was ~3600 tonne coloured clay product for filling.
small open cut on deeply weathered, kaolinitic, Torrensian rock. It was abandoned, and rehabilitated in 1984 using EARF - see MB 654.
weathered shale of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Production from 1987-96 was ~9,740 tonne of white shale product. Rehabilitation was completed in 1994.
deeply weathered shale of the Barossa Complex. Production from 1995-98 was ~19,400 tonne of white shale products. Rehabilitation was completed in 2006.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly, with subsequent drill testing identifying weak gold mineralisation in host Archean granitoid. The form as defined by drilling suggested mineralisation related to a redox boundary.
3m wide zone of Pb-Zn-Au-Ag in quartz-iron oxide-clay bands in host contorted, laminated siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Production from 1977-79 ~4t Pb ore, 2kg Ag ore & 1547gm Au.
micaceous hematite in host basal Aldgate Sandstone. Stratiform ironstone 3.5km long, width to 10m. Recorded production 10t in 1977. Resource >203,000 tonne grading 31.5% Fe.
last recorded production in 1988 and rehabilitated completed in 1988.
council pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, kaolinised metasediment of the Tindelpina Shale Member of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
Quaternary sand, with production in 1985 of ~10,700 tonne garden sand. Rehabilitation was completed in 2006.
Quaternary sand, with production from 1983-2002 of ~167,900 tonne garden sand. Rehabilitation was completed in 2007.
Quaternary sand, with last recorded production in 1994, and rehabilitated in 1998.
limestone of the Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation, with production from 2002-13 of ~154,000 tonne of limestone for road base material, minor concrete sand.
Mesoproterozoic dolerite sill in the Barossa Complex of the Myponga Inlier. Production from 1992-2013 was >5,000 tonne for road base material.
quartzite of the Saddleworth Formation, with production from 1978-2001 of ~151,500 tonne for road base material. It was rehabilitated in 2001.
sandstone deposit of the Barossa Complex, with production from 1988-2013 of ~111,000 tonne of road base material.

abandoned, and rehabilitated quarry of >15,000m2 x 1-8m deep on limestone of the Cambrian Wangkonda Formation, with production of spalls for breakwater at Wirrina marina from 1996-97 estimated at 445,400 tonne.
quarry on sandstone of the Belair Subgroup operated from 1986-1998 for estimated production of 36,200 tonnes.
Quaternary sand and indurated sand, with production from 1986-1991 of ~9,000 tonne mainly for garden sand, minor sandstone for filling, and minor foundry sand.
Tertiary sand, with production from 1978-98 of ~15,200 tonne garden sand. It was rehabilitated in 1995.
Quaternary sand, with production ceased in 1997 and rehabilitation was completed in 1998.
sandstone deposit of the Undalya Quartzite, with production from 1987-2010 of ~50,000 tonne for road base material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PM 170; WISTOW 2; WISTOW SLATE & WALLING STONE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: dark grey quartz-feldspar-biotite metasiltstone of the Tapanappa Formation worked for metasiltone products for use as dimension and decorative stone. Production from 1976-2013 was estimated at 25,000 tonne.

sand of the Pleistocene Blanchetown Clay. Production from 1974-2013 was ~296,000 tonne of which ~175,000 tonne was for foundry sand, and 121,000 tonne for garden sand. Workings are being progressively rehabilitated.
sand of the Pleistocene Blanchetown Clay, with seasonal production from 1983-2001 of ~14,000 tonne for garden sand product.
sand of the Pleistocene Blanchetown Clay, with production from 1995-2013 from 2 small pits of ~13000 tonne, including ~4,000 tonne for foundry sand, and the remainder for packing sand.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 5531; LANGHORNE CREEK; ML 4849; NALPA 1; NALPA STATION; TOOPERANG
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Holocene medium to coarse aeolian dunal sand parallel and marginal to the shore of Lake Alexandrina. Total production from 1988-2013 was ~173,000 tonne, being 132,000 tonne foundry and filter sand, ~41,000 tonne garden sand.
Holocene sand, with production from 1979-2013 of ~140,000 tonne building and packing sand.
Quaternary sand, with production from 1985-2005 of ~270,500 tonne garden and concrete sand.
large area of surface pale red-brown Holocene aeolian sand, tenure of 75Ha, with production from 1973-93 of ~247,000 tonne garden and concrete sand. Worked areas have been rehabilitated.
Pleistocene calcrete worked for road base material. Production from 1988-89 was ~9,000 tonne.
Pleistocene calcrete worked for road base material. Production from 1990-91 of ~8,000 tonne.
Ordovician Murray Bridge Granite worked for decorative stone, with production from 1988-2012 of >5000 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: D.L. SCOTT AND SON; EML 5709; MURRAY BRIDGE FREESTONE; MURRAY BRIDGE LIMESTONE; OBRIEN; TORODES
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Tertiary Bryozoal limestone of the Murray Group, workings of a shallow pit marginal to a creek near the River Murray. Production from 1991-2011 was ~1800 tonne dimension stone marketed as Murray Bridge Freestone.
pale red-brown alluvial sand worked from 1991-2002 for production of ~31,000 tonne garden sand.
pale red-brown Holocene aeolian dunal sand to sand spread. Production from 1993-2013 of ~86,000 tonne packing sand.
pale red-brown Holocene alluvial sand spread marginal to a small creek. Production from 2005-13 was ~64,000 tonne garden sand, minor for filling. It is being rehabilitated.
large area of ~20Ha of mining operations, on Pleistocene calcrete. Incomplete production records for period 1993-1996 of ~54,000 tonne. Resource estimate to 3m depth for EML 6424 was 300,000 tonne.
pale red-brown Holocene aeolian sand, with production from 1987-99 of ~122,200 tonne for garden sand product. It has been rehabilitated.
pale red-brown Holocene aeolian sand spread, with production from 2002-04 of ~300 tonne garden sand.
located on the bed of the Bremer River and has been partially rehabilitated.
Quaternary aeolian sand spread, with production from 2 pits either side of the railway line from ~1Ha x 1-2m deep from 1994-2012 of ~28,000 tonne garden sand.
produced garden sand from pale red-brown aeolian sand spread from 1996-2000, then rehabilitated.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ML 5975; ML 5976; MULGUNDAWA; NALPA EAST; NALPA WEST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Holocene playa salt lake complex, with series of evaporation and harvesting ponds developed for production from 1997-2013 of ~115,000 tonne salt.
rubble pit of 3.6Ha x 1-6m deep on Pleistocene-Holocene sand developed as source of road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CAWTES; EML 5866; EML 6423; ML 5865; SWANPORT LIMESTONE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of Pleistocene sheet calcrete, with production from 1994-2013 of calcrete, minor clay products for ~260,000 tonne of which >50,000 tonne was from underlying limestone for use in agriculture.
Holocene sand, with production from 1989-2009 of ~20,000 tonne garden sand. Worked out areas have been progressively rehabilitated.
2 pits (SE one abandoned) on sheet Pleistocene calcrete for production from 1998-2013 of ~180,000 tonne mainly for road base material.
Holocene sand overlying calcrete, with production from 1998-2005 of ~2300 tonne of garden sand, minor calcrete for road base material.
limestone of the Tertiary Blanchetown Clay worked in 1978 for production of ~125,000 tonne road base material. The quarry was rehabilitated in 1980.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; MURRAY BRIDGE CORPORATION; MURRAY BRIDGE FREESTONE; PM 272
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: council quarry developed on Tertiary limestone of the Murray group for use as road base material, and as a supply of building stone. Ceased operating in the 1970s and rehabilitation completed in 2001.
pale red-brown Holocene alluvial sand spread marginal to a small creek for production from 1995-2013 of ~148,000 tonne garden sand.
roadside pit of ~5,500m2 x 1-2m deep on Quaternary sand of the Moornaba Sand, and worked for road fill.

Holocene alluvial sand deposit in creek bed that traverses a sandstone unit of the Backstairs Passage Formation. Production from 1997-2007 was ~16,000 tonne garden sand, minor sandstone for decorative stone.
red-brown alluvial sand spread for garden sand from 1996-2005. It was rehabilitated in 2005 .
roadside scrape and shallow pit developed on granite outcrop (Cambro-Ordovician?) in host Cambrian Backstairs Passage Formation. Drilling identified resource of 32Mtonne to 50m depth.
Holocene sand overlying Bakara calcrete, with production from 1999-2005 of ~24,000 tonne of garden sand, and calcrete for filling.
Holocene sand, with production from 1999-2007 of ~27,000 tonne packing sand.

Holocene sand overlying Bakara Calcrete with production from 2000-13 of ~62,000 tonne of garden sand, and calcrete for road base material. Resource estimate in 2008 was 100,000 tonne sand, and 310,000 tonne calcrete (EML 6033).
Holocene sand deposit, with production from 2000-05 of >1000 tonne garden sand product.
tenure granted as ML 6069 on gypsum occurrence in 2000. No recorded production.

area of abandoned council pits of >20,000m2 x 1-3m deep. Pits developed on thin cover of Holocene sand over Pleistocene bakara Calcrete, and worked by the local council mainly for road fill. Recorded production from 2000-07 was ~40,000 tonne.
Pleistocene calcrete worked by the local council mainly for road base material, also for decorative stone, and specification sand. Production from 2003-12 was ~128,000 tonne.
Holocene sand marginal to the bed of a large creek eroded into Cambrian Tapanappa Formation. Production from 2003-06 of ~35,000 tonne for garden sand.
deposit of magnesite in interdunal lake bed, but no records of it having ever been worked.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CALCA QUARRIES PTY LTD; ML 5760; ML 5844; ML 5847; PADTHAWAY GRANITE; TATIARA GREEN; WILLALOOKA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: occurrence of Ordovician Marcollat Granite, with production from 1992-1994 of 1780 tonne for dimension stone.
council roadside pit of ~2Ha x 1-3m deep on white dolomitic limestone of the Padthaway Formation, and worked for road fill.
Quaternary sand with production from 1974-92 of ~43,100 tonne of mainly garden sand. It was rehabilitated in 1992.
abandoned council pit of ~1.3Ha x 1-3m deep, worked for road fill, and developed on white limestone of the Bridgewater Formation that is part of a low NS-trending ridge of considerable strike length.
sand and limestone of the Holocene Molineaux Sand, with production from 1985-2013 of >100,000 tonne, mainly concrete sand, minor limestone specification sand.
Holocene Molineaux Sand, with production from 1999-2013 of ~50,000 tonne packing sand. The site is being progressively rehabilitated.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BETTS; CAMPBELLS; EML 5447; EML 5697; EML 5858; EML 5879; EML 6009; EML 6087; EML 6186; HUDDS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: one of several adjacent pits on lagoonal Pleistocene white, dolomitic limestone to 1m thick of the Padthaway Formation, with clay, and red clay topsoil. Production of limestone from 1987-2013 estimated at >460,000 tonne for road base material.
limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, with production from 2001-13 of ~58,000 tonne for road base material. Resource for area 300m x 270m x 10m deep estimated at 1.5Mtonne at SG 1.9.
Holocene Molineaux Sand, with production from 1978-2011 of ~7,800 tonne garden and concrete sand. Mined out areas were being progressively rehabilitated.
sand of the Holocene Semaphore Sand Member, with production from 1986-2013 of ~75,000 tonne of garden and concrete sand. The pit was being progressively rehabilitated.

limestone deposit of the Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation worked from 1986-2013 for ~28000 tonne, mainly for road base material, minor end use in agriculture. It was being progressively rehabilitated.
small outcrop of Ordovician Taratap Granite, with production of ~119 tonne in 1985 of dimension stone with the trade name Kingston Blue.
sand deposit of the Pleistocene Padthaway Formation, with production from 1987-2001 of ~21,800 tonne concrete sand.
Pleistocene sand, with production from 2002-2013 of ~41,000 tonne concrete sand. White calcareous sand resource estimate Feb. 2018 of 36,000t within EML 6101.
Holocene gypsum on playa lake bed, with production from campaign mining from 1998-2013 of ~40,000 tonne for use in agriculture, and use in plasterboard manufacture.

Cu-Au-Ag-U-(REE) mineralisation in host hematite breccia, brecciated gneiss & granite beneath ~470m of flat lying cover sediment. resource for S zone 203Mt @ 1.31%Cu, 0.56g/tAu, 6g/tAg, 270ppmU.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup used as building stone in Quorn buildings including BankSA, Mill motel and railway station.
cross-bedded, feldspathic sandstone unit to 6m thick enclosed by red shale siltstone, dip 20W. Statigraphic unit is Bonney Sandstone. Used for old bridge abutments over Hookina Creek.
2 outcrops of Archean iron formation, 60-75 m long by 3-6 m wide. Drill testing of gold-in-calcrete anomaly (Excalibur prospect)returned no values of interest.

past production small, in-situ resources are large. Host is Wonoka Formation. Hard, dense, flaggy dolomite, limestone, slate, dolomitic siltstone used in railway bridge abutments for Pitchi Ritchi Pass rail line.

prominent linear magnetic anomaly, strike length ~14 km, and coincident with outcropping metasediment of the Mount Woods Domain (which included minor units with moderate to prominent magnetite content, possible banded iron formation (BIF).
prominent, linear, aeromagnetic  anomaly, strike length ~ 8 km, drill  tested in hole CR9307. The hole penetrated a broad interval of  magnetite-bearing rock grading 10-15% Fe.
small quarry on weathered, multi-coloured pastel sandstone to claystone of the Appila Tillite. Past production was unknown. In situ resources limited. Mapping along strike recommended.

near-coincident, circular mag-grav feature. Drilling penetrated low-grade Cu-Ag-Au mineralisation in magnetite-skarn alteration in host metasediment of the Wallaroo Group. Cover 800m of younger cover sediment.

several small pits on Appila Tillite. Medium to light-grey, hard quartzite, and a slightly weathered off-white to yellowish-grey feldspathic sandstone. Production for local use, in situ resources limited.

linear magnetic anomaly drilling identified BIF. Estimated resource was 1.6 million tonnes (Mt)/30 m @ 44%Fe (surface chip sampling only). Diamond hole REDD001 completed 2012 for no significant intervals of BIF.
sample of very coarse, crystalline magnetite rock collected in 1961 in Hinckley Range, Musgrave Block. It probably originated from an massive magnetite igneous segregation.

felspathic sandstone in 2 units 5m and 3m wide in host Watervale Sandstone Member. Production was substantial, and in situ resources are large. Stone was rated durable and warranted inclusion as future source.

series of linear magnetic anomalies trending for >1 km, and sourced by magnetite-bearing BIF of Hutchison Group. Inferred resource of 135Mt at 25.5%Fe, recovery 29.3DTR% for~24.5Mt recoverable iron. Part of the Fusion project.
