DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: prominent folded linear aeromagnetic complex being the southern extension of the Warramboo magnetic complex. Drill testing identified source as magnetite-bearing quartz-feldspar gneiss beneath 10-50m younger sediment, and saprock.
discrete magnetic anomaly drill tested to identify magnetite-bearing gneiss, best interval 58 m @ 22.7% Fe.

3 beds 5m, 20-30m and 30m wide of Leasingham Quartzite, worked in 3 adjacent quarries. Stone varied from white to yellowish grey, slightly weathered sandstone to mid to light grey quartzite. All stone buildings in Spalding were from here.
council pit of >10,000m2 x 1-5m deep on narrow unit of weathered quartzite of the Undalya Quartzite, and worked for road fill, minor road aggregate.

body of hematite and goethite formed by the replacement of limestone beds. Several quarries supplied material for use as a flux. Estimated production was 2032 tonne. The excavation is now in the residential area, and has been filled in.

located on a bold ironstone ridge developed on flat-lying Cambrian rock. Workings were small openings on goethite that were mined for use as a flux, and sent to Port Pirie. The ironstone was associated with phosphate-rich rock.
linear aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify magnetite-bearing gneiss Fe values 10-20%Fe from 24-157m. Depth of younger cover varied from 25-68 m.

world-class IOCG-type mag-grav anomaly in the eastern Andamooka Magnetic Complex. Drilling identified sequence of altered volcanics & metasediment, with significant Fe-metasomatism, minor Cu mineralisation beneath 400-500m of cover sediment.

60m x 30m body of magnetite, partly altered to martite and goethite. Host Archean metasediment. Resource ~175,800 tonne/30m. Surface sample at 44.3%Fe. DTR testwork recovered 79.9% of the iron at a grade of 65.7% Fe.
drilling west of Iron Baron identified 2-12m thickness of hematite and goethite scree eroded from the adjacent massive hematite deposits.
several scattered hills of Archean iron formation. They were tested in one drillhole which intersected iron formation from 50-72 m, grading 30-44% Fe.
erected in 1857 to treat copper ore from the district. It was purchased by the Bremer Mining Company in 1864 to refine the matte produced from the Bremer Mine. It operated until 1878.
epithermal-style Au-Pb-Zn-Ag mineralisation over an area ~4km2 in a complex vein system in host Corunna Conglomerate. Best value 21m at 21g/t Au and 83g/t Ag.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 classic beach placer deposits. Drilling identified a resource (2013) of  123Mt @ 7.7%HM for contained 5.2Mt HM @ 51% Zr, 4% Rt, & 27% ilmenite. foreshore HM sand deposit in host Ooldea Sand. ASX release by Iluka Resources for 31/12/2016 is 53.7Mtonne at 1.9% HM for contained HMS of 998,000 tonne at 64.8%Zr, 4.8%Rt, 11.1% Ilm, and 15.1% clay.

dolomitic, with ferruginous-manganese oxide-rich caps, with the slopes covered by similar debris. The mineralisation appeared to be surficial, about 1 m deep, up to 10 m wide, with grades estimated to be highest at the surface.

manganese oxide occurred in association with thin ferruginous caps on rising ground, also as pockets in the host dolomite. Claims were pegged, and some workings were opened, but the grade was too low to repay expenses.
areas of surface manganese oxides located near Constitution Hill in the northern Flinders Ranges. There are several small rises capped with ferruginous-manganese oxide enrichment.

small rise, 100 m long, adjacent to a road, and ~ 6 m above a nearby creek. It consisted of a ferruginous, manganese oxide-rich cap extending for some distance west up the side of a large hill. The host rock was a slate.

located in an embayment on the western shore of Pernatty Lagoon, and to the north-west of the main workings. There was minor production of manganese oxide from pits, and a single long cut. The host rock was Woocalla Dolomite.
reported to be 3 miles east of the Gunyah copper workings on the northwestern shore of Pernatty Lagoon.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: located east of the Sweet Nell copper mine. It was taken out for manganese in 1918. There was also a series of 10 mineral claims taken out east of the Sweet Nell mine for manganese over the period 1903-1918.
alluvial sand overlying basement of the Cambrian Carrickalinga Head Formation. The pit is located 5km east of Tanunda. Production of packing sand from 2006-10 was estimated at 4,000 tonne.
deposit of sand of the Woorinen Formation located ~8 km SW of Barmera. Production of garden and packing sand from 2006-09 estimated at 5000 tonne.
linear aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify magnetite-bearing gneiss, with Fe grades to 15-20%. Depth of younger cover sediment was 70 m.
bullseye aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify interval of BIF from 90-135 m, and Fe-rich pelite 135-154 m (EOH). There were no assays for iron. Depth to ""basement"" was 70 m.

linear aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify magnetite-bearing gneiss with sporadic assaying indicating Fe% in the 15-25% range. Banded iron formation (BIF) was penetrated in the last 4 m, but was not assayed. Depth to basement was 3 m.
linear aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify intervals of hematite-magnetite breccia. Depth of younger cover was 99m.
large, significant linear aeromagnetic anomaly. Several drillholes penetrated rock with moderate to weak content of magnetite-bearing skarn/metasomatite. Depth to basement varied from 60 m to >80 m.

linear magnetic trend from magnetite-bearing Braemar Ironstone. JORC inferred resource for 6.5km strike length 1.5Bt @ ~15%DTR, head grade 18%Fe for 228Mt contained magnetite concentrate at 69.8%Fe for 159Mt contained iron.

aeromagnetic anomaly source as magnetite-bearing IF of the Breaemar Iron Formation. Part of a larger, folded linear complex of 1.5-2.5km strike length. Preliminary results identified thickness of 40-60m for a single bed, target resource 50-80Mt.

prominent aeromagnetic anomaly, ~5 km strike, source magnetite-bearing IF of the Braemar Iron Formation. Exploration in 2011 identified a resource target for a NE-trending zone of 3-3.5km, and for a single bed of 100-300m thickness of 1-1.5Bt.

aeromag anomaly on mgt-bearing Braemar IF, thickness ~124m, Strike length 3-3.5km, head grades 10-30%Fe. Preliminary DTR testwork gave mass recoveries >20% for ~69%Fe magnetite concentrate product. Exploration target 300Mt.

quarry of ~4ha x 1-10m deep developed on grey dolomite of the lower member of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Originally worked for flux for use at the Port Pirie Smelters. later use for road fill.
prospecting pits for iron flux on goethitic laterite in flat country, no bedrock exposed.

several shallow pits developed on a ridge of ironstone, and formed by the convergence of 2 beds of hematite siltstone of the Braemar Ironstone at the keel of a S-plunging syncline
~260m east of Terminus Quarry, a number of pits and a shallow open cut to 4m deep on low-grade eluvium made up of ironstone scree cemented by clay and siliceous material, no bedrock exposed.

coarse grained, micaceous hematite in anastomosing veins to 70 cm thick, and subparallel to the strike of the enclosing rocks. Testwork confirmed its suitability for use in the paint industry. An estimate resource was 110 tons.

deep workings on vertical quartz veins associated with schistose, ferruginous lodes in a metasediment host (Stonyfell Quartzite). Production recorded of 1273 tonne @ 16g/tAu for 666.5oz (20.7kg) bullion gold.

production of metasiltstone from host Mintaro Shale from 2005-13 estimated at 250,000 tonne from a single pit. There is a smaller, abandoned pit ~140m to the east, no historic details known, and an adjacent, abandoned roadside council pit.

Permian coal seams in an elongate (25 x 2 km), northwest trending trough consisting of 6 major seams up to 15m thick. Tentative resource ~700Mt of sub-bituminous coal of variable ash content, with moderate S levels, and high salt content.
coal deposit discovered during exploration drilling in 1993 in Triassic sedimentary covering an area of ~3km2. Inferred resource of 23Mt of low rank coal.
roadside council pit of 10,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on weathered metasiltstone of the Saddleworth Formation for road fill.
abandoned council pit of <5,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered, grey-blue dolomitic slate to sandstone and siltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, pale brown shale/siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
tenure granted in 2006 as EML 6214 for limestone of the Gambier Limestone for road base material and agricultural enduse, no production reported.

deposit of sand and limestone of the Holocene Moornaba Sand. Production for 1 year from June 2006 of garden sand, ~38,000 tonne, and limestone for road ballast, ~25,000 tonne, for total  63,000 tonne.
drilling identified skarn-related Zn-Pb-Ag-Mo mineralisation associated with margins of altered monzonite dated at 1729 +/- 13Ma.
workings identified by field inspection, no records found. On 100K geology dataset it is located within the Skillogalee Dolomite.
deposit of the Holocene Bunyip Sand. Production from 1980-1988 of ~7500 tonne of filter sand. Rehabilitation was completed in 1989.
worked for concrete sand by a small dragline to a depth of 3.5 m for production of ~1200 tonne.  It was rehabilitated in 1998.
mining by Ministerial approval to extract clay for the lining of evaporative ponds at Kimberley Clark, Millicent. The pit was rehabilitated simultaneously. No production figure recorded.

abandoned shallow pit on Pleistocene sand spread, and developed by the Engineering and water Supply (E & WS) department.
shallow pit on dunal sand deposit.
quarry of ~5,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered gneiss deposit in Barossa Complex worked for road base material.
deposit of Holocene creek sand and gravel. Production estimated at 34,400 tonne of garden and concrete sand from 1980-94.
seasonal production from sandstone of the Tapanappa Formation for enduses as fill, road ballast, spalls, and specification sand. Total production from 2003-13 estimated at 33,000 tonne.
deposit of Pleistocene alluvial sand, estimated production of 1150 tonne from 1987-88. EML 6400 resource estimate ~100,000 tonne.

soil geochemical anomaly with drilling identifying weak Cu-Au-Ag mineralisation in altered host igneous rock. Only narrow mineralised intervals (max 2m @ 4.4g/t Au) were identified beneath previously identified, shallower high-grade gold intercepts.

drilling on magnetic anomaly identified elevated Fe2O3 values to 32.19% TiO2, 5.32% in host magnetite-bearing granulite. Al2O3 content of anorthosite recorded in some areas of 25-30%, though generally less.
deposit of limestone of the Bridgewater Formation. Seasonal production from 2005-13 of material for road ballast was ~10,000 tonne.
sand of the Bridgewater Formation, and located ~20 km SE of Millicent. Production of packing sand estimate of 24,000 tonne from 2007-13.
barite lode to 12m wide infilled a fault zone in host beds of the Umberatana and Wilpena Groups. Resource ~30,000t to 6m depth.
deposit of Holocene sand and gravel, with production of building, concrete and packing sand, and gravel from 2000-13 of ~133,000 tonne.
located on reserved ground, being a lens of jade, with surface dimensions of 1.5 m x 0.5 m.

located on ML 4339, pod 0.2m x 0.2 m, of coarse tremolite. There was no recorded production. Host rock was Miltalie Gneiss, and quartzite, calc-silicate of Warrow Quartzite. Area 5m x 0.6 m of massive, coarse-grained tremolite float.
located on ML 4898, and was a lens of jade, with surface dimensions of 0.2 m x 0.1 m.

nephrite recovered from numerous pods designated 114 A-G. Pale coloured, grey to grey-green. Some mottled green, which was considered attractive and easy to work. Total production from 1978-92 ~70 tonnes.

deposit of Quaternary sand, estimated 19,000 tonne production of garden sand from 1990-91. Rehabilitation was completed in 1993.

pit of ~1.6Ha x 1-3m deep on limestone of the Padthway Formation, and worked for road fill.

high-grade pod of surface mineralisation with average grade 7.5% Pb + Zn over 300 m2, and with maximum grades of 19% Pb, 33% Zn, and 158 g/t Ag. It was tested in 7 drill holes (PWP 1-7).
HM-strand line of the Loxton-Parilla Sand, western Murray Basin. Revised resource ~0.7Mt @ 4%HM for ~28,000t HM conc. Production 2007-15 >180,000 tonne HM conc.

lease on sand and clay of the Molineaux Sand for road making, and minor garden sand. Recorded production from 1973-77 of 4065 tonne.

drilling of gold-in-calcrete anomaly identified sub-economic primary Au, weak Cu mineralisation in a vein system in host fresh gneissic bedrock. Maiden inferred resource 94,000 oz (2665 Kg) contained gold.

marginal to ovate Oolgelima Intrusive Complex. Drilling identified IOCG(REE)-style mineralisation in host magnetite-amphibole-pyroxene rock. Best value hole WS003, 4m massive sulphide @ 1.12% Cu.

weak linear magnetic anomaly. Drilling identified weak, disseminated pyrite-chalcopyrite-sphalerite mineralisation in host meta-arkose of the Mount Woods Complex. Best values from 80-86m at 516ppm Zn, 85ppm Pb, and 73ppm Cu.

air-core holes with elevated Zn-Pb-Cu in host calcsilicate near base Warrow Quartzite, best value 2750ppmZn, 580ppmCu and 800ppmPb. Follow-up drilling identified marble with interbands pelite, with weak pyrrhotite and pyrite, no significant values.

Sn-Au-Cu mineralisation in wide, lode-like structure of strongly altered volcanics. Mineralisation identified as scattered poddy Sn-Au rich ore shoots in a widespread, lower-order remnant Cu anomalous envelope.

small, shallow pit developed on slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production records apparent.

prominent ~7,500nT aeromagnetic anomaly, tested in Hole KD94002, penetrating qz-hem-mt-chl rock, with 7m from 156m at 0.14 g/tAu. Petrological studies suggested that the anomalous gold bearing interval was of hydrothermal origin.

isolated aeromagnetic anomaly with reconnaissance drilling identifying poddy, ~40m thick magnetite-bearing skarn @ 40%Fe beneath ~90m cover sediment. Host dolomite/calc-silicate of Archean Sleaford Complex(?). No resource estimate.

~450m length of a sand dune located within a farming area. The dune trends WNW and has an overall length in the order of 6km. No production records apparent.
dunal sand deposit trending WNW with legth 1.6km maximum width above plain level ~100m. MC 3571 offered but not taken up by the interested party.
council pit of ~2Ha x 1-3m deep on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road fill material.
assay results from detrital davidite samples returned 2% and 4% U with 700ppm and 1250ppm Th respectively.
rubble pit with estimated production from campaign mining from 2006-08 was 22,000 tonnes.

low-grade Pb-Zn mineralisation in host calc-silicate of the Bimba Formation traceable over ~10km strike, and beneath 80-120m of sand and clay cover. Drilling penetrated up to 54m wide intervals with 1% combined Pb +Zn.

best value 8m at 3.28%HM in hole P1. Zone 300 m wide, to 16m thick, average 1.3%HM. Preliminary mineralogical examination indicated variable, modest to poor HM dominated by iron oxide.

magnetic lineament intersection. Drilling identified weak Cu mineralisation in host quartzite, with trace pink carbonate veining, and epidote alteration. Also tuffaceous wackes, metasomatite with minor pyrite, and trace chalcopyrite.

gossanous iron formation associated with magnetic anomalies. Diamond hole intersected 2 zones of anomalous Zn in chloritized gneiss and graphitic schist. Drilling confirmed presence of magnetite iron formation, best values 20-30%Fe.
complex gold-in-calcrete anomaly with drilling confirming weak Au-(Cu-Mo) mineralisation in host intensely deformed, altered meta-igneous rock.
low-grade, stratabound Cu-Pb-Ag-Co and Pb-Ag mineralisation over 45m interval in flat-lying pre-Pandurra Formation volcanic/metasediment host (informal Fresh Well Formation).

drilling identified narrow zone of anomalous copper geochemistry, and mapping several areas of anomalous scheelite, best value 1.5%W.  Host calc-silicate was sheared, disrupted and laminated. No follow up drilling.

magnetic complex on area of non outcrop WNW of Arkaba Diapir. Drilling identified altered mafic volcanic/intrusive and massive magnetite, presumed to represent xenoliths within the carbonate diapir. Altered rock Cu to 0.2%, with weak Au t 50 ppb.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: kimberlitic indicator minerals on N of island. 7 diamonds recovered. High resolution mag/grav conducted. Drilling confirmed indicator minerals below surface (at the overburden / bedrock interface) but no primary source rock was identified.
diamonds discovered near Echunga by gold panners in 1859, and reports of up to 200 diamonds including 50 saleable gems were recorded through to 1900. Host was Tertiary sands and gravels.

128 diamonds and fragments were recovered in the mid-1980s from Permian basal conglomerate. In 1998, an additional 56 diamonds were recovered from renewed exploration trenching, the largest being 3.5 mm and weighing 0.34 ct.
140 microdiamonds were found in shallow, weathered kimberlite, part of the Eurelia Kimberlite Field.
1 small diamond 0.9 X 0.5 mm was found in a creek gravels west of Kapunda.
single diamond weighing over 1 ct was found in alluvial gravels southwest of Mount Kingston near peake Creek. later prospecting returned 4 grains gold from basal conglomerate unit.
single diamonds were found from several sediment samples from the Pine Creek, The Oaks, Oak Park, and Double Dam areas.
single microdiamond size 0.5 x 0.4 mm was found in Narina Creek, 12 km SW of Mount Roebuck.

30 microdiamonds at 0.0068ct recovered from 3 samples on Manunda Creek adjacent to 5 kimberlites. Palaeo transport models link indicator minerals & microdiamonds to structural and mafic intrusve relationships.
soil geochemistry anomaly drill tested to identify graphitic, pyritic metasediment of the Karinya Shale. Only weak mineralisation was noted, with best assays of 1235 ppm Pb, 1425 ppm Zn.

anomalous soil geochemistry tested by drilling to identify weak mineralisation in metasediment at lithological contacts near base of the Karinya Shale. Assays were weakly anomalous in Cu, Zn, Pb, and As.

ironstone with anomalous base metals including Cu to 1%. Host limestone of the Milendella Limestone Member. Drilling identified ironstone thinner at depth (30m), with only weakly anomalous base metal geochemistry.
hole MT23C penetrated sediment with ~40 ppm U on clay interface with oxidised sand in an interpreted NW-trending palaeochannel.
AG0714 penetrated sediment with a 4 m wide gamma ray anomaly up to ten times background. Best assay was 213 ppm U.
anomalous Uranium assay values ranged from 93-158 ppm U, in host weakly altered metamorphic rock in the Coober Pedy Ridge Domain.
anomalous U in palaeochannel sand in several holes including hole U23 on the southernmost traverse, western end.
deposit of HM sands over an apparent width of 1-3.5 km and a strike length of 8km. Mineralisation interpreted as beach placer in style, averaging 10 m thick.

drilling identified HM mineralisation in 2 horizons. Bulk samples for upper horizon at 2.77% HM for 86.1% altered ilmenite & leucoxene. Lower horizon 1.94% HM for 66.1% altered ilmenite & leucoxene. Grades and volumes considered uneconomic.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested for best value 6 ppmAu in narrow shear zone in host metagranite of the Kenella Gneiss. Drill hole intercepts identified zone dipped ~35N as narrow shear zone 2-10cm wide.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested for best intercept of 21m @ 0.49g/tAu, including 4m @ 1.24g/tAu. Strong Au-Bi association. Elevated pyrrhotite and pyrite, trace ccp and Aspy in host biotite amphibole schist of the Lincoln Complex.
3 x roadside council pits for cumulative area ~3ha x 1-3m deep adjacent to a 2km stretch of the Strzelecki Track, and developed on clays of the Quaternary Pooraka Formation for use in road making.

narrow 5cm quartz veins in joint patterns in host sandstone of Cox Sandstone. Rock chip samples from spoils @ to 9g/t Au. Excavations were restricted to local zones where quartz veining was more intense. No production figures were determined.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ANABAMA AAA; BENDA PROJECT; GUM DAM
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: mapping, rock chip sampling identified >20ppmAu over 200m strike in 1-2m wide vein quartz in host metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Tested in 2 drill holes gave best assay of 15ppmAu, with anomalous Cu & As.

magnetic anomaly drill tested and identified weak Cu-Au mineralisation in quartz-magnetite alteration zone in host was metasediment of the Willyama Complex. Best assay was in hole M96RCDWK14, 0.4m at 6.77%Cu, 0.34g/tAu from 108.2m.
primary chalcopyrite penetrated within a magnetite-rich Wehrlite at the top of the Kalka intrusion, grades to 0.37%Cu, elevated Fe to >30%, Ti 7%, V >3000ppm.
pit presumed developed on shallow calcrete for road aggregate for the Jacinth-Ambrosia operations.
pit presumed developed on shallow basement for road aggregate for mine infrastructure at Jacinth-Ambrosia.
surface mineralised Bimba Formation. No production figures apparent.
drilling identified HM assemblage ilmenite (56%), zircon (16%), leucoxene (4%). Follow up identified thicker intercepts of low grade HM to 3%, and 3-15m thick. Probable J-bay feature.
supergene enrichment gives surface anomalies of 550ppm U. Best assay results from drilling indicate 290ppm U3O8. Mineralisation hosted in weathered sheared gneiss of the Peake Metamorphics.
roll front style mineralisation was intesected in multiple drillholes. Drillhole MT 97 recorded peak count from downhole logs of 2550 cps from 100m depth at clay interface.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MOUNT ALVEY EAST; MT ALVEY; TANKAANU MAGNETITE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historical geological mapping and sampling over the East Deering Hills area identified a zone of Pt-Pd mineralisation on the contact of gabbronorite with melagabbro.
identified from shaft symbol on Olary 1:250,000 map, no commodity information, presumed it is copper
long abandoned, part rehabilitated shallow council pit of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council quarry of >20,000m2 x 1-6m deep on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road fill. Now the site of a industrial winery complex.
deposit of Quaternary sand, which produced as estimated 68,970 tonne of foundry sand from 1981-1988.
council quarry of ~8,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white, Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
roadside scrape of >30,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
tear-shaped salt lake, dimensions ~800m long NW by maximum 400m wide SE. It is located ~3.4km east of the Princes Highway near Burnsfield (9 km N of Snowtown). Production from 2007-09 ~1000t.
drilling identified 7m-30m thicknesses of black organic-rich Tertiary. Test work from a 2m interval produced hydrocarbon yield of 106 kg/t, and showed potential for oil generation.
deposit of red clay in host slate of the Cambrian Carrickalinga Head Formation. Last recorded production was in 1982, with total production of 8115 tonne inclusive of 1080 tonne of slate.
scrape of ~2,500m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered, white clayey, fractured sandstone with interbedded siltstone and dolomite of the Bungaree Quartzite.
developed on a deposit of sheet calcrete in 2009, with production 2009-13 ~27,000t. Lease area 7.5 Ha, thickness of calcrete 1.5-2m. Resources ~150,000t.
roll-front type Uranium mineralisation, within sand of the upper Eyre Formation, and within the Carnanto Palaeochannel.. Best results from gamma 826 Cps from 103.25m in hole GNC009.

demagnetised splay of the Yerda Shear Zone. Drilling intersected minor quartz veining, and red rock alteration was encountered in host granitoids. Elevated gold values in saprolitic clay overlying basement.
Drilling identified zones of elevated metal values within the regolith interval, with maximum values of 0.4% Ni and 287 ppb Pt+Pd.

IP & gravity target drill tested and identified as altered metasediment with alteration and mineralisation assemblage of copper sulphide-pyrite-magnetite, possibly after intermediate volcanic host. Low level Cu-(Fe-Co-Zn) anomalism detected.
anomalism in an area of outcrop of weathered metasediment to gneiss. The areal extent of the anomaly was 2.5 x 1.2 km, trending NS. Sampling returned XRF values up to 36ppm U and 220ppm Th.
surface profile of calcrete present as a horizon of cap rock overlying a zone of progressively degraded limestone rock and marl, the profile to 1.5-2m deep. Resource >1Mt, no recorded production.

soil-Zn geochemical anomaly. Mapping identified stratabound gossan, with elevated zinc in host siltstone of the Bunyeroo Formation. Follow-up drilling penetrated black pyritic siltstone, with best values 1100ppmZn from 67-78m.
inferred resource of 45.5 million tonnes at a grade of 280ppm eU3O8 for an estimated 12,700 tonnes of U3O8.
2 small, adjacent roadside council pits of total area >5,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
NW-most 2.5 km of a linear 10km magnetic anomaly trending NW. Three lines of holes were completed across the anomaly for a best intersection of 4m @ 15.2% Pb, including 1m @ 21.3% Pb, with trace Zn.
mineralisation occurs in 2 zones of Uranium enriched sands. Drilling returned best results of 4m @ 0.055 % pU3O8 and 2m @ 0.039 % pU3O8.

foreshore HM sands deposit hosted by Ooldea sands. Drilling identified an elongate orebody, with measured resource for 31/12/2016 of 23.7Mtonne at 6.3% HM for contained HMS of 1.49Mtonne at 62.7% Ilm, 13.2% Zr, 0.9% Rt, and 9.4% clay.
best assay result of 390 cps in hole WT0004 with equivalent grade at 100ppm eU3O8 over 1.8m. Significant gamma anomalism was encountered in 4 holes
tenure granted over the NW end of a NW-trending longitudinal Quaternary sand dune. No recorded production.
large surface spread of Quaternay sand, operating only in 2009 for production of ~70,000t. Resources ~75,000t.
pit developed on a deposit of Quaternary sand. Estimated production in 2009 97,000 tonne.
pit developed on a deposit of Quaternary sand in 2009, with production 2009-13 ~30,000t.
epigenetic, structurally controlled Zn-Pb mineralisation in host basal Cambrian Woodendinna Dolomite. Resources ~40,000t @ 25.5% Zn.
several quartz reefs in host metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup outcropping between Watts and Kerosene Gullies. No production figures were determined.
Port Pirie Smelting Works, built in 1889, becoming the world's biggest lead smelter by 1934. Primary source of ore was from the Broken Hill Pb-Zn mines.

site of treatment plant used produce yellowcake from davidite concentrate railed from the Radium Hill mine from 1955-1962. Tailings confined to 6 dams over 22Ha with resource of ~100 tonne Ytrium and scandium oxide. Also ~20% rutle.
Mongolata Goldfield battery, crushed a total of 7600 tonne of ore for a recovery of 318 kg of gold bullion.
abandoned roadside council pit of >5,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Quaternary sand, and worked for road fill.
pit developed on a deposit of Tertiary limestone. Production 2009-13 >6,000t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: 840 PARATOO RAILWAY QUARRY; RAILWAY RESERVE 313; SA RAILWAYS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry of ~1.6Ha x 1-8m deep on dolerite for use as road seal aggregates, rail ballast, scalps and crusher sand.
tenure granted for Quaternary clay for the Hillgrove Resources ""Kanmantoo Project"" tailings storage facility. ~170,000 tonne recovered in 2011.
opened in the 1920- 1930's era and may not have even procured a Mining Lease.  A tramway was used to cart the finished product from the factory to the Marion Bay jetty.
Quaternary dune sand deposit measuring 600x80m and 3m deep, ie 144,000m3. Production estimate from dimensions of excavation is 15,000 tonne.

2 U-mineralised sand layers of the Eyre Formation. Resource drilling on the central (Saffron) area has identified an inferred resource of 4.36Mt @ 346ppm eu3O8 for ~1510 tonne contained U3O8. Further U identified at Bridget and Yolanda prospects.
drill hole BLD084 returned a result of 1,652ppm U3O8 over 7.5cm, within a zone of 329ppm U3O8 from 87.0 ¿ 87.4 metres.
drill hole BLD085 returned a result of 864ppm U3O8 over 10cm, within a zone of 247ppm U3O8 from 105.7 ¿ 106.1 metres.

surface samples of massive magnetite, magnetite-bearing gabbro with anomalous V, Fe. Coincident with folded linear aeromagnetic anomaly. Best value was 0.83% V2O5, 55.1%Fe from a sample of massive magnetite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEVERLEY; MC 4203; MC 4233; ML 6387; PARALANA URANIUM; PEPEGOONA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: roll-front U, mineral resource ~2.2 Mt at 0.18% U3O8, containing 4.0 kt (8.5 M lb) U3O8 (0.15m% GT cut-off).
limestone quarries developed on a deposit of Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation. Production from 2007-2013 ~8,000t.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 6272; P. STAUDE; PIGEON FLAT; SITE 27
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: limestone deposit of the Pleistocene Padthway Formation, with production from 2007-2013 estimated at 220,000 tonne of mainly road base material, minor limestone for agricultural use.
pit developed on deposit of Pleistocene Woorinen Sand, with production from 2006-13 estimated at 10,000 tonne.
sand deposit of a major Tertiary Palaeochannel, mainly for production of garden sand. Operations commenced in 2009, with an estimated 25,000 tonne recovered to 2013. No resource estimate.
deposit of Quaternary Molineaux Sand, production from 2006-12 ~19,000t. No resource estimate.
EML of 16Ha granted in the early 1970s. Subsequently shallow scrape developed for recorded production of 540 tonne of red plastic clay for use as road base in a six month period in 1973.

deposit of Middle Pleistocene Bakara Calcrete, overlain by a remnant east-west linear sand dune of the Pleistocene Molineaux Sand Dune System. Resources of 6000t of sand, & 800,000t of calcrete. Production 2010-13 ~90,000t.
deposit of limestone of Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation. Resource ~1.5Mt. Production 2010-2013 25,000 tonne.

narrow vein barite deposit, no production records. Host was metasediment of the Neoproterozoic Umberatana Group. A shallow pit occurs ~700m to the NW, and appears to have been used as a road metal pit by the local council.

wide spaced dragbit drilling identified geochemical anomaly. Follow up diamond coring failed to detect significant mineralisation. Holes penetrated sequence of muscovite-biotite-dolomite metasiltstone, with trace graphite, rutile, and pyrite.
worked a deposit of quaternary sand from 1980-85 for production of an estimated 19,900 tonne of sand for use as garden/filling sand.
Quaternary surface sand spread in open paddock in Aberfoyle Park. Recorded production in 1977of 190 tonne. Shallow pit is rehabilitated.

small deposit of unconsolidated alluvial sand with significant quantities of organic matter located adjacent to North Para River. Resource ~45,000t. Production from 2010 to 2013 estimated at >10,000 tonne.

surface sheet sand, clean to weak silty, generally meeting specifications for filling sand. Sequence of thin (~15cm) soil veneer, sheet sand, underlying clayey sand. Resources ~300,000t to 1-2m depth. Production to 2013 >1,000 tonne.
limestone deposit on Bridgewater Formation, resources ~260,000 cubic metres for mining to 2-3m depth. 2010-13 production <70,000t.
2 adjacent, abandoned pits of total area >15,000m2 x 1-2m deep on sand of the Permian Cape Jervois Formation, and excavated in the 1990s during constuction of the Wirrina Resort complex.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 3107; EML 3108; EML 3110; EML 3111; EML 3112; EML 3247; EML 3248; EML 3249; EML 4484; EML 4485; EML 4486; EML 4546; EML 4547; EML 4548; EML 4549; EML 4961; EML 5020; EML 5350; EML 5351; EML 5352; EML 5353; EML 5789; EML 5790; EML 5791; MC 3779; MC 3780; MOUNT ARDEN STATION; NANTILLA CREEK; PORT AUGUSTA (AMATEK)
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quartz sand to 3m deep in Sandy Creek, worked for distance >12km from 1961-2012 for >650,000 tonne. Resource estimated at 1.16Mt (1984).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLANCHEWATER PALAEOCHANNEL; CAULDRON ENERGY LTD; GEORGE CREEK
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: anomalous Uranium mineralisation over 12 km across widths up to 4 km returned a number of significant results, including 1m at 263ppm eU3O8.
early 2000s drilling identified 5m at 26.9%Zn within broader halo of 30m at 1.23% zinc. 2005 follow-up diamond drilling confirmed Zn mineralisation in host mylonite to 230m depth.

circular magnetic anomaly as possible carbonatite. Drilling identified banded amphibolite with no anomalous geochemistry recorded. 2009 shallow drilling returned Ni and Cr values >1000 ppm, anomalous REE 10-20 x crustal abundance.
>20m thick Tertiary coal seam penetrated at ~230m depth in intramontane Walloway Basin. Inferred a resource of 1-1.3 billion tonnes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ALFORD; BLUE TONGUE; BRUCE; LARWOOD; SIX WAYS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drilling identified Mo-Cu (Co) mineralisation in narrow, discontinuous alteration zones in host altered metasediment of Wandearah Metasiltstone. Later drilling identified Alford West prospect, best value 10m @ 4.3%Cu as chalcocite.

shellgrit for ~16 km within and bordering the 800m coastal protection zone between Port Broughton and Tickera. Production 115,635 tonnes since 1907. Drilling in 1989 for inferred resource of 26.6Mt, 3.2Mt outside the 800m coastal zone.

sediment-hosted Cu-(U) mineralisation in conglomerate intercalcated with Jarold Basalt Member Volcanics. Diamond hole PP5 identified disseminated chalcopyrite and chalcocite, best value 7.25m @ 0.84% Cu from 296.25-303.5m.
copper mineralisation in host Appila Tillite in the Black Hill anticline. Sampling of dump material by Utah developments in 1984 returned a sample with 6%Cu.
gossan sampled during regional mapping by State Geological Survey returned 21.4%Cu, 2.3 g/tAu, 920ppmZn & 440ppm Ag.

exploration for gold in the Paratoo Anticline and traversed by many quartz-iron oxide veins, gossans. Rock chip sampling disclosed widespread anomalous Au, Bi, Cu, As & Ag. Best value 4.4%Cu, 420ppm Ag, 1050ppm As.
copper mineralisation in quartz-goethite vein in host siltstone and sandstone of the Umberatana Group along a NW-trending fault zone. Drilling identified a best value of 2%Cu, elevated As.
copper mineralisation occurrence in quartz-infill of shear zone in a dolerite dyke. Rock chip sample gave value of 28.8%Cu.
concealed magnetite calc-silicate rock hosting Cu-Au mineralisation, with anomalous Mo, Co, Ag. Best intersection, hole KY1362, 14.3m @ 1.26%Cu, 0.2ppm Au.
IOCG-type mag/grav target, with drilling identifying variably altered, brecciated, mineralised volcanic rock beneath 870m of cover sediment. Assay results included 53m @ 0.02kg/tU3O8 from 907m.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Chalcopyrite,  Gold,  Molybdenite,  Uranium Minerals (Non Specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: gossanous ironstone with anomalous Au-Ag-Cu-Pb-Zn-Ba-Mo-U-Sb geochemistry. 35 aircore holes returned best value of 3m @ 0.86g/t Au in hole NKA405.

aircore hole ACJH 33 with 1m at 1g/tAu from 72m. Aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to identify weak Cu mineralisation in quartz-carbonate-chalcopyrite veins with associated albitic alteration in host altered, albite-magnetite metapelite.

weak Cu-(Au) mineralisation on albite-quartz-epidote & mica-rich metasediment of the Pelite Suite of the Willyama Supergroup. Aircore drilling identified trace Cu-Au anomalism associated with albitic bands, best value 3m @ 0.77g/t Au. Ref: Env 9894

circular aeromagnetic anomaly tested in 7 aircore holes. Holes penetrated laminated, pyritic shale to biotite schist to grey, micaceous, laminated slate and shale, possible Willyama Supergroup. Low-level Cu-Au anomalism was identified.

weak Cu-Au-Pb-Zn-Ag mineralisation drill testing identified Cu mineralised quartz/iron oxide breccia thought to be a palaeo-laterite, & basement of weak mineralisation in host clays of weathered basement of finely laminated phyllite, variably pyritic. Ref: Env 8068

magnetic anomaly interpreted as broad antiform in albite-magnetite rock. Diamond hole DD92CD1 penetrated flat-lying graphitic shale with disseminated to massive pyrite bands, trace sphalerite, and chalcopyrite. Ref: Env 8068
low level Cu-U anomalism was detected in red and green feldspar-amphibole-diopside-carbonate-iron oxide metasomatite. Best assay in PBD 29, 192-194m, 2m @ 0.68%Cu.

diamond drilling on basement high with crystalline basement at 36m of amphibolite representing metamorphosed basic volcanics of the Willamulka Volcanics. The hole penetrated an cumulative 6m @ 0.25%Cu from 74.5-97.5m.
stratabound Pb-Zn sulphides in host black shales, overlying Doora schist, associated with exhalative volcanics.

multiple diamond drill holes identified low-grade chalcopyrite and widespread pyrite mineralisation in carbonate-dominant veining in host grey metasediment. Aggregated sections from DDH213 for 213m @ 0.25%Cu, sporadic gold.
auger drill Zn-Pb-Cu geochemistry anomaly tested by IP with follow up diamond drilling. Hole DDH 183 penetrated significant Zn-Pb-Cu mineralisation in graphitic metasediment. Ref: Env 6999
developed on a low dunal sand deposit of the Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation. Resources within EML 6269 were estimated at 40,000 tonnes.  Production from 2008-13 was estimated at 17,000 tonne.
drilling identified mineralisation in hole DDH 1, down hole logs recorded a peak of 290 cps for the interval 17-23m. The corresponding analyses averaged 60ppm U3O8, maximum 90ppm U3O8.

gold in a series of parallel, gently dipping quartz veins from 2-20cm wide in host quartzite of the Gumbowie Arkose & along strike from Altimeter Mine. Total production from 1931-63 ~1.76kg bullion gold from 71.6t treated ore @ 24.6g/t.

series of parallel, gently dipping quartz veins from 2-20cm wide in host quartzite of the Fortress Hill Formation. Location is uncertain, the mine was located at the southern end of Cain's claim (Altimeter Mine). No production records evident.
series of parallel, gently dipping quartz veins from 2-20cm wide in host quartzite of the Fortress Hill Formation. Production to 1946 of 60.2 tonne for 2655.3gm gold at 44g/tAu.
series of parallel, gently dipping quartz veins from 2-20 cm wide in host quartzite of the Fortress Hill Formation. Production from 1932-38, 23.3 tonne yielded 426.6gm bullion gold at 18g/tAu.

surface anomalous molybdenum returned in samples of lateritic scree as strand line to the lake, which was located adjacent to a the Encounter Bay Granite, presumed source of the Mo. Sampling of the granite returned no anomalous values.

located ~800m WSW from #7 deposit. Vein of white and grey talc, ~ 45m long by 2.5m wide, dip 45N, discontinuous along strike. Tested in 16 airtrack holes in 1991/92 along the vein for only poor intercepts, further work not recommended.
located 1.1km WSW of # 7 deposit, a talc vein exposed in a bulldozer scrape. The vein dips S under quartzite. Not drill tested.
talc vein trending W, with tremolite present in host dolomite.Not drill tested.

located east of # 7 deposit, western extension of the Lady Doreen deposit. Several discontinuous seams of talc at Amberoona-Balcanoona Formation contact over 100m distance. Tested in 15 airtrack holes in 1991/92, with good intercepts returned.

talc vein trending NE, up to 5m wide, and in host dolomite. Exposed in a shallow costean. Also large body of tremolite located 7m NE. Tested in 3 diamond holes in 1990/91, with moderate to good talc intercepts.
talc vein of variable width trending EW over 275m length. Tested in 8 airtrack holes in 1990/91, for maximum width of 2m, dip 75S, western limit identified, eastern end open.
located 300m S of #4 deposit, brecciated talc, width not determined, section of strike exposed in creek bed.
located 1.3km SSE of #24 deposit, talc exposed in 4 rabbit burrows over strike length of 17m.
2.5m wide, highly cleaved talc vein traced along strike for 4km in host dolomite, talcose dolomite, minor coarse, crystalline dolomite.

veins of massive talc in host talcose clay and dolomite rock over a width of 20m. Drilling identified talc vein structure to 10m wide over a 50m length. 6 costeans exposed a zone of intense brecciation, alteration, and weathering.
2.3m wide talc vein trending 258, dip 80S, in host dolomite rock exposed in a costean. Drill tested in 2 airtrack holes for good intercepts of talc.
talc vein 1.5m wide, trending 104, dip 75S. talc float traced intermittently for 80m E. Tested in 4 airtrack holes, with only 1 hole intercepting a narrow vein.
talc vein 3.1m maximum width, trending 274, traced intermittently for 80m. Tested in 1 airtrack hole, with no talc intercepted.
talc vein, coarse crystalline in the hanging wall, vein 1.8m wide, trending 099, dip 65S, traced intermittently for 25m. Tested in 5 air track holes, with only 1 hole intercepting vein talc.

talc vein, exposed in dozer scrape, 1.3m maximum width, dip 80S, trending 285, traced intermittently for 15m. Eastern extremity truncated by coarse, crystalline dolomite. Tested in 2 air track holes, with good intercept of 2m in 1 hole.
talc veins cropping out intermittently over an EW trend for 180m, dip 75S. The veins infill a shear in host dolomite of the Balcanoona Formation. Indicated resource 3700 tonnes.
talc vein 1.6m wide, dip 80S, trending EW over a distance of 17m. Tested in 2 air track holes, which identified a 2m wide vein-talc.

talc vein, dip steep S, traced W along 287 trend for distance of 140m. Western extremity consists of coarse, crystalline dolomite. Tested in 6 air track holes, which identified a 1-1.5m wide vein over 100m.

talc veins exposed at creek junction, and on adjacent hillsides and gullies.Veins trend from 252-287, dip 60-89S. They appear to be separate veins. Tested in 14 air track holes, which identified a lack of strike continuity of individual lodes.
Highly cleaved talc vein 1.8m wide, possibly E extension of prospect K.
Highly cleaved, slightly chloritic talc vein ~1.8m wide, traced along a WSW trend for 40m. Tested in 3 air track holes, which failed to identify a definite talc vein.
talc vein ~1.0m wide, traced along an EW trend for 20m, western end truncated by a fault. Tested in 1 air track holes, which identified vein-talc 2m wide.

2 creeks coalesce several metres N of the main track to #8 deposit. Talc is exposed in both, and on the S side of the track. Tested in 2 air track holes, which identified only minor talc. Much of the exposed talc may be colluvial/eluvial/alluvial.

talc vein 1.8m wide, trend 288, traced intermittently for distance of 40m. Several parallel, smaller veins adjacent. Tested in 6 air track holes, which identified heavily iron oxide stained talc of poor quality.
talc float traced 15m west to where it crops out in a gully.
Isolated outcrop of Talc vein 0.8m, with strike extensions covered by alluvium. Several narrow talc veins crop out 60m to the S.
minor talc lode identified during company mapping, no other details available.
talc vein 0.8-1.4m wide, trending EW over a distance of 60m. Tested in 4 air track holes, which failed to identify the vein at depth.
talc vein 1.7m wide trend EW for a distance of 45m, plunge steep N. tested in 4 air track holes, which identified talc vein to 1m thick, dip 80N.

located 200m SW of Mount Fitton camp. Talc vein traced intermittently for a distance of 30m. Tested in 2 air track holes, which failed to identified talc vein. Geological Survey sample from late 1970s reported presence of scheelite.
several talc veins cropping out over an area 40m x 80m. The veins trend SW, and are up to 4.4m wide. Tested in 4 air track holes, of which 2 had moderate to good talc intercepts.
talc vein 0.9m wide trending 335, dip steep SSW, traced intermittently for a distance of 240m along strike of a shear structure, at variance with the dominant EW structures in the area.
2 talc veins exposed in a shallow open cut. Vein 1 2.2m wide, trend 259, dip 80N, vein 2 1.8m wide, trend 287, dip 87NE. A 6.3m wide vein exposed in a dozer scrape 25m to SW.
talc, lode developed in host Balcanoona Formation.
no details, talc lode identified by company exploration.
talc vein trending EW, traced intermittently for a distance of 100m.

talc cropping out on S side of SW-trending ridge adjacent to coarse crystalline dolomite. Main vein ~2.8m wide. Traced intermittently for 75m. tested in 7 air trak holes that identified a vein trending 070, dip 80N, maximum width 2.5m.
talc vein 1.4m wide, traced intermittently for a distance of 25m.
small open cut on EW talc vein. Tested in 11 vertical air track holes in 1986, with only minor intersepts of talc. Recommended re-evaluation by further drilling.
talc exposed in rabbit burrows over an area 60m x 150m. Tested in 6 air track holes in 1991, which failed to intercept a significant talc vein.
talc lode tested in 13 air core holes in 1986. Some good intercepts of talc identified.
talc lode tested on 2 air track drill traverses identified intercepts of grey talc.
resource estimate 36Mt @ 44.35Mgo. magnesite beds over 6.4km strike length, 12 magnesite beds with combined average thickness of 30.3m, ranging from 0.6m to 4m.
outcrop of massive manganiferous rock adjacent to a manganiferous chert outcrop 20km west of Kimba township. A rock chip sample returned a value of 37.2%Mn.

calcrete Cu-Au geochemical anomaly, 1500m long, NE-trend. Shallow aircore holes identified Cu-Au-(Co) mineralisation in weathered bedrock persisting for at least 900m, best assay 8m @ 2.35%Cu, 0.77g/t Au. Also 5m @ .32%Co.
calcrete Cu-Au geochemical anomaly drill tested in shallow aircore holes, with weak Cu-Au mineralisation in weathered Mesoproterozoic basement in NW-trending zone, best assay 0.27%Cu, 3m 1.18g/tAu.
deposit of Tertiary limestone from 3-10m deep partially exposed and under cover of a thin veneer of soil. Resources for 10 hectare tenement ~300,000t.
old Transport SA borrow pit with tenure re-granted in 2010 on outcropping dolomite of the Neoproterozoic Woocalla Dolomite. Resource ~2.5Mt to depth of 12m. Total production ~100,000 tonne.
Tertiary limestone worked in a shallow quarry as a source of limestone for industrial use. No production figures apparent.

minor pits on a low ENE-trending ridge ~400m long x 40m wide. Residual deposit of limonite prospected in shallow pits overlying ferruginous clay, no production figures apparent. Resources estimated at 142,000t in 1922.
coastal dune sand for recorded production from 1976-92 of an estimated 9100 tonne of sand for enduse as concrete sand, minor garden sand.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 6263; GAMBIER EARTH MOVERS; PORT MACDONNELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: quarry of >3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene lime sand of the Bridgewater Formation, estimated production in 2011 of 4,000 tonne.

2 adjacent, abandoned pits of total area >20,000m2 x 1-4m deep on a mantle of Pleistocene sand and clay overlying calcrete on Mesoproterozoic Oorlano Metasomatite, and worked for calcrete road fill by the then Highways Department in 1972..
4 separate leases taken out over an area ~7km EW by 1km NS on deposits of marble (deposits A to D) all in host Neoproterozoic Balcanoona Formation. No recorded production.
WC14 penetrated U-bearing clay of the Namba Formation. Analysis of 66-67.5m @ 520 pm, with gamma log indicating 50 ppm eU3O8, with the discrepancy indicating strong disequilibrium
drilling has identified a broad zone of low-grade HM-bearing sand over a strike length of ~12km, and from 1.3-2.4km wide, and from 4.5-9m thick. Inferred resource ~285Mt @ 1.9% HM.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEAUFORT EAST; BEAUFORT WEST; CLINTON PROJECT; MEL 3896; MEL 5186
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small, elongate body of lignite of the Tertiary Clinton Coal Measures over an area 7 x 4km. Number of relatively thin seams (2-5m) of high ash and moisture content. JORC resource ~249Mt of calorific value 10MJ/kg, 10.1% ash, 1.3%S.

1 main seam of low rank coal, with high moisture, sodium and sulphur contents, maximum  9m thick beneath 42m cover in host sediment of the Clinton Coal Measures. Total resource 2008 at 124Mt with calorific value 9.4, 10.55 ash, 2.2%S.

weak magnetic anomaly drilled to identify weak chalcopyrite associated with amphibole-magnetite-pyrite alteration system related to mafic intrusion in metasediment. Located marginal to the Pine Point Fault Zone. Best value 9m at 1.03%Cu
surface rock chip sampling identified anomalous Uranium up to 1200ppm U3O8. Follow up drilling returned anomalous values for U. Typical intercept was RC09BEC008 from 40-88m, 48m @ 340ppm U3O8
coal is banded, dirty with partings, generally 1 seam, dip ESE, thickness 2-8m, average 5.5m, cover thickness <55m, shallowing from S to N, . Resource drilling in 2009 identified resource ~60 Mt.

malachite and chalcopyrite in calcite lenses in sheared gabbro dyke intruding metasediment of Birksgate Complex. Drilled by Musgrave Minerals in 2011 to identify open ended mineralisation for >900m along strike, best value 16m @ 0.14%Cu.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AREA C; F. AYLIFFE; J. AYLIFFE; ML 225; ML 411; ML 413; ML 414; ML 415; ML 436; ML 437; ML 438; MOUNT GULLET; MS 1351; RED CLIFF; S.H. AYLIFFE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: low-lying samphire swamp ~2500 acres ( 1,000 hectares) suitable for development of ponding for crystallising salt from sea water accessed from Spencer Gulf. Estimated potential for 250,000tpa.

consortium looked at sourcing brine from the Beda Arm, and southernmost Lake Torrens. Preliminary investigations indicated a positive economic result for production of 0.5-1Mt brine per annum could be achieved consistently.
worlds largest producer of beta carotene, a safe source of pro-vitamin A from 400Ha of hypersaline ponding used to grow the salt tolerant alga.
area of >7Ha x 1-2m deep of council pits developed on weathered quartzite of the Simmens Quartzite Member for road making material.

magnetite skarn in host metasediment of the Hutchison Group. Resource estimate 7.86Mt @ 26.54%Fe for a 250m strike length of a potential 2.4km strike length. Significant Sn-W assays returned from several holes.
magnetite skarn in host metasediment of the Hutchison Group. Inferred + indicated resource 17.19Mt @ 25.19%Fe.
36 mud RC dill holes in 2010 confirmed mineralisation in 3 holes in the vicinity of the original discovery. Hole CBM008 penetrated 0.95m from 25.95-26.85m @ 0.032%eU3O8 in Tertiary fluviatile sand.
small, roadside council pit of ~7,000m2 x 1-3m deep on isolated outcrop of Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
council scrape of <6Ha x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council scrape of <20,000m2 x 1m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
council pit of <30,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
limestone and dolomite deposit in an old lake bed. First worked in 1929 from several pits in the area of which this might have been one.
small roadside council scrape of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
small roadside council scrape of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
small roadside council scrape of >5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
shallow council scrape of >5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered Arthurton Granite, and worked for road fill. In 1983 BHP Minerals identified elevated copper values in saprolite.
lease on Pleisrocene sheet calcrete for road base material. Production from pits of ~>6,000m2 x 1-2m deep from 2009-10 was estimated at 14,000 tonne.
low ridge of quartzite of the Warrow Quartzite, and overlying Recent sand spread, estimated production 2010-13 of 12,000 tonne, mainly quartzite, minor sand.

diamond drilling identified weak copper mineralisation in host argillaceous and chloritic metasediment, best value 2.3m @ 1.11%Cu, and wide zones of low grade mineralisation. Later drilling detected low-level gold anomalism, best assay 1.3g/tAu.

DDH25 penetrated lode at 170.6m as a narrow 30cm interval of chalcopyrite at 13%Cu. This was ~122m vertically beneath the depth of the old shaft. Other diamond holes drilled in the vicinity returned core with weak mineralisation only.
drilling of 7 holes in the vicinity of PMX 11. Highest readings in the interval 26-43m in holes PMX 11 and 13. Maximum value was 30ppm U3O8, 0.09%V2O5, traces Mo.
drilling of 7 holes in the vicinity of PMX 7. Highest readings to 60ppm equivalent in holes PMX 7a in host Tertiary Olney Formation. There was trace anomolous Mo.

diatomite-bearing clayon sand and grey to green clay deposited in the Holocene during periods of high rainfall and marine transgression. Drilling identified diatomite 0.7-2m thick, considered too low grade to be of economic interest.

embayment stretching from Lake Alexandrina then 15km E to Cooke Plains. Drill tested to identify 7 disconnected zones. Diatom content ~10-15%, maximum 30%, considered to be uneconomic due to the low and variable diatom content.

area of low alkali argillaceous rock in host Carrickalinga Head Formation.  Drilling for specification of Na2O + K2O generally <1.1%, and Al2O3/Fe2O3 from 0.5-1.2 identified an area of best grade above 320m contour level.
abandoned council pit of >5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, and worked for road fill.
series of adjacent council costeans for total area <10,000m2 to 1-3m deep on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council pit of >20,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, and worked for road fill. Now utilised as council storage yard.
2 abandoned, part rehabilitated pits 120m apart NS for total area ~1,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, and worked for road fill.
council pit of 1Ha x 1-2m deep, located east of the Kongorong Hundred Line road, and developed on Tertiary Gambier Limestone for road fill.
long abandoned, part rehabilitated council pit of ~30,000m2 x 1-2m deep on coastal limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: LLOYDS PIT; MC 4193; ML 6395; WHITE DAM GOLD PROJECT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 sub-horizontal to gently dipping, tabular zones of mineralisation, with the lower zone thicker and of better grade. Resources estimated at 2.449Mt @ 1.04g/t for 82,100oz contained gold.
gold prospect first identified by MIM Exploration in the late 1990s. Follow up drilling by Exco Resources confirmed low to moderate gold assays in the order of 2m at 0.1 to 0.2 g/tAu from 4 holes.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BALD HILL; MOYA MISSION; NORTH MURRAY BASIN; SINCLAIR FLAT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: intervals of lignite to lignitic clay at depths ranging from 155m to 257m in 4 holes over an E-W trending areal extent of ~150 km2.

rock chip sampling identified zone of anomalous Ba-As-V in host limonite incorporating abundant organic material, now leached and ferruginised. Auger drilling identified Cambrian Wanna Beds, also with anomalous Ba-V-As.

drilling identified oil shale in the Madura Formation, with best yield of 5-15l/t for 3m from 119m. Follow up drilling confirmed the occurrence average yield for the interval 84-94m of 56l/t. Concluded little potential for large, laterally extensive deposit.

several widely spaced zones of lignite, probably distributory channel zones in fluviatile-deltaic palaeodrainage. Estimated resource 1500Mt (1980), but at 45% ash cut off resource probably considerably less.

Tertiary coal deposit in host Pidinga Formation, and located at the southern end of the Tallacootra Palaeochannel. Resources were estimated at 800mt by SADME in 1976, though Grasso (1980) estimated 150Mt.

lignite deposit within Tertiary Pidinga Formation of the Tallaringa Palaeochannel, lignitic intervals to 25m thick at depths from 20-60m. The lignite seams are thin, discontinuous, and scattered through a thick, carbonaceous clay and sand zone.
Tertiary lignite of the Pidinga Formation in the Garford Palaeochannel identified in holes TPS 13 & 14. The coal was high in moisture, and substantially higher in ash than Chundie Swamps deposit.
lignite prospect, located within a broad, NE-trending topographic depression containing present day playa lakes. At Lake Anthony auger drilling identified up to 9m thickness of lignite.
lignite occurrence, located within a broad, NE-trending topographic depression containing present day playa lakes. At Lake Bring auger drilling identified up to 1m thickness of lignite.

regional geochemical sampling, infill lag and rock chip sampling identified gold anomaly of maximum 1.45g/tAu in Archean basement. 12 holes identified best assay of 1m @ 0.72g/t, and 3m @ 0.3g/t in weathered, Archean ironstone.
wide spaced grid aircore drilling, presumably on gold-in-calcrete anomaly over an area ~3km NE by 600m wide. Best value 8600ppbAu in hole 96BBAR020 from 34-35m. The majority of gold values were low.

massive hematite rock interpreted as weathered calc-silicate within the Warrow Quartzite. Unit was traced for ~100m along strike, is open to the north. Composite rock sample assayed 51%Fe, 240ppmSn, 2ppmAg, 0.21g/tAu.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by shallow drilling identified narrow zones of weak anomalous gold in bedrock of coarse grained, intensely chlorite-sericite altered, Hiltaba Suite granite. Best value was 10m @ 0.15g/tAu.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by grid aircore drilling identified SSE-trending zone of anomalous gold over ~700m, and open-ended in weathered Kenella Gneiss. Best value to 3ppm in hole NH32 from 42-44m.

single traverse of 4 aircore holes drilled in 1995 by Hiltaba Gold. Traverse identified anomalous gold, with best assay to 790ppbAu from 22-24m, and 1.07%Zn from 0-2m in hole WLTRC004 in weathered quartzite of the Tarcoola Formation.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by grid aircore drilling in 147 holes for 3777m. Peak value identified was 360ppb in hole 97HN003 from 20-25m. Basement rock was Hiltaba Suite granite, Gawler Range Volcanics, and a fine grained mafic rock.
gossan in host Saddleworth Formation and located on Section 6539, Hundred Talunga. Sampled by Aztec Mining Co. Ltd in 1988 to return best value 1.22g/tAu from sample 184080.
outcrop of metasediment of the Backstairs Passage Formation, with visible copper mineralisation returned best assay of 3.67ppmAu.

surface samples identified Cu-Au-(Co-As) mineralisation in quartz-filled shears in host shale of Yudnamutana Subgroup in nose of a regional anticline. Follow up drilling concluded the 8ppmAu values related to supergene enrichment.

occurrence of elevated Au-(Cu-Zn-Pb-As-Ag) cuttings of Kanmantoo Group siltstone from 42m from water bore NO 95062. In 1999 4 RC holes drilled in an EW traverse near the water bore for no anomalous geochemistry reported.

drilling identified lens of residual white clay with low plasticity. Testwork indicated clay of low plasticity, requiring blending for use in heavy clay industry. Resources ~143,350 tonne, coloured clay ~441,530 tonne.
surface rock chip sample of quartzite of the Wilpena Group sampled during reconnaissance survey by SADME in 1991 returned a value of 6.9ppm Au.

quartz vein in host pale brown metasediment of the Auburn Dolomite Member. Tested in vertical holes PDH1-7(no documents found), with hole PDH2 returning significant gold values. Resampling confirmed elevated, but less significant gold.

5 RC holes on gold/base metals prospect, with hole ELLARC002 returning best assay of 1.05% Zn from 40-42m, with anomalous Zn values recorded from 18-42m in host metasediment of the Tarcoola Formation.

exploration drillhole MER1 in 1996 identified anomalous Fe-Pb-Zn, in 2 zones from 34-42m, and 80-86m. No geological details given, hole drilled on Hiltaba Granite. Best assay 1.37%Zn, 0.4%Pb from 40-42m.

weak aeromagnetic anomaly it was drill tested in hole PPR 3. The hole identified significant sphalerite and galena mineralisation in dolomite laminae of the Tapley Hill Formation. Best assay from 140-144m @ 3195ppmPb, and 1945ppmZn.
drilling identified stratabound, weak Cu-Pb-Zn mineralisation at or near contact Tapley Hill Formation/Woocalla Dolomite with underlying Pandurra Formation over ~6km.
magnetite-destructive zone within Roopena Volcanics. Drilling identified low level Cu-Ag-(Pb-Zn) mineralisation in host volcaniclastic, coarse grained sandstone of Moonabie Formation.

Zn-(Pb-Cu-Ag) lode with quartz-calcite gangue, true thickness 2-3m, trending 280, dip 80S in host calcareous facies of the upper Sturt Tillite-lower Tapley Hill Formation, and near the contact. Resource ~260 tonne contained zinc metal.

deep hole on gravity target identified low-level Pb-Zn mineralisation of 5m @ 0.55Zn, and 0.2%Pb in quartz-carbonate crackle veined Wilyerpa Formation. Follow up identified no major Pb-Zn, poor lateral continuity of the sequence between holes.

MVT-type mineralisation in fracture zones in host Lower Cambrian Wilkawillina Limestone. Area was drilled in 5 holes, WD7-15, with best assay in WD 15 of 1.6% Pb + Zn from 10.3-11.3m, 1% Pb + Zn from 16.3-17.3m.
sample taken from shallow 1m deep pit on lead-zinc quartz vein mineralisation returned 8000ppmZn, 1180ppmPb.
4 holes drilled on the manganese deposit identified a false gossan of no significant depth extent. Karstic features were associated with Cu-Pb-Zn-Mn-Cd anomalies.

limestone deposit of the Lower Cambrian Wilkawillina Formation south of Brachina Gorge 2 locations investigated. Resource 7.6m3 at base Wilkawillina Limestone, grade 54% CaCO3, 40% MgCO3, 2nd 9.9m3 at top Wilkawillina, grade 97% CaCO3.

workings at top of Wilkawillina Limestone on occurrence of coarse, crystalline galena in a 1m wide quartz-calcite vein trending NS. Held as a ML between 1949-74 by C.A. Bairstow. Production of ~150t recorded, no grade determined.

stratiform zinc mineralisation in 2 stratigraphic levels in dolomite of basal Wilkawillina Formation, and central Parachilna Formation. Continuous for ~12km. 4 drill holes confirmed oxidised mineralised zone. Best value 1.05%Zn.

drilling identified altered Ajax Limestone. Chalcophanite was identified from 32-36m, and 72-76m. Limestone intensely altered to dolomite and siderite. Best values Zn, 0.7-4.9%, As, 465-2460ppm, Fe, 6-39%, Mn, 1.4-4.4%, and Pb, 82-550ppm.

widespread low-grade zinc mineralisation. Drilling identified 2m interval of massive sulphide in host equivalent to Broken Hill Group. Best values 2m @ 0.177%Cu, 135ppmCo from 49-51m, 16m @ 3075ppmZn from 116-132m in mafic and felsic gneiss.

diamond hole MCD-3/94 penetrated basement of quartz-feldspar-biotite-muscovite schist, minor gneiss, and sections with staurolite and garnet porphyroblasts. Best value from 93-97m 1635ppmPb, 6184ppmZn.

DD96MN33 penetrated sequence of calc silicate and gneiss with up to 3% layer-parallel sphalerite over short intervals, mostly in calc silicate. Best value 24m from 162m @ 0.16%Zn, and 16.7m from 202m @ 0.22%Zn.

2 diamond holes completed in Willyama basement (top at 420m). Minor Cu-Zn mineralisation identified in pyritic metasediment within Adelaidean Super Group. Best value 1.25m @ 0.88%Pb, 0.415%Zn, from 370.45m in hole 2.
hole ARRC001 identified pyritic albitite, with traces chalcopyrite in pyritic blebs and veins. Analysis gave best value 0.1%Cu from 129-132m in a ""red rock"" altered, pyritic, scapolite albitite.
geochemical target tested in grid aircore holes to identify best value 3m at 1.11g/tAu from 59-62m, and 3m at 10g/tAu 2.2%Cu from 80-83m (EOH).

drilling identified metasiltstone and calc silicate, with finely disseminated to laminated pyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite, rare galena. Best values 252.8-276m, 23.2m @ 0.36%Zn, 0.09%Pb, 2.3g/tAg including 0.25m at 4.55%Zn, 3.6%Pb, and 65g/tAg.

drilling identified metasediment of the Bimba/Ettlewood member at 240m, with 40m at 0.17%Pb, 0.15%Zn including 4m @ 1.41%Pb, and 0.7%Zn. Further drilling confirmed numerous stratabound zones of Zn-Pb-Ag mineralisation.

holes KP 31-34 drilled on Umberatana group quartz-sericite siltstone, with variable disseminated pyrite. Hole KP 31 identified anomalous Zn-Co-Cu in drill hole samples, best values 1000ppmCo from 24-25m, o.2%Zn from 29-30m.

reconnaissance percussion, with follow up diamond drilling in the early 1980s on anomalous bedrock geochemistry. Widespread secondary copper mineralisation was identified, best intervals KD9, 7m @ 5.38%Cu, KD12, 5.6m @ 8.5%Cu.

8-10mgal gravity anomaly drill tested to identify amphibolite of Lady Louise Suite with disseminated pyrite and pyrrhotite. Holes on magnetic anomalies or located on gossanous outcrop gave best value 1m @ 997ppmCu from 11m in host pelite.

surface copper mineralisation drill testing identified a granite gneiss as host to occassional traces of chalcopyrite and copper carbonates. A 12m composite sample of weakly mineralised rock gave 0.1%Cu.
outcrop of quartz-ironstone breccia in host metasediment of the Willyama Complex located ~3km W of Drennans Hut. Rock chip sample assayed 17.7%Cu, elevated As, Fe, Mn.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 3 mineralised horizons, possible exhalites to altered basaltic tuff in metasediment of the Brindana Schist. Mapping determined horizons of anomalous Au-Cu-W, Cu-Zn-As-Co, with best surface sample assay 3.95%Cu, 1.2g/tAu.
gravel sample returned a single microdiamond. Drilling identified indicator minerals and microdiamond most likely due to reworking from Mesozoic palaeochannels, not a local primary source.

aeromagnetic anomaly tested in drill hole RC94TR19, which penetrated quartz-mica siltstone of the Kanmantoo Group. A 5m interval from 40m with abundant quartz veining, magnetite and pyrite assayed 0.1%Co and 0.47%Cu.

aeromagnetic target dril tested to identify weak copper mineralisation as trace diseminated chalcopyrite, also in carbonate-feldspar-quartz altered fracture zones in host felsic norite. Best interval 3m @ 0.4%Cu, 0.1%Ni.

brecciated in places, identified by SADME during geological mapping of the Jamestown 100K map sheet extending for ~9km NS strike. Geochemical sampling identified patchy anomalous Cu-Co, best assay 1100ppmCo, 1500ppmCu.

anomalous Cu-(As) in brecciated, gossanous shale over 500m, best value 1.16%Cu in host diapiric rock associated with Mount Stuart Fault. Drilling identified mineralisation in basal Tapley Hill Formation, Tindelpina Shale. Best value 19m @ 1434ppmCu.

old diggings, with rock chip sample of mullock assaying 22.5%Cu. Follow up soil geochemistry failed to locate significant anomaly. Hole MWRC 12 penetrated slightly pyritic shales of the Tapley Hill Formation, no anomalous geochemistry.
old diggings ~1.8km S of Breaden Hill, tested in hole MWRC 11, which identified vein quartz and dolomite with trace pyrite and chalcopyrite from 52-60m, 8m @ 0.255Cu.

surface gossan with Cu-Pb-Zn-Ag mineralisation. Drilling identified pyrite and chalcopyrite mineralisation in quartz, dolomite veins in silicified, bleached Tapley Hill Formation. Best interval 8m @ 1%Cu, with associated trace Au-Ag.

stratigraphic drilling identified seams of high ash coal, best intersection seam 3.65m thick with 31% ash content, 12% moisture in hole 1A at 78m depth. Follow up drilling failed to identify consistent or widepread coal.

diamond drilling identified 2 sulphidic intervals in host schist with variable fluorite, tourmaline, allanite. Geochemistry returned anomalous Cu-Ni-Co-P-Ce-La-U. Best REE intercept 2.6m @ 1.19%Ce, 2.24%P, and 43ppmU.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Chalcopyrite,  Galena,  Molybdenite,  Rare Earths,  Sphalerite
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Arsenopyrite,  Chlorite,  Clay mineral,  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drilling penetrated feldspar-quartz porphyry and quartzite. 60m interval of sulphides identified, with best value 2m @ 0.27%Cu, 0.175Ni, 0.13%Co from 182.1m. Basal 18m from 274m was enriched in magnetite.
area between South Doora and South East Doora prospects. Tested from west to east in DDHs 46, 23, 68 and 200. Best assays in holes DDH46, 5.5m @ 0.55%Cu, and DDH24, 4.6m @ 0.98%Cu.

tested in 4 holes with best result PBP 34, with anomalous Cu from ~30m to base hole at 109m. Host dark grey microgneiss to hornfels of Oorlano Metasomatite. Zones of feldspar-hematite alteration. best assay was 1.3%Cu from 38-40m.

intervals of patchy vein, disseminated, and fracture fill with chalcopyrite, rare molybdenite, also pyrite and pyrrhotite in intervals of mafic diorite, and carbonate-veined metasediment. Best value 0.95%Cu, mineralisation style described as skarn-like.

located on the NE end of a prominent curvilinear, demagnetised zone, the Alford Shear Zone. Hosted in the Wallaroo group sediments. Tested in hole PBP 36 which penetrated albitised microgneiss of the Oorlano Metasomatite, with max 0.58%Cu from 118-124m.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Atacamite,  Chalcocite,  Chalcopyrite,  Oxidised copper minerals

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: near coincident magnetic and gravity anomaly tested in several diamond holes, with significant intervals of magnetite-bearing iron formation penetrated in PB 12, and minor Cu mineralisation in PB 24. Best assay 0.13%Cu from 263-264m.

abandoned workings, with sample of mullock at 5.6%Cu. Stream and soil geochemical survey, follow up drilling in hole S3 completed at 173.86m in granite overlain by shale, with no significant mineralisation recorded.

prospective contact of Tapley Hill Formation reduced shales with underlying oxidised sandstone of the Pandurra Formation. Drilling identified weak Cu-(Pb-Zn-Ag) in a sandy unit within the THF, best assay 0.55%Cu from 155.3-156m.

drilling identified vertical tension gashes infilled with chalcopyrite in basal finely laminated dolomite of Tapley Hill Formation. Underlying conglomerate carried disseminated chalcopyrite. Best value 0.77%Cu over 0.29m. Weakly anomalous Cu-Ag.

deep hole on linear magnetic anomaly as IOCG-type target. Weak mineralisation penetrated in basal Tapley Hill Formation from 432-433.1m for 0.67%Cu. Unmineralised basement of metasediment and volcanics penetrated at 631.98m.

single diamond hole on surface Au-(Cu) anomalism in Rischbieth Beds. Analysis results disappointing. Best results 0.69%Cu from 10-15m as chalcopyrite in quartz veins in host dolomite. Also 40ppbAu from 466m.

scattered talc mineralisation associated with diapiric dolomite-calcite rock exposed in a rail cutting. Drilling identified broad zone of gritty talc-clay material, no intervals of pure talc were identified.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Kaolinite,  Mica,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: copper minerals in fractures and disseminated in Andamooka Limestone at contact of massive and flaggy dolomitic limestone. Drilling identified 3 zones of goethitic material. Best values 3m @ 9.82%Cu, and 4.3%Pb, anomalous Ag-Co.

drilling identified trace chalcocite in fractures and intergranular filling in host Whyalla sandstone beneath Tregolana Shale, fluorite recorded. Weak Cu mineralisation recorded at top and base of Tapley Hill Formation of 1175ppmCu, and 3350ppm.

Mount Gunson-style, stratiform BM mineralisation on S portion of the ""Pernatty Upwarp."" ~1.7km long ENE by 600m wide. Best value 0.64%Pb, and 0.62%Pb. Thickness 7-10m average 0.2%Pb, 0.3%Zn. Better base metal values carried to 7g/tAg.

Mount Gunson-style, stratiform base metal mineralisation on S portion of the ""Pernatty Upwarp."" Drilling identified ~3.4km long ENE by 600m wide. Thickness averaged 7-10m averaging 0.1%Pb, 0.1%Zn, with values decreasing E

drilling to test local basement high. Holes MGC 38-40 identified enrichment in base metals at top and base of Tapley Hill Formation. Best alues 6753ppmCu at top THF in MGC 38. Also 4865ppmCu in similar position in hole MGC 40.

weak near coincident magnetic and gravity feature drill tested. basement at 290m of granite, pervasively hematite altered, with patchy chlorite-sericite alteration, some local strong fracturing, best value 4m @ 0.25%Cu, 4ppmAg from 416m.

gold-in-soil anomaly drill tested for generally low values for gold identified, with best value from hole 00RUDB023 beginning at 24m, 15m @ 0.35g/tAu, including 3m @ 0.84g/tAu in host sericite altered schist/metasiltstone of the Hutchison Group.

brecciated, gossanous ironstone as infill along a sub-vertical fault, cross-cutting metasediment of the Hutchison Group. Rock chip sampling identifying best assay 1.92g/tAu, anomalous Cu. Drilling returned poor results, best assay 4m @ 0.36ppmAu.
there was slight radioactivity in lignite of the Upper Jurassic Polda Formation, with highest readings in holes LDH 32A and LDH 58. Both holes recorded intervals of >300cps in lignite.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested in RAB hammer holes. Holes completed in Archean quartz-biotite-muscovite-feldspar schist/gneiss. Analysis identified weak anomalous  Au, As, Cu, Zn, Ni. Best assay  6m @ 297ppbAu, 0.27%As.
areas of anomalous Pb, Ag, Cu, and Zn geochemistry drill tested to confirm anomalous Pb, Zn, Cu values. Exploration company considered the region remained prospective.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: A2; MANX A2; UMBRIEL; UMBRIEL EAST; UMBRIEL WEST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: magnetic & gravity anomaly beneath ~130m cover. Basement of paragneiss, hematite/magnetite, basal dolomitic breccia. Weak Cu-Au mineralisation in chlorite alteration zones, with elevated Ba. Best Cu 0.5m @ 1.26%Cu, 0.62m @ 8.4ppmAu.

near coincident magnetic and gravity anomaly tested in 2 diamond holes. Identified highly sheared calc-silicate metasediment exhibiting variable carbonate+/-sericite+/-quartz+/-sulphide alteration and veining. Best value 0.19%Zn, 0.07%Pb, 1.5g/tAg.

magnetic anomaly drill tested to identify kimberlite. Tantalum values of 0.15% for 2m interval in hole MH14-56l. 2006 drilling failed to transect the zone of interest, identifying a leucite-rich body, possibly representing a leucite lamproite.

re-drill of gabbroic intrusive with anomalous nickel (6m @ 0.08%Ni) from previous drilling. Identified pyroxenitic material with low nickel values, maximum 550ppm. Enclosing gneiss with anomalous Pb-Zn in shears, best value 0.16%Pb, and 0.23%Zn.
small roadside pit on weathered Kenella Gneiss worked for material for road maintenance on the Kingoonya - Tarcoola road.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by drilling, mapping, rock chip sampling, and a Helimag survey. Weak gold mineralisation associated with hydrothermal alteration and shearing in host Kenella Gneiss. Best assay was MLK151, 2m @ 1.87g/tAu.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by grid drilling into weathered Sullivan Shale Member. No major gold mineralisation was detected. A number of holes identified anomalous gold values, best assay in hole MT62, 36-41m, 5m @ 528ppb.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly. Follow up RAB drilling identified anomalous silver in Garford Formation sandstone preserved on the flanks of low lying ridges and also within weathered St Peters Suite granite.

zone of brecciated, quartz-muscovite greisen on Anabama Granite. Old working consisted of an adit cut for ~8m SE into a quartz vein, no evidence of mineralisation apparent in spoils. Rotary percussion holes identified pyrite and chalcopyrite at depth.
molybdenum mineralisation to >500ppm in host, silicified Hiltaba Suite granite on the edge of a younger Hiltaba Suite granite intrusion.
rock chip sample from siliceous serpentinite with anomalous Cr geochemistry to 5700ppm, elevated Zn.
located ~3km due west of the Ronalds Well copper occurrence, rock chip geochemistry on green, nickel-bearing rock assayed 800ppmNi, and 1%Cr.
rock chip sample of an olivine picrite returned 0.5%Cr, 1550ppmNi, pt + Pd 34ppb, and MgO 31.1%.

buried southern margin N-dipping Giles Complex layered mafic/ultramafic intrusion with indications extensions to the lateritic nickel-cobalt ochre mineralisation of Claude Hills. Hole CHRC093 70m @ 1.18% Ni and 0.069% Co.

shallow RC hole STD 5537-2/E01A-2 drilled in regolith during exploration for diamondiferous kimberlite. Samples of green clays, presumably a weathered amphibolite returned anomalous Cr assays to 1.3%Cr from 15-18m.

shallow RC hole STD 5437-1/W03-1 drilled during exploration for diamondiferous kimberlite. Samples of weathered ultramafic returned Cr assays to 1%Cr from 24-26m. Petrology identified fresh rock as peridotite, pervasively altered to serpentinite.

drilling during exploration for diamonds identified samples of weathered pyroxenite returned anomalous Cr assays to 0.5%Cr from 54-62mm. Petrology identified fresh rock as altered pyroxenite, with most pyroxene altered to amphibole.

drilling during exploration for diamondsidentified samples of weathered, highly altered ultramafic returned anomalous Cr assays to 0.8%Cr from 76-86mm. Petrology identified fresh rock as highly altered ultramafic rock to serpentinite.
drilling identified ultramafic rocks with elevated Ni and Cr values, Ni sulphide identified as millerite. Abundant magnetite as an alteration product.
drilling identified metamorphosed ultramafic. Best value 4491ppmNi, 338ppmCo, 1.2%Cr. Reassaying by Werrie Gold returned 13m @ 0.26%Ni in DH 52.
drilling on core of Muckanippie Anorthosite Complex. Hole, MW5 identified dark green magnetite-quartz-biotite gabbro. Bottom hole sample returned anomalous Ce to 1500ppm, Nb to 1350ppm, 4.25%P2O5.
best mineralisation in diamond drill hole DD91GE12 which penetrated altered granites with best assay 1100ppm U3O8 over a 6.6m interval including 8500ppm U3O8 from 109.4-110.5m.
surface U mineralisation in host haematitic and granitic breccias tested in 8 holes. Only weak mineralisation recorded.

drilling identified anomalous Cu-Mo in host ferruginous rock, albitite, with disseminated and vein magnetite, coarse pyrite, and quartz vein material. Follow up drilling identified probable footwall albitite, no anomalous geochemistry. Deeper drilling needed.

aero-radiometric anomaly tested in 2 diamond holes. Prospectivity downgraded from drill results, Monazite grades do not improve with depth, secondary U mineralisation as fracture infill in pegmatite host dies out with depth.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Apatite,  Carphosiderite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Mica,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: high U of 1m @ 693ppm from 303-304m.The Uranium developed at the boundary between highly reduced gneiss and oxidised and brecciated hematitic gneiss.
best assays were 3050ppmCe in strongly potassium metasomatised feldspar-magnetite quartzite at 120-121m, 1850ppmCu, and 520ppmU in a granite dyke at 76.5-77m

area of shallow council scrapes of <20,000m2 x ~1m deep, and excavated on scree slopes immediately south of where Saltia Creek emerges from the ranges, presumably for colluvial gravels, and clay for road fill.
shallow pit on sands of outwash plain north of Saltia creek, and on the eastern outskirt of Stirling North opposite the rubbish dump. No production records.
2 long abandoned council scrapes of <20,000m2 x 1m deep, located on the eastern upper slopes of range of rock outcrop immediately NW of Quorn, and working colluvial gravels and clay for road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~8,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, whire to purple metasediment of the Wilpena Group, and worked for road fill.
roadside council pit of ~10,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered, white, kaolinitic metasiltstone of the Wilpena Group, and worked for road fill.
weak Pb-Zn mineralisation at depth in host basal Wilkawillina Limestone in diamond drilling ~10km west of the Flinders Range escarpment.
prominent outcrop of ironstone of Braemar Ironstone Facies, strike length 3.5km thought prospective for low-grade iron ore. Not drill tested (2010).
