old workings near Wyacca Mines. Drill tested in hole PP5 on gossan on Tindelpina Shale-Wilyerpa Formation contact. Hole identified narrow interval of carbonate-sulphide, best value 500ppmCu.

quartz-calcite-hematite-siderite-malachite vein 60-100cm in host siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation. Drill hole PP7 identified carbonate-sulphide veining in 2 pyritic intervals, best value 20-40ppmCu, 105ppmAs.

old workings near Wyacca Mines. Probably Prospect 21 in Env 1341. Workings developed on a quartz vein to 1m wide in host siltstone. Vein decreases to a few cm wide at depth. Dump material ranged from 0.09-3.5%Cu, maximum 6ppmAg.

abandoned, rehabilitated council scrapes, the northern pit of 3 over distance of 1.22km NS for total area of pits >20,000m2 x 1m deep, and developed on weathered metasediment of the Umberatana Group for material for use as road fill.
abandoned, rehabilitated council scrape of ~20,000m2 x 1m deep, and developed on colluvial slope for road fill material.

nodules and stainings of malachite in oolitic dolomite at base of Hawker Group carbonates. Little or no production. Host limonitic zone >2km. Drilling identified weakly elevated Cu, best zinc to 12,000ppm, anomalous lead related to MnO content.

group of old workings between the Black Eagle group of workings, and to the south the Beltana Silver Mine. Host weakly mineralised grey, fractured dolomite. Tested in several drill holes, which were abandoned due to caving.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese-bearing mineral, undifferentiated

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Pb-Zn show with old mine located in the Ediacara Range. No other details.
reconnaissance mapping by North Flinders Mines Ltd in the early 1970s reported gold diggings on the flats west of Patawarta Gap.
largest Cu mine in the Arkaroola Creek area, host Balcanoona Formation. Ore distribution is structurally controlled.
old workings on presumed surface uranium mineralisation in hematitic breccia of the Radium Creek Metamorphics, and on a linear fault trend.
surface uranium mineralisation on hematite-rich host Radium Ridge Breccias immediately north of Hematite Valley Prospect.
surface radiometic anomaly in metasediment of the Radium Creek Metamorphics tested in wide spaced drilling, holes PP 1-13.

old workings. 2 hole drilled 200m west in 2006 by Quasar Resources Pty Ltd on surface geochemistry copper anomaly failed to reach target depth. Host lithology unknown, but from 100K digital map is Wooltana Volcanics.
workings developed on surface Uranium mineralisation. Drill tested in holes RN 2 & 8.
old pit on surface mineralisation in Radium Ridge Breccias on ridgetop west of Bills Folly. Second, smaller pit 250m to west.
no details, small digging ~400m south of O'Donahue Castle Mine. Tested in hole NFOD 1 sited on surface zinc anomaly for disappointing results.
surface occurrence of brannerite tested in 3 holes HD 1-3, which failed to identify significant U mineralisation in host mica schist and gneiss of the Nooldoonooldoona Trondhjemite.

small area of scheelite mineralisation.Host was a recrystallised, metasomatised, biotite-plagioclase-tourmaline microdiorite. Chemical analysis returned anomalous values for W, Cu, Co. Drill testing in several holes identified scheelite in drill cuttings.

3 adjacent areas of  of council pits for total area <30,000m2 x 1-4m deep, located close to Balcanoona Station, and developed on weathered, white, kaolinitic metasediment of the Umberatana Group for road fill material.
surface iron oxide and manganese gossan with chemical analyses identifying anomalous Uranium. Drill testing revealed U anomalism caused by surficial enrichment process.

group of 5 workings over an area ~500m long EW by 100m NS, and located along the nose of an anticline close to the boundary between Pound Subgroup metasediment and limestone of the Hawker Group. Tested in several drillholes.

area of several shallow diggings on copper mineralisation. Regional setting on NW flank of the Moro Anticline. Malachite associated with quartz veining at contact of Pound Quartzite and overlying Ajax Limestone.
located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map, presumed surface copper show in veins in host Wilkawillina Limestone.
2 old shafts excavated on copper mineralisation on the nose of an anticline and close to the contact of Pound Subgroup metasediment and limestone of the Hawker Group. tested in hole BALCANOONA B 2.
historic working located from google earth, no other details, host is metasediment of the Parachilna Formation. Second shaft ~200m to NE.
located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map, presumed copper show in vein in host Freeling Heights Quartzite.
located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map. Tested in holes YP 9-10. Surface copper show in host metasediment of the Wywyana Formation.
no details, located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map.Presumed surface copper mineralisation in host metasediment/breccia of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
no details, located from mine symbols on Serle 1 mile shhet, and 100K topographic map. Presumed surface copper mineralisation in host metasediment/breccia of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
copper show in Ulupa Siltstone located from mine symbol on 100k topographic map, not visible on google earth.
no details, copper show in Bunyeroo Formation, and located from mine symbol on 100k topographic map.
copper mineralisation in host Merinjina Tillite, being the eastern extension of the stratiform mineralisation at Paulls Consolidated located ~800m to the west.
no details, presumed copper show in Curdimurka Subgroup, and located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map.
no details, presumably copper show in host Curdimurka Subgroup, located from mine symbol on 100K topographic map.
area of several council pits in the vicinity of a road junction for total area >10,000m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on Holocene sand spread for source of road fill.
2 shafts developed on surface copper mineralisation, ~450m apart NS, located on the Burr Crush Zone in host Merinjina Tillite.

no records relating to this mine have been found. Located from mine symbols on Serle 1mile sheet, and 100K topographic map. Possible workings on NE end of Burr Crush Zone on presumed copper show in crush zone in host Curdimurka Subgroup metasediment.
NW extension of Nichols Nob Cu-(Ag-Au) vein-hosted mineralisation in Tapley Hill Formation.
small magnetic anomaly of 1100nT drill tested, which identified basalt with 20m @ 900ppmCu from 50m. Cuttings with 1-35 pyrite.
no details, located from mine symbol on 100k topographic map. Presumably workings on veins with copper mineralisation in host breccia of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
no details, located from mine symbol on 100k topographic map. Presumably workings on veins with copper mineralisation in host breccia of the Curdimurka Subgroup.

weak magnetic anomaly on S flank of gravity anomaly. Drilling identified albite-magnetite gneiss/schist, with 0.3m band with 10-15% sulphides of 40% chalcopyrite, 60% pyrite, and thin red-rock alteration halo. Associated anomalous Fe, U, Mo, Mn.

drilling on shell grit deposit in the late 1960s on Sandy Point, Inkerman area. No individual resource figure for the area,  incorporated into general resource for shell grit on coastal areas to south.

drilling identified a section of the Narlaby Palaeochannel over a distance of ~40km trending NW. Best assays were IR 118, 2m @ 45ppmU3O8, IR 123 50ppm U3O8 from a 2m sample at the base of the channel.

gold-in-calcrete anomalies in the Eaglehawk area identified during exploration for ""Challenger"" type gold mineralisation in Archean metasediment of the Mulgathing Complex. Tested by RAB drilling for best intercept of 4m @ 0.12g/tAu.

grid drilling RAB holes on gold-in-calcrete anomaly identified a polymetallic suite of anomalous geochemistry at top weathered Mulgathing Complex granitoid. Values of Au 88ppb, Cu 220ppm, Zn 270ppm, Ni 1000ppm, As 266ppm.
coherent gold-in-calcrete anomaly to 35ppb tested in shallow RAB drill holes for best result of 8m at 0.22g/tAu and elevated Ni to 1750ppm.
small quantities of precious opal recovered from Early Cretaceous Marree Formation. Much of the opal was of a poor quality.
small quantities of precious opal recovered from Early Cretaceous Marree Formation. Much of the opal was of a poor quality.
NS-trending pod of massive hematite penetrated in drill holes. Formed by supergene enrichment of banded iron formation of the Lower Middleback Iron Formation.

large gossaneous zone ~3.4km NE of the Paratoo mine. Formed by weathering of weaky pyritic diapiric dolomite. The pyrite is slightly cupriferous. Drill tested in line of shallow holes for poor results.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLACK ROCK ROAD; ML 5000; ML 5291; ML 7234; SA RAILWAYS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: open cut 4km NE of Black Rock. Developed on metasediment of the Burra Group for use as railroad ballast, also road seal aggregate and road base material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; ORROROO ROAD; WALLOWAY CC#1
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: abandoned council, 2 bench quarry of <7,000m2, and developed on dolomite to dolomitic siltstone, with the quarry straddling the Brighton Limestone/Tapley’s Hill Formation boundary. Production was ~41,000 tonne.

weak surface copper mineralisation in metasediment of the River Wakefield Group. Follow up semi-regular grid drilling over an area of several square km identified persistent sulphide mineralisation, dominantly pyrite, no significant Cu geochemistry.

surface gossan strike length of >8km. Samples maximum of 6g/tAg. Drill testing at points along a 6km distance, with holes penetrating a manganese-iron oxide interval, with samples returning no anomalous values for Ag geochemistry.

drill hole EX 36 identified interval of pyrite, with high copper reported. Nearby hole EX 96 reported 2000ppmCu from basal Woocalla Dolomite. Follow up drilling identified Cu to 1500ppm in the basal Woocalla Dolomite.

drilling identified sulphide mineralisation in Woocalla Dolomite. Laminated shale underlain by 1-2m massive pyritic dolomite, with anomalous Cu in dolomite, and underlying sandstone. Anomalous Pb and Zn values were reported up hole in black shale.

weak copper geochemistry anomaly SE extremity of a magnetic high, best value 2.4%Cu, 250ppmMo, and 2.85ppmAu. RAB drilling identified weak copper mineralisation, best value 1500ppmCu in fine grained siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation.

initial drilling of magnetic target identified kimberlite. Close spaced drilling delineated a main body and a northern, satellite body. The kimberlite was characterised by abundant spinel, moderate to high chrome diopside, low garnet, trace ilmenite.
drilling identified mineralisation at or near the contact of an intrusive granite with ferruginous schist of the Hutchison Group. Best assay 350ppm U in hole KA 4.
adjoined the Lady Franklin ~400m to the south, reported 6 shafts sunk on a well developed quartz lode in host metasediment of the Hutchison Group.

3 prospecting pits on surface copper mineralisation. Hole RPAC 82 identified 1m of weak malachite mineralisation, with drill sample assaying 7.8%Cu. Further drilling to penetrate the lode at depth and along strike failed to identify mineralisation.

drill hole penetrated 5m of lignite, with base coal seam ~200m deep. 2nd hole ~5km SE penetrated 0.56m of lignite at ~137m. no follow up drilling. The exploration company concluded little prospect for discovery of an economic resource.
council pit of ~12,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, kaolinitic metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.

historic prospecting pits with visible galena in highly siliceous sheared rock. Resampling identified anomalous Cu, Pb, Ag. Extensive float of ironstone, presumed to be related to faults. A line of drill holes across the area penetrated mainly granite.

testwork on clay. Contained >60% kaolinite, from 15-30% quartz, trace ilite. Reported to be moderately crystalline. Particle size analysis and brightness determination of reasonable % <2 micron clay, brightness below that required for paper coating.

diamond drilling identified 20-30m thick tourmaline-silica-chlorite-siderite-dolomite breccia in lithic quartzite of Moonabie Formation. Best values 1-3%Cu. Chalcopyrite associated with carbonate alteration, 2 intervals semi-massive sulphide.
abandoned pit on vegetated sand dune, presumably mined for sand for local use.

drilling identified calc-silicate and schist with pyrite, anomalous Cu to 620ppm, Pb to 470ppm, Zn to 320ppm, 1 sample at 0.2ppm Au. Follow up drilling identified elevated base metals E of discovery hole, and profile 55, anomalous Cu, Pb, Zn values.

linear magnetic trend drill tested for ~5km. Best assay on profile 46 in host non-magnetic amphibolite BIF, peak values 1400ppmPb, 360ppmZn. W end near holes 105-106 elevated Cu-Pb-Zn values in tourmaline, graphite, pyritic quartzite.

magnetic trend drill tested for best value 6m @ 1070ppmCu. 8 central holes on peak of magnetic anomaly recorded anomalous base metals, best values 500ppmCu, 390ppmPb, and 1500ppmZn in RAM 130, and 2200ppmZn in RAM 268.

drilling identified basement schist to quartzite (Warrow Quartzite), metasediment, graphitic schist, with weak Cu-Pb-Zn mineralisation. Also graphitic schist to 8m @ 7.5%C. Testwork identified very small flake size, presence of pyrite.

weak gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested to identify quartz-feldspar-biotite gneiss, with minor skarn lithology of the Hutchison Group, with weak sericite-chlorite alteration, tr pyrite. Best Au 0.34g/t in hole 9 from 45-48m.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly tested by RAB drilling. 2 northern traverses identified contact of marble skarn with brecciated gneiss. Southern traverse identified deep weathering of biotite schist, with significant quartz veining. Best assay in hole 4, 0.46g/tAu from 12-15m.

drilling of magnetic anomaly on Kanmantoo Group metasediment. Hole PH 18 penetrated schist with pyrite and pyrrhotite from 88-104m, with anomalous Cu-Zn values to 430ppmCu, 320ppmZn. Follow up drilling failed to identify any anomalous Cu-Zn.
drilled in 16 holes in eastern part of the Polda Basin identified Eocene lignite in 8 holes. Resources ~220Mt of which 140Mt was below 200m. Quality comparable to other SA Tertiary lignites.
redox interface in sediments in holes RHC 8, 10, 11, 12 and 13, with anomalous Uranium identified in hole 8 (28ppmU). Drilling failed to identify any persistent U mineralisation.
outcropping Hutchison Group metasediment with anomalous Pb-Zn-Mn. 2 lines RAB drilling confirmed anomalous geochemistry, best values in hole 40, 320ppmCu, 300ppmZn, 9.455Mn.
TEM anomaly tested in a single drill hole, which identified graphite schist with anomalous Zn to 1410ppm, 7ppmAg, 620ppmPb, and 430ppmCu.

aircore drilling on magnetic anomaly identified weakly elevated Cu-Pt-Pd in host gabbro, maximum Cu 1350ppm, Pt + Pd to 242ppb. Follow up diamond drilling identified gabbro/diorite cut by multiple granite dykes to 16m thick. No significant assays. were returned.
gold geochemical anomaly tested in RAB drill holes for low-level gold anomalism, elevated Ni to 7100ppm, at base weathering profile on host granites, gabbros.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly at S extremity of the Yarlbrinda Shear Zone. RAB drilling identified sequence of mafic rock merging west into sheared granite on the YSZ, with anastamosing networks of fine grained pyritic alteration. Best assay 13ppbAu.
surface show of copper mineralisation on Rhynie Sandstone prospected in shallow trench, no recorded production.
shallow working on surface copper show on River Broughton Beds.

area of cupriferous greenstone, brecciated, carrying malachite, residual chalcopyrite, pyrite and limonite boxworks in quartz stringers. Mapping identified a large mafic intrusion. Detailed sampling revealed an erratic distribution of copper.

magnetic anomaly drilled to identify metasiltone, metasandstone with fine disseminated hematite after magnetite interpreted as of the Upper Albite Formation. Low base and precious metal values, best values 12m @ 0.12%Cu.

magnetic anomaly drilled to identify metasiltone, metasandstone of the Upper Albite Formation. Low base and precious metal values. Best values 30m  @ 176ppmMo, 6m @ 310ppmMo in host gossanous psammopelite, and 6m @ 0.15%Cu.

magnetic anomaly drilled to identify metasiltone, metasandstone with fine disseminated hematite after magnetite interpreted as of the Upper Albite Formation. Minor anomalous Cu-Ag values. Best value 3m @ 0.08%Cu.

intersection of Benagerie Fault and Oaklands-Frome structural corridor. Shallow drilling identified anomalous Cu-Zn-(Ag-Mo-Pb) intervals in both deeply weathered, and partly weathered basement of metasediment and volcaniclastics. No anomalous Au.

drilling identified a basin shaped area 7km+ long NS by 3.5km EW in the area of Owen township. Maximum thickness of Tertiary sand to 28m in holes 48 and 49. Bulk sampling determined suitability for amber-grade glass sand.

drilling identified NW-trending buried valley of Tertiary sand, 15km long by 1km in the northern section, widening to the south to >4km. Maximum thickness to 17m on the eastern side. Bulk sampling determined suitability for amber-grade glass sand.

Uranium mineralisation in basal sands of the Lake Namba palaeochannel identified in 3 drill traverses over a distance of >4km. Best assay 0.4m @ 0.112%eU3O8 at 70.4m in hole LN 11. The lease forms part of Heavy Rare Earths Ltd. Lake Namba-Billeroo project (2025).
weak U mineralisation associated with middle and basal Tertiary palaeochannel sands, though much of the basal sand appears to have been eroded away.

drilling identified a resource of clean, white kaolin developed via deep weathering of Kiana Granite. Resource of ~15Mt. Limited testwork on samples of kaolin indicated positive potential as an economic resource.
2X narrow 10m wide x 50m long NS quarries ~250m apart on magnesite beds in host Skillogalee Dolomite.
coarse sand mined from creek bed in section 17 by G.L.M. Combe.
section 86, P.W. and P.J. Gale, pit developed on deposit of Tertiary gravel and fine to coarse sand.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: P.W. AND P.J. GALE; RIVER BLOCK ROAD; YACKA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: section 86, P.W. and P.J. Gale, pit developed on deposit of Tertiary gravel and fine to coarse sand.

abandoned council pit of ~8,000m2 x 1-4m deep on northern alluvial banks of the River Broughton on the outskirts east of Yacka. The pit worked a deposit of fine to coarse Holocene creek sand and gravel.
pit developed on Holocene sand and gravel in Yackamoorundie Creek on EML 3093, granted 1958, abandoned in 1967.
pit developed on Holocene sand and gravel on Broughton River. Estimated production 11,000 tonne from 1973-89.

stratabound mineralisation in host black shale of the Elatina Formation. Possibly  associated with increased fracturing associated with small drag folds. Mineralisation extends for several km along strike.

aircore drilling identified 500m long gold-in-saprolite to 0.6ppmAu max, with anomalous Pb-Zn-As-Mo-Ag-Cu beneath average 50m cover. 3 diamond holes identified no mineralisation in fresh basement metasediment.
magnetic anomaly drill tested in hole SH11 DH37 which identified a magnetite skarn with trace chalcopyrite mineralisation.
magnetic anomaly drill tested in hole MH42 DH28, which identified a dark grey-black basalt at 25m depth, with secondary mineralisation to 0.34%Cu.
magnetic anomaly drill tested in hole MH43 DH26, penetrated weathered quartz-feldspar-mica/hornblende schist, top basement 75m. Geochemical analysis returned bottom hole sample at 89m at 0.28%Zn.
gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested in 5 traverses of aircore holes CR1-56. Best assay was 185ppbAu in a chlorite-sericite-pyrite altered granodiorite.
copper-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested in 3 traverses of shallow holes to basement in CAC36-47. Best values 5.3ppmAg in hole 40 in weathered adamellite, only low level Cu throughout.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly, shallow drill tested to identify best gold to 35ppb, and anomalous Cu at the base of deep weathering profile. The most anomalous area was centred on intense hematite +/- chlorite +/- pyrite alteration in Hiltaba Granite.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly, shallow drill testing identifieded NE-trending fault zone in variably hematite-altered Hiltaba Suite granite, sheared dolerite, and rhyolite (?Nyuts Volcanics?). Best assay was 6m @ 96ppb from 25m in hole CAC68.
Au (0.5g/t), Ag (18g/t), Cu (1.2%), Zn (0.51%), and Pb (850ppm) mineralisation in pyrite-garnet-biotite schist of the Tapanappa Formation, with mineralisation associated with shearing and veining.
site investigated for rip-rap for construction of Chowilla Dam. Auger drilling identified calcrete unsuitable for use.
investigations at Chowilla dam site for >4.6 million cubic metres of clean quartz sand for dam shoulder use.
production of brick shale of 290t in 1973 from pit at western end of PM 94. Production from 1973-76 was 13,242t of material from unit of pale, weathered shale in the Undalya Quartzite.

weathered shale resources developed on Woolshed Flat Shale. Drilling identified a 7km2 area of weathered shale suitable for brick manufacture between Gawler and Concordia. Follow up drilling is required to determine resources.
small vein uranium occurrence in host granite is recorded on Bimbowrie Station. Airborne surveys also highlight regions of high uranium concentrations.

hole MD RCP14 with 8m @ 18%Pb as cerussite as residual deposit over a W-dipping stratabound sulphide target. Follow up grid driling identified 2 narrow zones of bedrock mineralisation, for >400m, & open ended. Pb-Zn values maximum of 2%.
Zn-Pb-Cu calcrete anomaly. Aircore & resource drilling identified mineralisation in host volcanics of the GRV with inferred 2011 resource estimate 2.46Mt @ 2.3%Zn, 2.4%Pb, 24g/tAg.

drilling identified a 3km long zone of hematite alteration and enrichment overlying magnetite-BIF. Resource drilling has identified total resource of 103.3Mt, including ~101Mt of magnetite-bearing BIF

2 drill traverses identified anomalous base metals at same stratigraphic level in host Hutchison Group. Located adjacent to magnetic anomaly. Best values 243ppmCu, 417ppmZn on N traverse, and 902ppmCu, 343ppmZn on S traverse.

identified from 5 drill holes, best values DP24 and 30, intervals of radioactive sand ~55m below surface, appearing to be channel sand. Estimate of grade from radiometrics 0.05%U3O8. Best intersection close to the Hambidge National Park.

drill holes identified thicknesses of white kaolin in 2 holes DP 13, and 14 ~5km apart in a NW dirction. Samples submitted for analysis determined high brightness ad low Fe2O3 content. Recommendations were made for further testwork.

intervals of stratabound manganese enrichment in host Nuccaleena Dolomite, with elevated BM-Co-REE, including yttrium, neodymium and cerium. Best values 1m @ 31.7%Mn, 0.11%Co, 1039ppm REE, and K2RC002, 1m @ 33.6%Mn, 0.11%Co, 1667ppm REE.

occurrence identified by Archer Exploration during reconnaissance drilling for manganese mineralisation in the Ketchowla district. Drilling identified rocks with elevated REE, best value to 2537ppmREE.

linear magnetic trend drilled to identify bands of iron oxide and graphitic schist. Weak anomalous base metals and uranium. Thin band massive magnetite, 3m of graphitic schist described as of greater crystal size than other areas.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Graphite,  Magnetite,  Manganese Oxide,  Uranium Minerals (Non Specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: linear magnetic trend drilled to identify anomalous U to 1m @ maximum of 54.1ppmU. Elevated Pb and Zn to >700ppm were encountered. Bedrock lithologies of Hutchison Group.

NNW-trending magnetic anomaly drill testing weakly sulphidic, magnetite-rich (upper gabbro) to magnetite-poor (lower olivine-bearing pyroxenite), mafic to ultramafic sequence. Analyses revealed best gold value of 1.38ppm, no anomalous Ni.
anomalous radioactivity ~4 times background in eastern Polda trough in 3-6m thick sand unit at depths of from 30-60m.
roadside council pit of 0.6Ha x 1-3m deep on deeply weathered, white, kaolinised sandstone/quartzite of the Warrow Quartzite, and worked for road making material.
located at about the same stratigraphic level of the Upper Middleback Jaspilite, and ~900m ENE of the Silver Monarch Mine. Appears to be a single shaft.

weathered, finely bedded buff siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, with some sandy layers, minor bedding-parallel quartz veinlets, W dip strong bedding-parallel cleavage 280 strike, 40 deg, 5 deg flatter than bedding.
no details, located from mine symbol on 50K topographic map. Located ~1km due west of Yadnarie Mine.

council pit on limestone of Bridgewater formation. Later aircore drilling identified anomalous base metal geochemistry associated with weak gravity high associated with a sequence of metasediment and volcanic rock of the Hall Bay Volcanics.
aircore drilling identified multi-element anomaly at junction of 2 Tournefort metadolerite dykes, and adjacent to the margin of the Kiana Granite.
aircore drilling identified anomalous geochemistry associated with a point gravity high in host metasediment and volcanic rock of the Hall Bay Volcanics.
aircore drilling identified anomalous geochemistry associated with a point gravity high in host metasediment and volcanic rock of the Hall Bay Volcanics.
workings for manganese ~700m along strike and NE of the main Bendleby workings.
uranium assay of 2m @ 43ppm U3O8 from 38-40m in single hole, WG 096 in mid grey, reduced palaeochannel sand.
fluorite mineralisation as irregular patches and veins of purple fluorite on E slopes of Mentor Hill. Analysis returned a best value of 2.5%F, with base metal values low.

geochemical sampling programme of core samples identified anomalous Cu-Pb-Zn values consistently in a 6-14m thick band in host dolomite at the top of the Observatory Hill Beds. Mineralisation described as of Mississippi Valley style.

single drill hole completed during petroleum exploration in the Eastern Officer Basin. Geochemical sampling of core identified consistently anomalous base metals, also weak gold anomalism (to 0.13ppm) in possible Observatory Hill Bed equivalents. Mineral association and style was regarded as of Mississippi Valley type.
yellow carnotite on creek bank. Follow up costeaning and drilling of 36 holes identified weak mineralisation, best value from costeans 90ppmU, and 14ppmU in hole MD 63.
visible carnotite in riverbank in white-grey siltstone unit overlain by 10m of shale of the Mesozoic Marree Formation. Sample returned 160ppmU.

wide spaced drilling returning anomalous values from 1 hole of 5x background in hole MD 108 at 14.5m in siltstone of the Marree Formation. This was the hole closest to the outcropping carnotite reported near Tent Hill.

3-4 horizons of Braemar Ironstone intercalated with carbonate-bearing siltstone. It has a strong linear, aeromagnetic signature trend NW, for >30km for that part of the aeromagnetic anomaly within the Bimbowrie conservation park.
prominent tooth-like 5m tall rock outcrop of barite in a creek bed.
abandoned roadside council pit of >30,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
strand Tertiary HM sand deposit identified by drilling. Resource estimate indicated + inferred 27.5Mt at 7.4% HM for 2.04Mtonne HMS, being ilmenite dominant (>60%), with ~17% Zr, and 2% Rt
single drill hole YE 1858, with significant intervals of >1% HMS. Initial infill drill testing indicates the HMS intervals have no significant lateral extent.

HMS deposit located ~9km NE of the Jacinth-Ambrosia mining centre. Drilling has identified a 2013 resource of 110Mtonne ore at 9% HM. Revised 31st December 2016 Indicated + Inferred at 72.6 Mtonne at 12% HMS. Dominantly Ilm >60%, 13-18% Zr.

~2m wide zone of shearing in host albitised and silicified volcanic rock of the Abminga Subsuite in the Perryhumuck Formation. Ore minerals include chrysocolla, malachite, azurite, with considerable gossanous goethite associated.
small pit on westernmost pit of the scheelite ""line-of-lode."" Stratabound mineralisation in host albitised schist. Several tonnes excavated.

single drill hole intercept of anomalous Zn to 0.145%, and Cu to 0.1%. Sulphides penetrated included pyrhotite>>pyrite, also sphalerite, galena, chalcopyrite, most strongly between 220-240m in graphitic metasediment, probably of the Saltbush Group.

anomalous radioactivity detected by downhole logging in the Tertiary ""N""  sand. The uranium appeared to be preferentially deposited on black, carbonaceous mudstone within a sand unit at a redox boundary.

drilling identified metal values of 0.13%Ni, 0.18%Cr, 4.8ppbPt and 3.4ppbPd in host weakly serpentinised ultramafic, and chlorite schist. Weak mineralisation associated with sheared margin of a granite.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested to identify a S-dipping sequence of claystone, siltstone, quartzite and sandstone of the Tarcoola Formation. Best intercepts was in TOL001 4m @ 2.16g/tAu from 44-48m in sandstone host.
drill hole DD10EPS001 reporting 0.7m @ 633ppmU3O8 from 239.3m, and 2m @ 188ppmU3O8 from 178m. no further details, U mineralisation associated with IOCG-type mineralisation.

drill intercepts of anomalous Cu-Au mineralisation. Best intercepts DD10NEP008, 2m @ 283ppmU3O8, DD10NEP011, 3m @ 91ppmU3O8, with 1.09%Cu, and 0.46g/tAu, NEP10W, 5.7m @ 61.4ppmU3O8, with 1.56%Cu, 0.52g/tAu.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: source of linear magnetic anomaly as magnetite-bearing gneiss of Mulgathing Complex, width ~110m, strike length ~500m. Cover of 25m of Cainozoic sediment. Davis Tube testwork returned satisfactory mass recoveries of magnetite.

good surface indication of gold. Follow up prospecting in 1904 by an underlie shaft, shallow shaft, and pits. Yield proved to be poor. Lode is on a portion of the Dusholes Line of Lode of gold-bearing quartz veins in altered quartzite unit in Pepuarta Tillite.
1899 historic workings of small open cuts on the Dustholes Line of Lode on gold-bearing quartz veins in host altered quartzite unit in Pepuarta Tillite. Reworked by Mr Deuter in 1935.

worked in 1899 by T. Fuller, and again in 1935 by F. Day. Historic workings on a portion of the Dusholes Line of Lode, presumably on gold-bearing quartz lode on host quartzite unit in Pepuarta Tillite.
shallow roadside scrape of ~3,000m2 x 1m deep on weathered Pepuarta Tillite presumably for road making material.
no details, located on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Pepuarta Tillite.
shallow roadside council scrape of >1,000m2 x 1m deep on weathered Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
shallow roadside scrapes for total area >1Ha x 1-2m deep on weathered Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
shallow roadside council scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1m deep on weathered, metasiltstone of the Bunyeroo Formation, and worked for road fill.
several adjacent, abandoned roadside council scrapes south of the Peterborough - Broken Hill railway for a total area <20,000m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on Quaternary clay for use as road fill.
2 x abandoned 2-4m deep costeans on thin strat unit in weathered Appila Tillite. larger costean is 80m x 20m x 2-3m deep.

scrape of >500m2 x 1-2m deep on narrow sandstone unit in weathered Appila Tillite. malfords is the northernmost of 5 quarries that have been developed on the same stratigraphic horizon, with the quarries scattered along a strike distance of  ~6km.

numerous shallow pits, a main underlay, and a shaft on the 10m wide, on hydrothermally altered metasediment of the Appila Tillite, and on the main Mount Grainger Line of Lode. No production details available.
no details, workings between Shattered Dream and Medora South developed on quartz lode in the Appila Tillite, and on the Mount Grainger Line of Lode.
quartz lode in host Appila Tillite on main Mount Grainger Line of Lode and between Medora and North Medora, no details.
no details, gold workings near Oodla Wirra Flux quarries in host diapiric rock of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
historic trench developed on deposit of ochreous, manganiferous brecciated quartzite.
deposit of ochre developed on host metasediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
workings of main open cut developed on the Mount Grainger line-of-lode in 1894 on quartz-iron oxide lode in host Appila Tillite. No production record determined.

quartz lode in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite. The workings occur on the main Mount Grainger Line of Lode, and immediately north of the main underlay of the Mount Grainger mine. No production figure determined.
no details, historical workings of  2 small pits ~40m apart excavated on NNE-trending quartz-iron oxide lode in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation.
historical workings of 3 pits on quartz-iron oxide lode trending NE for ~60m in host metasediment of the Tindelpina Shale Member, no details of mining returns known.
group of 5 workings within 50m presumably on quartz-iron oxide lodes in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, no details of mining returns known.

historical workings of 2 pits ~40m apart on quartz-iron oxide lode trending NE in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite, no details of mining returns known. Located ~100m SE of Buttamuck Shaft in creek.
pits and trenchs on N-trending quartz lode over a distance of ~60m in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation.
shallow workings as the southern extension of the historic Union Jack Mine (mindep # 6237). No details, prospecting for gold mineralisation in quartz veins in host Tarcowie Siltstone.
no details, single historical pit on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, no mining return records known.
no details, single historical pit on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, no mining return records known.
no details, single trench on NNW-trending quartz lode in host metasediment of the Gumbowie Arkose.
single 10m long trench excavated on NE-trending quartz lode in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite, no mining return records known.
no details, pit on quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tindelpina Shale Member, no mining return records known.
no details, prospecting trench and pit on quartz lode on host Appila Tillite.
pit and trench following trend of quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation, no mining return records known.
pit and trench following trend of quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation, no mining return records known.
no details, area of pits on quartz lode in host Tapley Hill Formation, no mining return records known.

historical pits on NE limb of Grainger Anticline. 2-3 pits over a distance of ~130m on NW-trending quartz lode in host metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and ~200 E of Wallaroo United workings.
2 abandoned local council roadside pits !250m apart on weathered metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation. Estimated combined production of ,10,000 tonne.
abandoned roadside council pit of <2,500m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
historic workings for precious opal, part of the Mount Brady Field, developed on weathered Bulldog Shale, active briefly in 2010.
historic workings for precious opal, part of the Mount Brady Field, developed on weathered Bulldog Shale, adjacent to Cairn Hill haul road.
precious opal recovered from several bulldozer cuts immediately east of the Stuart Highway in breakaway country developed on weathered Bulldog Shale.
abandoned and rehabilitated council pit of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Quaternary sand colluvium, and worked for road fill.
rubble pit developed on a deposit of calcrete and sandstone for use in road making by operators of neighbouring uranium in-situ leach mining operation. Seasonal production from 1997-2000 of ~650t.
current retention lease 118 held for alluvial gold in bed of large creek. No production recorded.
no historical details, old workings developed on the western extension of the Kirkeeks Treasure mine, presumably on quartz lode in host Burra Group. No recorded production determined. Current ML.
current lease ML 5471 held over large creek for alluvial gold in the Teetulpa Goldfield. No historic records nor modern production figures. .
stratabound U mineralisation in host Eocene Kanaka Beds. Strike length 2.5km strike length in overall U-shaped body, open-ended along both arms. Inferred resources 21.8Mt @ 292 ePPM U3O8.

30m wide surface exposure of a manganiferous unit of the Middleback Subgroup over a NS-trend of ~3km. Surface sampling gave best assay of 27%Mn. Tested in 19 RC holes in 2011 (Archer Exploration website).
most NE of a series of workings proceeding NE from the Silver Monarch, and at same stratigraphic level of Upper Middleback Jaspilite. Workings appear to be several shallow pits, and costeans.
council pits of ~40,000m2 x 1-4m deep and developed for use as road fill. material tested for suitability as source of high grade industrial dolomite, and found unsuitable.

small abandoned pit of <1,000m2 x 1-3m deep excavated in white dolomite of the Katunga Dolomite, no details of tenure history or production known.

coincident IP and fault offset as indicated by magnetics. Drill testing identified basement of red-rock altered amphibolite, volcaniclastics, granite and quartzite, with degrees of shearing. 1m samples assayed for Cu, Au returned no anomalous values.
area of abandoned, roadside council scrapes for total area ~2,000m2 x 1-2m deep, and developed on white, weathered, clayey metasiltstone of the Brachina Formation for road fill.

surface copper mineralisation on E margin of microdiorite, with hornfels halo. Drilling identified low grade mineralisation within or adjacent to hornfels contact with the intrusion. The sulphide was predominantly pyrite with lesser chalcopyrite.
abandoned shallow roadside council pit of 10Ha x 1m deep on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road fill.
abandoned and rehabilitated council pit of ~1,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.

expired mineral claim MC 3180 of 96 Ha on ~1.5 km of longitudinal dunal seed gypsum of the Holocene Yamba Formation developed on the eastern margin of a flat salt pan located immediately east of the Barrier Highway, and 2.5km NE of Lancelot.
expired mineral claim over marble of the Cambrian Mernmerna Formation. Grade lower than that of Rapid Bay marble.
mineral claim over an area of 78 hectares on Tertiary Gambier Limestone, for use in the production of lime sand for agricultural use.
EML on Quaternary sand spread, no recorded production.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shallow pit on dolomite of the Bridgewater Formation. Recorded production from 2005-13 estimated at >30,000t.
shallow pit developed on Tertiary limestone. .

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: old pit on sandstone in host Stonyfell Quartzite. Recorded production against EML 4538 presumed to be from this pit was 470 tonne from 1977-79.
minor cutting on hillside unearthing white clay developed as weathered profile on metasediment of the Stonyfell Quartzite. Tenure granted as PM 177 in 1993, but no operation commenced.
shallow workings to 1m depth on exposures of red-pink, dolomitised bryozoal Gambier Limestone.
abandoned council pit of >1,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete for road fill.
abandoned quarry of <500m2 x 1-5m deep on Tertiary limestone of the Murray Group, possibly an historic quarry worked for local supply of building stone.

low rise of Pleistocene calcrete trending EW for ~2km x 200m wide on which there have been developed several shallow quarries worked by the local council for road fill. The quarries are located both north and south of the New Sturt Highway.
small pit on limestone outcrop of the Bridgewater Formation, adjacent to the large strip mining sand operation of Teagle Sand Mine.
workings on sandstone of the Emeroo Subgroup, and forming the walls to a deeply incised creek. Recorded production from 1977-90 of ~115,300t.
small pit developed on a Quaternary sand spread, estimated production from 1999-2012 of 5,600 tonne.
small pit developed on large vein quartz blow of the Lincoln Complex for decorative stone. Production of ~350 tonne from 1977-80.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: group of adjacent tenements on an area of sand spread, and a ~400m long, WNW-trending dunal sand deposit. Intervals of production from 1981-2012 of ~2,000 tonne sand.

rock sample of basement outcrop of granite gneiss of the Mount Woods Domain with 130ppm U, 1.19% P2O5, and 0.13%F. In adjacent outcrop to the west of Tertiary  dark brown sandy carbonate, U to 1450ppmU, 3-16%P2O5, 0.46-1.76%F.

2 holes on a linear magnetic anomaly. Basement at 94m depth. Interval 94-118m, oxidised carbonate with minor chlorite, amphibole and magnetite, 118-136m (EOH) calc-silicate, with increasing magnetite. 2nd hole as a water bore, TD 127m.
reported mineralisation identified in drill holes by OZ Minerals in 2010 and 20111. Copper sulphide mineralisation appears to be associated with magnetite-flooded breccias.

identified by OZ Minerals as a prominent NW-trending magnetic anomaly. No geological details available. Drill hole intersections of 107m @ 0.13%Cu, 0.15g/tPGE, 121m @ 0.5g/tPGE, 15m @ 1g/tPt, 0.66g/tPd. Exact location unknown.

near coincident magnetic gravity anomaly drill tested to identify variably brecciated, chlorite-altered, magnetite-hematite supported matrix of felsic granulite, mylonitised gneiss, felsic granulite/gneiss as per 112/281m.

drilling identified basement at 84m of marble, with weak magnetite and trace pyrrhotite and chalcopyrite mineralisation from 84-101m, also calc-silicate/clinopyroxene skarn to 122m. and actinolite-calcite-phlogopite-pyrrhotite skarn to 161m.

local magnetic anomaly. Drilling penetrated basement sequence at 119.5m of felsic-magnetite gneiss, with 2 bands of breccia with anomalous U (10ppm), Th (523ppm), Ce (777ppm) and La (446ppm). Monazite was probable causative mineral species.
gravity-subdued magnetics drill tested for basement at 75m of alkali gabbro, basic and felsic pegmatite (elevated Ba-Ce-Th-Be), granulite, and amphibolite (elevated Pd, Ni, Cr, Cu, Ba).
linear aeromagnetic anomaly ~4km drill tested in 1 traverse to confirm 80-150m thick magnetite-bearing Braemar Ironstone in 2 beds. JORC exploration target for 1.7-2.3km SL at 150-300Mt.

S extension of Muster Dam prospect, linear magnetic anomaly source as magnetite-bearing IF of the Braemar Iron Formation. Exploration target for a single bed, strike length 1.7-2.3km, width 80-120m of 50-150Mt.

magnetic anomaly with strike length ~7km with EL area held by Lion One Aus. PL. Resource of magnetite-bearing IF of Braemar Ironstone at 510Mt at head grade 26.4%Fe, for DTR of 26.9% at grind to 38 micron to give mt conc of 69.7%Fe.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: prominent magnetic complex on folded magnetite-bearing IF of the Braemar Iron Formation. Total JORC resource 2.38Bt of 14.1%DTR, with magnetite concentrate grade @ 69.7%Fe, 0.004%P, 2.83%SiO2, and 0.20%Al2O3.
linear magnetic complex source as folded magnetite-bearing IF of the Braemar Iron Formation. Located ~3km SE of the Hawsons Deposit. Preliminary drilling completed.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BIG PAV; BRAEMAR CENTRAL; BRAEMAR EAST; BRAEMAR WEST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: near surface magnetite-bearing Braemar Ironstone for ~20km strike length for >1Btonne estimated resource. 15Km northern extension remains untested. Preliminary testwork confirmed potential for recovery of high grade magnetite concentrate.

thin horizons of ironstone of the Braemar Iron Formation outcropping discontinuously for ~27km in a NE direction along the northern boundary of the Ordovician Anabama Granite. Tenure is largely held by Fe Mines Ltd in 2019.
linear magnetic anomaly presumed of magnetite-bearing Braemar Iron Formation. ~25km SSE of the Adelaide-Broken Hill railway line at Olary. Best intercepts 140m at 30%Fe. Resource drilling planned.

ovoid aeromagnetic low near Cornwall Granite with drilling identifying anomalous Cu-Zn mineralisation in altered metasediment. Best value 0.19%Cu. Drilling of gossanous float identified a Cu-U horizon, best U 2m @ 153ppm, also 6m @ 0.57%Cu, 0.25%Zn.

regional soil geochemical anomaly tested by drilling. No significant mineralisation. Geochemically anomalous Ni-Cu-Zn-Co in micaceous and mafic schist/gneiss, and Ni-Cu-Zn-Mn in banded biotite schist/gneiss.

U-channel anomaly defined by an airborne magnetic-radiometric survey. Drilling identified sub-horizontal zone of U3O8 enrichment at weathering front over area to ~1.5km by 1km, open to the east and south.

U-channel anomaly defined by an airborne magnetic-radiometric survey. Drilling identified sub-horizontal zone of U3O8 enrichment in host deeply weathered gneiss at weathering front. Best value 613ppm U3O8.

drill traverse on a NS-trending linear magnetic anomaly identified slightly elevated Cu-Zn values in hole MAC70. Also magnetite-bearing ironstone presumably of Braemar Iron Formation in MAC69 beneath a cover of 66m of flat lying younger sediment.

NNE-trending, 10-15m wide by 700m long zone of Pb-Au anomalism, best analysis 1.53%Pb, 0.77g/tAu. Follow up drilling gave disappointing results. Interpreted as basement quartzite intruded by volcanics with associated epithermal alteration.

uranium mineralisation in clay-altered Hiltaba Granite comprising clay (kaolin?) pseudomorphs after feldspar, quartz, and irregular patches of a platy aluminosilicate mineral with fine grained sulphides. Diamond holes confirmed Hiltaba Granite.

soil geochem Ag-Pb anomaly drill tested to identify Ag-(Pb)mineralised rhyolite breccias, epithermally altered volcanics. Zone ~1400m NW x 600m wide with irregular Ag mineralisation. Follow up drilling identified narrow zone of strong Ag mineralisation.

drilling by Phoenix Copper has defined a mineable resource of copper mineralisation immediately south east of the Mountain of Light mine, no figure determined.

bulk samples identified halloysite 9-72% of clay sediment. Electron microscopy showed halloysite crystallised as regular tubules showing a high degree of alignment.

hole FLORC4 with anomalous Ni, Co, V, Y, Zn, and REE (La to 569ppm, Ce 128ppm, Y to 985ppm) in host metamorphosed calcareous sediment, with the element assemblage suggesting a mafic volcanic component.
shallow council pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-2m deep on mantle of Pleistocene developed over Tetiary limestone of the Murray Group, and worked for road fill.

drilling identified altered, deformed meta-tuff as host to massive, bucky qtz-cb-hm-cl-cpy-py+/-sph-gal tensional veins & disseminated py & cpy to 2%. Best assay, 1m @ 0.35g/t Au, 0.21%Cu & 0.14%Zn, plus  264ppmPb & 76ppmBi @ 329m.

weak magnetic anomaly adjacent to the Anabama-Redan Fault investigated in 5 drill holes. Basal Tertiary chert carried framboidal pyrite and syngenetic chalcopyrite, with one sample returning 1070ppmCu.

BLEG gold-in-soil anomaly coincident with 2km long, linear magnetic anomaly marginal to Anabama Granite. Drilling identified phlogopite-altered schist of Umberatana Group. Elevated Cu and Zn values were recorded in basement on the latter.
council pit of ~25,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered, white, kaolinised, feldspathic sandstone of the Marola Sandstone Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned shallow council pit of .10,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of >5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.

linear magnetic anomaly, magnetite-bearing BIF of the Hutchison Group being the NE continuation of Koppio and Brennand deposits. Total recoverable iron ~14.7Mt. Deposit of Eyre Iron's Fusion project.  Lincoln Minerals Ltd. aquired the deposit from Centrex Metals (now Centrex Ltd.) in 2018. This now forms part of their Green Iron Project.

linear magnetic anomaly as magnetite-bearing gneiss beneath 50-100m of cover sediment. Drilling (2011) on portion of anomaly identified width ~200m. Exploration target 800-1000Mt. Southernmost of Iron Road's Warramboo Project.

At least 2 levels, main at ~14m with crystal opal, weaker level at about 10m with honey and grey potch opal with some colour. Possibly another level at about 12m. Alunite associated with levels, gypsum common throughout.
