abandoned council scrape of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
2 abandoned shallow quarries 10m apart developed by the local council on silicified metasandstone of the lower Skillogalee Dolomite, and worked for road making material.

narrow pit of >3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on bleached, weathered Skillogalee Dolomite originally worked by F.A. Mader for magnesite for 240 tonne from 1934-37. Production in 1927 of 31 tonne by B.F. Tanner on small deposit ~900m to the north.
2 adjacent council pits of <20,000m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
shallow quarry located on hilltop ~300m SW of the Burra open cut. Quarry developed in weathered metasediment of the Skillogalee Dolomite, presumably by the local council for road making material.
roadside council scrape of >1,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Rhynie Sandstone, and worked for road fill.

council pit of >3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on NS-trending strike ridge of a narrow unit of weathered, white, kaolinitic metasiltstone of the Rhynie Sandstone. Worked for road fill, with potential for expansion at depth and along strike to south by ~400m.
abandoned, part rehabilitated quarry of >2,500m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Heatherdale Shale, now site of a small dam.

surface copper mineralisation (bornite), and nickel mineralisation (pentlandite) identified on Archean of the Mulgathing Complex. The occurrences are within a calcretel Cu-Ni geochemical anomaly with dimensions 5km long.
large open cut ~1.5km long NNW by 500m wide by 10-15m deep, developed on Cambrian Andamooka Limestone for construction material for various infrastructure at the Olympic Dam mine.
small open cut ~100m long NS by 50m wide by 5m deep, developed on Cambrian Andamooka Limestone for construction material for various infrastructure at the Olympic Dam mine.
abandoned council pit of ~7,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Appila Tillite, and worked for road fill.

abandoned roadside scrape of <30,000m2 x 1-2m deep, worked for road fill by Transport SA during construction of the sealed Wilmington-Orroroo road, and developed on weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; MT. BRYAN EAST ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: roadside council pit of ~13,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Wilyerpa Formation, and worked for road fill. Rock described in open file envelope 9922 pp 485/486 as a slightly weathered, diamictite.
abandoned council quarry of ~7,000m2 x 1-6m deep on pale purple siltstone of the Brachina Formation, and worked for road fill.
2 roadside pits on lime sand of the Bridgewater Formation. located on N side of Woods Road. Presumably developed by local council for road base material.
roadside council pit of <4Ha x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene sand, and worked for road fill. The pit is located adjacent to the eastern margin of a playa lake.
2 adjacent council pits for total area <10,000m2 x 1-2m deep on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road fill.

hematite-magnetite breccia complex, with anomalous Cu-Au. RC and diamond drilling identified sub-economic chalcopyrite plus pyrite in breccia hosted by quartzite adjacent to granite pluton margin. Best value 10m @ 0.3%Cu.
detritus on S shore of salt pan with visible flakes of atacamite and atacamite in host arkosic siltstone of the Bunyeroo Formation. Also anomalous gold.
roadside council pit of >10,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.

goethitic outcrop drill tested in late 2012 for iron ore. Drilling returned significant values for Sn, Pb, Zn and U in host deeply weathered metasediment presumed Hutchison Group. Confirmed by diamond drilling for 12.3m @ 1.1%Sn.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Cassiterite,  Cerussite,  Sphalerite,  Uranium Minerals (Non Specific)

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: surface outcrop of goethite/hematite drilled and sampled in late 2012 by Ironclad Mining Limited. Drilling identified a resource of 0.12Mt at 57.5%Fe.

sample collected by Waldin Holdings Ltd in 1987 from a 12cm wide quartz vein in host siltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. The sample returned values of 2.3ppmAu, 3.1%As, 240ppmCu, 170ppmPb, and <1ppmAg.

sample collected by Waldin Holdings Ltd in 1987 from a qz vein with boxwork after pyrite in host siltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. The sample returned values of 1.1ppmAu, 340ppmAs, 160ppmCu, 6ppmPb, and <1ppmAg.
costean developed on NE-trending quatz lode in host Pepuarta Tillite. No production records apparent.

narrow zone ~8km long of Tertiary silcrete with samples returning maximum values of 490ppm U3O8 at the E end, and 390ppm U3O8 at the western end. Petrological examination identified a green mineral determined to be carnotite.

zone of argillic alteration associated with a carbonate horizon on a shear zone. Drilling determined zones of bleaching and argillation due to surface leaching rather than a primary alteration feature.

coincident gravity-magnetic feature. Drill hole DD12KMS003 returned 440.6m @ 0.43%Cu, 0.08g/tAu from 1005.4m.  Strong hematite-chlorite altered, heterolithic granite breccia with disseminated chalcopyrite, pyrite, and rare bornite.
COMMODITIES: Copper,  Gold,  Silver,  Uranium Oxide,  Uranium

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: roadside council pit of ~15,000m2 x 1-3m deep on wooded area of outcropping Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
no historical details, 2 quarries 10-20m wide extending in a NNE direction for 240m. Developed on narrow unit of weathered feldspathic sandstone of the Appila Tillite, presumably for building stone.
abandoned quarry of <5,000m2 x 1-5m deep on limestone of the Kulpara Formation, no details of its history, possibly council pit for road ballast. The quarry is now heavily overgrown.
abandoned quarry of ~600m2 x 1-10m deep on felspathic gneiss of the Barossa Complex, and worked for road making material.
quarry in felspathic paragneiss of the Barossa Complex, and worked for supply of road metal. Central pit of 3 adjacent quarries all operated for supply of a similar material for road metal.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: ALICE LODE; CAROLINE; HALLS LODE; HANCOCKS LODE; MOONTA; MOONTA WESTERN BELT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: most north-western lode system extended for ~700m NNE, roughly parallel to the other 2 main lode systems, and some 800m further to the NW. The lodes were uneconomic, host feldspar porphyry of the Moonta Porphyry, little payable ore.
council quarry of <15,000m2 x 1-5m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Appila Tillite, and worked for road fill.
roadside council scrape of ~1,500m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and worked for road fill.

area of pits adjacent to the Eyre Highway, with the main pit developed on weathered basalt of the Sleaford Complex, and several smaller pits on the overlying mantle of Pleistocene calcrete. Main pit now backfilled with sand, and rehabilitated.
roadside council scrape of >1,500m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.

2 open cuts in open paddock above Burra Oval, no historical records located. They were developed on metasiltstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale. The quarries are of historic significance providing stone for use in the mine and for local use.
open cut in open paddock E of old smelting works in Burra, no historical records located, presumably worked metasiltstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale for building stone for local use.
roadside council pit of >7,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside quarry, presumably developed by the local council for road ballast on metasiltone of the Watervale Sandstone Member.
abandoned roadside pit of ~2Ha x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Carrickalinga Formation, and worked for road fill.
auriferous quartz veins trending N in zones of more intense folding of host metasediment of the Rhynie Sandstone. Veins prospected for no returns, minor gold recovered from associated alluvials.

Alluvial gold in basal conglomerate of Algebuckina Sandstone, minor workings on quartz reefs in Peake Metamorphics. Bulk sampling of conglomerate in the late 1970s-early 1980s returned average assay of 0.036g/t Au.

alluvial gold (including nuggets) in host surface loam, gravel, and red clay. Small operations on auriferous quartz reefs in host Adelaidean sandstone. Production was estimated at 250oz (7.8 Kg) bullion gold.

large (>2.5km long), strong coincident IP and resistivity anomaly. Drilling identified the source as graphitic schist. Samples returned best value >7%TGC. Hole MDRC28, 20m @ 12.4g/tAg from 68m in wthd clay, with Zn and Pb at base.

3 roadside council pits for total area of ~2Ha x 1-3m deep, and over an EW distance of 800m on weathered metasiltstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone, with a thin mantle of Pleistocene calcrete, with both rock types used for supply of road fill.
2 shallow prospecting pits on quartz blows in host Tapley Hill Formation. They are the southernmost workings on the Mongolata Range, and south of the Mongolata Goldfield.

gold in shallow alluvium in several NE-trending gullies, and on adjacent hillsides of metasediment of the Umberatana Group. Source possibly brecciated ironstone emplaced on a fault. Production ~1000oz (31.1kg).

2 abandoned quarries of total area >2,500m2 x 1-5m deep on granite gneiss of the Rathjen Gneiss, no production history determined, presumably worked by Transport SA and local council for road making material.

alluvial gold, minor quartz-iron oxide reefs. Production mainly from the alluvium was estimated at 750oz ( 23.3kg). Many shallow shafts spread out across sections 682, 619, 631, 695, Hundred Nuriootpa.
alluvial gold in Recent sandy clay, some small nuggets recovered. Some auriferous quartz reefs were worked on section 527, but returns were poor. Total production 12.4-15.6 kg (400-500 oz) gold.

declared goldfield of ~160km2 surveyed over Hundreds Anna, Dutton and Brownlow. Mines located near the foot of the ranges, with shafts to 6m on water worn wash with fine gold. No production figures were recorded.

alluvial gold, minor workings on quartz-iron oxide-pyrite lodes in host slate of the Burra Group. Total production from the area, including Lady Edith and Uraidla hard rockmines was estimated at 2,000oz (62.2kg).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CHRISTINAOS; MINEFIELDS EXPLORATION; ML 3475; SICKERDICK MARBLE; TRURO TALC PROJECT
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: talc beds and lenses in bends of fold structures, and with stratigraphic control in host metamorphosed carbonates of the Hawker Group. 1970 resource estimate for a cut off at 70% talc 320,605 tonne at 81% talc, with 3.56% Fe2O3.
abandoned quarry on metasediment of the Normanville Group. No historical detail apparent.
weathered sandstone and limestone of the Cambrian Normanville Group. Production from 1977-97 was estimated at 36,000 tonne sandstone, minor limestone for road ballast.

malachite mineralisation in host sediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Best value in the area of the original discovery of 4m at 4.2%Cu from 5-9m in hole S5. Soil geochemical survey for NE-trending anomaly >50ppmCu over an area 300m x 100m.

3 IP anomalies along strike from the Monster Mine. Drilled by Phoenix Copper in 2012. Mineralisation of pyritic, quartz-carbonate veined, dolomitic siltstone with ccp, bornite at sheared contact of marble breccia and banded dolomite.
abandoned quarry of ~800m2 x 1-5m deep on narrow weathered sandstone unit of the Mintaro Shale, possibly for building stone for local use. .

abandoned narrow costean of ~750m2 x 1-6m deep cut into S slope of hill of narrow unit of weathered metasediment of the Appila Tillite. No historical details, possibly worked for building stone for local use.
surface copper show in host calcareous slate of the Saddleworth Formation. The mineralisation may be associated with a serpentinised mica peridotite dyke, trend NE, and with kimberlitic affinities.
abandoned council pit of ~1Ha x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside pit of <1.5Ha x 1-2m deep, located adjacent to the Barrier Highway. Developed by the Highways Department for road ballast on Tertiary clays.
abandoned council scrape of <3,000m2 x 1-2m deep on narrow unit of weathered dolomite of the River Wakefield Formation, and worked for road fill.

2 IP chargeability and resistivity anomalies drill tested in March 2013. They penetrated Zn-Pb-Ag-(Au) mineralisation in highly altered marble of the Hutchison Group. Best intersection was 30m at 1.9%Zn, 21g/tAg, 0.27g/tAu, from 132m.
abandoned roadside cutting of ~700m2 x 1-5m deep on weathered, metasomatised, coarse crystalline marble of the Skillogalee Dolomite, and worked for road fill.

quarry developed from 1933-39 on weathered shale of the Saddleworth Formation in a series of small quarries and one main quarry, this quarry on sections 201, Hundred Gilbert. Overall production from all quarries was 1213 tonne of shale.

series of shallow pits extending for 200m around the nose of a major fold. Historical details unknown, commodity uncertain, possibly dolomite for road ballast, or historical quarries for building stone.
abandoned roadside council scrape of <5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside quarry of ~2,000m2 x 1-8m deep on weathered unit of sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone, possibly worked by local council for road fill.
narrow abandoned council pit of ~1,600m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered dolomite of the River Broughton Beds, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~4,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Anama Siltstone Member of the Rhynie Sandstone, and worked for road fill.

regional gravity anomaly ~2.5km NE of Carrapateena, with resource drilling confirming a series of Cu-Au-Ag mineralised pipe-like hematite breccia structures. Inferred resource (2018) 104Mtonne at 0.7%Cu, 0.5g/tAu, 3g/tAg.

outcrop of ironstone ~3-5m wide, dip steep, trend 050 magnetic. Surface samples 40-55%Fe. Ironstone is mapped as in host Tarcowie Siltstone. Regional aeromagnetics indicate an associated magnetic anomaly, though of limited strike.

electromagnetic anomaly drill tested in March-April 2013, which drilling identified the source of the anomaly was graphitic schist of the Hutchison Group. Best value was 15m at 20.7%TGC from 14-29m in hole WG118.
1 of 4 historic dimension stone quarries in feldspathic sandstone units. Combined production >60,000 tonne, production from Quarry 1 was ~12,000 tonne. It has been backfilled to surface.
tenement granted in 1993 to Rocla Pty Ltd on a sand spread adjacent to a salt lake. Surface stripping of vegetation was completed, though subsequently there was no recorded production.

discordant olivine basalt dyke emplaced at low T in Umberatana Group shale and siltstone. Prospective for nepheline (a feldspathoid) for use in manufacture of glass and ceramics. Unsuitable due to its low nepheline, and high Fe content.

quartz-barite veins intrude the Burkitt Granite and the overlying Corunna Conglomerate. A resource of 100's tonne barite for an area around 2 old pits. Grade was considered to be unsuitable for use as oil drilling additive.

flaggy siltstone of the Mintaro Shale outcropping in a creek was investigated in 1954 as a possible resource of flagstone of similar quality to that of the world famous Mintaro slate quarries. Further testing by drilling is required.

co-incident EM and gravity anomaly drill tested to identify significant intervals of massive sulphide in host igneous rock of intermediate to mafic origin. Main sulphides pyrite and pyrrhotite, trace chalcopyrite.

calcrete geochemical anomaly, with widespread anomalous copper values. 200m x 200m sampling grid defined a >40ppm Cu area of ~4km EW by 1.5km NS, and open to the east, south and west. Prospective for IOCG mineralisation.

no historical details, small workings on mineral claim 2898 (lapsed) granted for gem, semi-precious stones, presumably for chrysoprase, jasper and chalcedony developed on ferruginised Giles Complex mafic and ultramafic igneous rock.

agate over several square km, and on the eastern side of a large creek. Occurs in situ in Andamooka Limestone, and on gibber plains. Quality is generally poor consisting mainly of amorphous lumps of red and white chalcedony.

NE-trending vein-quartz worked in the 1960s in 4 separatel pits located over ~600m apart. Worked for road aggregate. Host was sandstone of the Mesoproterozoic Broadview Schist. No total production figure identified.
unconventional gas (shale gas) project within the Nappamerri Trough, Cooper Basin. Operating company is Beach Energy on tenure PEL 218 owned by Beach Energy (70%), Chevron (30%).

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: COOPER BASIN JV UNCONVENTIONAL GAS; PPL 101; PPL 102; PPL 11; PPL 113; PPL 7; PPL 8; PPL 9
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: recent exploration for unconventional (shale) gas. A Coober Basin JV has been formed with a company partnership; Santos Ltd (66.6%), Delhi Petroleum Pty Ltd (20.21%), Origin Energy Resources Ltd (13.19%). Operator Santos Ltd.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: PEL 115; PEL 516; SENEX ENERGY SOUTHERN COOPER BASIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: unconventional (shale) gas project in the Cooper Basin operated by Senex Energy Ltd on PEL 516, PEL 115. No published resource estimate. Commodities of interest include shale oil, shale gas, basin-centred gas, deep coal gas.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BEACH ENERGY JV COAL GAS AND SHALE GAS; PEL 94; PEL 95
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: unconventional (shale) gas project in the Cooper Basin. Operating compay Beach Energy on PEL 94, PEL 95. No resource estimate published, commodities of interest are shale gas, and deep coal gas.

unconventional (shale) gas and coal seam gas project in the Cooper Basin, operating company Strike Energy Ltd. No resource estimate published, commodities of interest include shale gas, and deep coal gas.

unconventional (shale) gas project in Otway Basin, operated by Cooper Energy, and Beach Energy. Company tenure includes; PELs 186, 255, 494, and 495. No resource estimate, commodities of interest shale gas, basin-centred gas.

geothermal source by radiogenic decay of heat producing Mesoproterozoic basement of Mt Painter Complex. Deep drilling & testwork identified a natural geothermal system. Total estimated recoverable resource 38,000 PJth.

Joint Venture for generation of geothermal energy from hot rocks on the Cooper Basin in South Australia. Current reported geothermal resource of 59,200 PJ recoverable thermal energy ~7,000 PJ end user energy.

phosphate rock at or below Lower Brighton Limestone. Pit 1 the southernmost, a longitudinal pit with ~10m phosphatic kunkar. Pit 4 2.7m of pale, flinty calcium phosphate with veins of glassy wavellite. A sample assayed 20.7% P2O5.

residual deposits formed by replacement of limestone by phosphate rock and clay preferentially along joints and solution cavities  in host limestone of the Cambrian Kulpara Formation. No production figure recorded.
abandoned scrapes of ~6Ha x 1-2m deep on Tertiary ferricrete, and worked for road fill.

2 shallow pits 150m apart developed on metasiltstone of the Emeroo Subgroup presumably by the local council for road base material. Prospecting in early 1900sc identified phosphate nodules, not confirmed in follow up investigation by Geol. Survey.

secondary accumulation of phosphate rock on a stratabound phosphorite. Host was at the contact of Brighton Limestone and underlying argillite and arenite of the Tapley Hill Formation. No production figure recorded.
small roadside council pit of ~800m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered ABC Range Quartzite, and worked for road fill. One of 3 quarries within 2 km on a low range of hlls between RedHill and Crystal Brook.
abandoned quarry of ~800m2 x 1-5m deep on weathered sandstone of the Undalya Quartzite, possibly an historic quarry worked for building stone for local use.
shallow historic quarry ~600m east of Beetaloo Valley Road, and on metasiltstone of the Appila Tillite. No details, identified from quarry symbol on 50K topographic map series.
3 roadside council pits over a distance of ~650m for cumulative area of ,20,000m2 x 1-2m deep, developed on weathered dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite, and worked for road fill.
no details, identified from mine symbol on Pirie 100K topographic map. Presumably an old prospecting show for dolomite possibly by BHAS for flux for the Port Pirie smelter.

abandoned council scrapes of <15,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill. Second quarry ~ 300m to west into low hill adjacent to a creek, dimensions ~80m long x 4m deep.

pit developed west of Yongala on quartzite of the Burra Group for road making material. Tested in 3 diamond holes in 1964 as a source of railway ballast and found to be unsatisfactory for this purpose.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~12,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside borrowl pit of >20,000m2 x 1-3m deep on narrow unit to 30-50m wide of weathered metasiltone of the Auburn Dolomite Member of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.

phosphate rock occurred as nodules in the soil profile, also a residual deposits associated with manganese oxide, presumably developed on stratabound low-grade phosphorite beds in the Burra Group. No recorded production figure.

weak bullseye magnetic target with marginal arcuate (skarn?) magnetic anomaly. Drill holes identified leucocratic Christie Gneiss, with anomalous values for tungsten over a 50m interval to maximum 0.12% WO3.
4km prominent aeromagnetic anomaly tested in 4 diamond holes. W-dipping sequence of BIF weathered to ~100m. Initial Davis Tube testwork favourable. Conceptual exploration target of 275-500Mt.

one of several targets identified in the Investigator Resources Peterlumbo project area. Grid soil geochemical survey has identified anomalous silver over an area 5km x 7km located ~3km east of the Paris deposit, best value 2065ppm Ag.

commodity uncertain, area of diggings marked on 50K topographic map. On satelite imagery appears to be disturbed ground over a ENE-trend for ~50m. Workings are close to the Adelaidean - Cambrian contact.

diamond prospect identified by Stockdale in 1992 when loam sampling returned samples with anomalous picroilmenite in an area stretching ~15km EW from immediately west and continuing east and north of Venus Bay. No source identified.
kimberlite sill drilled and sampled for negative results for diamonds. Sill thickens (up to 3.9 m) towards the northwest and is gently folded to a shallow, southeast plunging syncline.

kimberlite sill discovered in 1973. Bulk sampling by Stockdale failed to detect diamonds. Recent work has shown East and West sills, previously considered separate bodies, are probably related and appear to be nearly horizontal.

7m thick lignite seam from 195m located near the base of the Tertary Renmark Beds. Also 2 kimberlites identified in drill holes in basement to the Tertiary Murray Bain sediment. Non diamondiferous, evolved kimberlites, age date 179 +/- 2 Ma.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Chromite,  Chromium Diopside,  Perovskite,  Picroilmenite,  Pyrope

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small non-diamondiferous kimberlite pipe in host Burra Group metasediment, and discovered in 2004, located 5.3km SE of Lyndoch, no further details.
located adjacent to Stockwell township, non-diamondiferous kimberlite pipe discovered in 2004. Host rock is limestone of the Normanville Group.

heavy mineral stream samples recovered indicator minerals. Drilling intersected diatreme facies kimberlite with matrix supported mafic breccia fragments, including rare eclogite clasts up to 7 cm in diameter. No diamonds were reported.

cluster of diamondiferous kimberlite dykes at the SE end of the Eurelia Kimberlite Field. A series of 13 trenches in deeply weathered kimberlite beneath shallow cover provided samples from which >400 microdiamonds have been recovered.
swarm of ~15 thin, scattered, discontinuous non-diamondiferous kimberlite dykes, all trending NW, and located marginal to the Walloway diapir.

NW area of the Eurelia Kimberlite Province. Scattered 5 dykes over an area ~5.6km EW by 1.4km NS. Naming convention for dykes is MOO prefix series, and dykes K09, and K09b. Dykes MOO-79B, 44B, and K09b are diamondiferous.
~10km NE of Peterborough. The field field consists of 2 clusters; one of two small pipes (TW05 and TW76) and a second of two sills further to the southwest (PTB-74a and PTB-74d).
~6km E of Peterborough. The field includes 2 dykes, PTB_61D, and PTB-67a, both diamond-bearing, and 1 pipe, TER-P18.
located in the Terowie Kimberlite Province, and ~14km ESE of Peterborough. The field has 3 non-diamondiferous pipes, TER-23, TER-63A, and TER-64A.
centered on an area ~14km SE of Terowie. A group of 9 non-diamondiferous thin sills-dykes and one pipe.

found using detailed magnetics, followed by costeaning, or drilling if the depth of sediment cover was excessive. The field includes a cluster of  11 dykes, 2 sills and 1 pipe, all non-diamondiferous and scattered over an area of ~1.5km2.
non-diamondiferous kimberlite field of 4 dykes identified by costeaning, and some drilling. A deep diamond hole HLD 1 failed to intercept kimberlitic rock.
several kimberlite dykes, Mungibbie 01–05, discovered by DeBeers in the early 1970s. Mungibbie 05 was excavated and bulk sampled by De Beers, with no diamonds reported.

field comprises 2 pipes, 2 dykes, and 1 sill on the east side of a north-south trending range of hills (Mittopitta series), plus a series of 9 dykes and 1 sill on the western side (the Wonna kimberlites). No diamonds have been recovered.
one of a group of new kimberlite fields recently discovered following the exploration activities of Flinders Mines Limited.The field includes 1 pipe and 4 dykes, all non-diamondiferous.
one of a group of new kimberlite fields recently discovered following the exploration activities of Flinders Mines Limited. The field includes 3 pipe and 4 dykes, all non-diamondiferous.

field consists of 4 pipes and 24 dykes distributed in several clusters of small pipes and associated dykes over a NS distance of >7km. It includes the Pandappa dykes and sills to the south. No diamonds have been recovered.

2 sills 80 cm wide and 60 cm apart trend NE exposed in prospecting trench. Serpentinised euhedral olivine phenocrysts in a groundmass of flow orientated mica laths and described as a mica-peridotite with kimberlitic affinities.

near co-incident mag-grav feature drill tested in 4 diamond holes. Magnetic basaltic trachy-andesite likely source of magc anomaly. IP anomalies due to saline groundwater. High K2O interval 149-152m (45% K2O) in volcanics in hole MGYC4.

unusual intrusive rocks, possibly lamproite. 2 diatremes 4km apart, S diatreme with Cu diggings at contact. Petrology determined the matrix as tuffaceous, with geochemistry indicating a lamproite/calk-alkaline lamprophyre.

drill test of surface geochemical anomaly on GRV in area of EW-trending shears identified chlorite-sericite-epidote altered GRV, no anomalous base or precious metals. Best assay 98KE008, 15m @ 1360ppmPb.

grid RAB drilling on 3 lines for 43 holes for 1576m, average depth 36.7m. The holes penetrated a series of basaltic dykes in host deformed, Archean Glenloth Granite, also GRV. A wide area of low-level anomalism was detected.

4 shallow holes on Giles Complex for best value was 0.3%Ni. Sampling W of holes in 1984 for orthopyroxenite with MgO values >30%, none of the samples were assayed for Ni, Cr, or base and precious metals.
surface samples from anorthosite returned values for Al2O3 at 25%. 10 km east 2 drillholes adjacent to the railway also penetrated anorthosite with chemical analysis of drill samples at >23% Al2O3.

IOCG-type mineralisation beneath ~800m cove. Barren Donington Suite granite, then 15m @ 1.23% Cu in strongly hematite altered rock, underlain across a gradational boundary, by 104m @ 0.27% Cu in shale of the Walleroo Group.

very thick, graded, resedimented hematitic breccia, similar to some upper sections of the Olympic Dam Breccia Complex. Davidson et al (Econ Geol, v102, 2007 pp 1471), do not comment on mineralization of the breccias complex.

2 diamond holes drilled on gravity anomaly targeting Proterozoic magmatic PGE-Ni-Cu mineralisation. Rare pyrrhotite and pyrite detected, possibly magmatic, however the results for Pt, Pd, Ni and Cu were low.
shallow, oval shaped deposit of kaolin of ~427,200 tonne located in weathered zone of basement rock. The clay has considerable sand and silt fraction.
shoreline outcrop of granite sampled in 2005, and on adjacent St. Peters Island with analysis returning tin values in excess of 0.1%Sn.
pit of >25,000m2 x 1-3m deep. Worked from 1925-29 a mantle of Pleistocene calcrete over Murray Group limestone for road fill. No production figure available
no recorded details, shallow historic quarry on quartzite of the Appila Tillite, possibly for supply of local building stone.

magnetic anomaly marginal to a circular non-magnetic core. Aircore drilling identified copper-gold mineralisation associated with elevated levels of REE and magnetite alteration, possibly indicating IOCG-(U) affinity.
COMMODITIES: Copper,  Gold,  Tungsten,  Beryllium,  Rare Earths

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drilling on the southern extension from the Portia deposit on similar host metasediment of the Portia Formation initially identified 4km of strike of continuous Zn-Au mineralisation. Follow up drilling identified Cu-Au mineralisation.
IOCG prospect with drilling identifying weak Cu-Au-(U-Ag) mineralisation in fault breccia in hematite altered dolostone and andesite. Best value 10m @ 0.57%Cu, and 0.23g/tAu, with anomalous Ag and U.
moderate amplitude gravity anomaly. Drill testing identified a mineralisation in hematite-veined and brecciated coarse grained greywacke.

drilling identified bimodal volcanics, tuff and slate of upper greenschist metm, actinolite-albite-chlorite-epidote-leucoxene +/- qz and sericite alteration. Best values to 0.2%Cu, 0.1% Pb, and 0.5%Zn.

EREBUS, coincident geochem and VTEM electromagnetic anomaly on the Menninnie Dam trend, and located ~5km SSW of Menninnie Central. Best value was 13.3g/tAg coincident with a strongly altered epithermal zone.

coincident electromagnetic and geochemical anomaly. Reconnaissance drilling penetrated basement rock with weak sericite alteration associated with minor Pb-Zn mineralisation. Peak values were 1,599ppmPb, 999ppmZn, and 1.6g/tAg.

secondary yellow urophane occurred as thin coatings on joint planes on host Carappee Granite. Reconnaissance drilling of the surrounding Tertiary sequence identified a thin zone of weakly elevated radioactivity at the redox boundary.

located in a repeat antiform with attendant faulting. Importantly the prospect area was located on the NMS9 marker bed in the Kooringa Member. The prospective area was marked by the presence of several iron oxide blows.
drilling identified relatively fine heavy mineral sand of the of the Loxton-Parilla Sand, with 6m at 1.29%HM from 15m depth in hole KA077.

drilling for HM sand for best result 6m at 1.36%HM from 15m depth in hole KA022. part of the C1 package, a younger strandline, being distinguished from the B1 unit by the different trend of its constituent strandlines.
drilling suggests HM-bearing strandline with strike continuity of >30km. Thickness to 3m, grade ~2%HM, mineralogy promising.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Andalusite,  Goethite,  Leucoxene,  Monazite,  Rutile,  Tourmaline,  Zircon

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: lignite near the top of the Tertiary Knight Group. Areal distribution 11km2. Resource (1981) is 33.6Mt. Quality assumed to be low-rank brown coal (lignite), of poor quality with high moisture content, also high in sulphur, sodium and chlorine.
hole KK02 penetrated ultramafic with minor magnetite, pentlandite, and violarite at 171m depth. Samples returned values of 0.135%Ni, 0.125%Cr, and 34.3%Mg.
Tertiary lignite deposit in host Upper Renmark Beds. Areal extent ~200km2 for estimated 580Mt of low quality, high ash, high sulphur lignite, minimum depth to top seam of ~120m.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MURRAY BASIN NORTH; NORTH MURRAY BASIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 3 holes penetrated intervals of lignite to lignitic clay at depth from 62-133m. A bedrock sample from hole 39 returned a value of 4300ppmZn. The holes covered an area of ~150km2.
2 holes penetrated intervals of lignite to lignitic clay at depths of ~120m. Hole 81MBR 47 drilled 1.4m lignite, and hole 81MBR 49 ~1.4m being a split seam.
occurrence of Tertiary lignite in host Upper Renmark Beds identified by drilling by CRA Exploration in the early 1980s. 1 hole, 81MBR 16 penetrated 3.54m of lignite from 151.8m.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MURRAY BASIN SOUTH; SOUTH MURRAY BASIN
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: single hole (81MBR 59) occurrence of Tertiary lignite to lignitic clay in 2 seams, maximum thickness 1.7m at depth of 119m, and in host sediment of the Upper Renmark Beds.

widespread heavy mineral mineralisation in a series of strandlines with a general trend ESE for distances to ~30km, and over a NE-SW distance of 15-20km. HM of composition 5% rutlie, 10% leucoxene, 27% ilmenite, and 11% zircon.

drilling identified 2 lens, one of >400m long, ave 7m thick at 1.39%HM, 18-26m of overburden. Composition ~ilmenite and leucoxene dominant,  moderate zircon, rare rutile. A second lens ~800m long, 2m thick, estimate ~1.5%HM.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Ilmenite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Leucoxene,  Monazite,  Rutile

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ESE trend of a photo interpreted strandline on traverse AG03. Hole AG03 660 penetrated 3m at 3.19%HM from 15m, and 1m @ 2.13%HM from 20m, also hole AG03 740, 2m @ 1.75%HM from 15m.

extensive strandline trending ESE for ~60km, with its eastern end running into Danggali Conservation Park. Fluvial sands were identified in drill holes over a 200m width, 3-4.5m thick, under 3m of cover, with grade estimated at 2.5%HM.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Ilmenite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Magnetite,  Rutile,  Zircon

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: strandline of ~12km length running into the NW border of Danggali Conservation Park. Drilling identified intervals of HM accumulation to 3.6%HM.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Ilmenite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Rutile,  Zircon

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; PETER ROAD; SHERLOCK SOUTH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: abandoned roadside council pit of >6,000m2 x 1-5m deep on no details, roadsite quarry on ~5m thick section of undifferentiated Pleistocene limestone horizon, and worked for road making material.
loose near-surface deposit of shell debris 2-3m thick, shell:sand ratio of ~55:45 for resource ~34,000 tonne.

dune set worked for sand for general purpose use. Shallow pit and scrape developed on a low NNW-trending sand dune to 3m maximum height. Mining proposal (2013) has been submitted for an adjacent dune ~400m to the west.
EML of 9.4Ha granted in 2013 on NW-trending low Holocene sand dune adjacent to the Adelaide - Broken Hill railway. resource ~140,000 tonne, production to end 2013 ~6,000 tonne.
EML 4503 of 11Ha granted in 1976 on Holocene sand spread for sand for use in the construction industry. Recorded production of 4900 tonne in 1976.

narrow ~550m long x 100m wide Holocene sand dune trend NNW. Mining claim 2870 applied for in 1994. Mining of the western side only has been completed, with significant resources remaining. No records for production figures apparent.
area of 426Ha centred on Mambrey Creek on W side of Augusta Highway. Sought commodities natural gravel, and calcrete. Production 1977 of 65,000 tonne of calcrete for use as road base material.
narrow Holocene sand dune trend NW for ~800m, with ~350m section with apparent workings, no records of tenure or production. Mining Claim granted for 12 months in 2012 on the unworked SE section.
shallow abandoned council scrape of ~1,000m2 x 1m deep on weathered on weathered Ordovician granite, and worked for road fill.

coincident soil geochemistry and magnetic anomaly ~4km long NS interpreted as as representing a fault zone. Subsequently drill tested in 23 shallow rotary air holes. No 2m intervals of samples assayed >0.5g/tAu.

old workings NW of Round Hill Dam near peak of quartzite. Quartzite underlain by gossanous siltstone with minor quartz veining. In 1987 Battle Mountain (Australia) Inc sampled dump material for values ranging from 0.56 - 1.29g/tAu.

historic shallow workings over a NW trend for ~150m. In 1987 Battle Mountain (Australia) Inc sampled vein material of quartz-iron oxide composition from the old dumps. Host was iron-rich siltstone. Best value was 0.61ppmAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Malachite,  Pyrite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: workings 500m S of Black Hill Bore with dumps sampled by the Geological Survey in 1985 for values of 4.96g/tAu, and 0.08g/tAu. Lease granted to F.A. Teague in 1936 for a reported production of 5.08 tonne for 45.76gm at 9g/tAu.
local magnetic anomaly drilled to identify mafic intrusive with elevated Cu-Co-(Au). line of old prospecting pits on gossan 1.6km to SE drilled for no anomalous geochemistry.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: NORTH WEST WINNOCH; STATION 55; THE OAKS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: altered siltstone in a drainage located on a fault that juxtaposes Tapley Hill Formation to Appila Tillite. 4 rock chip samples returned slightly anomalous Cu values of 520, 100, 280, and 76ppm, with negligible Au.

old workings with Cu carbonate-stained wall rocks, and quartz veins. Host very fine, pyritic siltstone, bleached and leached, possibly of the Wilyerpa Formation. Sample of brecciated vein-quartz assayed 8.22%Cu, and 0.005ppmAu.

old workings adjacent to the Barrier Highway. Copper mineralisation associated with ferruginous quartz veining in host silty sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone. A sample of vein material returned 1.48%Cu, 0.22g/tAu.

prospecting pits from early 1990s. Mineralisation in narrow, quartz-iron oxide veins paralleling the bedding (30/85W). A mullock sample returned 840ppmCu, 0.18g/tAu. Host rock comprised quartz sandstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone.

pits, and shaft on quartz-iron oxide vein carrying chalcocite, copper carbonate. Sample (B70R) of vein material returned 1.48%Cu, 0.22g/tAu. Host blue-grey Tindelpena Shale and quartz sandstone of the Appila Tillite.

pits, and 15m deep shaft on 20cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein carrying chalcocite, copper carbonate. Sample (B69R) of vein material returned negliible Cu and Au. Host pyritic siltstone, thin interbeds of dolomite of the Tindelpena Shale.
old workings on a prominent outcrop of patchy, ferruginous silica breccia, possibly Holowilena ironstone. Opened by Chinese copper workers. Bedding trend is 065, dip 55NW.
location uncertain, vertical shaft to 45-50m at the contact of Braemar Ironstone, and Appila Tillite, presumaby gold. A second prospecting pit is located ~150m to the NE along the ridge.
outcrop of leached claystone of the Woocalla Dolomite in the area of Hesso Homestread, with reported quarrying of the leached white clay regolith profile for clay for refractory and ceramic use.
small roadside pit with observed bouldery diatomite exposed. Drill testing in 11 holes in 1998 identified a sequence of sand and clay, with no significant diatomite observed.

IOCG target on a gravity anomaly near interpreted location of regional contact between basement metamorphics to unmetamorphosed GRV-equivalents to the south. Tested in 2 deep holes for best value 2m at 0.46%Cu from 363m.

IOCG target of 3mgal, 800nT magnetics. Drilling identified sequence of magnetite-albite-actinolite-diopside altered metasediments intruded by unaltered granite. Trace only ccp, py. Best interval 1.9m assayed 0.26%Cu from 398m.

IOCG gravity target. 1 drill hole penetrated fine grained, altered, mafic volcanics. Anomalous Zn-Pb towards the base of the hole was associated with a shear zone. Best interval 4m @ 0.11%Zn, 200pmPb from 328m.

prospecting pits on low ridge on zone of quartz veining trend ENE, and carrying weak copper carbonate staining. 7 samples returned a best value of 135ppb gold. 1 small <1mm gold nugget was recovered from drainage to the south.

small adit and tailings with copper carbonates. Drill tested in holes Wilcowie 1-3 for maximum 1.5%Cu. 100K geology indicates host is of the Skillogalee Dolomite, though later mapping suggests Callanna Group.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Barite,  Calcite,  Iron oxide (non specific),  Pyrite,  Quartz,  Siderite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: roadside scrape of >25,000m2 x 1-3m deep, and developed on Pleistocene calcrete for road fill.
outcrop of ironstone of the Mulgathing Complex identified by Marmota Energy during geological mapping. 8 rock chip samples over an area ~200m x 150m returned elevated values for Fe, maximum to 58%Fe.
roadside council scrape of ~7,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation, and worked for road fill.

Tertiary lignite discovered in 1922 by drilling. 2 seams in host Blanche Point Marl equivalents. Lower seam 6-12m, overburden thickness ~73m. Iindicated resource 400Mt. probably connects to N to Bowmans Lignite deposit.
deposit of volcanic ash at the northern end of Lake Leake worked prior to 1949 in a shallow roadside pit. Resource identified as extending along the eastern shoreline, estimated 76,500m3.
shallow pit for lime sand and volcanic ash developed on sequence of 60cm of lime sand over 2m of calcrete over volcanic ash. No production figure determined.
deposit of Quaternary volcanic ash on the NE shore of the lake, with resource estimated in 1949 of 30,600m3.
quarry developed on Taratap Granodiorite for dimension stone, and also for road base material by the local council.

2 roadside council pits of total area ~25,000m2 x 1-3m deep on sand of the Pleistocene Molineaux Sand, and worked for road fill. One pit is located adjacent to Jabuk Road, with the second pit located ~1km to the SE.
roadside pits over ~9.5Ha x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene Bakara Calcrete, overlain by a remnant east-west linear sand dune of the Pleistocene Molineaux Sand Dune System.

stone reserve of ~9Ha on boundary between sections 60W and 179, Hundred Morgan, with shallow abandoned council scrape of ~2.5Ha x 1-2m deep, part rehabilitated, and developed on weathered metasediment of the Appila Tillite for use as road fill.
Ni-Cu-(Co) sulphide gossan. Best assay 0.23%Ni, 0.17%Cu, 482ppmCo, and 220ppb Pt + Pd. The gossan can be traced over a strike length of 110m, and is associated with a gabbroic intrusive.

surface EM for conductive targets. Drilling penetrated narrow zones of dissemnated to massive sulphide associated with graphite. Best values to 0.5%Ni, 0.8%Cu, and 0.6g/tPt + Pd + Au. Host gabbro, pyroxenite of Giles Complex.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly drill tested to identify Proterozoic plutonic and metasediment rock. Shallowest depth to basement was ~100m, with weak sulphide mineralisation identified. Native gold was identified in one petrology sample.
Highways Department open cut developed in limestone/dolomite of the Balcanoona Formation for supply of road seal aggregate. Current dimensions ~260m x 160m, status abandoned.
workings for road seal aggregate on gravel of sandstone and quartzite in the current bedload of Windy Creek.

open cut developed for supply of road seal aggregate in calcareous metasiltstone of the Wirrapowie Limestone.
scrape on creek bed for supply of gravel of sandstone/quartzite for use as road seal aggregate.

quarry 120m long NNE by 30m wide developed for supply of road seal aggregate in host calcareous metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation.
exact location uncertain within the Radium Hill mine area. Pegmatite gneiss was excavated for use as road seal aggregate.
shallow quarry on the southern slope of a hill of calcareous metasiltstone of the River Broughton beds. Quarry dimensions ~90m EW by 45m NS developed for local supply of road seal aggregate.

abandoned, roadside council pit of ~10,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered metasediment of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
scrape on quaternary calcrete developed for supply of road seal aggregate. Current workings in separate scrape ~300m to NE, with access road S of MackIntosh Road.
shallow quarry dimensions 340m EW by 60m wide in Quaternary calcrete developed for supply of road base material, and road seal aggregate.

quarry developed on metasediment of the Balquidder Formation for supply of road seal aggregate.
large interstate open cut ~700m long EW by 200m wide in Proterozoic quartz-feldspar gneiss worked for construction materials including road seal aggregate.
large interstate (Victoria) open cut ~300m diameter in Tertiary basalt worked for construction materials including some supply of road seal aggregate to South Australia.

refers to unpublished documentation of testing of near surface Mesoproterozoic dolerite dyke for supply of road seal aggregate.
pit developed on Quaternary surface calcrete for road base material and road seal aggregate for construction of the Eyre Highway.
refers to unpublished documentation of testwork on near surface calcrete for suitability for use as road seal aggregate.

shallow pits on rhyolite of the Eucarro Rhyolite of the Gawler Range Volcanics developed for supply of road seal aggregate.
workings on current bed load of creek for sandstone and quartzite pebbles for processing for use as road seal aggregate.

shallow pit on surface Quaternary calcrete worked for road base material, and road seal aggregate. LA test results indicate a hardness value of the order of 25 - 30.
single bench quarry of ~6,500m2 x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete overlying Tertiary Nullabor Limestone, and worked for road fill and road seal aggregate.

limestone of the Padthaway Formation from the excavation of Drainage Channel M used as road seal aggregate and road base material. The material is atypical of the region in its increased hardness.
aircore traverse identified near surface HM 50:50 magnetite:zircon, with horizon confined to near surface Quaternary poorly sorted braided river channel system of the Pooraka Formation. .
abandoned, roadside quarry of ~1,500m2 x 1-4m deep, and developed on weathered metasediment of the Appila Tillite for road making material.
silver geochemical anomaly. Preliminary shallow RC aircore drilling confirmed significant silver values including a best value of 10m @ 990g/tAg

kaolin in weathering profile on Monarto Granite. Drilling identified kaolin in several holes, however quality was not sufficient to meet specification. Best result was hole M1, best interval 2-4m, with Al2O3 23.81%, and Fe2O3 1.37%.

located on the Paling Range, heavy mineral deposit identified by Rio Tinto during drilling of 6 traverses in 2007. The drilling identified a zone of HM 28km long x 6km wide, and 4.5 - 12m thick. Estimated resource was 50Mt @ 1.7%HM.
resource of limestone of the Norwest Bend Formation that forms a hardcap to underlying limestone of the Murray Group drill tested for use at the proposed Chowilla Dam site
horizontally bedded Tertiary limestone exposed in the sloping bank of a billabong on the south side of the river on section OE, Hundred Cadell, and worked for building stone.
clay samples from a green clay thought to belong to the Blanchetown Formation thought prodpective for activated clays (montmorillinite).
shallow pit developed on Tertiary Limestone of the Murray Group, with the rock being locally silicified, and considered supply of hard rock for use in construction of the proposed Chowilla Dam.
deposit of Pleistocene ferruginous, silicified sandstone used in construction of Lock 5. Resources are likely to be large, though covered by significant overburden.
area of deposit of ferruginous, silicified sandstone of the Woorinen Formation developed on several low rises SE of the township. There are several shallow scrapes developed on the material.
area of subcropping to outcropping kunkar investigated for construction material for use in building the proposed Chowilla Dam. Resource of 1.9 million cubic yards was determined (~3Mtonne @ SG 2.2).

area of subcropping to outcropping kunkar investigated for construction material for use in building the proposed Chowilla Dam. Resource of ~150,000 cubic yards was determined (~300,000 tonne @ SG 2.2).

lunette-style dune ~4km long NS developed on E margin of a playa lake, and investigated as a source of gypsum. 2 auger holes identified orange-brown silica sand within 30cm of the surface, and extending to at least 4m depth.
deposit of quartzite of the Backstairs Passage Formation investigated as a source of construction materials. Tenure as EML 6408 was granted to Topcoat Asphalt Contractors Pty Ltd in 2013.

one of 4 quarries developed on phyllite, schist, quartzite, and sandstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale, and worked for crushed rock in the 1950's. The quartzite beds proved to be too thin to be worked profitably.
