lease granted in 1973 as PM 157 for clay over an area of alluvium bordering a creek located adjacent to Middleton Road. Some excavation of clay, presumably by the local council for road making material.
historic shallow quarry developed on ferruginous siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation presumably for construction materials for local use.
historic quarry of ~2,400m2 x 1-4m deep on ferruginous siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, possibly worked for building stone.
historic shallow quarry of ~300m2 x 1-4m deep on ferruginous siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and possibly worked for building stone.
2 adjacent roadside council pits of <15,000m2 total area x 1-3m deep, worked for road fill, and developed on deeply weathered, kaolinitic granite of the Moody Suite.
abandoned shallow pit of ~1,600m2 x 1-3m deep on low, NS-trending ridge of weathered metasiltstone of the Belair Subgroup, and worked for road fill.
shallow council pit of ~7,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white, weathered, clayey metasediment of the Appila Tillite, and worked for road fill.
shallow abandoned roadside pit of <15,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white, weathered metasediment of the Wilyerpa Formation, and worked for road fill.

area investigated by Leyland Bros in mid 1970s for cement sand. Magnetic anomaly investigated by Craton Resources NL in 1998. Exploration confirmed source was strongly hematite-altered quartzite and dolomitic siltstone, with trace pyrite.

roadside scrape on pale green, porphyritic vesicular volcanic rock of the Truro Volcanics, presumably developed by the Highways Department for road base material. The vesicles to 1cm are infilled with distinctive pale lime-green epidote.
1-2m deep pit developed on NW-trending ridge of calcrete for supply of road making material during construction of the Burra to Morgan sealed road.

large quarry in Central Western Victoria district on Palaeozoic schistose to gneissic quartz mica (biotite & muscovite) metasediment of the St Arnaud Group. Used for  reconstruction of the Dukes Highway (Bordertown to the Border).

multiple-bench quarry located ~10km N of Alice Springs, and developed on migmatite for the supply of road seal aggregate, and road base material. It is an alternative suppply of road making material for the northern areas of SA.
developed in joint surfaces on goethite outcrop, and also as disseminated thorium-bearing mineral in host metasediment of the Tapanappa Formation.
piles of paddock stone of Pleistocene calcrete from numerous sites in the Hundreds Sherlock and Peake used as road making material in the mid 1950s.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MOUNT VICTOR EAST; MOUNT VICTOR WEST
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: drill testing of portion of extensive outcrop of Braemar iron formation by Pepininni Minerals Ltd, and exposed on the N limb of a regional scale anticline confirmed significant thickness of iron formation with grades >18%Fe.

prospect for heavy minerals identified in 3 holes in 1991. TA 10, 16-30m 1.42%HM, TA 11, 18-27m, 1.33%HM, and TA 12 18-26m, 0.3%HM, average HM of 31% ilmenite, 17% leucoxene, 5% rutile, 25% zircon, and 22% trash minerals.
workings on gold mineralisation within a zone of EW-trending quartz-tourmaline veins over an area ~250m long by 30m wide in host metasediment of the Tapanappa Formation.
soil geochemical target, with a local aeromagnetic anomaly. Follow up drilling identified a best value of 8m at 0.32g/tAu in oxide zone in host weakly magnetic gneiss.
heavy mineral to ~0.5% penetrated in 2 traverses in marine sand of the Bridgewater Formation. Visual estimate of HM 0.5 to 1%, for32% ilm, 8% lx, 9% rt, 9%zr, trash 42%.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CYCLONE EXTENDED; WANNA LAKES; WANNA SOUTH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: heavy mineral sand deposit in Western Australia, classic J-Bay entrapment site. Mineral resource (2010) of 137Mt @ 2.2%HM. Grade 31% zircon, 3% rutile, 6% leucoxene, 55% ilmenite, 4% trash minerals.

HM sand deposit in WA, and located ~2km N of the Cyclone HM deposit. Interpreted as HM accumulation in estuarine environment. 2010 determined an inferred resource in 2010 of 106Mt at 1.5%HM at a 1% cutoff, no grade information.included.
heavy mineral sand deposit in WA as accumulation along outlet of the Lefroy palaeochannel. Dimensions ~1.5km long by 300m wide. Grade  maximum 5%, with HM content of 82% ilm, 1.4% zr, 3% lxe, 2% rt.

heavy mineral sand deposit located in the SW limit of the Eucla basin. Drilling identified  resource (2013) of 470Mt at 4.6%HM. Grade was 35% leucoxene/altered ilmenite, 26% ilmenite, 0.5% zircon, and 0.6% rutile/anatase.
heavy mineral accumulations in minor strandlines located in the western Eucla Basin, WA. Preliminary drilling identified up to 4.2%HM dominantly ilmenite, with low rutile and zircon content.

silver in soil survey completed by Investigator Resources in 2012 with follow up scout drilling of the anomalous area. The drilling identified widespread silver mineralisation with one hole finishing at 4m at 24g/tAg, and 0.28g/tAu.
small occurrence of talc in fault zone in creek bed in host Skillogalee Dolomite. Talc is pale grey, contains a high content of siliceous grit, with overall talc content <50%.

Tertiary sand deposit as capping on low hills investigated in 1965. Testwork determined a high proportion of fines and gravel. Average clay content 19%. Resource estimate 76,500m3 or ~122,000 tonne (at SG 1.6).

gossan with anomalous Cu and zinc. Drill testing confirmed weak Cu-Zn mineralisation associated with a quartzite unit. Surface geochemistry by Minotaur Exploration identified values of 1.7g/tAu, 8.5g/tAg, 0.165Cu, and 2.1%Pb.
weak surface U mineralisation drill tested to return best value 179ppm U3O8 in pyritic biotite-rich schist of the Hutchison Group.
linear conductor drill tested to determine weak u mineralisation in a pyritic, biotite pelite, best value 169ppm U3O8.
Grampus Quartzite for potential use as railway ballast. LA abrasion testwork determined rock unsuitable for use as railway ballast. Resource estimate ~1Mt.
drill testing of gypsum exposed on E shore of Lake Torrens gave best result of a gypsum bed to 10m thick, thinning rapidly E. Grades <60% fine seed gypsum admixed with fine red-brown sand and clay.
drill testing of gypsum exposed on E shore of Lake Torrens gave best result of minor  beds of fine seed gypsum, best gypsum content to 60%, and admixed with fine sand and clay.
quarry of ~1.5Ha x 1-5m deep developed by the Highways Department in ~1980 on a low strike ridge of deeply weathered ABC Range Quartzite for road fill.
zinc target tested in 2 holes for weak willemite mineraisation  adjacent to a diapiric- Wilkawillina Limestone contact. Overall grade in the most promising veins gave values of 0.1%Zn, 0.1%Pb.
abandoned roadside council borrow pit of >10,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.

Holocene shell grit of the St. Kilda Formation for ~12km between Port Pirie and Port Germein. Resource figure ~3.7mt including 2.9Mt outside the 800m coastal reserve, and 800,000 tonne inside, grade estimate 48% CaCO3.

Holocene sand spread, with workings located at the corner of Pirie Blocks and Davis roads. EML 4545 located immediately to the north, but no production recorded. Presumably worked by the local council for construction material.

lateritic nickel deposit comprising ochreous goethite plus clay, and derived from deep weathering of host dunite and peridotite of the Wingellina layered igneous complex.  April 2014 resource 187Mt @ 1%Ni, 0.08%Co, 47%Fe2O3.
COMMODITIES: Nickel,  Chrysoprase,  Cobalt,  Iron,  Iron Ore,  Rare Earths

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: massive to disseminated Voiseys Bay-type Ni-Cu mineralisation hosted by shallow WSW-plunging concentrically zoned pipe of gabbronorite intrusive of Giles Complex. Inferred resource 446Mt at 0.33%Ni, and 0.35%Cu at 0.2%Ni cutoff.
COMMODITIES: Nickel,  Copper,  Gold,  Silver,  Cobalt,  Palladium,  Platinum

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: narrow horizons of massive titaniferous magnetite rock in host Giles Complex, and persisting for tens of kilometres. Drilling confirmed 1.32m with 32%Fe, 18%TiO2, 0.9%V2O5, 0.6g/tPGE, and 0.21% Cu.
weak Ni-Cu sulphide mineralisation in host pyroxenite of the Michael Hills Intrusion of the Giles Complex.
Ni-Cu-PGE mineralisation in pipe-like body at intrusive boundary of Giles Intrusive Complex with ring Saturn Complex, a feeder pipe to the Giles Complex.

surface linear anomalous PGE geochemistry, with drill testing identifying 3 posibble PGE reefs  in host ultramafic intrusive located in interpreted magmatic flow through zone on the S-faulted margin of the ringed Saturn Complex.

area of ~6km2 of qz veins in host felsic volcanics of the Giles Complex, and carrying copper mineralisation. Drilling identified hydrothermal Cu and deper magmatic (Cu\xe2\x80?Ni\xe2\x80?(Co) sulphide mineralisation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOSTON SHAKER; HAVANA; HAVANA DEEPS; HAVANA SOUTH; SWIZZLER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shear-hosted gold mineralisation with associated biotite-pyrite alteration in host Archean kspar-dominant qz-fx gneiss. Resource 116Mt at 2.06g/t for 7.72Moz contained gold.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BLOCK 14; BRITISH; BROKEN HILL LINE OF LODE; CBH RESOURCES LTD; CENTRAL BLOCK; JUNCTION; KINTORE OPEN CUT; MINERALS MINING AND METALLURGY LD; PROPRIETRY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 9 complexly folded ore lodes over a strike length of 7.3km, with anoverall form of doubly plunging coat hanger. Production from 1885-2013 >260Mt. Total resource of S and N leases 30/6/20212 16Mt at 9.6%Zn, 8.4%Pb, 108g/tAg.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Gahnite,  Garnet,  Magnetite,  Pyrite,  Pyrrhotite,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BROKEN HILL; POTOSI EXTENDED; POTOSI NORTH
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Pb-Zn-Ag ore in host Hores Gneiss on NE extension of the Broken Hill Main Lode. June 2012 remaining resource as published by Perilya Ltd was 1.6Mt at 14%Zn, 3%Pb, and 46g/tAg.

surface deposits of peat on E side of the range from Tantanoola in the south to Robe in the north assessed in 1958. Best quality peat was located between Hatherleigh and Mt. Hope drains N of Rendelsham. Ash content 16-26.8%.

swamp in low lying area investigated in 1958 for its potential as a supply of peat. Spagnum moss peat was reported within 2 only of a number of small bogs, with the spagnum moss confined to a small area.

alteration zone, with rock chip, stream, and soil geochem identifying anomalous gold. Drill tested in 3 holes, with best result from hole HWRC01with elevated gold over 14m interval (max to 0.33ppm 54-56m) in green, altered siltstone.

exploration of the N extension of the Kingston Fault with drilling identifying source of IP chargeability anomaly of pyritic and graphitic msed. Hydrothermal alteration of dolomite identified with formation of sub-economic talc in drill holes.

quartzite of Gilbert Range Quartzite diamond drilled in1960 to identify its suitability for use in road making. Its was found suitable, with probable large resources available, estimated initially at 3.4Mt for 15m depth.

rock chip gold of 0.2ppm from weakly gossanous phyllite of the Undalya Quartzite, with follow up IP and 3 diamond holes. Weak gold to 32ppb in siltstone marginal to qz-fx porphyry intrusion, within weak pyrite alteration contact zone.

Cu-Au mineralisation as copper carbonates in quartz-iron carbonate breccia in host siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation. 4 grab samples in 1986 gave values from 1-11.8%Cu, with 2 values at 0.67g/tAu and 1.15g/tAu.
workings on a steeply dipping NE-trending quartz vein in metasediment of the Enorama Shale, bedding trend EW. Prospecting pits continue along the line of lode for ~800m to the west.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BRENNANS GULLY; FLACKS GULLY; ML 5486; MURPHYS GULLY; SALT CREEK; WAKEFIELDS GULLY
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: alluvial gold was discovered in early 1886 in the main stream channel, and tributaries, which were prospected for a total ~3km length from the junction with the main Salt Creek. No individual production record determined.
shaft adjacent to Triumph Mine, and on the Waukaringa line of lode. No details determined, presumed workings on quartz lode in host Tarcowie Siltstone.

mine near the eastern end of the Waukaringa Line of Lode working Main Reef to >2m width, being auriferous quartz veins at the contact of Cox Sandstone Member with Tapley Hill Formation. No production record determined.
2 underlay shafts on South Reef. South Reef is 60-65cm thick, and contains spotted slate bands in quartz and ironstone. South Reef occurs at a shale-sandstone contact within the Cox Sandstone Member.

shafts on South Reef, prospecting the area between West Alma and Sebastopol. South Reef consisting of quartz and ironstone, minor siltstone in host massive sandstone of the Cox Sandstone Member for little to nil gold recorded.

an adit, 2 underlay shafts, 2 vertical shafts sunk on Waukaringa Main Reef to test the downdip extension. Lode of quartz-iron oxide is from 10-20cm wide, and includes some yellow-brown ochreous claystone.

workings west of Virginia Mine, with history largely unknown. Workings developed on a number of EW-trending quartz reefs. 1986 sample from dumps returned 3.9g/tAu, 5g/tAg, 265ppmCu, 930ppmPb, 1620pmZn, 610ppmAs.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: 2 SHAFT; GREAT BRITAIN GOLD; GREATER BRITAIN; VIRGINIA WELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shaft excavated in 1890 on gold claim 271, with mine reworked again in 1894 by deepening it slightly, and driving east and west on a 20cm wide quartz-iron oxide vein. Now capped with a windmill, and used as a water bore.

quartz-bearing gossan in host metasediment of the Belair subgroup. A small amount of clear quartz with terminations occurred. A nearby pegmatite vein trended 070-080, crosscutting a large glassy blue quartz vein.

wide-spaced group of milky quartz veins, with minor to major pyrite in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. There was some hydraulic brecciation and cavity fill, also some Fe-Mn oxide, and silica cemented breccia.
prospecting pit presumably on quartz veining in host Saddleworth Formation, and identified by Longreach Metals NL in 1971 during reconnaissance mapping. No historical records of mining activity.
roll-front type uranium deposit from which U3O8 is recovered via an in-situ leach process.

prospecting pits presumably on creek alluvium identified by Longreach Metals NL in 1971 during reconnaissance mapping ~1.8km west of the Waukaringa Goldfield. No historical records of mining activity.
prospecting pit identified by Longreach Metals NL in 1971 during reconnaissance mapping in metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DALKEY; MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: no details, part of the Miltaldie - Dalkey group of workings for NS distance of ~4km, and located at the northern end of the line. Workings on vein Cu-?(Pb-Ag-Zn) mineralisation in host metasediment of the Yudnamutana Subgroup.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: no details, part of the Miltaldie - Dalkey group of workings that extend over a NS distance of ~4km, with Dalkey Mine located at the southern end of the line. Vein Cu-?(Pb-Ag-Zn) mineralisation in host Yudnamutana Subgroup.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DALKEY DIGGINGS; MILDALTIE COPPER AND SILVER; MILDALTIE DIGGINGS; RADIUM HILL COPPER
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: no details, part of the Miltaldie - Dalkey group of workings and located ~1km NE of the main shaft (mindep #782). Presumed workings on vein Cu-?(Pb-Ag-Zn) mineralisation in host metasediment of the Yudnamutana Subgroup.
area of  ~30Ha of scrapes developed on modern creek alluvials that were screened for sand and gravel for road fill and road aggregate.

roll front U mineralization in Tertiary sands in area of buried escarpment along Anabama-Redan Fault. U mineralization associated with pyritic clay zone adjacent to Miocene sand section. Best value 0.7m @ 0.073% eU3O8 at 102.2m.

large resource of white kaolinitic clay derived from weathering of underlying Bendigo granite. Testwork on 2 samples indicated variable reflectivity. 1 sample from hole KR23 with 50% halloysite in the 2 micron fraction.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BASIN DAM; GOSSES RIDGE; MOUNT SCRUB; PENNY CREEK
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: anomalous Bleg sample with follow up geochemistry & drilling identifying local areas of altered metasediment, with anomalous Au-As-Sb. Possible potential for Carlin-style ultra-fine gold.
roadside quarry for road metal in fractured, and broken quartzite of the Grampus Quartzite located on the Hallett Thrust Zone.
road ballast quarry used by the local council for suppply of road making material. Mapped as Waukaringa Siltstone on the State MGA100k geology GIS dataset.
roadside quarry used by the local council for road ballast. Mapped as Saddleworth Formation on the State MGA100k geology GIS dataset.
several shallow scrapes to 1.5m deep over <20,000m2 total area. Pits developed on Pleistocene calcrete, with thin overburden of clayey sand, and harder, cacareous soil cap, and worked for road fill.
several shallow roadside council scrapes for total area >6Ha x 1-2m deep on sheet Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
small roadside quarry of <5,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered ABC Range quartzite, and worked for road fill. Likely additional resources confined to ~300m along roadside reserve, and in both directions.

5 shallow scrapes on drift sand over an area of 1.3km x 1.5km, presumably developed by the local council for construction material. Single exploration drill hole for base metals drilled in the area (PWD4) to 54m in 1975.

shallow abandoned council scrape of >4Ha x 1-2m deep on weathered ABC Range quartzite, and worked for road fill. The quarry is located on a low strike ridge of length ~3km, with potential to supply significant additional resources (see mindep #3995).

several shallow scrapes developed on drift sand overlying calcrete over an area ~3.5Ha x 1-2m deep. Potential for additional resources within an area ~1km x 0.8km of low dunes with sparse cover of natural vegetation.
abandoned roadside trench of ~5,700m2 x 1-6m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
shallow abandoned roadside council scrape of ~9,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Mintaro Shale, and worked for road fill.
council scrape of ~6,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council scrape of ~14,000m2 x 1-2m deep on white, weathered to clays metasiltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone, and worked for road fill.

several shallow abandoned scrapes of >15,000m2 total area x 1-2m deep, and adjacent to the Barrier Highway. Worked for road fill on white, clayey, weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation.
roadside council scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on white, weathered to clays metasiltstone of the Pepuarta Tillite, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on white Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.

small sand pit of <1,000m2 x 1-3m deep, located adjacent to Princess Highway, developed on a deposit of red-brown dunal and drift sand with dimensions ~350m long NS x 50m wide, and worked for road fill material.
extended area of up to 9 shallow scrapes for combined area >30,000m2 x 1-2m deep, located west of Princess Highway and north of Gade Road, and developed on Pleistocene calcrete for road fill.

PEPR submitted in June 2014 for a small mining operation to recover walling stone from quartz-muscovite-biotite schist of the Kanmantoo Group. Proposed mine area is 2Ha, with resource estimate of 50 - 100,000 m3 to 8m depth.
PEPR submitted in June 2014 for EML 6435 for crushed sandstone of the Bridgewater Formation for construction material. Resource for 14.53Ha to 4m depth of ~436,000m3.

PEPR a2019693 submitted in June 2014 for EML 6432 to mine Pleistocene calcrete for road making material. Resource estimate for area 121Ha worked to 4m depth was 2-5 Mtonne calcrete/10Ha. Pit to 2016 developed over area ~2Ha x 1-4m deep.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: EML 6420; EML 6425; MASTERS SAND DUNE; WHITELAW ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 leases granted on surficial Quaternary, reddish dune sand deposits of the Fulham Sand. Resource estimate for EML 6425 only for 8Ha area is 90-120,000 tonne.

surface Quaternary red, dunal sand deposit of the Fulham Sand, dimensions ~1.6km long NW by 100m wide by 3m thick. Resource ~500-600,000 tonne based on 3m depth over an area 1km x 200m. Production in 2013 ~40,000 tonne.

gold mineralised quartz vein in host hydrothermally altered basal arkosic sandstone of the Appila Tillite, and underlying Burra Group shale. Zone 4m wide x 40m long, and of unidentified depth extent was identified. Gold grade ~3.5g/tAu.
shallow ~100m2 pit on metasiltstone of the Tarcowie Siltstone developed for the supply of road making material. It is located adjacent to the Terowie - Peterborough sealed road.
shallow council pit 100m NS by 70m EW on metasiltstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone developed for the supply of road making material.
small historic workings on joint-controlled quartz-iron oxide-pyrite veining in brittle fractured quartzite of the basal Appila Tillite. samples returned values from 0.05 - 0.12g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 3 prospecting pits on historic ML 5395 excavated across joint controlled quartz-iron and manganese oxide-pyrite in host metasediment of the basal Appila Tillite. Samples returned values of 0.08 - 0.10g/tAu.
MINEROLOGY_GANGUE: Iron oxide (non specific),  Manganese Oxide,  Quartz

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: magnetic anomalies marginal to proposed buried igneous complex were drill tested for no significant associated geochemistry.
magnetic anomaly on eastern margin of proposed buried igneous complex was drill tested to identify metasomatised carbonate with no associated anomalous geochemistry.
old shaft on shear-hosted copper show in shale of basal Appila Tillite, and tested at depth in single diamond hole for weak mineralisation only.
quartzite of the Cambrian Inman Hill Formation tested and found suitable for use as aggregate for use in dam construction at the proposed Chowilla Dam Site.

unit of quartzite of the Appila Tillite assessed by the Geological Survey in 1952 for supply of construction material for the local council. Plane table survey indicated sufficient volume could be recovered.
abandoned council quarry on slate of the Tarcowie Siltstone. 1952 resource estimate of ~200,000 tonne of poor quality material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AUSTRAL BLACK GRANITE; BLACK HILL GRANITE; IMPERIAL BLACK GRANITE; R.J. TILLETT; ROCKLA
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small abandoned quarry opened in 1962 by R.J. Tillett, and last worked in 1966 for total production of ~1620 tonne.

significant strike length of continuous, drag folded magnesite beds in host Skillogalee Dolomite. Global resource only estimated at 12Mt, no grade estimate. 77 samples from 5 traverses average ~43%MgO.

nodular magnesite associated with dolomite of the River Wakefield Subgroup. Magnesite float assayed 45.2%MgO. Mapping identified conglomeratic magnesite interbedded with dolomite in Wirreanda Dolomite Beds.

magnesite is crystalline, occurring in lenticular masses, with green-grey to brown colour. Host rock is pale grey dolomite of the Balcanoona Formation. Inferred resource was 140,000 tonne per vertical metre at 93.1%MgCO3.

crystalline magnesite in lenticular masses, with green-grey to brown colour. Host rock is pale grey dolomite of the Balcanoona Formation. Inferred resource was 6,000 tonne per vertical metre at 95.1%MgCO3.

crystalline magnesite in lenticular masses, with green-grey to brown colour. Host rock is pale grey dolomite of the Balcanoona Formation. Inferred resource was 30,000 tonne per vertical metre at 94.7%MgCO3.
residual magnesite in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Southern most tenure as MC 15311 of a series of mineral tenements on the upper Skillogalee that worked from 1910s to 1940s.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: G.L. ECKERT; J. BAKER; J.R. ECKERT; MC 16225; MC 16226; MC 16231; MC 16232; MC 16249
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: residual magnesite beds in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Northern most tenure as MC 16226 of a series of mineral tenements on the upper Skillogalee that worked from 1910s to 1940s on pods of magnesite.
residual magnesite beds in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Tenure as MC 16249, no recorded production.
residual magnesite pods in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. One of 3 adjacent tenements granted in the late 1930s, and on the same trend over a strike distance of ~5km.
isolated residual magnesite pods in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Tenure in 1095, and 1936, recorded production 113 tonne.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: F.H. DEGENHARDT; MC 136; MC 137; MC 15642; MC 15827
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: isolated residual magnesite pods in host dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Tenure in 1936 as MC 136, 137, and MC 15827, 15642 for ~282 tonne total production.

abandoned, shallow roadside council scrape of >10,000m2 x 1-2m deep on >150m wide unit of weathered dolomite of the Skillogalee Dolomite, and worked for road fill. The unit can be traced north for >10km.

area of a group of 5 adjacent historic tenements granted on beds of sedimentary magnesite in host Lower Member of the Skillogalee Dolomite, and over an area of ~700m NS x 500m EW. No subsequent production recorded.
small historic roadside quarry on outcropping limestone of the Sellick Hill Formation. Sample site 4 of Bulletin 38, page 17 for 3 channel samples for CaCO3 from 75.1-86%.
deposit of crystalline marble of the Sellick Hill Formation near Second Valley. Resource estimate 2.4Mtonne.

small abandoned quarry on grey-green calc-silicate rock.  Sampled in 1962 as location 2 and location 3 to the north on thin marble, which assayed CaCO3 79.3%, MgCO3 0.82%, SiO2 9.1%, Fe2O3 1.17%, Al2O3 7.25%, and P2O5 0.05%.

roadside council scrape of >1,000m2 x 1-2m deep on limestone of the Cambrian Angaston Limestone, and worked for road fill. Sampled as location 7, figure 12 in Bulletin 38 for assay of CaCO3 87.5%, MgCO3 6.3%, SiO2 3.2%, Al2O3 0.4%.

small quarry developed on white clay deposit developed on deeply weathered host schist and gneiss of the Barossa Complex. Worked 2 contorted zones of kaolin-mica to 4m thick in host folded biotite schist.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Clay mineral,  Feldspar,  Kaolinite,  Mica,  Rutile,  Sillimanite

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOOLEROO SCHOOL BUS ROUTE; DISTRICT COUNCIL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: abandoned roadside council pit of >10,000m2 x 1-3m deep on deeply weathered to white clay metasediment of the Cradock Quartzite Member of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~4Ha x 1-2m deep on deeply weathered to white clay metasediment of the Cradock Quartzite Member of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for supply of road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; ROSS MCCALLUMS ROAD; SITE 8
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: small roadside quarry on deeply weathered to white clay Tertiary, silcreted sandstone, presumably a local council pit for supply of road making material.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BOOLEROO SCHOOL BUS ROUTE; DISTRICT COUNCIL; STONE RESERVE 1
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 2 adjacent abandoned roadside council pits of total area >15,000m2 x 1-3m deep on deeply weathered to white clay metasediment of the Cradock Quartzite Member of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
small roadside council pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-3m deep on deeply weathered to white clay metasediment of the Appila Tillite, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council pit of ~5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on deeply weathered to white clay metasediment of the Cradock Quartzite Member of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.

no details located from mine tenement map for Hundred Willowie, tenure GL 1914, presumably over quartz veining in host metasediment of the Appila Tillite. The claim is located near the nose of an S-plunging anticline.
workings located on ironstone on flat-lying Cambrian rock. Worked for flux, and sent to Port Pirie. The ironstone was associated with phosphate-rich rock.
abandoned council pit of ~7,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white, deeply weathered, clayey sandstone of the ABC Range Quartzite, and worked for road fill.
abandoned council scrape of ~7,000m2 x 1m deep on Pleistocene calcrete for supply of road fill material.

shaft on secondary Cu mineralisation with no depth extent. Mineralisation associated with top Benbournie Dolomite. Auger drilling of 19 holes for best value 305ppmCu, though consistently high values of >100ppmCu were obtained.

workings on secondary Cu mineralisation with no depth extent. Mineralisation associated with Skillogalee Dolomite. Auger drilling of 19 holes for best value 305ppmCu, though consistently high values of >100ppmCu were obtained.

yellow-brown limestone of Callanna group investigated for railway ballast. Drilling confirmed unsuitable for use as railway ballast. Resource estimate was >>75,000m3 (or 170,000 tonne for density 2.7).
historic shafts on surface show of copper mineralisation located on NE-trending shear in host Tapley Hill Formation.
abandoned roadside council trench of ~1,700m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered, thin bedded blue-grey slate of the River Broughton Beds, and worked for road fill.

small quarry of ~1,500m2 x 1-2m deep on blue-grey, thin bedded dolomite used for road making material, with the dolomite unit traceable south for several km. Dolomite unit is flanked by 2 quartzite units.
abandoned council pit of ~2,500m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, grey pyritic slate of the Tindelpina Shale Member, and worked for road fill.
long abandoned council pit on Tertiary sand and gravel occupying a rise overlooking Spalding. It contains some objectionable ferruginous, strongly silicified bands with a low dip evident.
long abandoned council pit of <1,00m2 x 1-2m deep on Tertiary sand and gravel and used for supply of road fill.
12m thick quartzite of the lower Gilbert Range Quartzite. Resource estimate to 20m depth was 46,000m3 or 125,000 tonne (density 2.7).

2 narrow, steeply dipping quartzite beds of the Belair Subgroup investigated by the Geological Survey in 1959 for supply of material for road making. The requirement was for ~125,000 tonne (46,000m3).
red and yellow alluvial clay exposed during excavation for a dam were tested and found to be suitable for use in brickmaking. The clay is probable deeply weathered slate of the Saddleworth Formation.

shallow scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1m deep on weathered metasediment of the Appila Tillite for road fill. Area to N was inspected by the Geological Survey in 1962 for supply of minimum 54,000m3 of material for road fill.
sand and gravel has been mined from an active creek bed over a distance of ~1.7km. Additional resources are apparent for up to 6km downstream from the old workings.

quarry on quartzite of the Grampus Quartzite, being pale pink to brown quartzite to 30m wide. Testwork on 2 samples of diamond core gave LAA and plasticity index figures higher than normally required. Resource ~150,000m3 or 400,000t
quartzite/sandstone unit exposed in railway cutting, and at the crest of Dowds Hill potentially OK for use as railway ballast.
40m high of blue-grey quartz biotite schist to schistose metasiltstone of the Woolshed Flat Shale considered for use as road aggregate. Historic adit of 55m length for gold and base metals.
2 quarries on developed on deeply weathered shale and slate of the Tapley Hill Formation. Clays vary from white to brown, yellow, red, purple.
near horizontal Upper Eocene sediment comprising Blanche Point Marl, Tortachilla Limestone for >382,000m3 of clay with >50% montmorillinite.
roadside pit in shale of the Tapley Hill Formation, presumably developed as a local source of road making material. Tenure granted to Hawker Earthmovers PL in 2005, subsequently cancelled in 2009.
2 barite veins as fracture fill, and traversing a dolomite ridge of the Wywyana Formation, and which is part of the Patawarta Diapir. Inferred resource to 5m of 1100 tonne oil drilling grade.
abandoned scrape of ~7,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Waukaringa Siltstone, and developed by Transport SA for source of road making material.
anomalous Uranium mineralisation over 12 km across widths up to 4 km returned a number of significant drill sample results, including.65m at 137ppm eU3O8.
roadside council pit of ~8,000m2 x 1-3m deep on white, clayey, weathered sandstone of the Parachilna Formation, and worked for supply of road fill.

sampling identified 4 values >1%P in host limonitic siltstone and sandstone of the Parachilna Formation. Individual phosphatic bands to 5-10cm in width. Beds traced for~460m.Values probably represented secondary enrichment.
weak indicationns of phosphate-bearing metasediment of the Parachilna Formation. Follow up investigation confirmed phosphate as collophane encrustations on fracture surfaces.
resource of >153,000m3 (0r 380,000 tonne for SG 2.5), of sandy red-brown clay suitable for use in the manufacture of interior bricks.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: GOLDEN BELT; GOMERSAL COPPER; LEE, HUSSEY AND COTTRELL
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: 15m deep open cut on copper carbonate mineralisation in shear in host sediment of the Saddleworth Formation. Production 2,032 tonne @ 3.8%Cu, & 12,000t talcose clay suitable for brickmaking. Untested below oxidation zone.

drilling identified 8m of quartzitic sandstone with only minor clay content of the Bunkers Sandstone. The material though probably suitable for use as rail ballast lacked sufficient resource size to provide the quantities required.
shallow council open cut of ~10,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone, and worked for road fill.
quartzite/sandstone of the Waukaringa Siltstone assessed in 1954 for resource estimate for a 365m long quarry to plain level of176,000m3 or 460,000 tonne for SG 2.6.
para-amphibolite, and banded gneiss of the Willyama Complex worked for road making material.

Recent sand dunes and outwash clays and gravel with trace bands of heavy minerals occur on the beach as a result of storm action, and also as rare grains in sand dunes. Dominant heavy mineral was ilmenite.

2-3m wide zinc sulphide lode with a quartz-calcite gangue in host brecciaed tillite of the Sturt Tillite. 2 drillholes which confirmed continuity of mineralisation at depth, being dominantly sphalerite, pyrite, covellite, with only rare chalcopyrite.
thin lime sand spreads and low dunes of lime sand in the Perlubie beach area ~17 km north from Streaky Bay. A sample had an insolubles content of 13%.

large area of thin, surficial spread of close-to-shore, unconsolidated calcareous sand dunes rising to 30m in height, and located at Fowler Bay. 3 lines of samples across the deposit returned values of 47% caO, 3.5% MgO, 6.5 - 7.5% SiO2, and 0.36% SO3.
pit of ~5,500m2 x 1-3m deep on white, kaolinitic, weathered metasediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup, and worked for road fill.

small occurrence of Ordovician porphyritic granite, deeply weathered, showing only 1-2m above the general land surface. Investigated by the Geological Survey in 1955 as a possible source of road making material.

considerable resources of massive, relatively unjointed Ordovician, variably porphyritic biotite-hornblende granite over an area of 50km2. Probable suitability for source of road metal, potential for dimension stone.

deeply weathered fine grained sandstone of the Tapanappa Formation suitable for use as road base material, but not for use as road aggregate. Resource ~85,000 m3 to 10m depth (or 200,000 tonne for SG 2.5).

2 shallow excavations on a low ridge of metasediment of the Appila Tillite just south of Peterborough. Southern pit is ~600m due north and along strike from the southern pit. No history of activities has been determined.
narrow trench developed on metasediment of the Appila Tillite for a local supply of building stone, and by the local council for construction materials.
recent stream channel load of gravel worked by the old Highways Department for railway works including ballast. Gravel is dominantly quartzite eroded from the Flinders Range to the east.

outcrop of a hard band of calc-silicate rock assessed in 1951 foruse for road making. Resource ~26,000 m3 of hard material, and >50,000 m3 of softer material. Petrology confirmed a para-amphibolite to calc-silicate rock.

following a request to visit a site the Geological Survey confirmed very faint bluish tinge on kunkar due to the presence of copper carbonate. The kunkar was exposed over an area 60m x 15m. basement rock is of the Rhynie Sandstone.

native sulphur occuring as nodules enclosed in gypsum in a narrow clay bed of Sub-recent age. It is believed to have formed by bacterial decomposition of organic remains. Not considered to be of economic interest.
bed of marble of the Katunga Dolomite up to 60m wide, and extending for at least 800m to several km. Potential for large resources to >500,000 m3 or >1 Mtonne.
quartzite of the Warrow Quartzite investigated for road making material. Resource estimate >1 Mtonne). Drilling was recommended, but not carried out.
contorted metasediment intruded by quartz veins and granite assessed for its potential as dimension stone.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: MURRAY BRIDGE FREESTONE; MURRAY BRIDGE LIMESTONE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shallow quarry in Tertiary Mannum Limestone and worked for dimension stone. The rock is marketed as Murray Bridge Freestone.

limestone of the Tertiary Mannum Limeston for road base material, and as a supply of building stone of rock equivalent to that marketed as Murray Bridge Freestone. The exposure is for ~1.5 km along the east cliffs of the Murray River.

limestone of the Tertiary Mannum Limestone for use as road base material, and as a supply of building stone of rock equivalent to that marketed as Murray Bridge Freestone. Rehabilitated and now an industrial site.

historic quarry on weathered arkosic sandstone of the ABC Range Quartzite. Resource estimate was >150,000 tonne for a mine developed to 20m depth. The stone appeared to be of good quality, with little banding.

Hiltaba Suite granite assessed by the Geological Survey for its suitability as a source of dimension stone. Sample DS 56 is described as a red coarse-grained granite, with minor pyrite. Drilling is recommended to test the colour with depth.

2 domed outcrops of Carappee Granite as grey to ?pink, foliated, coarse-grained porphyritic granite. The stone is a relatively attractive grey, tabular coarse-grained granite which may have local potential as dimension stone.

outcrop of Minbrie Gneiss assessed for dimension stone. Rock is a pink to grey, banded, foliated, medium-coarse grained, foliated granite gneiss for small blocks for niche markets. Requires mapping, drilling and test block sampling.
large mass of relatively homogeneous granite assessed for dimension stone. It is a pink-red, coarse-grained granite, with potential dowgraded due to its distance from infrastructure.

Hiltaba granite outcrop assessed by the Geological Survey in 2001 for dimension stone. It is a pink to pale red, coarse-grained granite, with outcrop near road relatively joint free, possibly OK to be quarried.

3 large granite domes of an inhomogenous, grey, banded, megacrystic augen gneiss which may be suitable as a banded granite product. The area contains numerous outcrops of Minbrie Gneiss which warrant further investigation.

mine developed on barite lode as shear infill. Lode with dimensions ~110m long NE by 4m wide for recovery of ~3,000 tonne oil drilling grade. Remaining resource ~2,000 tonne. Host Tapley Hill Formation.

council pit of ~6,000m2 x 1-5m deep on white, kaolinised metasiltstone of the Emeroo Subgroup for use as road fill. The sequence includes thin interbeds of shale, siltstone and sandstone, low dip to W.
shallow quarry on metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation presumably developed by the local council for road making material.
council borrow pit of >7,000m2 x 1-2m deep on white, deeply weathered metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.

mag anomaly adj to diorite tested in diamond hole. Penetrated metasediment of Willyama Complex with  laminated ccp & magnetite replacement bands. Best value 10.9m @ 0.84%Cu, 0.64g/tAu, 5.4g/tAg, 493ppmMo, 186ppmU from 209.5m.
COMMODITIES: Copper,  Graphite,  Gold,  Molybdenum,  Silver,  Uranium,  Vanadium

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: soil geochemical portable XRF Cu anomaly not yet drill tested at depth. Historic drilling of upper saprolite only gave best value 4m @ 0.12%Cu, with 15 holes assaying >500ppmCu.

silver-in-soil geochemical anomaly with dimensions ~500m x 250m tested by shallow RC percussion drilling to identify sequence of Proterozoic metasediment, with epithermal quartz veining. Anomalous Pb & Zn in hole UMAC009.
silver-in-soil geochemical anomaly drill tested to identify altered GRV volcanics and breccias. Best value 18m @ 1.22%Pb from 42m in hole PPRC258.

copper-in-soil geochemical anomaly drill tested to identify widespread epithermal-style Pb-Zn-Ag mineralisation related to GRV volcanism. Best assay is from hole PPRC278, 3m @ 0.52%Pb, from 51m.Also significant graphitic schist.

magnetic, gravity, and silver-in-soil geochemical anomaly NW of Paris Silver Deposit. Drill tested to identify Ag-Pb mineralisation in GRV volcanic breccias. Best value hole PPRC285, 42m @ 0.46%Pb from 21m.

weathered shale of Saddleworth Formation mined from 1952 to supply material for brickmaking to Burnside Brickworks (see mindep #3294). The rock was hand quarried, and transported several km by truck to the brickworks on Wyatt Road.
long abandoned council roadside pit of <1,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered schist and gneiss of the Backstairs Passage Formation for supply of road fill.

site investigated for railway ballast. 1 diamond hole for 27.6m of very hard Barunga Sandstone with 14% clay material in thin beds of mudstone. The clay content was considered too high and the site was abandoned.

quartz reef exposed on a low ridge 2.5 km west of Yallunda Flat. Investigated by the Geological Survey to identify resource >30,500m3 or >70,000 tonne for SG 2.2, enough to supply the required amount.

weathered sandstone investigated for use as silica sand for glass making. Also cross-cutting white kaolinised qz-feldspar dyke for use as ceramic clay. Testwork indicated viable grade of both sandstone and clay.

white talcose clay as weathered Skillogalee Dolomite, and exposed in a railway cutting with testwork confirming suitability for use in ceramics manufacture. Field inspection revealed limited resource size.
dolomite outcrop of the Skillogalee Dolomite on the S side of Pine Creek ofor ~55,000 m3 or 140,000 tonne of quality suitable for use as bitumen screenings.
dolomite unit of the Ketchowla Siltstone investigated for use as road aggregate. Testwork on 1 sample identified OK for that use. Resource estimated at >46,000m3 (or 115,000 tonne for SG 2.5).

location of material suitable for road making. Subsequently opened by the local council. Kunkar outcrop over several acres N of and near Orrorro, with probable further resources available in neighbouring paddocks.
pit developed by the local council on outcrop of siltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation striking NS, and showing well developed bedding plane parting and cross jointing.
2 shallow scrapes developed by the local council on outcrop of weathered, laminated siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation striking NS.
council scrape of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered, soft grey and brown siltstone of the Auburn Dolomite, and worked for road fill.
small roadside council pit of ~1,500m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill. Possibly site 6 as identified by Geological Survey in 1962.

60cm layer of calcrete developed on brown, weathered slate to tillite of the Appila Tillite. Identified by the Geological Survey in 1962 as suitable for road fill. Now site of an abandoned shallow council scrape of ~3,000m2 x 1-2m deep.
site investigated by the Geological Survey in 1962 for material for road making. now site of abandoned council pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered metasediment of the Appila Tillite.
council pit of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on narrow unit of deeply weathered, white, kaolinitic sandstone of the Undalya Quartzite, trend NS, and worked for road fill.
narrow unit of weathered metasiltstone of the Tapley Hill Formation investigated by the Geological Survey in 1962 for use as road fill. Small council pit developed, now abandoned.

dolomite inlier in host diapiric Callanna Group brown, phyllitic slate investigated by the Geological Survey in 1962 for use as road fill. Small council pit of ,1,000m2 x 1-2m deep developed,  now abandoned.
outcrop of brown, weathered slate of the Tapley Hill Formation investigated by the Geological Survey in 1962 for use as road fill. Small council pit of ~2,500m2 x 1-3m deep developed, now abandoned.
abandoned hillside council scrapes of ~5,000m2 x 1-2m deep located adjacent to Jamestown-Hallett sealed road on weathered metasediment of the Tapley Hill Formation, and worked for road fill.
roadside council pit of ~13,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, blue dolomite of the Auburn Dolomite, and worked for road fill. Investigated by the Geological Survey in 1962.
area of red-brown Holocene sand spread, with historic, and current workings located over a surface area of ~50Ha, and to depths variable from 1-3m.
Recent red-brown sand spread, one of 3 areas of similar material on Section 25, Hundred Morgan. No records of tenure, presumably worked by the local council for construction material.

narrow quartzite of the Mintaro Shale worked for supply of road base material. Several tonne quartz crystal recovered from seams containing many well formed crystals. Crystals were considered unsuitable for piezo-electric purposes.

small, historic quarry of >1,000m2 x 2-5m deep on a narrow unit of quartzite of the Mintaro Shale, possibly worked for building stone for local use. The same unit is exposed in a deep cutting on the Sturt Highway some 300m to the north.
historic roadside quarry next to the Sturt Highway, and developed by the local council on a narrow quartzite unit of the Undalya Quartzite, presumably for road making material.

abandoned historic quarry of ~450m2 x 1-5m deep on slaty tillite of the Wilyerpa Formation and worked for building stone. Maximum quartzite outcrop not of sufficient size to supply the required volume of 40,000m3.

quarry on weathered, hard, green shale and siltstone of the Appila Tillite,  trend NNE, with steep W dip. Reported as providing good road making material. Prominent qtze ridge to west estimated 500,000 - 1Mtonne material on Section 614.
shallow roadside council pit of ~8,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered, white, clayey metasiltstone of the Ulupa Siltstone, and worked for road fill.

hill of white to grey fine grained dolomitic marble, with grey to green bands. 4 samples taken along a line to the east of centre of the body showed relatively low content of acid insoluble mineral, with average value being 5%.
abandoned council roadside pit of >4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete for use as road fill.
abandoned roadside council pit of ~9,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.

shallow pit on weathered, silty schist of the River wakefield Formation. Material ripped to ~2m depth, with a thin layer of kunkar overlying. Quality of material is fair due to its platy nature. Considerable oversize boulders were produced.
2 small abandoned quarries on coarsely crystalline marble, possibly those referred to in report book RB 49/00188 as operated by Mr R.G. Howard for use in the monumental trade.

substantial resource of blue dolomite of the Castambul and Montacute Dolomite, and quartzites of the Woolshed Flat Shale. Calculated resource 6.3 million m3 of dolomite, and 1.4 million m3 of quartzite to RL 260m.
Tertiary coarse sand to grits with up to 6m of unconsolidated sand. Testwork indicated suitable for use as concrete sand.

outcrop of Symons Granite assessed as dimension stone. Rock is an attractive porphyritic granite with blue quartz crystals and suitable for a range of uses from building stone to kitchen and bathroom benches.
group of 3 shallow borrow pits north of Whyte Yarcowie, and developed for local road making on siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation.
abandoned shallow roadside borrow pit of ~3,000m2 x 1-4m deep on weathered Ulupa Siltstone, and worked for road fill.

borrow pit in Terowie, and developed for local road making on siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation. Rocks described as grey-green siltstone, and pale yellow-buff laminated siltstone, with kink folding.
shallow roadside borrow pit of ~5,000m2 x 1-2m deep on weathered iron oxide stained metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation, and worked for road fill.
shallow shaft developed on flaser bedded Tarcowie Siltstone.
2 shallow pits developed on quartz vein in host flaser bedded fine sandy Tarcowie Siltstone.

stratabound mineralisation in host metasediment of the Willyama Complex. Upper suite of Zn>Pb in ""reduced' sequence (Broken Hill Group, Lower suite of Cu-Au in Thackaringa strata (Kalkaroo deposit equivalent?). No orebodies identified.
Skarn W-Zn deposit in Willyama Complex metasediment, possibly remobilised SEDEX deposit.

stratabound calc-silicate of the Parnell Formation, Broken Hill Group, Willyama Complex, hosting scheelite mineralisation. Scheelite commonly associated with grossularite garnet in calc-silicate, in pods 2-50m long by 0.3 - 2m wide.
scattered scheelite grains in calc-silicate host of the Parnell Formation, Broken Hill Group, Willyama Complex. Described as belonging to the Corruga-type tungsten and base metal deposits.

Cu-Au -Fe mineralisation occurs in a 4km long, NE-trending zone, within which are 3 steeply dipping anastomosing lodes. Origin as possible infill of retrograde shear, with mineralisation style comparable to IOCG family.
MINEROLOGY_ORE: Azurite,  Chalcopyrite,  Chrysocolla,  Malachite,  Sphalerite,  Valleriite

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: ore zones of mineralised shears in NE-trending unit of quartz-sulphide rock that can be traced for several km. Drill tested in the early 1970s by CRA Exploration for disappointing results.

stratiform BIF trending NE for >750m, deformed and metamorphosed to produce a massive to banded magnetite-quartz rock historically mined for flux. Drill tested at depth to identify massive pyrite and pyrrhotite, with elevated Cu, Zn, Pb.

qz-py horizon trend 060. Py, ccp, sphal intersected at depth. Host rock is phyllitic chlorite schist of the Willyama Complex. Drilling in the 1970s found up to 3g/tAu in surface samples, and 4m at 16g/tAu in a RAB hole at SW end.
shallow quarry developed by the local council for road making material on weathered, feldspathic sandstone of the Rhynie Sandstone. E boundary is sharp over fine grained sandstone and siltstone.

small ~5,000m2 x 1-3m deep council borrow pit developed on surface Pleistocene calcrete layer to 1m thick over weathered basement of interbedded sandstone, arkose, and phyllite of the Skillogalee Formation.
area of small shallow, abandoned borrow pits developed on ferruginous weathered, quartzite, mottled yellow-brown to brown, with dip to SE. Staratigraphic unit is ABC Range Quartzite.
quarry on quartzite of the ABC Quartzite exposed in north side creek bank for road making material. Second quarry ~1.1 km to the west, with mudstone and siltstone interbeds.

2 abandoned council borrow pits on sandstone of the Leasingham Quartzite Member, and worked for road making material. Southern pit is narrow 60m long NS by 10m wide, with second pit 90m to the north ~30m square.
council roadside pit of ~5,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered, grey-green siltstone of the Appila Tillite. The rock has wavy laminations, with cross bed truncations.

roadside council borrow pit of ~4,000m2 x 1-2m deep on thin layer of Pleistocene calcrete overlying deeply weathered to clays diamictite of the Appila Tillite, The rock shows liesegang ring weathering.
quarryon sandstone of the ABC Range Quartzite, and used for road base material. Rock is fine to medium grained sandstone.
vertical shaft several 10s metres deep on ironstone breccia in host Skillogalee Dolomite. identified during regional mapping, no information on history.

Cu-Ni-PGE mineralisation in steeply dipping altered gabbro, intruding contact zone of Mela Diorite intrusive, and an amphibolite metabasalt of the Giles Complex. Hole CZC0118 penetrated 148m at 0.94%Cu, 0.09%Ni, and 0.24g/tPGE.
shallow roadside borrow pit of ~6,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Mintaro Shale, and worked for road fill.

shallow council roadside pit with area ~25,000m2 x 1-2m deep developed on surface layer of Pleitocene Ripon calcrete. The quarry is developed on a low  EW-trending ridge that extends from near the Murray River then east for ~25km..
area of several abandoned, shallow council roadside pits within 700m distance, and with cumulative aea of ~4Ha x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene sheet calcrete, and worked for road fill.

fine to coarse Holocene sand ridge within the River Murray Valley, with dimensions 350m long by 50m wide, and up to 8m high worked for building/concrete sand. Located within the Morgan Conservation Park, with mine now rehabilitated.
lenticular bed of coarse sand to 2.5m thick of the Loxton Sand. Used in construction of channels within the Cadell Irrigation Area. Small quantities were also utilized by the local council.
2 adjacent, shallow pits of ~2.5Ha total area x 1-3m deep,located SE of Wangary and south of the Flinders Highway, developed on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation for road fill.
small, abandoned council borrow pit of ~600m2 x 1-3m deep on deeply weathered granite of the Donington Suite, and worked for road fill.

Quaternary high silica sand. Samples and testwork identified clean, well graded, high silica sand, only known deposit in SA in the 40-50 AFS size range. Not suitable for petroleum fracturing or propping sand. 1983 resource ~2.2Mtonne.
numerous steeply dipping white quartz veins cross cutting quartzite and shale of the Pualco Tillite, and mined for exposed aggregate. Production ceased in 1975.
widespread silcrete preserved as plateau in the neighborhood of Allandale Homestead. Resource estimate >>200,000 tonne. Selected samples of silcrete proved suitable for refractory silica bricks.
widespread silcrete preserved as plateau SE of Mount Harvey. Resource estimate ~170,000 tonne. Not sampled, but grade probably same as that of Allandale deposit.
few small pits excavated on subdued outcrop of Kanmantoo Group quartz rich schist, with quartzite beds to 40cm wide, and over an area 150m x 100m. Possibly suitable for road making material.
roadside council borrow pit of ~15,000m2 x 1-2m deep on Pleistocene calcrete, and worked for road fill.
large resource of quartz rich biotite schist of the Backstairs Passage Formation. The material is closely jointed, and similar to material in the Victor Harbor quarry.
weathered biotite schist of the Balquhidder Formation worked from an old roadside. Further resource could be recovered by extending the old pit to the NE along strike into section 188.
old workings on 1m thick quartzite and schist scree on the lower slopes of Peeralilla Hill. Most of the rubble has maximum dimension of <25cm, and contains some clayey sand.
lateritised Permian sandy clay to pebbly sand on decomposed Kanmantoo greenschist. Suitable for road making if thoroughly mixed during extraction. A trial pit was recommended.
large shallow pit developed by the local council on white ?calcrete or deeply weathered metasediment of the Emeroo Subgroup for road making material.
shallow pit developed on a NW-trending longitudinal sand dune ~700m long by 50m wide.

coincident gravity and intense magnetic terrain drilled to identify vein and breccias-hosted weak Cu-(Au-Mo) mineralization in variably altered metasediment of the Wandearah Metasediment. Cover of 60-160m of Tertiary sediment.
presence of an iron ore quarry was recorded on section 409, Hundred Clinton in the early 1900s by the Inspector of Mines. It had been worked to supply flux for smelting copper ores.
abandoned roadside borrow pit of >1,000m2 x 1-10m deep on weathered metasediment of the Anama Siltstone Member of the Rhynie Sandstone, and worked for road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: DISTRICT COUNCIL; FRESHWATER CREEK NORTH ROAD
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shallow roadside pit of ~4,000m2 x 1-3m deep on weathered metasediment of the Gumbowie Arkose, and worked for road fill.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: BURRA MANGANESE AND SILVER MINING CO.; IRON MINE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: shaft developed in ~1888 on a pod of manganiferous ironstone, with reported production of 1,000s tonne of manganiferous ore for use as flux.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMALGAMATED ASBESTOS INDUSTRIES NL; ML 2762; RUEDIGERS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: satellite deposit of the Ruedigers Asbestos mine (mindep # 4016). Production ~150 tonne asbestos in 1942. Host was altered limestone of the Lower Skillogalee Dolomite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMALGAMATED ASBESTOS INDUSTRIES NL; ML 2759; RUEDIGERS
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: satellite deposit of the Ruedigers Asbestos mine (mindep # 4016). Production ~3 tonne asbestos in 1942. Host was altered limestone of the Lower Skillogalee Dolomite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMALGAMATED ASBESTOS INDUSTRIES NL; ML 2759; RUEDIGERS; VALLEY HOLE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: satellite deposit of the Ruedigers Asbestos mine (mindep # 4016). Production ~58 tonne asbestos in 1942. Host was altered limestone of the Lower Skillogalee Dolomite.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: AMALGAMATED ASBESTOS INDUSTRIES NL; ML 2755; RUEDIGERS; STRONG FIBRE
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: satellite deposit of the Ruedigers Asbestos mine (mindep # 4016). Production ~2.5 tonne asbestos in 1942. Host was altered limestone of the Lower Skillogalee Dolomite.
roadside council quarry of ~10,000m2 x 1-8m deep on weathered metasiltstone of the Mintaro Shale, and worked for road fill.

historic quarry of <250m2 x 1-8m deep on narrow sandstone unit of the Leasingham Quartzite Member of the Mintaro Shale, probably worked for building stone.

palaeochannel uranium for 23m of radiometrically anomalous sand and clay in drill hole 07RMCD002, 2.5m at 108 eppm U3O8 in sand and clay interbeds in hole 07RMCD009. Drilling identified a cell of U3O8 mineralisation beneath silcrete layer.
drill testing of gossanous iron formation failed to identify any base metal values of interest. Graphitic schist gave C values >1%.
single diamond hole drilled for the Highway Department in 1954 to test a portion of a narrow strike ridge of outcropping ferruginous quartzite of the Middleback Formation for use as road aggregate.
historic abandoned quarry of 100m2 x 2-5m deep on slaty siltstone of the Saddleworth Formation, and presumably worked for building stone for local use.
anomalous gold to 53ppb in drill hole CAR084, with follow up grid calcrete sampling confirming a coherent gold-in-calcrete anomaly.
Co-Au prospect in NSW of similar origins to the Mutooroo Cu-Co-S deposit in SA. Recent drilling by Alloy Resources returned a best intercept of 23m at 0.14%Co, 0.4g/tAu from hole DDHOT1 from 41-64m.
Co-Py mineralisation in host quartz-albite gneiss of the Willyama Complex. Inferred + Indicated resource 54.9Mtonne at 910ppm Co (cutoff 800ppm), and 17.92% Py.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: aircore drill traverse by Investigator Resources on soil geochemical anomaly identified narrow 3m intervals of low-level Ag anomalism. Also graphitic schist with TGC values variable from 6-10%TGC.

soil silver geochemical anomaly identified in 2015, and drill tested in shallow aircore holes. Samples returned low level anomalous values for Ag-Cu-Pb at shallow depth, Best value 15m at 6.6g/tAg, 0.17%Cu, and 0.11%Pb from 55m in CDAC030.

DEPOSIT_SYNONYMS: CLAY AND MINERAL SALES PTY LTD; EML 6474; MC 4408
DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: deposit of WNW trending Holocene clean, dunal sand to 1-3m above surrounding plain. Dune dimensions ~550m long x 75m wide x 2m deep, and underlain by sheet calcrete over older aeolian sand. Resource estimate using SG 1.8 of 110,000 tonne.

WNW-trending Holocene dunal sand to 1-2m deep x 1,125m long x ~80m wide for estimated resource 250,000 tonne for SG 1.8. Dunal sand is undelain by sheet Pleistocene calcrete overlying older Tertiary sand.
weak copper mineralisation associated with late stage qz-carb to qz-epidote veining in host Palaeoproterozoic rocks. Best values 1m at 0.18%Cu in hole SHDH009.
exploration of Frome Embayment for roll-front U. Best value hole EAR19, 1.48%U in 30cm sample of core of white clay, with unidentified dark brown, carbonaceous mineral.

nodules of celestite associated with coarse xtalline gypsum near top of a Quaternary lacustrine gypsiferous clay. Chemical composition of hand selected nodules was in the range 90-92% SrSO4, and 1%BaSO4.

nodules of celestite associated with coarse xtalline gypsum near top of a Quaternary lacustrine gypsiferous clay. Chemical composition of hand selected nodules was in the range 90-92% SrSO4, and 1%BaSO4.

bullseye magnetic anomaly drilled to identify Proterozoic altered volcanic breccia beneath cover of 307m of  younger sediment. Py>ccp was present throughout the breccia, interpreted as volcanic vent complex. Ave value for 192m at 665ppmCu.

rock chip sample from quartz veins marginal to a dolerite dyke returned a value of 0.5g/tAu. Subsequently drill tested for best values in hole MOORC012, 3m at 0.13%Cu, 0.5ppmAg, low gold values. Drilling confirmed weak copper mineralisation marginal to the dolerite dyke.

area of several council rubble pits on Pleistocene calcrete for road fill. In 2013 Murray Zircon completed several holes along the main road during exploration for heavy mineral sands. Hole MZX2260 identified 1m of bentonite clay from 26-27m depth.
skyTEM conductivity anomaly drill tested for source identified as pyrrhotite-dominant breccias marginal to a narrow gabbroic intrusive.

reconnaissance check in 2014 by Crossland Strategic Metals of original elevated REE values from silty sand of Warburton River System in NGSA survey confirmed enrichment of HM including HM with elevated REE values.
follow up drilling in 2008 of gamma ray anomaly in hole Moorari 2 failed to identify anomalous radioactivity in drill samples.

drill testing of previously recognised gamma log anomalies from oil and gas exploration drilling confirmed anomalous gamma log values to 100cps in carbonaceous clay underlying thick, oxidised basal sand of the Eyre Formation.

AEM survey with follow up grid aircore drill holes over a wide area for best value in hole CUN034, 2,5m at 43.4ppm eU3O8 in host sand of the lower Eyre Formation, and where it is overlain by a lignitic unit.
outcrop of coarsely crystalline marble of the Balcanoona Formation investigated for its potential as dimension stone.
several drill hole intersections of Tertiary lignite, with best intersection in hole FN030, 21m from 36-77m.
aircore drill traverses for HM sand exploration revealed widespread low-grade HM content.
drillhole SE 396 penetrated  6.4m of lignite from 110.3m. In 2009 Iluka Resources indicated potential to extend sub basin to SW and west.
historic pits on surface copper mineralisation. Tested in 2 percussion holes in 1969 for no apparent depth extent. geochemical soil sampling program by Panda Mining Ltd in 2009.
historic prospecting of a gossanous shear ENE from the Baratta line of lode.

skyTEM conductivity anomaly drill tested to penetrate interval of ~5m of 10-30cm bands of massive pyrrhotite>pyrite, trace only chalcopyrite in host gabbronorite and pyroxenite of the Giles Complex. Best copper value 2,500ppmCu.
sample of black mineral from Mesoproterozoic pegmatite intruding calc-silicate/marble of the Birksgate Complex returned values for total REE of 9%. Confirmed by Musgrave Minerals in 2009.

small hill with single NS-trending 10-20cm wide quartz vein with malachite that cross cuts an EW-trending quartz-epidote vein, both in host mafic rock of the Giles Complex. Revisited by Musgrave Minerals Ltd in 2010.
abandoned council pit of ~3.5Ha x 1-2m deep on low rise of Pleistocene sheet calcrete, and worked for road base material.
drill testing of gravity anomaly in area of burued granite (180m cover), confirmed alaskite affinities, with best value 3m at150ppmU from 168m in hole COD008.
roll-front, and silcrete-hosted U mineralisation in local shallow basin of Eyre Formation. Resource estimate 82 tonne contained eU3O8 at grade >100ppm eU3O8.
roll-front, and silcrete-hosted U mineralisation in local shallow basin of Eyre Formation. Resource estimate 268.5 tonne contained eU3O8 at grade >100ppm eU3O8.

exploration for roll front uranium by Adavale Minerals PL from 2007-2013 included ground geophysics, mapping, geochemical sampling, and follow up drilling. At Mumpie elevated levels of U were encountered in weathered lutites
SW appendage of U mineralisation to the larger Jubilee U resource. U mainly confined to scarp-bound silcrete.
possible volcanic centre with sulphide-bearing exhalites, and weak sulphide mineralisation.
abandoned council pit of ~2Ha x 1-3m deep on Holocene dunal, pale red-brown aeolian sand of the Moornaba Sand, and presumably worked by the local council for road making material.

exploration of palaeochannel sand in Algebuckina Sandstone. Rotary mud drilling of RepTEM and microgravity anomalies returned best value of 295cps (hole APRM201) from gamma logs, with follow up geochemistry failing to confirm anomalous U.

mag/grav feature on major Florieton Fault drill tested to identify turbidite sequence. Hole DEL10AC214 identified localised schist with strong sericite-quartz-clay alteration, with elevated values for Cu-Au-U, including 2m at 0.26g/tAu from 68m.
exploration by Goldfields Australia PL in 2011 on magnetic and gravity features identified best value 0.41g/tAu in hole DEL09AC097.

deposit of limonite>>goethite in host banded iron formation of the Lower Middleback Iron Formation. Resource drilling has identified a total resource (23/7/2017) of 5.9Mtonne at 53.5%Fe at cut off 47%Fe to a depth below surface of ~90m.

quarry on Pleistocene calcrete worked for road base material. Drilling confirmed calcrete profile to ~7m deep, with chemical analysis and metallurgical testwork indicating suitable for use in acid neutralisation in HPAL processing plant.
exploration of ESE extension of Wingellina deposit. Single drill hole intercept of Ni oxide-bearing clays over Giles Complex mafic/ultramafic rocks. Hole CHRB0012 with 31m at 0.3%Ni.
drill traverse across Paling Range with HM intersections 3-6m thick at depths 15-42m, grade 1.2-2.3%. Variable composition, zircon 6-25%, ilmenite 36-73%.

exploration for heavy mineral sands by Iluka Resources in 2008 identified significant intervals in several aircore drill holes. Best values hole EP1006 13.5m at 1.5%HM at 27m, and hole EP1033 4.5m at 3.9%HM at 15m.

exploration for heavy mineral sands by Ikuka Resources in 2011 by aircore drill traverses identified intervals of heavy minerals. Best values EP1238, 1.5m at 13.7%HM from 31.5-33m, hole EP1233, 1.5m at 10.9%HM from 30m.

exploration for heavy mineral sands by Ikuka Resources in 2005 by aircore drill traverses identified intervals of heavy minerals. Best values EP303, 1.5m at 3.1%HM from 36m, hole EP296, 1.5m at 3.3%HM from 13.5m.
2 small aeolian dunes of the Holocene Bunyip Formation, with thickness of 0.5m of sand meeting specification for concrete sand. Disadvantaged by presence of overburden of fine sand.

historic quarrying of the limestone cliffs . Visited in 1950 to test the suitability of stone for building stone. Rock appears to be too friable for quality stone. Petrology confirmed a friable, sandy limestone of the Tertiary Morgan Limestone.
occurrence of mineral specimens of the minerals allanite, zircon, and euxenite, U and REE-bearing minerals in host pegmatite.

occurrence identified during regional mapping of the 250k Alberga map sheet in the mid 1950s of yellow-green beryl, and small tantalite crystals in host pegmatite. Location not accurrate, reported only as near Windmill Well.
intense circular magnetic anomaly drill tested to identify 42m interval of crystalline magnetite from 190-232m, minor quartz within host GRV volcanics. No anomalous base or precious metals.

calcareous, laminated and phosphatic sandstone, with patchy manganese oxide staining on Brighton Limestone. Sampled in 1977 by the Geological Survey for return of low values. Abandoned roadmetal quarry develped by local council on the site.

rock chip samples with elevated REE (#1563989), including Nd to 1,650ppm, Sm to 250ppm, La to 3,300ppm, Pr to 550ppm, and Ce to 4,950ppm. Sampling over an area ~1.5km NE by 600m wide, with anomalous REE.

rock chip traverses across outcrop of Yerila Granite by CRA Exploration PL in the early 19902 over an area of anomalous radiometrics. Samples returned weakly anomalous values for REE. Source of radiometric anomaly probably thorium.
CUMBERLAND, 2 rock chip samples from siliceous ironstone on W margin of the Yongala Diapir. Appear to be at the same stratigraphic level. Elevated REE values range from 1300-1700ppmCe and 1000ppmLa.
gravity anaomalies NW of White Hill Mafic Complex, drill tested in 2 holes for thin interval of weakly anomalous P -(REE).

low ridge of exposed Pleistocene sheet to nodular calcrete immediately SW of Morgan township, with multiple small pits excavated within an area ~1km long  NW by >500m wide. Material used for road maintenance by the local council.
area of exposed Pleistocene sheet to nodular calcrete located adjacent to the Morgan Road, with 2 pits excavated for supply of road base material.
area of exposed Pleistocene sheet to nodular calcrete located adjacent to the Morgan Road, with several pits excavated for supply of road base material.

area of ~2km2 of multiple abandoned council pits developed on exposures of Pleistocene sheet calcrete, and worked for road fill.
east for ~5km from Mount Mary adjacent to the main road multiple roadside pits on Pleistocene sheet calcrete, and worked for road fill.
shallow council pit of ~1Ha x 1-4m deep, and developed on clay and gravel of the Pleistocene Telford gravel for supply of road base material.

historic workings on Fe-Mn ironstone on Teatree fault. manganese and iron oxide ironstones as cappings to 6m depth, and carrying anomalous Cu-U, best values in drill samples of 9,200ppmCu and 77ppm U.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic trending on S extension of Sliding Rock Lode. In 1972  tested by Endevour Oil NL in hole PDSL2 for hole was terminated at 23m in Parachilna Formation due to unsatisfactory sample returns. No anomalous geochemistry was reported.

historic workings on show of malachite staining developed on weathered, leached, and sheared sandstone of the Parachilna Formation. Sample collected by Aberfoyle Exploration PL in the early 1980s returned values of 180ppmCu, 120ppmZn.

small lode of shear-hosted vein quartz carrying pitchblende in host quartzite of the Freeling Quartzite. Tested in 1 diamond hole to confirm persistence of lode at depth, but not considered to be of economic significance.
no details, copper show recorded during exploration by Anaconda Australia Inc. in 1966. Host mapped as metasediment of the Wonoka Formation.
copper show identified in 1966 during mapping by Anaconda Australia Inc. Location mapped as close to contact between Merinjina Tillite and overlying Tapley Hill Formation.
historic workings on show of copper mineralisation in host diapiric Curdimurka Subgroup. Located by Anaconda Australia Inc in 1966, and explored further by Aberfoyle Exploration PL in the mid 1980s.
historic working on copper show, and mapped by Anaconda Australia Inc in 1966. Located within diapiric Curdimurka Subgroup.
minor workings on copper shows ~380m south east of the main open cut at Old Nuccaleena in host tectonite. Second group of minor workings across the creek and 350m to SSW.
minor workings on copper shows ~1.2km south of the main open cut at Old Nuccaleena, and developed in Tapley Hill Formation.
zone of copper mineralisation in faulted Brachina Formation. Detailed mapping, and geochemical sampling confirmed a Cu-As anomaly in gossan after pyritic siderite +/- quartz veins.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: historic workings on shows of copper mineralisation in altered Callana Beds of dolomite emplaced in an EW-trending fault zone. Rock samples returned anomalous values for Cu, As, Co, and Ni.

scattered workings developed along a shear-hosted ESE-trending quartz vein carrying copper and gold mineralisation. Workings distributed over a distance of ~500m. Host is metasediment of the Mesoproterozoic Willyama Complex.
historic workings on copper, lead, zinc and silver mineralisation associated with gossanous quartz veins as infill of shear/breccia zones in host Bonney Sandstone.
historic prodpecting pits on gossanous Pb-Zn mineralisation in host metasediment of the Bonney Sandstone. Cauldron Energy sampl taken in 2013 (MR13RC068).
historic pits on ironstone carrying Pb-Ag mineralisation. Host is metasediment of the Bonney Sandstone.
historic shaft to >5m deep on gossan, with visible pyrite. Sampled by Cauldron Energy Ltd in 2013 for return of copper at 2.52% Cu. Host is metasediment of the Bonney Sandstone.
historic shaft to ~50m deep on gossanous quarz vein from 2-10m wide, with visible galena. Sampled by Cauldron Energy Ltd in 2013. Host is metasediment of the Bonney Sandstone.
rock chip sample from a feruginous quartz vein in host metasediment of the Belair Subgroup. Chemical analysis returned values of 2.15%Zn, 300ppmPb, 170ppmAs, 20ppmBi, 220ppmCd, and 17ppmAg.
weathered mafic/ultramafic rock of the Mulgathing Complex, with Cr values to 7,700ppmCr, Ni to 1,670ppm.
phosphorite of the Mernmerna Formation identified over a strike length of ~2.5km. Best value sample # 2,053,285, State geochem database, with 8.38% P2O5, also elevated F to 6,720ppm, and U to 23ppm.

weathered, earthy, argillaceous and arenaceous strata of the Tarcowie Siltstone. Flinders Mine Ltd sampled a phosphate rock in 2008 for a returned value of 21.1% P2O5 (sample # 1,694,990 State geochem database).

drill hole HKN 99 with Proterozoic metapelite for 84-88m @ 4m at 4,575ppbAu. Calcrete grid sampling by shallow auger drilling identified significant accompanying calcrete anomalies for gold, silver, arsenic, and copper.
igneous complex, and adjacent skarn lithology drill tested to confirm elevated geochemistry for Zn-Pb, minor Cu-Ag-Au mineralisation.

historic workings sampled by Shell Company of Australia Ltd in 1982, with sample F2 returning a value of 5.5ppm Au from a sideritic brecciated rock, with minor quartz in host diapiric sediment of the Curdimurka Subgroup.
historic shaft, with rock outcrop sampled by Cauldron Energy Ltd in 2013. Sample no. MR13RC041 returned value of 6.45 ppm Au, 4.15% Pb, 0.257%Zn, 17.8ppmAg, and 3.1%As.

gold-in-calcrete anomaly on the Yalbrinda Shear Zone, and drill tested by Equinox in 1996. Drill traverses confirmed pyrite altered Hiltaba Granite, variously sheared, with best intercept 4m at 0.64g/tAu.
gold exploration in the lakes area east of Mt Finke. Rock chip sampling gave best result 1.47ppmAu. 1 2-5 gm gold nugget discovered on the lake bed.
3 aircore drill traverses on magnetic complex with widespread elevated values for Cu, also scattered elevated values for Au, Mo, As, Zn.
elevated base metal values to >1%Zn, Pb, Ag, As in core of Kspar-qz-sericite rock of the Bimba Suite.

rock sample from outcrop on a creek bank of fractured, very silicified, yellow-brown quartzite, with abundant malachite, and chalcocite. Chemical analyses returned values of 39.5%Cu, 100ppmAg, 120ppmZn, 40ppmPb, and 40ppmNi.
outcrop of fossiliferous red marble of the Cambrian Ajax Limestone considered to have potential for dimension stone. 8 tonne bulk sample taken for polished slabs. Resource estmate 10 Mtonne.
soil Zn anomaly, with associated gravity anomaly in area of structural complexity in hematite-altered Wilkawillina Limestone.
single aircore drill travers 900m N of Neitherleigh Park prospect. ).2%Cu, 2.1%Pb in hole ALAC 030 indicates strike continuity of mineralisation.

grid aircore holes on 5 NS traverses. Bedrock lithology penetrated at ~30m depth of deeply weathered gneiss and intrusive anomalies carrying broad intervals of elevated values for base metals. Best values 1.75%Pb, 0.235%Zn, 16ppmAg.

tenure as ML 4602 granted in 1978 for recorded production of 87 gm gold. located on southern limit of the historic Jupiter Creek alluvial diggings, and presumably worked Tertiary gravels for alluvial gold.

tenure granted in 1991 as ML 5772 on historic workings located on the southern end of the Grainger line-of-lode. Recorded production in 1992 of  1.3 oz (32gm) gold. Host is altered metasediment of the Appila Tillite.

low lying swamp area considered for salt production. Advantages proximity to sea, and transport hub, disadvantage, winter flooding, and small area available.

no details, located from mine symbol on unpublished State mineral occurrences 250K map series. Host sequence from 100K digital geology dataset is of the Curdimurka Subgroup.

occurrence of Tertiary ferruginous, cemented sandstone tested in 3 diamond holes for its suitability for use as road aggregate. testwork indicated suitable for use as base course material, but not for aggregate.

located during reconnaissance mapping of the Oraparinna Diapir by R. hare and Associates in the mid 1960s, one of many small barite shows identified within the area of the Oraparinna Diapir, and associated with brecciated rocks close to the rim of the diapir.

no details, historic diggings on copper show in diapiric rim rocks of the Oraparinna Diapir, possibly of a prospecting nature,  identified during reconnaissance mapping in the mid 1960s during company exploration.
no details, located from mine symbol on map produced during reconnaissance mapping by Asarco in the mid to late 1960s. Copper show on breccias associated with rim rocks of the Oraparinna Diapir.
