shallow pit of ~0.8Ha x 1-5m deep on weathered metasediment of the Etina Formation, and developed for source of road base material.

east-west line of shallow drill holes on Pleistocene olive brown clay to test the suitability for brickmaking. Testwork indicated excess presence of carbonate, and soluble salts rendered the material not suitable for brickmaking.
mixed sand and gravel creek deposit investigated for source of aggregate from coarse fraction. Potential for hard rock quarry on quartzite unit that occurs in the vicinity.

mixed creek sand and gravel deposit as possible source of road and concrete aggregate. Exposures of creek sections reveal thin beds of gravel interbedded with sand, with uppermost 60cm comprised of coarse to pebble sized gravel.
historic workings on copper-gold mineralisation on shear in host Rathjen Gneiss, and traceable for >1km along strike.

historic workings on the northernmost lode identified on the Kitticoola Mining Field. Lode trends WNW, and can be traced for >500m along strike. Copper-gold mineralisation was worked from a narrow shear lode in host Rathjen Gneiss.
abandoned local council roadside pit of <1Ha x 1-4m deep developed on Tertiary clay and sand deposit, and worked for road base material.
quartz veined shear to 3-4m wide in host Golden Pole Granite carrying tourmaline, iron oxide, minor copper carbonates, and chrysocolla.

near vertical, WNW-trending irregular quartz veined shear to 2-3m wide in host altered tillite of the Neoproterozoic Hamilton Creek Member. Worked in an open cut on vein containing quartz, jasper, iron oxide, malachite and azurite.

2 near vertical quartz veins as shear infills, trend N15E, widths from 60cm to 120cm. Host rock is tillite of the Neoproterozoic Hamilton Creek Member of the Fitton Formation. Ore minerals include copper carbonates and chrysocolla.
quartzite unit of the Stonyfell Quartzite investigated by the Geological Survey in 1949. Resource estimate 531,000 tonne on S slopes of Slapes Gully western side of Section 1058.

Pleistocene very plastic, mottled clay to 3-4m thick underlain by sandy clay. Mix of sandy clay, and plastic clay suitable for use in brick making. Using an SG of 1.9, the resource estimate for a 3 acre area was 130,000 tonne to 5m depth.
wide spaced shallow drilling in 1950 determined a resource of clay suitable for brickmaking over an area >300Ha. Area is now covered by residentual housing.
12m interval of Pleistocene white clay penetrated in  drill hole, and underlain by Cambrian dolomite and limestone of the Parara Limestone.
stratiform copper mineralisation on host Ukaparinga Schist of the Burra Group, on S extension of copper mineralisation of the Ukaparinga copper deposit.

Hopefull Hill is situated in a late Archean-Proterozoic greenstone belt in the central Gawler Craton. it encompasses three distinct greenstone belts: the Mullina Well, Hopeful Hill, and Lake Harris belts. The greenstone sequence lies beneath thin (<50m) Quaternary sand and Eocene fluvial channel deposits. A zone of complex aeromagnetics, with drilling confirming the magnetic signature is due to mafic/ultramafic rocks including komatiite. Geochem analysis of samples identified komatiite with weakly elevated Ni-Cu-Cr values. best gold value 3m at 0.24g/t in HH28.

linear aeromagnetic anomaly drill tested to confirm western continuation of komatiite-bearing sequence of the Lake Harris Komatiite, with best values in hole THAC 44, 9-72m, 63m at >1,000ppm Ni, >1,000ppm Cr in host meta-komatiite.

calcrete geochemical anomaly drill tested to determine best value 4m at 211ppbAu from 44-48m in hole MKRB 151 in host quartz-biotite schist of the Mulgathing Complex.

crystalline gypsiferous sediment in lake beds, accompanied  on the leeward side by deposits of dunal flour, and seed gypsum.

resource of offshore sand at depth suitable for dredging for use in beach replenishment. Estimate 4 million m3 or 6M tonne over an area 2km2 offshore from Port Stanvac jetty.

located from mine symbol on plan S15586. Workings of shallow pits over ~30m along a NS-trending line of lode, presumably on show of Cu-Au mineralisation in qz vein in host Mesoproterozoic Willyama Complex metasediment.
shallow prospecting pit south of the OBriens group of workings. Presumably developed on quartz veining with copper mineralisation in host Willyama Complex metasediment.

drill tested attenuated-ENE syncline of Willyama Complex including prospective, sulfidic Bimba Formation with anomalous Zn-Pb.

pits on gossanous Bimba Formation. Sampled by Aberfoyle in 1990 for maximum 0.6%Cu, 445ppmZn, 0.07g/tAu. 3 lines of aircore holes to N completed by Aberfoyle in 1999 for only weakly elevated base metal values in host Bimba Formation.
historic workings on qz veins with malachite and anomalous gold, best value to 11.9%Cu, 7.4g/tAu.

magnetic anomaly drill tested for cumulate base metals for no significant values. Cored hole indcated drilled at contact of host metasediment with gabbro sill. Sulphide concentrate with anomalous gold to 200ppb.
drilling on linear magnetic anomaly in Cambrian basement to Murray basin for fresh diorite at ~158m. Elevated Cu-Zn values in weathered zone below 136m.
magnetic feature drill tested to identify magnetite skarn with 825ppmZn, 38.4%Fe, 8,370ppmMn, 15ppmCo, 10ppmMo, low values for other base and precious metals.

early 1990s bedrock drilling traverse completed by the Geological Survey, with hole MUR 07 returned values to 88ppmAg, 1,850ppmCo from quartz veining in Adelaidean sandstone host, possibly of the Burra Group.
drill testing of magnetic anomaly associated with Bendigo-Kia Ora magnetic complex. Basement of andesitic basalt and limonite-magnetite clay with geochemical values to 910ppmCu, 2.5%Mn, 0.14ppmAu.

drill hole CAR 116 penetrated silicified, brecciated, sericitised granite, with chemical analysis of drill samples returning values anomalous in As from 8-32m (including 630ppm from 8-14m), Pb to 165ppm from 26-32m, Au to 8ppb from 32-36m (EOH).

surface sample 1039176 returned anomalous values for As (4915ppm), Ag (18ppm), Cu (620ppm, Zn (1820ppm), also elevated values for REE. Host is hydrothermally altered adamellite of the Pitjantjatjara Supersuite.

surface samples 1039234 returned anomalous values for As (6375ppm), Ag (33.5ppm), Cu (590ppm, Zn (3235ppm), also elevated values for REE. Host is hydrothermally altered adamellite of the Pitjantjatjara Supersuite.
surface sample 1039304 returned anomalous values for As (1,085ppm), Ag (44.5ppm), Cu (200ppm, Zn (210ppm). Host is hydrothermally altered metasediment of the Birksgate Complex.

rock chip samples collected by CRA Exploration PL in 1996 from outcrop of Palaeoproterozoic metasediment of the Yoolperlunna Inlier. Geochemical analysis returned anomalous values for As to 220ppm, Pb to 1,000ppm, Au to 1ppb.

conductivity structure drill tested in 4 holes. Basement at 96-116m depth of graphitic shale, siliclastics, sandstone. Best  values 6,556ppmZn from 241-242m in LMD001A, 12 samples from LMD002-3 at 3-7.5%C.
shallow pit of 0.25Ha x 1-3m deep on Pleistocene calcrete developed by the local council for supply of road making material.

copper staining of small quartz veins, and located in the nose of the Moro Anticline. Host was the Pound Quartzite. Mineralisation as hairline veins of quartz, with copper carbonate staining, and as patches and bunches of copper carbonate.
historic prospecting on copper show in host metasediment of the Bungarider Subgroup of the Burra Group.
one of several adjacent copper shows in host Boorloo Siltstone prospected in 1917, and inspected by Utah Development Ltd in the 1970s.
minor historic workings on copper shows over >150m strike length. Host is of the Top Mount Sandstone Beds.
historic shallow diggings over strike length of ~200m developed on narrow stratigraphic unit of metasediment within the Auburn Dolomite Member, possibly for phosphate rock.
historic shallow pit developed on regolith of the Saddleworth Formation, possibly for clay for construction purposes.
series of shallow historic pits developed over a strike length of >150m on a narrow stratigraphic unit of bluestone of the Saddleworth Formation, and for use as building stone.
large area of ~5.5Ha of multiple historic small shallow diggings on weathered Saddleworth Formation, presumably for clay for construction purposes.
series of shallow historic pits developed over a strike length of ~2000m on a narrow stratigraphic unit of weathered Saddleworth Formation, presumably for clays for use as construction material.

large area of scattered historic diggings at 2 stratigraphic levels on weathered Saddleworth Formation. Southernmost of diggings on same stratigraphic interval that extends along strike for ~4.9km to the NNW. Presumably worked for clay.

exploration by Copper Range in 2006, with rock chip samples from a road cutting returning elevated values for copper. Samples were of metasediment of the Bunyeroo Sandstone showing smears of malachite on fractures and bedding planes.

negatively polarised, linear magnetic anomaly drill tested. Source is diorite, with hole 1 with intervals of altered diorite marginal to hornfelsed xenoliths carrying weak pyrrhotite to chalcopyrite mineralisation. Geochemistry elevated but uneconomic Cu-Ni.
drill hole 82FN13RM1 with elevated Ag 6m at 1g/t from 101m in host altered calc-silicate.
weak gold anomalism in basal Tertiary to maximum 103ppb. basement depth 126-207m of Kanmantoo Group metasediment, volcanics and volcaniclastics.
weak zinc anomalism in weathered Truro Volcanics in basement to Murray Basin cover depth 131-156m.
weak Cu mineralisation in the weathering profile of host Adelaidean carbonaceous siltstones of the Wonoka Formation in a structurally prospective area marginal to the Bendigo Fault.
linear magnetic anomaly marginal to the Bendigo Fault drill tested in 2 holes to confirm weak Cu-Au anomalism in host metasediment possibly of the Appila Tillite.

roadside council pit of <1Ha x 1-4m deep on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road making material.
roadside council pit of ~0.2Ha x 1-4m deep on limestone of the Bridgewater Formation, and worked for road making material.

shallow, abandoned pit of ~0.5Ha excavated on Tertiary Melton Limestone.
magnesite as beds up to 1m thick interbedded with dolomite, chert and siltstone of the Skillogalee Dolomite. Mundallio North refers to a strike length of ~7km on which there are no recorded workings.
gypsiferous dunes on S margin of an ENE-trending salt lake. Tenure in 1987 over ~4km strike length. No production, extent and quality of gypsarenite remains untested.
historic mining lease 5287 granted in 1985 on the old Algebuckina Goldfield, on outcropping flat lying sheet conglomerate north of Neales River. Recorded production from 1990-93 was ~135 gm.
alluvial sand recovered from bed of creek, with production from 1980-82 of 6,600 tonne.

historic workings on quartz reefs in host Saddleworth Formation. Explored in 1987 by Battle Mountain (Aust) Inc to confirm workings on narrow quartz veins in host metasediment of the Saddleworth Formation.
lamprophyre intrusion of minette variety in regionally favourable area marginal to Darling-redan lineament, with potential for lamprophyre - mesothermal gold deposit model.

kimberlite sill discovered in 1973. Bulk sampling by Stockdale failed to detect diamonds. Recent work has shown East and West sills, previously considered separate bodies, are probably related and appear to be nearly horizontal.
ultramafic intrusive in NE sector of the Spalding Diapir with erratic but elevated copper, also anomalous Cr, Pt, Pd.

historic prospecting shafts on a hillside developed on brown-yellow, quartz-hematite breccia after siltstone of the Wilyerpa Formation. Texture includes gossanous boxworks. Geochemical samples returned 640ppmCu, 5ppmMo, 710ppmZn, and 60ppmNi.

historic prospecting shafts on a hillside developed on diapiric, brown-yellow, quartz-hematite breccia with marcasite in host after siltstone of the Pualco Tillite. Geochemical samples returned 340ppbAu, 590ppmZn, and 58ppmNi.

rock chip samples from granodiorite, and amphibolite of the St Peters Suite with elevated values of tin to >400ppm. Also several narrow lamprophyre dykes thought to be of an intrusive age related to St Peters Suite magmatism (1620-1610Ma).
corundum occurrence in altered corundum-rich schist in hydrothermally altered ultramafic emplaced in Paralana Fault zone
rock chip samples of ironstone on the Arcoona Plateau. Elevated values for Cu to 100ppm, U to 23ppm thought to indicated potential for nearby ore deposit.

drill testing of W portion of 3.5km2 of 17km2 synclinal fold basin containing intervals of magnetite- hematite-bearing Braemar Ironstone. XRF & chem analyses confirm head grades >20%Fe. DDH14 completed for 486m at 24%XRF Fe from 127m.

coincident magnetic and gravity anomaly drill tested in DD88ME-2 to identify a sequence of volcanics and mafic to ultramafic intrusives with weak sulfide mineralisation. Later modelling indicated the historic hole missed the target.
zone of intense hydrothermal alteration, with associated quartz veining, dolomitisation and silicification. Weakly anomalous in base and precious metals.
zone of elevated base and precious metals in drill hole intervals of altered diorite of the Bendigo Granite, and host metasediment of the Appila Tillite.
western contact zone to the Bendigo Granite with host siltstone of the Ulupa Siltstone with strongly anomalous values for copper to 750-3,850ppm, and with slightly anomalous gold.

diamond hole KM1 sited on magnetic feature targeting Zn SEDEX prospect. Hole penetrated black shale of Tapanappa Formation with elevated to 500ppmZn, lesser Cu-Pb. Also lamprophyre dykes with elevated base metals, best Au to 10ppb.
small magnetic anomaly with associated green fuschite rock exposed in prospecting pit. Drill tested in 2 aircore holes to determine Ni-Cr-Co anomalism to 0.3%Ni, 0.2%Cr, 0.1%Co.
ultramafic to mafic rock of Fowler Belt identified in aircore holes for best values to 1.68%Ni, 51ppb Pt + Pd, 2,160ppmCo.

gld-in-calcrete anomaly to 10ppb drill tested to identify anomalous As to 415ppm, weak Au to 0.1ppm. Host qz-fx-bi gnss of the Mulgathing Complex.
arcuate linear magnetic anomaly on differentiated mafic intrusion marginal and west of the regional Muckanippie Anorthosite Complex. Best values >1,400ppmNi, >5,000ppmCr.

grid drilled in 2011 on a SW-trending target for best result 1.5m at 29.6% HM from 52.5m in hole MAR0909, zircon to 47.8%. Follow up drilling confirmed HM mineralisation inconsistent, thin, deep, and predominantly low to moderate HM grades.

RC aircore drilling for best interval 2m at 0.51g/tAu from 52m. Follow up hole DNM583 drilled to basement for no significant values returned.

drill testing of a linear magnetic anomaly for best value 7m at 0.18%Cu in hole SP09.
surficial gossanous unit within Willyama Complex with elevated gold to 0.45g/t. Drill tested to confirm weak copper enrichment, with no associated gold values.

drilling south of Vertigo orebody confirmed base and precious metal mineralisation in altered calc-silicate altered metasediment, and with an orientation comparable to that of Vertigo.

DEPOSIT_SUMMARY: Mapping, surface sampling, and re-assaying of historic drill samples by Petrotherm Ltd. in 2024, found high-grade titanium rich heavy mineral sands (HMS) over several kilometres In the Muckanippie Suite. Further exploratory drilling by Petrotherm Ltd. is planned to test for high Titanium-Vanadium bearing source rock horizons for primary VTM style deposits. Phase 2 drilling completed in 2025 included 73 holes (2225m of drilling) confirmed the high HM concentration with over 90% of the holes intersecting at least 5m  >5% HM conentration. The northern most hole ended in strong mineralisation, with further extention to the mineralisation to the north. Phase 3 program to be planned to include additional drilling and sampling to inform mineral recovery and success of the seperation techniques.

Muckanippie Ti is a placer-type heavy mineral sand occurence found by Marmota Ltd. following the 2024 discoveries of Titanium-rich HMS by Petratherm Ltd., at their nearby Rosewood and Claypan prospects. Initial drilling tested a 1.5 km by 750 m total magnetic intensity anomaly identified within a newly interpreted paleochannel. The bends in this channel are seen as highly prospective for the concentration of placer type HMS minerals

Rock chip sampling by Petratherm in 2024, returned TiO2 assays ranging between 5.7% and 31.5% TiO2. Higher-grade mineralised horizons were found on the southern side of an interpreted high Titanium-Vanadium basement source rock horizon which has a distinctive magnetic signature. The Claypan Prospect has a high potential for basement-hosted Ti-V targets immediately below and adjacent to the HMS mineralisation.

The Carinya uranium prospect, was lidentified by Afmeco Pty Ltd (Afmeco) in 1980. which found anomalous surface uranium mineralisation. The prospect is a part of Lincoln Minerals regional ‘Yallunda Uranium Project’. Surface exploration in 2024/25 aims to define any further geological structures that might explain the anomolous uranium.

Exploration by Indiana Resources Ltd. in 2022, established the presence of significant REE values in the regolith near the Minos Gold Prospect, as part of their Central Gawler Project tenements.  Assays confirmed widespread REE mineralisation, with intersections up to 76m thick recording high total REE (TREO) and magnet REE (MREO) values. The source of the REE has not been identified, however as the REE mineralisation is hosted in regolith and weathered saprolite/clays it is likely associated with the weathering of the alkaline Hiltaba Granite and gneissic basement rocks of the Gawler Craton.
The Partridge Prospect is located a short distance to the NW of the Minos gold & REE prospects within the Lake Labyrinth Shear Zone.

Earea Dam Goldfield is an area containing a number of individual historic mines and workings along a strike length of about 650 m. The field was discovered in1899 when a Mr J.W Kingsmill found specimens of gold-bearing quartz in surface outcrops near Earea Dam on Wilgena Station.  The field produced 59.2 kg of gold from 1869.6 t of ore (average grade 35.3 g/t) during the 1899–1903 and 1933–41period with production predominantly from the Wilgena Enterprise and Perseverance Mines.
